Spike Bears reside in the plains and mountainous regions of Jixia. 
They are named for their spike-like manes on their backs. 
When hunting, they strike the weak spots of their prey with mighty palms. 
 
Travelers passing through areas where Spike Bears are known to inhabit often carry their favorite foods, such as honey and fish, to divert their attention and avoid becoming targets.
It calls itself a "little healer" and is obsessed with all sorts of unconventional remedies, some of which may not be trustworthy.

Mechanoid fighters forged from a mysterious metal. 
 
Their armor is embedded with shiny plates, making them incredibly durable. 
 
In combat, they use basic yet effective moves. 
 
The scars and gashes on their bodies speak of their lives as battle-hardened soldiers.

A multi-functional, adjustable telescopic drying rack made of sturdy, lightweight material.

Inspired by the mecharms of Luban from the Star Team. It features windproof clips, is durable, and has a high load-bearing capacity. It sold out immediately upon release and is a favorite among Jixia students. It is said that many Chang'an mechanists visiting Jixia also keep one as a souvenir.

Due to its telescopic nature, many martial arts students use it as a pull-up bar in their doorways or against walls for training anytime, anywhere. Every school year, the Hundred-Treasures Workshop prepares a batch in advance for freshmen.

A Mechcraft warrior wielding a blade of fire. Beneath the black-gold armor, a fiery core burns ceaselessly. The Ten-Thousand-Forge Blade is highly skilled in close-quarters combat, striking with the weight of a mountain. The intense heat of its massive fire blade is enough to melt metal. Few creatures dare to provoke the Ten-Thousand-Forge Blade, and it does not provoke others. Combat is no longer its mission, but its fated destiny.

A noble and elegant bird with a slender build. The blue-purple icy feathers on its eyelashes resemble the dark, distant mountains, giving it an air of unreachability.\n\nUnlike the Cloud-Unseen, the Distant-Mountain-Dark does not like to be close to humans. When it encounters visitors, it flies away after a brief glance, as if expressing its dissatisfaction at being disturbed. They are often used as a metaphor for those who are highly focused.

Flamecap Shrooms have undergone mutations under the influence of Aercocoon. They have eye-catching red caps resembling open umbrellas. 
 
 
 
They release spores as a self-defense mechanism. Some Gourmets use them to ignite their stoves, which is efficient. However, beware that the flames might consume more than just firewood.

Leaf Lizardlings are commonly found in Jixia. Their skin color perfectly matches the surroundings, providing superb camouflage. This ability helps them protect themselves and hunt prey. \n \nThey are believed to be the juvenile stage of the Leaftail Lizards, hence the name.

The Dream Demon of Painted Shadows is the embodiment of darkness in the dream. Now, its ambition has expanded, twisting everyone's dreams into a disaster.

[Three-Phase Illusion]: The Dream Demon of Painted Shadows cycles between wolf, bear, and human forms, each with unique combat tactics.

[Nightmare Seizure]: When in bear or human form, it summons Nightmare Butterflies to snatch a player and fly toward a Nightmare Rift. Teammates must shoot down the butterflies in time, or a devastating explosion will be triggered upon falling into the rift.

[Vine Binding Kill]: The Wooden Fence King releases vines to bind all players and summons Wooden Fence Spear Guards to charge across the field. You must break free from the vines as soon as possible to avoid attacks.\n\n[Spirit-Absorbing Giantization]: The Wooden Fence King absorbs the vitality of surrounding small wooden fences, its body expanding rapidly and covering itself with an indestructible thorn armor. At this time, Bombardment Guards appear on the sidelines throwing fire bombs. Only by picking up the fire bombs and throwing them at the Wooden Fence King's armor can you gradually dismantle its defense; otherwise, its power will continue to grow with its size until it crushes the entire field.

Larger than a typical Aero Jellyfish, the Aero Specter has a deep color and eye-catching patterns on its exterior. 
Its tendrils move gracefully like the accessories on an elegant gown. 
 
Students who first encounter it are easily attracted by its beauty, unaware of the suffocating danger that lurks behind it.

Modified by the academy, they gather Sorcery energy for attacks behind Nimble Vanguards. \n \nThe academy commands them to only attack students who attend the trial. If their cores are attacked, they move anomalously or spin in place.

A dark, eerie figure, an incarnate nightmare.
The tall, slender Dreamslayer lurks in the shadows and dreams, waiting for the perfect moment to strike.
The shadows beneath its purple feathers are the prey's final memory, and the moon-blade it wields is the pride of a lone hunter.
The Moon-blade Dreamslayer is born from dreams, one with everything around it.
It moves through the air with ease, its gorgeous slashes like phantoms.

It tears through dream after dream, traversing fantasy after fantasy.
Its dark footsteps are merely the prelude to the hunt; the dreams of the mediocre are the food it survives on.
Beautiful and elegant, it always carried a hint of sadness—until it met you.

Often found in Jixia ruins, they have a pot-like body and four spider-like legs. 
When alerted, their bodies glow, foreshadowing an impending icy blast. 
 
The terror of their explosion is akin to the bone-chilling sensation of a sudden snowstorm.

Quakecannon Aeroclads are an upgraded version of the Artillery Aeroclad, crafted from Aerux by the academy. 
Cannons peek from their Aerux-covered shoulders, firing cannonballs infused with the power of ground-shaking forces. 
 
Students who challenge them after refining their footwork are often dismayed to find that their opponents have also grown stronger. 
A staggering strike from a cannonball numbs their limbs, a harsh reminder that they still have much to learn.

[Nut Bait]: The Armored Rat King summons several small armored rats to roll around and cause chaos. One of them carries a special nut; defeating it leaves the nut on the field. The Armored Rat King then pulls all players in and binds two of them with resonance vines (the bound are silenced, and if they get too far apart, they are pulled back). The remaining teammates must pick up the nut to lure the King's charge. The two players connected by vines must pull in opposite directions to use the vines as a tripwire to trip the charging giant rat.

It reigns atop the Aerux, leaving no space for anything else to endure. 
 
Its mane has crystallised into glittering shards, while its vast shadow stretches across the mountains at dusk. 
 
Born at the Aerux's core, where Aerflow runs densest, it wields overwhelming power—yet finds no worthy foe, and with each passing day, grows ever more alone. 
 
With ease, it shatters boulders and snaps trees, its strength unmatched. Still, no opponent has risen to challenge it. 
 
For years, a nearby town offered rewards for its defeat. Now, that town lies abandoned and in ruins—nothing remains but rotting wood and scattered pages, a silent warning to all who would come near.

A lost Sorcery creation of the academy. 
The hollow globe emits a Sorcery energy that has manifested in the form of a flame. 
It floats midair with its rather unsettling appearance. 
 
The Wind Delicacy is agile and quick to evade, making it hard to deal with. 
There are many rumors of people being chased by blue flames at night in areas frequented by the Wind Delicacy.
A playful yet affectionate Divine Beast cub, agile and loyal. \nDespite its young age, it has already developed a love for angling and will keep you company during your angling sessions.

They can't speak, yet they follow her every command. 
In the stories of protection and sacrifice, they've created a more brutal legend. 
"Protect Zero Zero One." 
An eternal order and a beautiful name.

Patrol Sentinels are Mechanoids created by the School of Mechcraft to patrol and guard Jixia. 
They are mainly made of pure white oak and gold-trimmed metal, small and agile. 
They are equipped with leaf-shaped blades propelled by the drive and slash at targets in a scythe-like fashion. 
 
They are occasionally put to work trimming the shrubbery in the gardens by instructors.

Bronze Constructors are Mechanoid workers who repair facilities in ruins. 
Resembling crabs, they have two pincers, walk on four legs, and have bronze shells of Aerux with glittering markings. 
They maintain large bronze facilities as well as Mechanoids. 
 
They are kept busy all day mending things. If not disturbed, they just ignore anyone who comes along.

Mushrooms mutated by the influence of the Aercocoon. They have eye-catching purple caps resembling open umbrellas. The Umbrella Spore-shroom releases spores as a defensive mechanism.\n\nThose who wield blades and spears keep their distance from these mushrooms. It's not that they are invincible, but their numbing spores are incredibly annoying.

Scorch Lizardlings are commonly found in Jixia. 
Their skin color reflects their affinity for fire, which serves to deter enemies. 
 
They are believed to be the juvenile stage of the Scorchtail Lizard, hence the name.

It's the very definition of "well read." More than that, it's dedicated to solving people's problems with the books stored in its belly. Its greatest wish is for everyone to fall in love with reading.

Freeze the camp with ice, and burn it with fire. 
 
Those words are carved into the Mechanoid. They show the creator's understanding of war and explain its purpose. 
 
Two energies fused and fed each other, amplifying the cannon fire so no defense could hold. 
 
Yet the Mechanoid lay abandoned beneath the ruins. It never got a chance to be used. The horn for the counterattack never sounded—the craftsmen who built it had already died defending it.

Originally created by the academy to simulate battle scenes, these little Mechcraft minions quickly gained popularity due to their adorable appearance. \n \nLoyal and dependable, they are their master's most thoughtful guards.

He has lingered for a long time in this world, while his companion has returned to where it came. 
 
The Sentinel wanders the valleys. He is a cavalier without a ride. The giant sword on his shoulder shows the hard-to-believe size of his companion. 
 
The only thing he can count on now is the giant sword that's become a part of him. His powerful strike can still cut through mountains and rivers even without a vertical dive. 
 
The dragon rider still holds the pact with the dragon. Since the ride is gone, the place where they parted is likely to be where he will spend the rest of his days.

[Desperate Fire Shield]: The charges initiated by the four phantom clones of the Blade-Severing Spirit must all be lured into the Lone Halberd Spirit's Fire Shield. Any mistake will result in failure to break the shield, testing the team's precise execution and coordination.

Fighters of the Saepes tribe.
Clad in leaves, with twisted vines wrapped around a crude blowpipe.
Saepes Scouts excel at ambushing enemies from the shadows with blowdarts; the poisoned projectiles leave enemies in constant misery.

According to research, the toxins in Saepes blowdarts come from a variety of sources, including but not limited to: Poison Bubble Buds, Leaf-tailed Lizards, Jade Tear Fruits...

The leader of the Embermanes has fiery hair and blade-like claws. The flames are fierce, but its hair never burns.
Having fought its way to kingship, it leads the pack.
The flames it breathes scorch its throat, making it even more excited.
The burning prey is a playful toy. It is the one in control, while the challenger is only fit to defend.
The Embermane once challenged others, but now, it has become the king.
At this moment, the red shadow standing among the beasts will shock all living things.

With its arrival, the fire ignites.
With its departure, the fire will eventually extinguish.

Often found in Jixia ruins, they possess a crab-like pincer and an ice cannon that emanates frost. 
They emit extreme cold to resolve issues caused by overheating within the ruins. 
 
Each time a novice explores the ruins, the Herb Garden welcomes a new patient with frostbite injuries.

Truth lies in the straightforward, not in the twisted. 
A shadow with few words, an old friend who is not skilled in rhetoric. 
Golden veins emerge from illusions, and mighty power rises from a fixed gaze. 
The long staff shakes the earth and mountains, leaving destruction in its wake. 
When the withered hand flips, rivers and seas freeze, and even the horses fall silent. 
 
The frosty-haired, iron-faced figure—did it ever crack for a moment, revealing a hidden frustration that no one could understand? 
The moon-like, razor-sharp gaze—did it ever sweep across the disciples, seeing through the bloodshed and chaos that was to come? 
The silent Sentinel remained silent. Perhaps the shadow had no words, or perhaps the old friend had nothing left to say.

Flamebearer Falcons circle the lands of Jixia. 
Their fan-shaped crowns are particularly magnificent. 
These entirely flame-red raptors excel at launching sudden attacks from above. 
They are swift as a gale, making them difficult to defend against. 
 
Cannoneers have a special affection for Flamebearer Falcons, and many Mechanoid Birds are modeled after them. 
However, most only mimic its appearance.
Dodou, wearing a small straw hat and cape, loves to play practical jokes on people.

An ancient creature from the Dreamscape,  
it possesses a hooked beak and claws sharp as blades. 
Its resonant tail follows its slender body, dancing through the air of the Dreamscape. 
 
It attacks swiftly at close range, unexpectedly casting spells in the fray. 
But its presence becomes most threatening when it appears alongside other Dreamscape creatures. 
Anyone caught in such peril can only pray to be awakened from the dream.

Saepes Summoners are born with the will of their ancestors and use that power to protect their people. Each carries a twisted, forked staff that hums with whispers only Saepes can hear. 
 
As tribal leaders, their main job is to choose the best places for future generations to grow and thrive. 
 
Researchers believe the tribe's success comes from the special bond between them and their younger, unevolved members.
The Armored Rat King has been nourished by cloud currents for years. It is massive with thick, hard armor, and it sneaks into the fields to steal grain during village festivals.

The Dragonpike Sentinel is one of the Trialgiver Sentinels in the ancient Enlightenment Trials. Clad in black armor with gleaming gold accents on his arms, this sentinel wields a pike that brings enduring conflicts. He has waited here for millennia to pass on his endurance skills. 
 
Only those with a heart filled with determination can hope to withstand the power of thousands. The Dragonpike Sentinel and his challengers excel in prolonged battles, never shying away from clashes. However, age has finally taken his toll, forcing him to bend his back. 
 
Can you bring back these battle skills as sturdy as the mountains on the barren battlefield?

The giant Palisaepes live underground. The fruits growing on their twisted branches are infused with properties of various plants to produce herb-like effects. 
They are highly accurate throwers who never miss a target. 
 
Herbalists have attempted to obtain these fruits in pristine condition for study but have consistently failed to get close. 
They usually return peppered with slivers of fruit.

Beast eyes glare with malice, iron claws strike hard. Its spine is like rock, its stride like a gale. Beneath its fur, a violent heart beats. Its hammer strikes like thunder across the plains. Plunder and conquest are its only understanding of martial arts. This tiger-kin bandit leader awaits the mercy of the legendary hammer-wielder. 'Quiet in the woods yesterday, fierce down the mountain today.'

Spring brings growth, fall brings fruit, with branches heavy with ripe produce. 
 
In its prime, the Saepes sways with plentiful fruit, thanks to the fertile soil. 
Its sturdy trunk absorbs and transforms Aerflow into three distinct streams, while its fruits shimmer with radiant light. 
Though all creatures covet its fruit, the Saepes fiercely resists. 
Across the vast, boundless forests of Jixia, its seeds are scattered far and wide. 
 
No fruit starts off as a fruit. 
A fruitful giant Saepes also needs to initially break through the earth's crust.

This place was ruined by excessive flooding. The craftsmen worked around the clock to come up with a solution. 
 
Station Ruins Sentry, shaped like a bastion, hides the secrets of the past. 
 
Its large, many-jointed legs give it remarkable flexibility. 
 
With strong defenses and powerful attacks, it is built for simple, brutal tactics that crush invaders. 
 
Station Ruins Sentry was created to move stones and hold back the sea, leaving behind a vast underground world of winding rivers and strange creatures.
This cat, though lazy and gluttonous and hardly brave or loyal, will treat you the same whether you're at your best or at your worst.

Its roar is thunderous, its movement like the sound of the sky. 
Once galloping across vast plains, the thundering bull's enormous horns contain the power of thunder. 
Now it treads leisurely, accompanied only by the sky. 
Its dark fur surges continuously, like raging waves. 
It holds its own place. Anyone who steps foot within will face a thunderous strike. 
Perhaps it once tried to live in a herd, but those who got close have likely turned to ashes. 
 
It wanders, it stands still. 
It destroys, it's lost. 
Now, it's time.

Naughty Civets, occasionally found in the wilderness of Jixia, are cute creatures with orange fur coats and conical hats. 
With massive ears, snowy white manes, and smooth fur, they enjoy collecting and mixing various plant materials, displaying adeptness in creating herbal mixes. 
 
Some Herbalists keep Naughty Civets as companions to gather herbs together. 
Legends speak of a particularly knowledgeable Naughty Civet who even accepted a human apprentice, who later became the renowned Herbalist known as the "Sage of Healing."

A Mechcraft warrior wielding a blade of fire. Beneath the black-gold armor, a fiery core burns ceaselessly. The Ten-Thousand-Forge Blade is highly skilled in close-quarters combat, striking with the weight of a mountain. The intense heat of its massive fire blade is enough to melt metal. Few creatures dare to provoke the Ten-Thousand-Forge Blade, and it does not provoke others. Combat is no longer its mission, but its fated destiny.

These creatures have dull, dark colors that allow them to perfectly blend into their environment. 
They are extremely fast and leave ephemeral phantoms of their passage in faint light. 
 
They silently leap within the shadows, appearing as one with the shadowy world. 
Their presence seems to have been forgotten, with no records of any of them being caught before.

Bronze Gunners are defensive Mechanoids found in the ruins. 
Their four legs are scattered, with a cannon at the center, ready to eliminate any intruder. 
They are capable of both offense and defense, switching between the two as the situation evolves. 
 
It is hard to explain the inspiration behind them, but it must have had something to do with a creature that lived in the sea or the river.

Driven by hunger, the Armadillo Rat King unleashes its full strength. Summoned Armored Rats are much tougher, while nut bait now wears off quickly. \n \nThe little Armored Rats now have greatly increased health, requiring heavier firepower to dispatch quickly. Dropped nuts lose their lure range very quickly, so the nut carrier and vine handler must act in perfect sync. Any delay can break the bind and cost you the supply cache.

Saepes King rules with absolute authority. It uses its scepter to overpower anyone who opposes it. 
 
Vinebind Assault: Thick vines trap all players while Saepes charge in with spears. Break free quickly to avoid the incoming strikes. 
 
Soul Siphon: Saepes King drains life from nearby Saepes, growing huge and wrapping himself in thorn armor that blocks damage. Saepes Catapultors spawn and fling fireballs—grab those fireballs and throw them at Saepes King to shatter his armor. Otherwise, his size and power will keep increasing and threaten to crush the whole area.

Lord Botu is a cold hunter who has fallen into the dream. He comes wrapped in darkness, vowing to drag this dream into total destruction.\n\n[Deepest Nightmare]: Lord Botu summons a deep darkness that devours everything. The bright area around the Nightmare Light Platform can protect players from the continuous erosion of the darkness. Only by finding the two Nightmare Feather Guards that appear in the darkness, defeating them to seize the Nightmare Light, and successfully escorting it to the Nightmare Light Platform to light it up, can the darkness be dispelled and force him to appear.

Artillery Nebuclads are ranged Mechanoids created from Aerflow crystals by the academy. 
They bear twin crystalline cannons on their wrists, obscuring their Mechcraft markings. 
The radius of their cannon fire and attack frequency have significantly improved in quality. 
 
Many students avoid fighting them out of fear of their power. 
Their capabilities often make people wonder about their design intent.

Crazed Nebuclads are melee Mechanoids created by the academy. 
 
They are slightly bigger, with shinier armor. They wield their crystal blades reversely, striking in an unpredictable manner. They can force most students to admit defeat by striking only with the back of the blade. 
 
Their costly manufacturing process was controversial within the academy, until all misgivings were put to rest with a display of their capabilities.

[Phantom Charge]: The Blade-Severing Spirit splits into four phantom clones to lock onto different players and charge.\n\n[Precision Guidance]: The Halberd-Severing Spirit's fire shield is still on the field. Four players must accurately identify and guide their respective clones to crash into the fire shield, while staying spread out to avoid overlapping paths.

House spiders absorb Aerflow to spin webs that are light yet extremely durable. Because they have saved many lives, they are considered a symbol of good luck by the people of Jixia.\n\nWhen villagers fleeing from battle hid in the mountains, enemy soldiers pursued them closely. With no way forward, they found only tattered spider webs. In their moment of crisis, the webs seemed to sense their plight and receded, revealing a hidden cave. The villagers crouched inside to hide, and the webs returned to their original state. When the pursuers arrived, they found no trace of the villagers and eventually dispersed.

Tigrex has fully awakened his ancient bloodline. A primal beast with raw power and rock-solid defense is unleashed. 
 
Fury Shield Charge: When Tigrex charges, his Shield becomes much tougher. You must focus your attacks and deal heavy damage to break it. 
 
Earth Shatter: Right after the charge, Tigrex jumps and slams the ground repeatedly, creating full-screen shockwaves. The shockwaves cannot be dodged by jumping or dashing. Only the Shield on the field can block it.

They live in the fertile lands and are born with the will of their ancestors, using their power to protect their kind from enemies. 
 
They carry a twisted, forked staff that hums with mysterious whispers only they can hear. 
 
As leaders of the tribe, their main job is to find the best place for future generations to grow and thrive. 
 
Researchers believe that the special connection between them and their unevolved descendants is the secret to the tribe's success.

Reedepes live in wetlands. 
They wield a massive club that has been slightly worked on, and can handle it with ease despite its size. 
 
For these Reedepes, the club is more for ritualistic dances rather than for a combat.

These deer, found across Jixia, are said to originate from a distant frozen land. 
Their dreamlike blue coats earned them the name "Frost." 
This vivid hue attracts predators though. 
Frost Does only have short antler buds, which may not defend against predators but grant them greater agility. 
 
Severe cold is rare in Jixia, but herds of Frost Stags and Does huddle together when it hits, shielding their old and weak at the center. 
Hunters believe this stems from an ancient habit inherited from their icy homeland.

A bronze mechanical guard dormant in the Jixia ruins, shaped like a sitting tortoise. A stationary bronze turret used for defense. When facing enemies, the hidden cannons behind the four dark doors will turn and fire in unison. Its immense power, gained at the cost of mobility, deters anyone coveting the ruins' treasures. Some Gate-Breakers who study firearms will pay a high price for these mechanisms.

Humans assimilated by Dreamweavers after falling into Dreamscape have become Fall Dream Sprites, obsessed with sorcery as they weave boundless energy into illusory Dreams. "Might as well dream big," say the disciples at the Dream Repository.

Patrol Guardians are Mechanoids created by the School of Mechcraft to patrol and guard Jixia. 
The wings on both sides generate an elemental shield that deflects damage. 
Equipped with multi-elemental energy shields, they can protect themselves and allies. 
 
Life is precious, after all, even Rebels who find themselves in danger will receive help from Patrol Guardians.

A delicate and elegant chiming alarm clock, a godsend for those who struggle to wake up.

Baihui Workshop specially collaborated with Shye and a renowned palace musician to create this masterpiece. Place this alarm clock by your bedside; it can lull you into sweet dreams at night, ensuring a good night's sleep. In the morning, it will wake you with ethereal, dreamlike chimes. Even Master Zhuangzi highly recommends it.

Master Zhuangzi often gets lost in his dreams and loses track of time. Master Confucius has reminded him many times, but to no avail—Zhuangzi is as prone to falling asleep as ever. The Baihui Workshop alarm clock uses a gentler, more thoughtful way to wake him. Although he is still often half-asleep, at least he no longer misses meetings.

They are tasked with guarding Jixia's ruins. 
Adorned with glowing patterns etched into their bronze bodies, they wield ancient pikes with deadly precision, delivering swift and lethal strikes. 
 
Rebels or curious students alike who venture into the ruins are met with their cold steel.
Disciples of the Obsidian Flame Hall are skilled with firearms. They are not only adept at modifying them but also have deep insights into combat.

Flysol Shrooms have undergone mutations under the influence of the Aercocoon. 
Their large caps are edged with sharp, fang-like spikes. 
When threatened, Flysol Shrooms throw their caps like spinning blades at enemies. 
 
Research suggests that these tooth-like spikes are actually part of the mushroom's skin—a defensive adaptation to deter predators.

Bi Fang, the essence of wood; it looks like a bird and does not eat the five grains.
A giant bronze bird, chirping day and night. Its cry is fierce, and all who hear it weep in sorrow.
Bi Fang has forgotten many things, but it remembers its own name.
Its single leg is rusted, its wings are mottled, but its eyes still burn with a cyan, scorching fire, matching the deep flow-patterns on its body.

The tall ship gave it the mission to fly, to guard, and to fight.
But now the ship has capsized, and it still tries to fulfill its mission, even though everything it could protect has turned to ruins.
So it cries out, to at least hold onto its name, with a pride that is almost shattering:
Bi Fang, Bi Fang.

Giant Palisaepes that reside underground. 
 
The strange fruits growing from their twisted branches have long since rotted with time. 
 
They are exceptionally precise throwers, able to aim and release in one fluid motion—rarely missing their mark. 
 
Perhaps they have deliberately allowed their fruit to decay as a defensive measure. Most creatures are driven off by the stench before they can even approach, making it remarkably effective.

Bluegale Falcon gracefully circles the lands of Jixia,  
sporting fierce and beautiful indigo crowns. 
Fiercely hunting in dense forests, they use gusty winds and cold lightning to their advantage. 
 
The relationship between Flamebearer Falcons and Bluegale Falcons remains a mystery, 
and many storytellers take advantage of their similar appearances to spin tales of them supporting each other.
A wise cat who studies astrology and Sorcery. Years of learning have given it deep understanding of the world.

The Megadrive Hammer is the ultimate creation of the Academy's "Extreme Exploration" philosophy. It uses unprecedentedly tough materials to push load-bearing limits, and its deceptively simple design ensures that every strike carries the power to crush mountains.

They patrol the Underhall, detecting trespassers and emitting an alarm before attacking. 
 
Eons have passed, yet they remain on duty, immune to the ravages of time. 
What they are supposed to protect and why they do it have long been forgotten.
Croaky is an affectionate little chatterbox with a puffy bib and a round belly. It is overjoyed just to be with you.

A crystal ore bearing the features of Aerux in Jixia. Its fine texture resembles silk. \nIt is said that the Aerux deposits in the deepest reaches of Jixia were occasionally exposed to the open air through geological events and eventually came to form these Aerux Fiber Ores, brimming with power. Beware of those sharp spikes.

Leaning on a single pillow, in dreams I seek, yet dreams fade away, as the lamp's flame grows weak. 
 
Nightmare Weavers, gorgeous as if they keep the dreams of all creatures, drift through the depths of the gloomy ancient Dreamrealm. 
They cocoon the sleeping, upholding peace in that realm. 
Their wings resemble a flower bud, but when disturbed, they open to reveal an eye-like pattern that sends chills down the spine. 
 
Some return from their dreams with a different interpretation, perceiving the Nightmare Weaver as a naive young girl calling for her elder sister. 
Could this be an illusion caused by the scales on the Nightmare Weaver's wings?

Razor Aeroclads are melee Mechanoids crafted by the academy using Aerux. Their bark-like bodies are clad in Aerux armor etched with curved patterns. Wielding a single wooden blade, every movement from drawing to sheathing is clearly visible.\n\nThe Aeroclad series consists of basic Mechanoids created by the Mechanist Academy using Aerux as the primary material, reinforced with metal.

This place was ruined by excessive flooding. The craftsmen worked around the clock to come up with a solution. 
 
Station Ruins Sentry, shaped like a bastion, hides the secrets of the past. 
 
Its large, many-jointed legs give it remarkable flexibility. 
 
With strong defenses and powerful attacks, it is built for simple, brutal tactics that crush invaders. 
 
Station Ruins Sentry was created to move stones and hold back the sea, leaving behind a vast underground world of winding rivers and strange creatures.

These birds living in the Dreamscape Area boast elegant forms and fantastical plumage. 
While similarly colored, Nightmare Peahens cannot display like Peacocks. 
Child-rearing peahens prioritize survival—swaying bright tail feathers to dazzle predators and escape. 
 
Many newcomers to the Dreamscape Area gaze at these birds for what feels like a long time. 
Yet afterward, they recall it as only a brief glance. 
Many believe these birds can warp one's sense of time, thus keeping their distance.

Armadillo Rats are small rodents that live in the Jixia forests. They have a gourd-shaped brown shell on their backs. 
 
They are very gentle. When threatened, they pull into their shells to protect themselves. Only the young will bite with their teeth and claws if they are in danger. 
 
They eat medicinal herbs. Herbalists carefully follow them, hoping to find herbs, but few Herbalists can track an Armadillo Rat alone, so they usually team up with Hunters.

A dark, eerie figure, an incarnate nightmare.
The tall, slender Dreamslayer lurks in the shadows and dreams, waiting for the perfect moment to strike.
The shadows beneath its purple feathers are the prey's final memory, and the moon-blade it wields is the pride of a lone hunter.
The Moon-blade Dreamslayer is born from dreams, one with everything around it.
It moves through the air with ease, its gorgeous slashes like phantoms.

It tears through dream after dream, traversing fantasy after fantasy.
Its dark footsteps are merely the prelude to the hunt; the dreams of the mediocre are the food it survives on.

A secretive practitioner of the ancient Sorcery, 
Her true identity remains concealed. 
Amidst the chaos of the world, she stands in silence. 
As the wind whispers through her robes, 
She steps into the eternal night, 
Becoming a solitary beacon of light.

The two birds have parted, and the defector has returned home. Following the sunrise, the Crimson Falcon flies from the edge of the sea to Jixia. It is the king of the sky, diving like falling fire to hunt. Its selection of prey goes far beyond mere hunger; only the strongest are chosen. Hunting is a life-or-death ritual, and only the survivors enjoy a moment of peace.\n\nNo one knows what it seeks in this land, but in truth, the Crimson Falcon is not searching for anything—this continent is merely a branch for it to rest upon.

The Dream Demon of Painted Shadows' control over the dream realm deepens, tearing open more Nightmare Rifts, but also making its own creations vulnerable.\n\n[Rift Proliferation]: When the Dream Demon of Painted Shadows changes form, the number of Nightmare Rifts on the field increases, significantly increasing the pressure on teammates to rescue. At the same time, the protection of the Nightmare Butterflies that snatch players is greatly weakened, making them more fragile and easily shattered.
The Mechanoid Waiter will take care of your every meal.

A Bronze Axe General that has been dormant since its creation to fulfill its duty of protection. It awakens among the rubble, its only directive inscribed on its bronze body: expel all intruders.

[Lost Reinforcements]: The Bronze Axe General summons two Lost Cannons to fight alongside it; these should be cleared first.

[Rock Shield Formation]: The Bronze Axe General deploys a shield in the center of the arena and summons stone pillars at the four corners. It then cycles through targeting a single player or all players. Everyone must use the stone pillars as cover to hide, then work together to push the pillars over onto the Bronze Axe General to break its shield and stun it.

Unlike common Wolvines, this subspecies has very thick calluses on their front paws. 
Their fur is perpetually coated in mud and soil, and their scales have hardened into tough shells after countless burrowing attempts. With a swift flick of their paws, they can effortlessly burrow into the ground, moving with remarkable freedom. 
 
They are more adept at assisting in hunts, preparing the terrain for their more aggressive partners.  
Brave and meticulous explorers often follow their tracks to assess the current geological conditions.

In the north of Jixia, there is a giant beast with four legs that likes to hide in lightning and often fights with fire to the death.
When the fire dies, the thunderclouds rise.
The lightning-wielding giant lizard is the mortal enemy of the wildfire giant lizard.
Its massive body, shimmering with faint light, is often hidden within lightning.
It grants its victims a painless death the moment it appears.
It is the darling of lightning and the apex predator of the wilderness.

It rests like a crag, immovable.
Only when the enemy's fire begins to spread will it lift its noble head and let out a roar that shakes the earth.

Oil secreted by the Cloudeater when nourished by Aerflow. Once lit, it burns for a long time with a subtle, calming fragrance. It was once used by the people of Jixia for lighting.\n\nA Cloudeater once threw a grease-covered fur ball into a fire, teasing a hunter sitting by the campfire. After his initial panic subsided, the hunter realized this oil was the perfect fuel he had been searching for, and he wrote extensively about it in his observation journal.

The giant Palisaepes live underground, with special fruits growing on their twisted branches. 
They are highly accurate throwers who never miss a target. 
 
The Herbalist's latest research on Palisaepes indicates that these fruits are not seeds but a byproduct of their bodily functions.

Stone hides the portrait, colors fade away. Springs circle the empty hall, where ages stay.
Since the day of its creation, it has fallen into a long slumber.
In the few times it has awakened,
it saw an old man with a frosty beard standing with his hands behind his back, and a young man in his prime studying diligently behind him.

Stars shift and seas change. The pillars supporting the sky collapse, and the cauldrons supporting the earth crumble.
The Bronze Halberd-Wielder remains oblivious,
sleeping in the empty room, waking from dreams amidst the rubble.
It does not know where the past bustle has gone, only remembering the mission forged into its copper body:
To guard, to guard, until the armies retreat, until the long dream is worry-free.
Aloof and calm, with a scholarly demeanor. It is always ready to lecture everyone and everything.

The Radish King reigns supreme, a terror known far and wide. Its gleaming kitchen knife hints at danger beneath its playful demeanor, as it vows to defend the dignity of the Radishes through battle. 
 
Vine Command: Leaping to the center of the arena, the Radish King knocks back all players, then sounds its horn to ensnare three targets in twisting vines and drag them close. Anyone dragged to the Radish King faces a deadly strike. 
 
Groundbound Cutters: Meanwhile, the knife-wielding Radishes burrow along the edges, chasing unbound players. Guide these little attackers to sever the vines and free your allies before it's too late.
Though timid, it's full of curiosity—take it on your adventures!
Don't let its arrogant appearance fool you; it's actually quite timid and has made quite a fool of itself due to its own clumsiness.

These giant Saepes carry shields as hard as boulders. 
The shields have been enhanced with special methods, making them impervious to ordinary attacks. 
 
In some folk paintings, giant figures are depicted wielding similar shields.

Sentry Mechanoids are battle Mechanoids built by the academy. 
 
The smooth spheres and rounded columns reflect the master Mechsmith's design style. 
 
With powerful weapons, they far outmatch regular troops. 
 
They are deployed only after key structures are destroyed, then move in to support advancing allies.

They are the captains of the bronze Mechanoids that guard the ruins of Jixia. 
Adorned with glowing patterns etched into their bronze bodies, they wield ancient pikes with deadly precision, delivering swift and lethal strikes. 
 
It is said that only those who have demonstrated great valor in battle receive the title of commander. 
One must vanquish a hundred foes to earn the right to lead a hundred soldiers.

For the ideal I hold dear, I'd die a thousand times without regret. 
 
 
 
Between the thin divide of life and death, a figure lingers between two realms. Life was traded for honor, forsaking the mortal form to bring an end to strife, but the power from the imprint was too much to handle. But even in rust, the glory remains eternal. 
 
 
 
Like Volcanic Stone leaping into the fire, brilliance fades into silence. The dust of time forms a mountain of fate that weighs on all. Beneath the lofty mountain, the foolish stand proud and unyielding. They rise above the choice of life or death, heading towards an uncertain future.

It lurks in the nightmares of students,
absorbing the obsessions and darkness in people's hearts to reshape itself.
From the bite of a mad wolf to the pounce of a giant bear,
it gradually condenses the power of destruction within endless bestiality.
This shadow born of dreams attempts to break the boundary between reality and illusion, using sharp blades to tear the present world apart.

"The more awake you are in a dream, the more trapped you are in reality."
The awakened shadow projects the despair and darkness from the depths of the soul into people's dreams,
and thus the dream twists into this dark incarnation of disaster.

The Rebels turned against the academy as a result of differences in their Martial Arts beliefs. \n \nRebel Vanguards fight with a mallet and a shield, making them strong at defense and quick to launch counterattacks. Most of them come from outside Jixia and joined the Rebels to gain more power.

Superior Glintspear Effigies are Mechanoid fighters forged from a mysterious metal. Their gleaming red armor commands respect. Driven by internal power, their strikes are precise and lethal, piercing through enemies like a tiger entering its den. Their comrades have long since passed, yet their unfinished mission keeps them standing guard.

A strange creature from the Dreamscape. 
 
Its shifting body glows with a soft blue light as it floats in the air. Unlike the Eerie Dreamtangle, it is not openly aggressive. Instead, it slowly wraps its vines around targets, making them sink into beautiful but unreal dreams. 
 
Some students from Jixia, feeling stressed in real life, often get lost in the forest. Pleasant dreams can help people escape their worries for a while, but getting lost in them only leads to deeper trouble.

The one who stayed behind lingers in this world, while their companion has returned to where it came. The Sentinel wanders the valley, bearing the name of a knight, yet its mount is nowhere to be seen. The oversized greatsword it carries confirms the incredible size of its former partner. Though it now relies solely on the greatsword fused to its body, even without the momentum of a charge, its heavy strikes can still cleave through mountains and rivers.\n\nDragon Knights still uphold their oath to their dragons. Since the dragons are gone, the place where they parted is likely the final resting place for the rest of the knights' lives.

[Eternal Barrier]: The thorn armor covering the Wood Fence King's torso becomes exceptionally tough, requiring more fire bombs to break.\n\n[Fury Drain]: The Wood Fence King's attack power rises rapidly while in its giant form. The team must intercept and throw fire bombs with extreme efficiency; any delay will cause the survival space to shrink drastically.

Stonepines tower above, lush and green, as if standing amidst the clouds.
Treasure hunters and adventurers visiting the Ghostpath City know to steer clear of a certain dark patch of land, even though the soil looks no different from anywhere else, and even supports a dense grove of trees.
But they know those aren't trees—they are a single, colossal trunk, reaching high into the clouds.

Once, the Earth-Shaking Wildwood was just a young Saepes. Time gave it a gargantuan body, but eroded its clarity of mind.
After being abandoned in this cage, it always tries to hold onto everyone who passes by, but people only scream and flee.
It doesn't understand, so with each subsequent attempt, it becomes more forceful and frantic, pushing the very objects of its affection further away.

Shielded Aeroclads are defensive Mechanoids constructed by the academy using Aerux. 
Multiple layers of Aerux form their large shields, extending across their arms. These shields are reinforced with Aersilk, making them easier to repair. 
 
Small animals like to hide beneath their shields during hot summers for shade, and the Shielded Aeroclads never chase them off.

The soldier, who wielded dual blades, came from an army outside Jixia. His Flow was drawn to the Calamity Star, and whenever the star struck the land, he would appear with the meteorite and attack any living creature.

Palisaepes Shamans are from the fertile land. 
Holding tightly onto a flowering staff, they use their unique power to enhance allies and weaken enemies. 
 
Records indicate that they mimic human ceremonies and ritualistic behaviors.

Palisaepes Shamans are from the fertile land. 
Holding tightly onto a flowering staff, they use their unique power to enhance allies and weaken enemies. 
 
Records indicate that they mimic human ceremonies and ritualistic behaviors.

Priests of the Saepes tribe.
They are vines formed from the extension of the tribe's will, capable of using the power of their ancestors to defend against invading enemies.
The scepter they hold is forked and twisted at the top, wreathed in whispers that only they can understand.

Saepes Summoners guide the migration of the Saepes tribe, always finding environments suitable for the growth of Saepes trees.
Researchers believe that the unique connection between the Summoner and the Saepes tree is the key to their tribe's survival and prosperity.

Spike Bear cubs. 
 
Sporting sturdy manes, they are widespread throughout Jixia. Though small in size, they can curl into balls to attack. 
 
Spike Bears, mammals that raise their young, often appear in pairs. If a cub is attacked while alone, it calls for its parent's help.

Stone relics fade with time, as the years deepen around the empty hall. 
 
It was awakened only few times. The old man with a white beard stood before it, followed by diligent young men. 
 
As time passed, the pillar collapsed and the land cracked. 
 
Dual-Axe General woke up amidst the ruins. It didn't know where the liveliness of the past had gone, but it remembered its mission: To protect and defend, until the enemy armies retreat, and until people can dream without concerns.

Combat Mechanoids forged from mysterious metals. Armored with gleaming, reinforced scales, they are heavily fortified and intimidating. The Blade Effigies wield their blades with basic, disciplined techniques. One doesn't need to look closely to see the scars covering these machines; the remaining marks seem to tell the story of the hardships they endured as soldiers.

Stone relics fade with time, as the years deepen around the empty hall. 
 
It was awakened only few times. The old man with a white beard stood before it, followed by diligent young men. 
 
As time passed, the pillar collapsed and the land cracked. 
 
Dual-Axe General woke up amidst the ruins. It didn't know where the liveliness of the past had gone, but it remembered its mission: To protect and defend, until the enemy armies retreat, and until people can dream without concerns.

Grows in areas thick with vegetation, this dangerous plant resembles a withered wildflower but harbors hidden toxins. 
 
The Toxic Bubble Sprout releases poisonous bubbles to attack creatures that pass by, absorbing their nutrients. 
 
Ancient herbal texts record the medicinal value of its toxic sacs: 
 
"...Take two taels, boil dry with water, drink one sheng warm. Refreshes the mind, reduces fever, and eases pain."

Standing on four legs, it often hides in the blazing flames. When it encounters thunder, it fights incessantly. 
 
When the clouds fall, flaming columns reach the sky as this giant flame-breathing lizard razes any land it treads upon to ash. The destruction it causes is difficult to repair, as no greenery can survive its flames. 
 
Many have attempted to vanquish this pestilence, but few have succeeded. Even if they manage to harm it, their actions only further enrage it. 
 
The source of its irritable nature lies in the storm clouds that gather in the skies. 
 
Yearning for a clear crimson dusk, it stops at nothing to achieve it. The battles between these lizard kings appear endless until a person riding a strange steed enters the scene.

The two Sentinels act as one, dominating the battlefield through perfect teamwork. Even a small mistake can lead to disaster. \n \nTo break Pickaxe Sentinel's Inferno Shield, ALL four phantom clones of Doomblade Sentinel must strike it. This tests your team's coordination.

A strange creature from the Dreamscape. 
 
Thorny vines hold a deep blue light inside. 
 
It sends prey into wonderful dreams, making them unable to escape. 
 
Each Dreamslayer once had a happy life. It is said that the Dream Totem records the Dreamslayer's story before it became a resident of the Dreamscape.
A mysterious, feature-light creature in tune with nature that loves to circle around you.

The Ruin-Guarding Mystic Sentinel is a giant bronze construct forged by ancient craftsmen. Shaped like a roof ridge, it crushes all intruders with immense force.\n\n[Bronze March]: This giant construct locks onto the Burning Mountain Pivot as its target, relentlessly advancing on its limbs, and will continuously attack the pivot upon arrival until it is destroyed. Players must do everything in their power to stop its advance.

[Vine Binding Kill]: The Wooden Fence King releases vines to bind all players and summons Wooden Fence Spear Guards to charge across the field. You must break free from the vines as soon as possible to avoid attacks.\n\n[Spirit-Absorbing Giantization]: The Wooden Fence King absorbs the vitality of surrounding small wooden fences, its body expanding rapidly and covering itself with an indestructible thorn armor. At this time, Bombardment Guards appear on the sidelines throwing fire bombs. Only by picking up the fire bombs and throwing them at the Wooden Fence King's armor can you gradually dismantle its defense; otherwise, its power will continue to grow with its size until it crushes the entire field.

Originally crafted by the academy to simulate battle scenes, these little Mechcraft minions soon gained popularity for their cute designs. \n \nThough they have left the battlefield, they remain ready for action at all times.

These birds living in the Dreamscape Area boast elegant forms and fantastical plumage. 
Their feathers are influenced by the Dreamscape, becoming dazzlingly vibrant. 
Only stags can fan their tail feathers—resembling a dream butterfly's wing or a kalekaleidoscope of blossoms. 
 
The unfurled tail acts like a magnificent screen, irresistibly drawing human eyes. 
Legends say prolonged viewing amplifies dark thoughts, hence their name "Nightmare Peacock." 
Yet if an innocent bird awakens malice, does it not prove the darkness already resided within?

The Hellbound Sentinel, having fully unleashed its primal essence, has become a living catastrophe. Stars swirl in its grasp, threatening unparalleled destruction. 
 
Cataclysmic Stars: The summoned stars are now empowered by their essence, becoming far more stable. You must strike with greater force to shatter them. 
 
Cosmic Vortex: The rotating starlight walls spin at extreme speed, with openings vanishing in an instant. This means immense pressure when hunting down the constellation shadows. It tests the team's DPS and coordination to the limit.

Stone relics fade with time, as the years deepen around the empty hall. 
 
It was awakened only few times. The old man with a white beard stood before it, followed by diligent young men. 
 
As time passed, the pillar collapsed and the land cracked. 
 
Dual-Axe General woke up amidst the ruins. It didn't know where the liveliness of the past had gone, but it remembered its mission: To protect and defend, until the enemy armies retreat, and until people can dream without concerns.

Created by Yango, these puppets execute melee attacks with their razor-sharp blade hands. Stretching out their weaponized arms, these intricately-carved wooden marionettes swirl in a dance of knife tips.  \n \n"Forget about complicated tricks, and you shall attain true beauty."

Beautiful feathers that only a very few Croakies grow when nourished by Aerflow. They are fluorescent white, soft, and light, making them irresistible to touch.\n\nAccording to hunters, Croakies with these white feathers are highly favored by others. The saying that "obtaining a Joy Feather brings good luck in love" seems to have originated among Jixia students from this.

They live in the fertile lands and are born with the will of their ancestors, using their power to protect their kind from enemies. 
 
They carry a twisted, forked staff that hums with mysterious whispers only they can hear. 
 
As leaders of the tribe, their main job is to find the best place for future generations to grow and thrive. 
 
Researchers believe that the special connection between them and their unevolved descendants is the secret to the tribe's success.

A crystal infused with Aerflow. The surging Aerflow within carries the power to grant hope in desperate moments. It is often used to craft ornaments as a symbol of protection.\n\nExhausted from a long battle, the general could no longer dodge the enemy's blade. Yet, the expected pain never came. The crystal on his chest glowed, restoring strength to his arms... When all returned to silence, he pushed aside the enemy's cold body. The crystal on his chest remained warm, accompanying him as he greeted the dawn.

Silkfoxes are named after their red and white coats, resembling fine brocaded silk.
They have long, elegant ears often admired by poets.

Their fur is also used to make the highly prized brush known as the Etherbrush.
Legends claim that blessings written with this brush help Aersilk Harvesters reap bountiful harvests.
However, this may simply be a marketing ploy invented by Traders.

A giant beast in the north, with four legs. It hides among thunder and often fights to the death with fire. 
 
When the flames are extinguished, storm clouds rise. 
 
This thunder manipulator is a mortal enemy of the Wreckflame Lizard. Discreet flashes of light surround its large body, hidden within the thunder and lightning. 
 
It deals a painless, instantaneous death to its victims. 
 
Beloved by thunder and lightning, it reigns supreme. 
 
Steady as a stone, it is not easily moved from its perch. Only when the flames of its nemesis begin burning will it raise its head and roar.

Saepes Brutes' buds on their heads have finally bloomed. 
 
Their heavy clubs are unchanged, but their fighting skill has grown through experience. 
 
Wooden clubs may be weak against the Embermane's fire, yet years of growth and fighting side by side have closed every opening the enemy could exploit.

Might as thunder, movement like the sky's roar.
The Thunder-Bull that once galloped across the vast plains carries thunder in its massive horns.
Now it keeps to itself, keeping company only with the purple clouds.
Its dark fur ripples constantly, like a raging sea.
Its territory is its thunder pool, its fortress.
Any creature that steps foot here will face a thousand-fold thunder strike.
Perhaps it once tried to live in a herd, but those who drew near have surely turned to ash.

It wanders, it stands still.
It destroys, it is lost.
Now, the time has come.
Mingie, an unofficial member of the Secrets Club, calls itself the "Know-It-All of Jixia," though its gossip may not always be reliable!

The Shadow Ripper Sentinel is one of the Trialgiver Sentinels in the ancient Enlightenment Trials. Clad in black armor with gleaming gold accents on his arms, this sentinel wields a dagger that gleams and delivers swift attacks. He has waited here for millennia to pass on his swiftness skills. 
 
Merging with the shadows and blending into darkness, the Shadow Ripper Sentinel possesses a deep knowledge of speed. He and his challengers have countless times sliced through the dreams of the naive in the dead of night. Yet, ultimately, they were submerged in the flow of history. 
 
Can you bring back these battle skills as swift as the night wind under the light of the full moon?

Fighters of the Saepes tribe.
Clad in leaves, with twisted vines wrapped around a crude blowpipe.
Saepes Scouts excel at ambushing enemies from the shadows with blowdarts; the poisoned projectiles leave enemies in constant misery.

According to research, the toxins in Saepes blowdarts come from a variety of sources, including but not limited to: Poison Bubble Buds, Leaf-tailed Lizards, Jade Tear Fruits...

Stone relics fade with time, as the years deepen around the empty hall. 
 
It was awakened only few times. The old man with a white beard stood before it, followed by diligent young men. 
 
As time passed, the pillar collapsed and the land cracked. 
 
Dual-Axe General woke up amidst the ruins. It didn't know where the liveliness of the past had gone, but it remembered its mission: To protect and defend, until the enemy armies retreat, and until people can dream without concerns.

Hunchshell Turtles live near water and have thick shells with dull colors.
Although they move on land, they always stay close to the water.
Since they are very slow, their only defense against danger is hiding inside their strong shells.
They also sleep in their shells at night.

No matter how busy or stressful life gets, these turtles find peace every night by resting in their protective shells.

Mechanoid fighters forged from a mysterious metal. 
 
Their armor is embedded with shiny plates, making them incredibly durable. 
 
In combat, they use basic yet effective moves. 
 
The scars and gashes on their bodies speak of their lives as battle-hardened soldiers.

Phantom Rabbits are known for their distinctive ears, which resemble large eyes and often confuse predators.

When viewed from the front, these markings create a fearsome appearance, deterring enemies with a Dreamscape-like gaze.

The origin of these unique "eyes" remains a mystery, but one thing is certain—this adaptation has granted Phantom Rabbits an unusual peace in a world where only the strong survive.

A giant beast in the north, with four legs. It hides among thunder and often fights to the death with fire. 
 
When the flames are extinguished, storm clouds rise. 
 
This thunder manipulator is a mortal enemy of the Wreckflame Lizard. Discreet flashes of light surround its large body, hidden within the thunder and lightning. 
 
It deals a painless, instantaneous death to its victims. 
 
Beloved by thunder and lightning, it reigns supreme. 
 
Steady as a stone, it is not easily moved from its perch. Only when the flames of its nemesis begin burning will it raise its head and roar.

A strange creature from the Dreamscape. 
 
Thorny vines wrap around a Dream Butterfly. 
 
It sends prey into wonderful dreams, making them unable to escape. 
 
Research shows that it is closely related to Dreamslayers and Dream Totems.

Bronze Turrets are defensive Mechanoids found in the ruins. 
Their four legs are bunched together, charging for a powerful blast with their two cannons. 
A single blast is enough to shatter any armor. The only way around them is to avoid them. 
 
For some reason, they have been restless, a sign that this place has never been forgotten.

Rainbunnies are cute creatures characterized by their wholly white coats, often serving as inspiration for toymakers.

Legends suggest that Rainbunnies are extremely sensitive to the weather, possibly due to their preference for consuming only the freshest plants.
Hunters frequently spot them foraging for food after rainy days, and villagers observe their activities to predict when the rain will end.

After enduring the trials of the world, the floral crowns atop the Saepes Brutes have finally bloomed. The massive clubs in their hands are no different than before, but true mastery of martial arts has never been about the weapon itself. While their weapons still fear the scorching flames of the Scorched Fluff, years of careful maintenance and fighting side-by-side mean the Saepes Brutes will no longer give their natural enemies an opening.

[Stubborn Plant Protection]: While dragging a teammate, the Radish King generates a sturdy thorn armor. Although the blade-wielding small radishes can cut the vines, they cannot break the armor.\n\n[Scorched Earth Obstacle Breaking]: Rescued players must lure the unactivated self-destructing radishes on the field to collide with the Radish King, or lure it to step onto the previously left burning ground. Only through continuous burning can its armor be gradually dismantled; otherwise, the armor will remain.

Bi Fang is a magical bird spirit made of bronze. It does not eat normal food like grains. 
 
It cries out loudly day and night. Its voice is strong, but anyone who hears it feels sad and may even cry. 
 
Bi Fang has forgotten many things, but it always remembers its own name. 
 
It has one rusty leg and worn-out wings, but its eyes and the lines on its body still shine with a bright blue fire. 
 
Long ago, a great ship gave Bi Fang the job to fly, protect, and fight. 
 
Now the ship is gone, and everything Bi Fang once guarded is destroyed. 
 
Still, Bi Fang tries to keep its promise. It calls out its name with pride, even though it is broken: 
 
"Bi Fang, Bi Fang."
The crane leads to a master of quick-cutting blades. Show respect before seeking wisdom.
Disciples of the Obsidian Flame Hall are skilled with firearms. They are not only adept at modifying them but also have deep insights into combat.
The Heir of the Shattered Blade

A rare spider found only in Jixia, it carries a "shell" woven from Aersilk on its back, faintly glowing with a golden hue. This shell serves as its home, which it has carried since youth. \n \nInherently shy, the spider retreats into its shell at the sight of people. Fascinated by shiny objects, it quietly pilfers small trinkets and stows them away inside its delicate home.
Dodou, wearing a small straw hat and cape, loves to play practical jokes on people.

Rebels who turned against the academy due to conflicting martial arts philosophies. Rebel Vanguards wield hammers and shields, excelling in defensive counterattacks. Many of them come from outside Jixia, joining the rebels in pursuit of power.

An unyielding gatekeeper, one who can hold the pass against a thousand riders. With a massive shield, it blocks all who stand before it, enduring like a mountain even in ruin. Forged from a fallen hero's shield, it stands as the pinnacle of mechanised defence. 
 
When icy boulders fall off the cliff, there is no retreat. Its core is etched with unbreakable resolve, its defence impenetrable. 
 
Its back faced the country it fought to defend as the underhanded cavalry streamed into the pass. In the dying light of dusk, as shadows stretch long, reinforcements emerge.

A Mechcraft warrior wielding a blade of fire. Beneath the crimson armor, a fiery core burns ceaselessly. The Ten-Thousand-Forge Blade is highly skilled in close-quarters combat, striking with the weight of a mountain. The intense heat of its massive fire blade is enough to melt metal. Few creatures dare to provoke the Blazing Blade Warrior. Every swing is accompanied by scalding steam and churning magma. Combat is no longer its mission, but its fated destiny.

The two birds have parted. The defector has returned to the homeland. 
 
With the breaking of the dawn, a Red Falcon flew from across the sea to Jixia, illuminated in the sun's glow. 
 
It is the apex hunter of winged creatures, and each time it dives at its prey, it resembles a ball of divine flame falling from the sky. 
 
Its choice of prey goes far beyond filling its belly. Only the strong are selected. 
 
Hunting is a life-or-death ceremony, only the survivor can enjoy a moment of peace. 
 
No one knows what it is looking for on this land. In fact, it is not looking for anything. This continent is just a branch for it to rest.

These ancient defensive Mechanoids were designed with Heavy Iceshield Effigies in mind. 
Their tower shields are adorned with Mechcraft patterns that channel potent energy, making them even harder to budge. 
 
The Academy's Mechanoid shields were largely inspired by this design. 
It's hard to imagine the kind of enemies that would require such powerful defensive Mechanoids.

Fighters of the Saepes tribe.
The spear tip in their hands resembles a vibrant bud ready to bloom.
Do not be deceived by its colorful appearance and overlook its terrifying piercing power.

Although Saepes weapons are very crude, they cherish them greatly and often use stone tools to polish and maintain them.

The Mysterious River Sprite is incredibly tiny, nearly invisible to the naked eye. From a distance, it appears as a faint blue glow. 
It emits a gentle warmth that heals nearby creatures. 
 
"It doesn't matter what kind of creature or what kind of pain—these little guys can heal them all. They're born with hearts of gold."——A Jixia student, half his body wrapped in bandages, said in the infirmary. 
Some scholars collectively call Jixia's River Sprites "Sproutlings".
High in the clouds, the tiger reigns supreme. The madman who claims to be the strongest master has been waiting with his blade for a long time.

Tigrex, a fierce Rebel leader in the mountain forests, now bursts into the Three-School Showdown. With iron claws and relentless force, he wants to dominate the competition and prove that only destruction shows true power. 
 
Brutal Charge: Tigrex locks onto one player and charges toward them repeatedly. The targeted player should avoid staying close to allies so they don't get hit, while others should attack Tigrex from behind. The final charge is red-glowing. It's stronger, so be careful. 
 
Earth Shaker: Tigrex leaps to the center of the arena and slams the ground several times, sending out circular shockwaves. Jump or dash to dodge the waves. The final slam is red-glowing and is more powerful. Watch out.

These birds living in the Dreamscape Area boast ethereal blue feathers. 
Dreamveil Peacocks possess light-blue wings adorned with intricate patterns, accented by pink, ink-blue, and white. 
When they fan out their tails, it resembles a painted scroll. Their feathers are often sold as luxury jewelry materials. 
 
In dreams, Dreamveil Peacock and Peahens frequently appear together, gliding gracefully through Dreamcache Wood. 
Peacock and peahens stay closely bonded. 
Legends say that if a peacock appears alone, its colorful tail turns into a bizarre nightmare that slowly consumes consciousness. 
On the other hand, a lone peahen brings serene dreams and restful sleep.
A Dream Journey to the Sea of Clouds
Always plotting a "big plan," it sees itself as the team captain and you as its trusted lieutenant.
The crane leads to a master of quick-cutting blades. Show respect before seeking wisdom.

They are the generals of the bronze Mechanoids that guard the ruins of Jixia. 
Adorned with glowing patterns etched into their bronze bodies, they wield ancient pikes with deadly precision, delivering swift and lethal strikes. 
 
They have mastered the art of war and represent the highest command of the bronze Mechanoid army.

[Phantom Charge]: The Blade-Severing Spirit splits into four phantom clones to lock onto different players and charge.\n\n[Precision Guidance]: The Halberd-Severing Spirit's fire shield is still on the field. Four players must accurately identify and guide their respective clones to crash into the fire shield, while staying spread out to avoid overlapping paths.

Dark wings cry low, disaster looms; shadows sweep through gold and silver light.

Black feathers drift down, and calamity follows. This is the first impression people have of Litian: ominous, dangerous... Pair after pair of uneasy eyes watch him, but Litian never cares.
To Litian, only two things matter: first, flashy moves; second, shiny gold rings. Everything else is trivial and unworthy of mention.

Time long past is buried beneath the yellow sand. Now, Litian works as a treasure hunter, his mission to acquire more gold rings.
Wherever there are gold rings or treasures, Litian will find his way there.
And for the right price, his martial arts and the hook-swords in his hands can be yours to command.

Toxic Tiles are invented and refined by a School of Mechcraft instructor. 
Beneath their harmless sparrow-like appearance lies a deadly weapon. 
They release a toxin derived from highly poisonous herbs, designed to catch victims completely off guard. 
 
As illness requires medicine, so too does the sickness of gambling addiction. To this end, the instructor consulted an Herbalist Toxineer, "Only a taste of their own medicine can cure their addiction."

An orphan under the starry sky, a talent in history. After leaving that desolate land with a Croaky, Vesper has always followed in his mentor's footsteps. Selfless battles have left him with dense scars, and a regretful past has etched traces of rebellion into his heart. Vesper is waiting—waiting for his master to teach him the truths of the world, and waiting for the moment his ultimate mission arrives. Thus, he has spent half his life trying to understand his master, his mission, and his honor.

[Evil Shield Charge]: The Savage Tiger's shield durability is greatly increased during its charge. The team must focus fire to deal massive damage to break it.\n\n[Earth-Shattering Impact]: After charging, the Savage Tiger immediately leaps to the center of the field and slams the ground repeatedly, causing screen-wide shockwave damage. Only by picking up the dropped Mechanical Heavy Shield can you block it; jumping or dodging is useless.

A dark, eerie figure, an incarnate nightmare.
The tall, slender Dreamslayer lurks in the shadows and dreams, waiting for the perfect moment to strike.
The shadows beneath its purple feathers are the prey's final memory, and the moon-blade it wields is the pride of a lone hunter.
The Moon-blade Dreamslayer is born from dreams, one with everything around it.
It moves through the air with ease, its gorgeous slashes like phantoms.

It tears through dream after dream, traversing fantasy after fantasy.
Its dark footsteps are merely the prelude to the hunt; the dreams of the mediocre are the food it survives on.

Those who cross the Great Wall shall not return alive.
This stumbling, lost soul was once a vanguard of the Great Wall Garrison.
He once sparred with Kai and shared wine with Hua Mulan.
Until that battle, to protect Mulan, he was infected by the power of monsters.
He once wanted to end his own life, but was stopped by his mother.

Unable to suppress the demonic influence, he locked himself in a cell.
Only by picking up the carving knife in his hand could he soothe his manic bloodlust.
Not just because of those stone statues, but because of the past he could never forget.

Wildmane Boars are common and adaptable beasts found throughout the land. 
These strong creatures have curved tusks, a gray-colored coat, and a wild white mane of thick hair. 
Wildmane Boars usually move in packs, so caution is advised when encountering them in the wilderness. 
 
If you wish to avoid being rammed into the air or having sessions with herbalists, it's best to steer clear of these boars. 
There was once an apprentice Hunter who ignored this advice after putting on the Hunter uniform for the first time and was carried to Frostcloud Town before midday.

Coldspear Marshals are Mechanoid fighters made from a mysterious metal. 
Their angular helmets and shoulder pads are inscribed with a diamond pattern, hinting at an unusual origin. 
The metal point of their wooden spear twinkles faintly, making it highly intimidating. 
 
The lonely silhouette of the spear and its cold light come on the wind, seeking only to protect this land. 
The history remains sealed in a secluded corner, but it's never forgotten.

Standing on four legs, it often hides in the blazing flames. When it encounters thunder, it fights incessantly. 
 
When the clouds fall, flaming columns reach the sky as this giant flame-breathing lizard razes any land it treads upon to ash. The destruction it causes is difficult to repair, as no greenery can survive its flames. 
 
Many have attempted to vanquish this pestilence, but few have succeeded. Even if they manage to harm it, their actions only further enrage it. 
 
The source of its irritable nature lies in the storm clouds that gather in the skies. 
 
Yearning for a clear crimson dusk, it stops at nothing to achieve it. The battles between these lizard kings appear endless until a person riding a strange steed enters the scene.

Mushrooms mutated under the influence of the Aercocoon. 
They have eye-catching pink caps resembling open umbrellas. 
Erosion Cap Mushrooms release spore cores for self-defense. 
 
Herbalists have been exploring the potential medicinal uses of their toxic spores,  
though they haven't had much success yet.

The soldier, who wielded a ringblade, came from an army outside Jixia. His Flow was drawn to the Calamity Star, and whenever the star struck the land, he would appear with the meteorite and attack any living creature.

Palisaepes Tallshields live underground, with an extraordinarily strong arm as a result of the overgrown branches. 
This arm serves as a sturdy shield to fend off upcoming enemies. 
 
Palisaepes Tallshields are good team players as they will protect others of their kind behind in battle. 
They also use their shields to store rain and distribute it to their small friends afterwards.

An ancient creature from the Dreamscape,  
it possesses a hooked beak and claws sharp as blades. 
Its resonant tail follows its slender body, dancing through the air of the Dreamscape. 
 
It attacks swiftly at close range and may even make use of Dream Rifts to launch surprise attacks. 
But its presence becomes most threatening when it appears alongside other Dreamscape creatures. 
Anyone caught in such peril can only pray to be awakened from the dream.

Created by the academy, they stand in front of Adept Sorcerers and wield swords and shields for close-quarters combat. \n \nFor some reason, their shields bear an etching of a bird. It is said that this bird sings an inspiring song during battle.

A curious fruit that resulted from the absorption of Aerflow. 
An eternal blaze envelopes it. 
The Flameroll Fruit gravitates towards light, using rolling smashes to chase off obstacles to its sunbathing. 
 
When an extinguished Flameroll Fruit was served up to a Gourmet, he posed a question that troubled many for a long time: "Is this cooked or raw?"

Ice Pikedice are invented and refined by students from the School of Mechcraft. 
They are modeled after and proportionally scaled from a game piece. 
Fitted with a single cannon, they discharge various energies depending on their module attributes. 
 
Despite their blocky appearance suggesting clumsiness, 
they are surprisingly fast, capable of instantly leaping in front of nearby students.

An ancient defensive stationary mechanical construct.
The Qiancui Shield Automaton was designed with practicality in mind.
The mechanical patterns on the tower shield channel superior elemental energy, making it even harder to shake.

The shields of the mechanical constructs developed by the Academy are largely based on this construction.
It is hard to imagine what kind of enemy would require a mechanical construct with such powerful defensive capabilities.

The mechanism core has gone completely berserk, summoning four abandoned turrets to fight alongside it at the start.

[Thunder Array]: The stone pillars are indestructible under the blessing of thunder; players must work together to break them before they can be toppled. Meanwhile, the General's charge and destructive beam will be accompanied by large-scale lightning strikes across the field.

[Twin Abyssal Terrors]: The Ruin Guardians will be awakened and join the battle. During this time, the Bronze Halberd General will intermittently trigger unavoidable ground-shaking sparks across the field. Players must quickly defeat the Ruin Guardians under the dual pressure of lightning storms and sparks.

Large lizards commonly found in the forests and wetlands of Jixia.  
They have flamboyant fringes on their heads to scare off enemies. When threatened, they spread their crests and emit deadly secretions. 
 
According to the Herbalist's journal, their skin color changes based on the environment. Will their true form be revealed if they are raised in a nondescript environment over generations?

[Fire Shield Collision]: The Blade-Severing Spirit locks onto a player to charge, while the Lone Halberd Spirit activates a Fire Shield in the center of the field. Players must lure the Blade-Severing Spirit to collide with the Fire Shield three times to successfully break the shield; otherwise, they will suffer massive screen-wide damage.

The young Armadillo Rats found in the forests are endearingly cute. 
They sport hemispherical shells on their backs. 
They curl into their shells to defend against attacks, ready to roll away at a moment's notice. 
 
Many Jixia residents have tried to keep these adorable creatures as pets, 
but as they grow, their instinctive desire for the wild often leads them to escape their owners' grasp.

The Rebels turned against the academy as a result of differences in their Sorcery beliefs. 
They carry even more Telepathic Threads in their wristguards to decrease any adverse impacts of energy fluctuations. 
However, they cannot use spells that last long, so they mostly favor ones with brief and explosive power. 
 
Their hyper-sensory attunement to energy is also a form of overload for their brains, and they often find themselves battling fatigue as a result.

Stone relics fade with time, as the years deepen around the empty hall. 
 
It was awakened only few times. The old man with a white beard stood before it, followed by diligent young men. 
 
As time passed, the pillar collapsed and the land cracked. 
 
Dual-Axe General woke up amidst the ruins. It didn't know where the liveliness of the past had gone, but it remembered its mission: To protect and defend, until the enemy armies retreat, and until people can dream without concerns.

Like a delicate flower, 
She quietly blossoms on the frigid battlefield. 
Amidst the withering surroundings, 
She thrives like a steadfast bloom within the stone, 
Embracing every new challenge.

Bats that inhabit the caves of Jixia. 
Their small size and narrow wings allow them to deftly navigate the night sky. 
Crimson Moon Bats, with their extraordinarily sharp hearing, identify their prey in darkness and attack swiftly. 
 
Perhaps driven mad by dark, menacing forces, the Crimson Moon Bats have descended into frenzy. 
Their once mild nature has vanished. Now they see all living beings as malevolent foes.

Tender buds fill the body, learning to walk clumsily.
When delicate vines take root in the old shell that has become nutrients, a new life begins.
Its thorn-covered body protects the fragile main bud.
The face on the mask is merely a disguise.
At this moment, it is full of longing.
It must embrace and communicate sincerely with every creature it meets for the first time.

Does their cyclical life count as a continuation of the self?
When most of what belongs to the self is replaced, can the core that guides their consciousness remember the former self?

A Master doll holding a ruler, intricately carved from cloud root, with a smooth and polished finish.
