Dear Tata, 
 
 
 
Greetings! It's been nearly half a year since we last met. I hear Tata's is doing well. I've heard great things about your two new desserts. It seems your growth has far exceeded my expectations! 
 
In addition to experimenting with new recipes daily, don't forget to practice the basics. Every step, from chopping to wok tossing, must be strictly practiced as Grandpa taught us. Don't slack off. I've informed the elders at home to announce you as the successor. Keep up the good work and carry on our family's culinary legacy! 
 
I haven't been feeling well lately, experiencing hot and cold flashes and occasional fainting spells, possibly a lingering effect from that unknown beast's Sorcery attack. Many Herbalists have treated me, but I haven't seen much improvement. Don't worry though! It's nothing compared to the worse conditions I faced as a military chef. 
 
Focus on running Tata's and spreading your signature dishes across Jixia. Don't forget to have your staff practice their basics. By the time you're done with your busy period, I should be feeling better. Then, I'll make a special trip to Frostcloud Town to see you!

Martial Arts is the art of merging the spiritual energy of the places with the human spirit. To reach the pinnacle, one should embrace a humble heart and a focused mind. At the beginning of your practice, rise at dawn and walk into a quiet valley. Let your heart soak in the sunrise. 
The practice of Martial Arts begins with quieting the mind. Sit steady as a bell, and keep your spirit as clear as a mirror. First, cultivate your mind and nature to make them as calm as still water. Look inward to sense the flow of energy. Absorb the spiritual energy of the places and expel impurities. When your energy flows without obstruction, your inner strength will begin to form. 
Next, move your body from stillness to motion. Start with steps as smooth as flowing clouds and water, and perform techniques as light and swift as a bird. Hands grasp the wind, and palms move without a pattern. Use your will to guide your energy, and use your energy to control your body. Though techniques change like a thousand rivers, the essence remains the same. Don't get caught up in stiffness—instead, reach a state of fluid freedom. 
The art of the sword and blade is like a graceful, divine dance, each step filled with spiritual energy. The sword rises from the heart, and the blade is born from the will. Those who practice should come to understand its profound nature, adapting to changes with ease. The sword points like stars, and the blade dances like a whirlwind. Reaching the highest level of wonder is the ultimate state of a martial artist. 
To understand this way, first cultivate your mind, then train your body, and finally, discover the magic of the sword and blade. Don't rush for quick success. Instead, hold on to a steady heart. As your practice deepens daily, you will eventually grasp the essence of Martial Arts, rising from ordinary to saintly.

They have worked in secret, pulling unseen strings, shaping the very thoughts of men, persuading us that "harmony between man and dragon" is real, with the goal of dominating Primaera once again.

This supplement to the Saepes Compendium, authored by the Hunter, Mu Ping, documents the physiological characteristics and various types of the Saepes. 
Saepes emerge from Saepes seeds, though the precise ratio of occurrences is still under study. Currently, let's just stick with the word "random". 
Note: Data from the last decade suggest that about 20% of Saepes seeds grow into living Saepes. 
Newly sprouted Saepes are the size of a human fist, resembling wooden dumplings with diminutive limbs that allow upright stance and mobility. These limbs, functioning as roots, draw nutrients from the soil and water, while their leafy heads, resembling hair and beards, photosynthesize to sustain their daily activities. 
Note (by a Seeker): Local folklore portrays the Saepes as wood spirits corrupted by some foul energy, notorious for abducting mischievous children at night. These tales likely originated to ensure children adhere to their bedtime schedules. 
Beneath the bark-free patches of the Saepes, the life-infused phloem is visible. This tissue moves sugars from the leaves, thus fueling the entire organism. Saepes are exceptionally good at absorbing nutrients, allowing them to store energy quickly and run for days without tiring. 
Note: During rituals, Saepes can dance non-stop, day and night. See Saepes Unveiled: Habits and Society for more information. 
Saepes are completely covered in a layer of tough bark, which is both a water barrier and a shield against blades and arrows. Resembling strange masks and armor, the bark wards off wild predators like Razorfang Boars, and Spike Bears. As Saepes grow, their old bark sheds, revealing fresh bark underneath that allows them to keep growing. Typically, adult Saepes are as tall as an average person. 
A rare few Saepes live exceptionally long, growing into large Arbor Saepes that tower over humans and often become community leaders. The largest Saepes known to us are called the Giant Saepes, which are as big as several Arbor Saepes combined. They move with four legs and often camouflage themselves as a small hill. Their long tails end in a flower that can launch fruit, deterring anyone who dares come close. 
Saepes have evolved to move and adapt to different environments, similar to other thriving plants in Jixia. Depending on where they grow, Saepes can mimic local vegetation to blend in. In wetlands, they resemble the aquatic plant Changpu, also known as Tyhpaepes, while in the northern Dreamscape, they adapt to the powerful dream-like surroundings and are known as "Dream Saepes." 
At the end of their lives, Saepes would stop moving and eventually harden into tree-like forms.

An excerpt from the "Wooden Hedge Encyclopedia" written by Mu Ping, a Jixia hunter, detailing the physiological characteristics of wooden hedges and the various kinds that exist.

Living wooden hedges originate from wooden hedge seeds. As for the ratio, it is still under research at the research center, and we can only say they are produced "randomly."

Note: Data from the past ten years shows that wooden hedge seeds capable of becoming living wooden hedges account for about twenty percent of the total.

Newly activated wooden hedges are only about the size of a human fist, shaped like wooden lumps with tiny arms and legs, and can stand and walk just like humans. Their hands and feet are actually roots and stems, which can absorb nutrients by anchoring into soil and water; leaves grow on their heads, looking somewhat like human hair and beards. Academy research shows that these leaves can utilize sunlight to convert the air drawn in by the leaves and water absorbed by the roots and stems into sugars, sustaining the wooden hedge's daily living and movement needs.

Note (Naturalist): Jixia folklore has different views on this. In local oral tales, wooden hedges are wood monsters brought to life by turbid Qi, wandering around at night to grab disobedient children. Making up such stories is likely to scare kids into going to bed on time and staying indoors in the middle of the night.

Through the few areas on a wooden hedge's body not covered by bark, one can see the inner phloem parts saturated with the breath of life. The phloem transports the sugars produced by the leaves throughout the wooden hedge's body. Their nutritional conversion and absorption capabilities are exceptionally strong, allowing them to accumulate a lot of strength in a short time and run continuously for days without fatigue.

Note: During ceremonies, they can dance day and night without stopping! See "Detailed Wooden Hedges: Living Habits and Society" for details.

Wooden hedges are covered from head to toe in hard bark, which is a stratum corneum formed after the inner phloem ages and dies. It prevents water loss and provides formidable protection, capable of withstanding blade edges or arrowheads. It also makes them look as though they are wearing bizarre masks and armor, sufficient to deter and scare away wild natural enemies such as deer, saber-toothed pigs, and thorn bears. Once the bark accumulates to a certain thickness, it falls off, exposing the newly grown bark underneath. In this way, wooden hedges gradually grow, becoming larger and larger. A common adult small wooden hedge is similar in height to an average adult human.

A very small number of wooden hedges have particularly long lifespans, growing into arbor hedges two to three people tall, and often serve as core members of a wooden hedge community. The largest individual currently observed in the wild is the giant wooden hedge, which is as large as several arbor hedges combined. It walks on four limbs and spends most of its time lying in place, camouflaged as a small mound, with only its tail upright on guard. The giant wooden hedge's tail is very long, with a large flower at the tip that can spray fruits. Anyone who approaches rashly will receive a severe beating.

Evolution gives wooden hedges more than just migration capabilities. Like most plants that successfully thrive and flourish in Jixia, wooden hedges have exceptionally strong environmental adaptability, and those growing in different environments will display varying appearances that match their surroundings. For example, in wetland areas, the leaves on a wooden hedge's body become very similar in appearance to the aquatic plant cattail, hence they are also called "cattail hedges"; whereas in areas of the northern region with strong dream power, variants known as "dream hedges" live there.

When life comes to an end, wooden hedges gradually stop moving and eventually become completely still, turning into wooden hedge trees.

稷下游猎家暮平撰写的《木篱大百科》分册，记载了木篱的生理特征，以及各种各样的木篱。 
 
活体木篱从木篱种子中产生，至于是怎么个比例，现在还在研究中心，我们只能说是“随机”产生吧。 
 
批注：近十年的数据显示，能成为活木篱的木篱种子，占总数的二成左右。 
 
刚活化的木篱只有人的拳头那么大，外形就像是长着细小手臂和腿的木头团子，可以和人类一样站立和行走。手和脚实际上就是根茎，可以通过扎在土地、水中吸取养分；头部会长出叶子，看起来有点像人类的头发和胡子。学院的研究表明，这些叶子能利用阳光，把叶子吸进来的气和根茎吸取的水分变成糖分，维持木篱的日常生活行动需要。 
 
批注（风物家）：稷下的民间传说对此有不同的见解，本地的口传故事里，木篱是被浊气污染而活过来的木头妖怪，晚上到处抓不听话的熊孩子。编这种故事很可能是为了吓唬小孩，让他们按时上床睡觉，别大半夜出去转悠。 
 
透过木篱体表没有树皮遮挡的少数区域，能看到内部浸透着生命之息的韧皮部位。韧皮能把叶子产生的糖分输送到木篱全身。它们的营养转化和吸收能力特别强，短时间能就能积攒很多力量，可以持续奔跑好几天而不感到疲惫。 
 
批注：在仪式上，它们能不分昼夜地一直跳舞！详见《木篱详解：生活习性与社会》。 
 
木篱从头到脚覆盖着坚硬的树皮，是内部韧皮老化死后形成的角质层，既能防止水分流失，也可以提供强悍的防护力，能抵挡住刀刃或箭头，看上去也很像戴着怪异面具、身披铠甲，足以威慑和吓跑野外的天敌，比如鹿、刃牙猪和刺熊。树皮积攒到一定厚度后就会掉落，让底下新长成的树皮露出来，如此木篱就会逐渐成长，体型变得越来越大。常见的小木篱成体，身高和普通成人相差无几。 
 
极少数木篱的生命周期特别长，能长成两三人高的乔木篱，往往是一个木篱社群的核心成员。目前观测到野外最大的个体是巨木篱，有好几只乔木篱合起来那么大，它用四条腿行走，平时大多数时间趴在原地伪装成一个小山包，只有尾巴竖着担任警戒。巨木篱的尾巴很长，顶端有一朵能喷出果实的大花，要是贸然靠近，就会被痛打一顿。 
 
演化带给木篱的不仅是迁徙能力，大多数成功在稷下繁茂生长的植物一样，木篱对环境的适应性也特别强，在不同环境生长的木篱会呈现出与环境相匹配的不同样貌。例如在湿地地带，木篱身上的树叶外观就变得很像水生植物菖蒲，也被称为“蒲篱”；而在北地梦境之力强劲的地区，则生活着称为“梦篱”的变种。 
 
生命走到尽头时，木篱会逐渐停止活动，最后完全静止下来，成为木篱树。

Once upon a time, there was a master archer at the Red Falcon Hall. One day, while hunting in the mountains, he held his bow in contemplation, watching his flying prey without firing. And now, the traditional Three Birds with One Arrow trial of the Red Falcon Hall was founded by the former hall master inspired by this very event. 
 
Trial Instructions: 
First, anyone caught cheating or taking the test for another will be permanently disqualified. 
Second, inspect your bow and arrows before training; damaged or defective gear must not be used. 
Third, do not use excessive force to avoid damaging the test facilities. A student once shattered a target with a single arrow—let this be a warning to all.

Source: Jixia Academy Suggestion Box 
Content: Anonymous suggestions for the Academy 
Editor's Note: Interesting suggestions deserve a spot in the paper. I'm not just filling space; I want to collect more opinions so everyone can be heard. 
  
Suggestion One: 
Dear Headmaster Fuzi, I am a herbalist with some feedback. 
I recently developed a new type of plant with effects unmatched in the King's Continent. Once planted, its vines actively seek out nearby people and wrap around injured joints or fractures. 
What a great invention! Yet, the staff at the Hall of Benevolence listed it as contraband. I've said it before: it's perfectly safe and won't grow into skin. The itching is just the wound healing, not the plant sowing seeds under the skin. 
I hope the Headmaster will take this seriously and give a great invention a chance. 
  
Suggestion Two: 
Dear Headmaster Mozi, I'm a hardworking young man from the village below (that's how the matchmaker always introduces me). I'd like to ask for a favor—is that possible? 
Forgot to write what the favor was, so I'm adding it now. 
I live not far from the Academy, just two miles away, but there's no Cloudship dock and the mountain paths are hard to walk. Every time I carry a basket up the mountain to deliver goods, my back is about to break. I bought an ox, but it's getting smaller from exhaustion. I hope you can lend me some Cloud-Piercing Wings so I can just zip right up! It would be even better if you could modify them for my ox. 
  
Suggestion Three: 
Dear Headmaster Fuzi, I am a student at the Martial Arts Academy. 
I was on duty at the Hall of Benevolence a few days ago and intercepted a dangerous plant carried by a herbalist. Although I didn't let him in, he spilled a few seeds during the argument. By the next day, they were taller than a person and kept trying to wrap around me. It took my classmates and me a lot of effort to clear the plant away. 
However, strange things have been happening since. I was poisoned by that plant and have been having increasingly severe hallucinations. 
A few days ago, I saw a basket of potatoes flying on Cloud-Piercing Wings. I thought I was just tired and ignored it. 
This morning, I saw an ox carrying a basket of potatoes, riding Cloud-Piercing Wings, flying straight toward me... 
I hope you can help me find that herbalist or find me an antidote.

取材：稷下学院意见箱 
内容：针对学院的匿名意见 
编者按：有趣的意见也可以占个版面，小编并不是为了凑字数，而是为了收集更多人的意见，让所有人都能被看到。 
  
意见一： 
尊敬的夫子院长，您好，我是一名百草家，有点意见想跟您反馈。 
我最近研究出一种新型的植物，它的功效绝对是在王者大陆首屈一指的。它种下之后，长出的藤蔓会主动寻找周围的人，然后用细小的藤蔓缠住人受伤的关节，或是骨折的地方。 
多么好的发明啊，结果这东西居然被善生厅的执勤人员列为违禁品，我都说过了，这个东西绝对安全，绝对不会长进人皮肉里的，感觉痒是因为伤口在愈合，不是植物在皮下播种。 
希望院长能重视这件事，给伟大发明一次机会。 
  
意见二： 
墨子院长好，俺是山下一个勤劳肯干（村里媒人总这么介绍俺）的小伙儿，俺想让你给俺行个方便，你说方不方便？ 
忘了写具体怎么方便了，俺补上。 
俺住的离学院不远，就二里地，没有云舟栈，山区的盘山路也不好走，俺每次自己背着篓子爬上山，给学院送点东西，腰都快累折了，后来买了头牛，牛给累的越来越小了，希望能给俺借用一下冲云翼，哧溜一下子就飞上去了！要是能改造一下，给俺的牛用就更好了。 
  
意见三： 
夫子院长您好，我是武道学院的一名学生。

Clouds and Earthquakes: 
The people of Alsahraa have long noticed unusual cloud formations in the sky, often signaling impending disasters. 
Strange-looking clouds frequently bring torrential rain and thunder, while vividly colored clouds are often accompanied by earthquakes. 
Additionally, changes in the scent of the wind, odd behavior in animals, and sudden plant withering can all point to major wind vortices, underground eruptions, or wildfires. Some instruments from the School of Mechcrafts in Jixia can be used to study the hidden connections between these phenomena.

Herbal medicine is not just about plants. Every living thing has its spirit, and insects, the smallest of creatures, offer endless benefits and hold medicinal value that cannot be overlooked. 
Creating medicine from insects requires specialized techniques and tools. These materials have stricter storage requirements than common herbs, as inappropriate conditions can alter their chemical composition, affect their medicinal properties, and even make them harmful to humans. 
Here we introduce some of the medicinal insects found in Jixia. We hope you exercise caution when you encounter them. 
 
The Yellow Herbal Butterfly, one of the most common butterflies in the Jixia Plains, has wing scales often used by Herb Societies as medicinal guides. The Blue Herbal Butterfly in the mountains and the Red Herbal Butterfly in the north offer similar uses. 
This shows that harvesting herbs from insects does not harm them. Another example is the Medicinal Horn Beetle. This little creature, which only appears on rainy days and raises its horns like tiny umbrellas while moving, sheds shells that can be used to make medicine. 
 
These tiny creatures might carry toxins powerful enough to take down a beast—or hold the key to saving a life. Respecting every living being is a sign of respect for our own lives.

This manual is designed to train idle Mechanoids for tour guide duties. It aims to increase Jixia Academy's influence and showcase the School of Mechcrafts' outstanding creations.

Here are some excerpts:

We're pleased to take you on a tour of Jixia Academy. First, let me introduce myself. I'm a tour guide Mechanoid from the School of Mechcrafts, and my name is Ji Guanren.

In front of us is the School of Martial Arts, led by Headmaster Fuzi, the greatest warrior in Primaera.

Headmaster Fuzi built the School of Martial Arts around the central Tower of Enlightenment. The school is centered around the training field, surrounded by the Strategy Room, the Meditation Hall, and the Aerforge.

This is where martial arts students train their bodies, sharpen their minds, and balance themselves to embark on the path of martial arts.

Not only that, but I, Little Ji, used to work here as a training partner Mechanoid.

Don't be surprised—that's just a showcase of the School of Mechcrafts' capabilities.

Also, don't be fooled by Headmaster Fuzi's kind appearance—he's actually quite strict and traditional. Some jokes are best left untold; ask any student if you don't believe me...

Now we've arrived at the School of Sorcery on the south side of the Tower of Enlightenment, led by Headmaster Zhuangzi. For students aspiring to master sorcery, this is the ideal place to study sorcery laws and enhance their powers.

Here, people can not only explore various ways to advance sorcery energy, but also delve into the rules of dreams with Headmaster Zhuangzi.

He remains true to himself, acting naturally and caring only about sorcery energy and dreams, nothing else.

If you greet Headmaster Zhuangzi and he doesn't respond, it means he's fallen asleep...

Finally, we've reached the most renowned institution in Jixia and also Little Ji's hometown—the School of Mechcrafts!

The School of Mechcrafts, led by the Mechcraft expert Master Mozi, is where students with a practical spirit learn the principles of Mechcraft, design, manufacture, assemble, and test Mechcrafts.

The entire School of Mechcrafts functions like a well-oiled machine, built around the massive Aerflow Weaver. Each building is connected to the weaver.

Most Mechcraft students excel in technology but struggle with social interactions and prefer not to leave. For them, the academy is everything, and Headmaster Mozi is the perfect example. However, among the three headmasters, he's the most difficult to deal with. To put it simply, he's stubborn and has a quick temper.

By the way, Little Ji never lies. Since everyone's here, it wouldn't be right to leave without some souvenirs for your family and friends, would it?

I left home when I was young and fancied myself an adventurer. Wherever I slept, I had the most beautiful dreams. Within two days of each dream, I'd stumble across a treasure. Before long, I had more riches than I knew what to do with. 
 
 
 
But wealth draws eyes. Bandits caught me and forced me to help them find treasure too. Yet no matter how hard I tried, nothing appeared, not a coin, not a gem. 
 
 
 
Worse still, the treasures I had already claimed began to vanish in their hands. They thought I was hiding some mysterious power and, terrified, let me go. After that, I began dreaming again. And the treasures returned, one after another. Looking back now... perhaps those treasures were born from the fine dreams themselves.

At this moment, the stars reveal their message: Till we meet again.
There is a strong smell of gunpowder on these lizard carcasses.

A Letter of Severance 
 
Yan Fengbai, 
 
In days past, we called each other brothers. Together we endured every hardship to enter Jixia in pursuit of the pinnacle of Martial Arts. Yet the Academy's strict rules choked all freedom, and so we left, seeking our own path and journeying to Dreamwhisper Lake. 
 
 
 
I believed that, having left the Academy behind, we would surely gain much. But you... you heard tales of so-called Finedream Weavers, and day after day chased after their shadows, forgetting entirely the way of Martial Arts. 
 
 
 
Lately you have been ever more lost in idle dreams, beyond persuasion, unfit to walk the path beside me. Forgive me for leaving without farewell.
The eternal light endures, the pillar of heaven stands firm. Traveler, speak no more—disturb not the heroic souls.

This book will use the practice of archery to clearly explain the often-overlooked principle of steadiness in Martial Arts in an accessible manner.

I've been studying "Tips on Movement" for a while, but I still can't grasp some of its concepts. 
 
 
 
"Motion arises from stillness, and movement returns to stillness"—what does that mean? 
 
 
 
I've tried various methods of exerting force, but to no avail. 
 
 
 
With no answers, I decided to observe the state of the lotus flowers as described in the text. 
 
 
 
The lotus flowers and leaves in the pond stand upright. They're steady without wind, but when the wind blows, ripples spread across the entire pond. Still, I couldn't comprehend the subtlety described in the writing. 
 
 
 
I then observed the branches in winter. Pine branches often break under heavy snow, while plum branches quickly shake off the snow after accumulating a certain amount. 
 
 
 
After a heavy snow, many pine branches broke, but the plum branches remained intact. 
 
 
 
As the spring breeze blows, my long-standing confusion is finally cleared up. 
 
 
 
I rose to practice my movements and, in doing so, found significant insights.

April 25 \n \nOn our retreat, we were attacked by Mechcraft monsters and forced to take shelter in the Core Control Room. After the collapse of the building, this place isn't far from the outside world; we're planning to slip out once the monsters wander elsewhere. While waiting, we examined the records of the core's operations and maintenance. Cross-checking them with the intel we had before setting out, we pieced together the likely cause of the accident. It seems that the Rebels, seeking to seize something from the Obsolete Pavilion, sent one of their Mechanoids into the recycling station. During processing, the Mechanoid awoke and took the core. The maintenance report from March 30, which noted unstable energy readings, confirms this. The Mechanoid went on to wreck the place and attack the two investigation teams sent out earlier. For now, all we can do is wait for the monsters to leave and carry these preliminary findings back with us.

The movement of herbal leaves hints at their mountain origins. 
 
For the Herbalists, plants are their best guides. With their deep knowledge of medicinal plant distribution, they never lose their way in the wild. To help others understand the natural landmarks that guide the Herb Society, here's an introduction to the medicinal plants across the different terrains of Jixia. 
 
 
 
On the Open Plains: 
 
Waxgrass: Abundant across the plains, Waxgrass is distinguished by its golden petals, which exude a honey-like sweetness. This plant is frequently used in the creation of healing ointments. 
 
Herbal Fan: This less common plant features fan-shaped, neatly folded petals and is highly valued in medicinal recipes for its effectiveness. 
 
Redhorn Ginseng: A rare find, this herb resembles traditional ginseng but is known for its potent healing properties. Due to its rarity and potency, only seasoned Herbalists typically handle its harvesting. 
 
In the Mountainous Highlands: 
 
Celeste Herb: Commonly found in the highlands, this pale blue herb is ground into a fine powder, renowned for its healing properties. 
 
Pipe Bamboo: This rarer herb has long, slender stems and leaves that mimic the appearance of a musical pipe. It is often used in brewing high-quality medicinal soups. 
 
Gentility Herb: The most prized in the highlands, this herb features purple petals and a pistil shaped like a beast's eye. It is celebrated for its strong healing effects and is essential in treating serious ailments. 
 
In the Northern Region: 
 
Healing Wings: Vibrantly colored, with petals that transition from pink to light blue, this herb is abundant and provides significant healing effects. 
 
Dreamfish Herb: Resembling a swimming goldfish, this herb is bitter when ground but is considered a top-tier medicinal herb due to its potent properties. 
 
Bitterword Grass: Rare in the northern region, this herb has thin, elongated stamens that look like a child sticking out their tongue. Its ointment is highly effective and sought after. 
 
Aquatic Herbs: 
 
Green Elder Herb: Found along the water's edge, this herb has slender blue petals and is often used in healing recipes for its elegance and effectiveness. 
 
Purple Crispa: Typically growing in water, this herb has a soft, purplish-blue texture and is versatile in various medicinal brews. 
 
Medicinal Boatleaf: Unique to specific water bodies, this herb has flowers and fruits shaped like small boats, floating on the water's surface and used in specialized medicinal preparations. 
 
 
 
Effective remedies come from nature's bounty, so we should always gather herbs with care and respect. Each act of mindful harvesting is a true celebration of life.

Springbrook Plains: The First Stop in Jixia, a Magical Green Land with War Ruins 
 
Believe it or not, you won't be wasting time reading my articles. What I'm about to show you is the most magical, mysterious, and unimaginable place in the world—Jixia. It is the gathering place of all the marvels of the wise and mysterious eastern continent. I can swear by the stars, the sun, and even in the name of my dearest mother (Mother, I have a feeling I will find a way to cure you in this magical East), that everything I describe is absolutely real! 
 
"There must be a place at the other end of the world that rivals or even surpasses Navenia"—this was my thought when I first arrived in Jixia. Later, I learned that the area I first set foot in is called Springbrook Plains. The structures and that towering building here seem to have been designed without considering the mountains and valleys. They look as if they fell from the sky, landing naturally among the mountains and along the rivers, blending perfectly with the land. I swear, I have traveled all over the West and have never seen buildings this tall, not even half as tall. The structures here are filled with the beauty of the East and exude a natural and mysterious aura. 
 
All of this is built on the ruins of an ancient battlefield. People believe they can still draw mysterious powers from the ancient underground sites and study these ancient relics to restore the once god-like powers! Travelers from afar are not the only ones who come here; many young, passionate faces also arrive from all directions. They are students coming to study in Jixia. These young people walk on the rubble of the old academy that collapsed in the war, with new buildings rising from the ruins. Life springs anew on the scars of this land. The wheel of fate keeps turning, what a magical cycle of renewal and coexistence! 
 
There are even more incredible things that left my mouth agape for ten days and nights. Here, I saw creatures called Saepes that move and act just like humans, labor Mechanoids that move on their own, and gears that turn without any external force. You might say that some of these things exist in Navenia too. Yes, Navenia's steam technology is unparalleled in the world, but I once studied a Mechanoid for a whole day and night and couldn't find its power source. It didn't even emit a puff of steam. I have to believe that the East has its unique charm and magic. And yes, I mean real "magic." 
 
You might think I'm making this up. Oh no, the greatest traveler cannot be dishonest. I have no doubt about the construction of these great structures and Mechanoids because I have seen people with magical abilities on this land...

Contributor: Song Tuantuan, student at the School of Mechcrafts 
 
Content: Thoughts on Mechanoid Design and Combat 
 
Editor's Note: "Non-aggression" does not mean avoiding all conflict; excessive tolerance can also be a sign of weakness. 
 
When I was working on that big Mechanoid, I was just following my teacher's instructions. As a new student, I couldn't even fully understand a set of Mechcraft Dice, let alone design such an elaborate Mechanoid! However, after the agricultural Mechanoid failed, Senior Su Qing led a few of us to retrieve it from the fields. After carefully dismantling it and identifying its design flaws, Senior Su redrafted the design, removing the weaker plant identification feature and greatly enhancing its guarding capabilities. Once we submitted this revised design to our teachers, we quickly received approval to begin experimentation. 
 
Although Senior Su is a top student by every measure, we juniors didn't want to waste this hard-earned opportunity. We persuaded him to act as a supervisor, refraining from direct involvement and focusing only on inspection and final acceptance. Fortunately, Senior Su is very amiable and willing to let us have our way, so we poured our efforts into the Mechanoid, creating the initial version based on our own understanding, before calling upon Senior Su for a test spar. 
 
To be honest, I felt quite anxious. Senior Su wielded his Energy Core, testing the Mechanoid with a variety of intricate attacks, while we watched anxiously from a distance. Not long before receiving this assignment, I had learned about Master Mozi's ideal of "non-aggression." This is a profound philosophical concept that I still don't fully comprehend, but I clearly remember how the Mechanoid had accidentally pushed Uncle Zhang into the ground while assisting with farm work. I thought to myself, no matter what, conflict is never good—if humans and Mechanoids are always fighting, how can we ever achieve world peace? 
 
I expected Senior Su to spend a lot of time testing, but after a few rounds, he returned, pursing his lips, and asked which "little genius" had led the design improvements. We exchanged glances, explained that we had discussed and worked on it together, and shared what we had learned from Master Mozi. 
 
Senior Su showed a mixture of amusement and frustration. He explained that while the Mechanoid had strong defense and endurance, its offensive capabilities were nearly nonexistent—such a design could not fulfill its guarding duties. Furthermore, "non-aggression" means avoiding "unjust" conflicts, not abandoning all weapons. As for what constitutes "unjust," I believe it will take me a long time to truly grasp this lesson.

When she was young, Perilla was timid and withdrawn. She kept to herself, and people often whispered that she was too quiet, that a child like her would never amount to much. 
 
But Perilla was never truly alone. She had the world's bravest friend, Aqing. Aqing once told her that she would become the greatest Herbalist in the world. 
 
"The greatest Herbalist?" Perilla had asked. "What's that?" 
 
Smiling, Aqing took her hand and led her off to find the Herbalists. 
 
Under flowing starlight and a blazing sun, the two followed in the Herbalist's footsteps, learning how to gather herbs, how to tell one plant from another. 
 
Aqing was always half a step ahead, holding Perilla's hand, guiding her through the undergrowth, cutting through confusion and fear alike. In those days together, Perilla kept telling herself that Aqing was amazing, and that she would have to work twice as hard just to keep up. 
 
One night, beneath a sky crossed by shooting stars, Perilla asked Aqing what her dream was. Aqing laughed and said she wanted them both to become the greatest Herbalists in the world. Seeing the light in Aqing's eyes, Perilla silently made the same vow. 
 
But time moved on, and Aqing left as suddenly as she had come. Perilla stayed behind in the Herb Garden. Whispers began again, and once more she slipped quietly from everyone's sight. Aqing's dream was to become the best Herbalist together. Perilla's dream was simply Aqing. 
 
She began to follow in Aqing's steps: learning how she spoke, studying the same books, searching for traces of her in old notes and margins. Whenever confusion or hardship stopped her in her tracks, she asked herself what Aqing would have done. 
 
Had she caught up? Or had she only become a smaller shadow of the girl she admired? 
 
Carrying that uneasy question in her heart, Perilla finally became the head of the Herb Society, and that day, she saw Aqing again. 
 
"Did I ever catch up to you?" she asked softly. "Have I become even a little like you?" 
 
"You've always had your own path. You've always been you, Perilla. And to me... you've always been the finest Herbalist in the world."

I sneaked up to the top floor, wanting to see what was happening outside. But the moment I looked, she stopped me and pulled me back.

The white clouds that usually gathered around the slopes of Mount Jixia had been stained a deep gray, as if smoke were spilling across the entire range. And that dark mass spreading from Springbrook Plains... it came from the army marching out of Horizon Harbor.

She snapped at me to leave and threw her fur cloak over my shoulders. Just then, a sharp crack cut through the air. A thunderous blast followed. And after that... I couldn't hear anything at all.

During the recent construction of the Wondrous Maze, the transport carrying team stone materials in the northern canyon accidentally cracked part of the canyon wall, revealing an ancient stone gate.  
  
The Seeker Society has assigned me to investigate. As I explored the crevice, I found that the mechanism used to seal the gate is much more complex than anything I've seen before. I would greatly appreciate your guidance, and if you have time, perhaps you could join me in this investigation.

The Dreamslayer is skilled in ambush, deception, and disguise. All students are urged to exercise extreme caution. 
 
 
 
If you encounter anyone at Dreamwhisper Lake who speaks unclearly or has a cold demeanor, please be on high alert.

The forbidden land, the peak of the Heavenly Pillar.
It has been a long time since I last returned here, and I never expected to find it in such a state.
However, for now, this is the only foolproof plan.
Therefore, let those who see this stele take heed: do not approach the peak of the Heavenly Pillar.

A automaton giant! 
 
 
 
I never thought they would send something so enormous just to deal with Jixia. 
 
 
 
That monstrous body, even walking is enough to crush people. 
 
 
 
Dozens of students did not make it back today. I do not know how many will return tomorrow. I hate my own cowardice, but I cannot escape the fear in my heart. 
 
 
 
Every time I see it stepping across the battlefield, I cannot move. My feet freeze. I cannot even dodge. 
 
 
 
But I do not want to stay like this, afraid and powerless...

Dad used to say Xiaoyuu was too tiny to be useful. He has no idea how clever Xiaoyuu really is. Xiaoyuu can carry messages for people. When I grow up and make Mechcrafts, I want to build ones just as smart as Xiaoyuu! 
 
 
 
Xiaoyuu, Xiaoyuu, please swim to Mother and ask her when she is coming, alright? 
 
The boat stopped. This place is so pretty. The mountains reach all the way up to the sky, and the fields stretch farther than I can see. There are many shiny green stones too. I picked up a bunch for Mother.
A cold-blooded Dreamslayer is on the loose, and it is the duty of us students to eliminate evil.\n\nHowever, our strength is limited and not all evil can be eradicated.
In a desperate situation, Eternity's low roar pierces the night. A tribe from the sky brings new stories.

Captain Qi, \nGuess what? I found a treasure on the road—it's alive! It's your team member, Nangong Jing. This little one has been circling around the Aership Station nonstop. I warned you when you were selecting team members that She couldn't tell east from west and would surely get lost. I invited you multiple times to form a team with me, but you always refused. Now we're competitors! Your team member is in my hands. How about you surrender early? Come find me at Dainty Vale.
Our defense is as steadfast as rock. Our attack is as fierce as fire. \nThe honor of the Vanquisher is etched in history.

The dead are gone, and the living are filled with regret... Let us return, may all wishes come true. May the power that reaches the heavens return to glory once more... Looking from afar, I vow to retrieve it.

Fifty years of fishing, and today I'm ashamed! 
 
 
 
These young folks nowadays, who knows what they're thinking? They've invented some fish-shaped Mechcraft to place underwater. Back in my day, I was known as the legendary fisherman whose rod flew like a falcon, but today I got fooled by a mere Mechcraft designed to look like a flying fish! The old men fishing with me all mocked me, saying I've gone from "hawk-rod" to "rat-rod." What an absolute disgrace!

The Greenwhisper Treasure helped me get in. 
It is said that one needs to unite seven keys and head north into the deep cave to solve the Mechcraft riddle. 
 
It sounds like a puzzle. I'll pass. 
 
Could it be a trial set up by Master Mozi? Bring it on. 
 
A treasure that requires three keys to unlock? Must be something good.
This Mech Core, crafted with the aid of large machinery and featuring excellent texture and workmanship, is equipped with a uniquely structured energy lock.

[Research Notes]
……
I have been exploring the fusion of consciousness and mechanisms.
It is known that the Divine Rune Mechanism Workbench can infuse mechanical creations with Divine Rune energy, and this energy is essentially a conductible "flow."
This led to a hypothesis: Does human consciousness also belong to a special kind of "flow"? If we can borrow the conduction logic of Divine Rune energy and find a suitable connection method to import the consciousness flow into the mechanical body, perhaps we can achieve <69D0FF>deep integration of consciousness and mechanism.</>
However, this method is still under research and should not be attempted rashly.

Dear Yu, 
How have you been? I heard you've been inquiring about some ancient secrets. If I'm not mistaken, it should be related to the place I have in mind. 
 
As old classmates, how about we compete to solve some puzzles? If you can reach the end, I'll share the clues I've obtained. The current score is ninety-six to eighty-seven, and I'm close to reaching a hundred wins. To avoid any claims of unfairness, I'll just give you some free points this time. 
 
There are six <69D0FF>Aerflow Towers</> in this mountain. I've designed six trials based on them. Complete them to unlock the barrier. The answers you seek are in that room. Once you've seen the truth, you can decide if you want to find me.

Yesterday I was exhausted. Maybe it was nothing more than a dream, but I can still remember the way my heart raced... 
 
 
 
<69D0FF>Night seemed to fall</> all at once, and something about the altar and the clearing around it changed. The <69D0FF>Giant Saepes</> appeared in the distance, moving as if pulled by some unseen force, circling the place in silence. Even the faint candlelight seemed to jump in time with the trembling earth... 
 
 
 
I remember ducking into the bushes nearby. Fatigue washed over me, so heavy I couldn't fight it. When I woke, the sky was already bright. The fear was gone, and the Giant Saepes, if they had really been there, had vanished without a trace.

What happened today is just a warning. If the academy hasn't resolved the issue with that beast by the end of the Enlightenment Trials, I will return. Then, she will enter the valley and deal with it her way.

The falcon, a dominant species, patrols its territory to hunt. However, recent observations suggest they are not patrolling but are instead searching for something. There is one area they consistently avoid, which suggests that their fear is causing them to be cautious.

The art of cannons is all about ignition and explosion. Yet their potential is ultimately tied to Mechcraft. Simply delve into these Mechcrafts without a clear understanding is unlikely to lead to any significant progress beyond the current state of technology. 
 
 
 
Sorcery, on the other hand, taps into the orders of nature and allows one to harness the power of the world. If we can combine it with cannons, we might open up a whole new path...

After becoming a Godforged, many envied me. At first, I thought it was great: power, respect, glory.

But is sacrifice the destiny of a Godforged? In the last battle, I was the only survivor of a ten-man squad. I can't turn back; I can only move forward. But I don't want to die yet—there's research unfinished, a promise I made to her. I can't just throw my life away.

But I can't show weakness. As a Godforged, I have to fight whether I'm ready or not.
I can do this. I must.

Time flies. In the blink of an eye, you've already been gone for five years. 
 
 
 
The world has changed countless times in those years, though you may not have noticed. 
 
 
 
I know our child and I were always your greatest concerns. 
 
 
 
When you were here, we shared your world. And if you could see us now, I believe it would still be the same. 
 
 
 
This summer your brother came through West Aerfall on business and stopped by our home. He brought Haishu the talisman you left behind, the one that wards off illness. 
 
 
 
Sometimes, in his dreams, Haishu whispers "Mom." He knows you're watching over him, and he feels safe. 
 
 
 
Just a few days ago, I took Haishu up into the mountains. I told him you loved Staring Gent, so we gathered a whole basket. 
 
 
 
I've left the flowers and this letter here. If you can see this, please come back and visit us. That would be enough. Truly, that would be enough.

Written by Tata: \nBeakshade and Aerdo Berry are common cooking ingredients in Northton, which can be used to prepare various dishes. Here's a recipe for the cake made by Beakshade. Combine Jihu Barley flour from the Harvest Fields with some Aersilk, knead well, and let it rest for ten minutes. Divide the dough into palm-sized pieces, mix in freshly chopped Beakshade, and shape it into your preferred bird form, like Pome Magpie or Aershroud. Finally, place the dough in a steamer and wait for thirty minutes before enjoying.

April 26 
 
I am the Mechsmith assigned to this investigation team. When we heard the monster's footsteps fade, we began our retreat—only for it to double back the moment it caught our noise. In the end, the captain shoved me into this small chamber and pressed this notebook into my arms. Outside, I heard screams that dwindled into weak groans. I fear the captain and the rest are gone. Our plan had been to release Mechcraft Kites from the core control room and wait for rescue. But we learned that the monster can strike them all down. 
 
During the last attack, I noticed something strange: the monster's features did not match the Rebel's. Instead, there was something oddly familiar in its form—yet I can't quite put my finger on it. Could this undermine our earlier conclusions? Now, the only remaining Mechcraft Kite is the one in my hands, and I don't have the strength to escape the monster's pursuit. 
 
Captain, comrades, the two teams before us, the staff of Obsolete Pavilion—I don't want anyone else to die here. To prevent any further potential casualties, I must get this information out. Perhaps I can draw the monster's attention, buy enough time for the Kite to escape. I have been far luckier than the rest. So let me use this pen to bid you all farewell. If you can, come to this chamber and take away what remains of their belongings.

Master Shi Yu:
We are all slowly recovering, which is wonderful. I've met some extraordinary people recently—would you like to hear about them?

There is a lady named Shye with a beautiful smile; a hot-tempered boy who uses a machine gun, whose temper sometimes reminds me of you; a very confident, seemingly radiant boy named Novar... And a strange uncle who kept staring at my mechanical wings. It turned out he thought they had several issues and gifted me a new pair... I'll bring them to show you when I visit.

Reporters: Lin Mengchu, Han Qing (Intern) 
 
As the pace of life accelerates, many students are overwhelmed by the pressures of daily life and study, leading to poor sleep quality and difficulty concentrating. The author believes that mental health may be the next major challenge the academy must face. 
 
According to our reporters' investigations, the prevalence of mental disorders among Jixia residents—primarily depressive and anxiety disorders—has been rising annually. Currently, the prevalence of depressive disorders in Jixia is 2%, while anxiety disorders reach as high as 5%. 
 
This means that one in every fourteen people suffers from a mental disorder. These figures indicate that mental health issues like anxiety and depression are becoming increasingly common in Jixia, signaling that the academy must prioritize mental health, provide timely intervention, and implement controls to prevent these from becoming social issues that hinder Jixia's overall development. 
 
However, there is still a lack of awareness regarding mental health in Jixia. Many residents ignore or avoid these issues, silently enduring the consequences. At the same time, the lack of a socialized mental health service system in Jixia restricts both the demand for and the utilization of such services. 
 
Here, the Iridescent Weekly calls on every friend currently trapped in pain and suffering from mental health issues to face them head-on; you are not fighting alone. We also call on the academy authorities to actively address mental health, promote mental health education, build support services, and listen to every cry for help.

Long ago, in the Serene Wilds Pool, there lived a special fish. As it swam, its body illuminated the water like the bright moon, earning it the name "Moon Carp." The fish was as light as a feather, gliding silently through the water. Its glow was said to heal sicknesses and turn pebbles into pearls. A saying went: "Should you catch a Moon Carp, blessings will be forever yours." \n \nAs word spread, many tried to catch it. November 7th 
 
I came to Jixia Academy to make a name for myself and earn respect. But now I broke free from the academy's constraints and did something... Is this really okay? 
 
No, I shouldn't blame myself. There's nothing wrong with the pursuit of strength. To those who doubt me—just you wait!

Jixia Mountains: The Peak of Knowledge, Home to Jixia Academy

From almost any part of Jixia, you can see a tower that pierces the sky, with clouds and birds circling its middle. After days of traveling in Jixia, I followed this tower to the crown of wisdom and knowledge in the east—Jixia Academy.

Here, I never felt the curiosity or distance often experienced by foreigners. Students (and even some non-humans) come from all over the world, making foreign faces quite common. What truly sparks people's interest here is only the methods to transcend oneself and constantly refine one's strength in knowledge, martial arts, and magic.

When I heard the tower's name, I didn't find it exaggerated or doubt it at all—Tower of Babel. This name truly suits it. The three great colleges built around the miraculous Tower of Babel form the core area of Jixia Academy. Jixia students train here in the three foundational disciplines: Sorcery, Martial Arts, and Mechcraft. The overseer of each college is one of the Three Sages of Jixia—three legends who have reached the pinnacle in their respective fields.

There’s a strong academic atmosphere here, along with a fascinating diversity of teachers and students. The academy facilities, constructed from the peculiar Aerflow drawn down by the Tower of Babel, are not only clever and interesting but also beneficial for student learning, research, and daily life.

Great travelers make friends wherever they go, and Macaroni’s friends are everywhere. Yet the friends I’ve met at Jixia Academy still made me feel… how should I put it? As an ancient eastern proverb says, “beyond the sky lies a vaster sky; in the world there are also stronger champions than the strong.” Here I’ve met a friend who draws power from stars to defeat monstrous beasts, a hundred times his size, engulfed in blazing flames! I’ve also met a friend who can control time within a small area, even reversing it briefly! By the time I witnessed another beauty using sorcery to shatter solid rock with a mere silk scarf, I was no longer particularly surprised… And people like them are merely one among the many seeking knowledge here, each possessing their own special powers and abilities—as commonplace as every Hydrestan having a pair of eyes.

I haven’t even mentioned their teachers—the Three Sages of Jixia: the mightiest warriors of the east and the wisemen who draw power from their surroundings. They teach those who come here to wield martial might and sorcery, and to drive machines with their will. It’s precisely these great powers and mentors that attract the best from across the east and foreign lands to seek the limits of sorcery and martial arts. And for me? Even more delightful is the constant stream of people bringing with them delicacies from every corner of the world. What could be more enticing than that for a food lover?

The fruit is sweet and is known for its vision-enhancing properties, offering effective relief for eye fatigue, stinging around the eyes, redness, swelling, and dryness.

My name is Mikilin. Aside from being a food connoisseur, I've held many roles throughout my life. 
 
 
 
To explore the history of cuisine, I studied knife techniques at the School of Martial Arts; to understand the perfect cooking temperatures, I delved into the study of combustion at the School of Sorcery; and to master the crafting of culinary tools, I honed my skills in forging at the School of Mechcrafts. 
 
After completing my studies, I traveled across Jixia, seeking out flavors that have long vanished from history. Comparing the old with the new, I've discovered that the culinary path we're on might be filled with hidden risks. 
 
Let me start by sharing some long-lost dishes recorded in ancient texts. 
 
 
 
It's said that in ancient times, to boost the morale of soldiers before they set out on campaigns, a type of jerky was prepared to enhance their physical strength. This jerky was marinated using over twenty different ingredients, each processed uniquely. 
 
Afterward, a rare brewing liquid was prepared and placed in a sealed smoking chamber to lock in the jerky's moisture and nutrients. The smoking process required Sorcery techniques to precisely control the temperature, ensuring the correct doneness. 
 
This jerky was easy to digest, and it was said that just one piece could sustain a person for three days without the need for additional food. Moreover, its taste was reportedly so exquisite that its value on the battlefield even surpassed that of captured weapons. 
 
 
 
The recipe was a closely guarded secret, with a dedicated department responsible for its development and improvement. As a delicacy, it had evolved into a strategic reserve of national importance. 
 
What struck me most was the meticulous care taken by the ancients when preparing food. In contrast, modern cuisine often focuses solely on presentation—controlling heat, cutting ingredients aesthetically, and so forth. Many ingredients are now pre-processed by Hunters before being mass-delivered to restaurants. This processing suppresses much of their potential. 
 
Jixia overflows with abundance, but have we truly brought out the best in what we have? 
 
 
 
In modern times, with the advent of technology, culinary practices are transforming. I recently observed a prototype at the School of Mechcrafts—a fully automated cooking stove designed by a young student. This device handles everything from ingredient preparation to cooking and plating, promising consistency and precision in culinary outputs. Though still a prototype, I believe it has great potential. It's one of the reasons I originally pursued Mechcraft myself. 
 
 
 
However, this creation has left me with mixed feelings. Throughout my travels in Jixia, I've encountered passionate individuals dedicated to culinary arts, from Gourmets at Cloudreach Tower to local innkeepers and bustling diners. 
 
 
 
Their dedication adds a human touch to food that no machine can replicate. The thought of Mechcrafts replacing this human element brings a sense of loss—while we might achieve consistent quality, the warmth of human interaction in cooking and sharing food might diminish. 
 
As an enthusiastic lover of food, I recognize my role to be appreciating and assessing dishes in my own way and imparting my knowledge to students with sincerity. I don't expect my opinions to last or my tastes to be widely recognized. 
 
 
 
In the end, amidst all the exquisite flavors I've tasted, the most heartwarming ones are those infused with human passion and connection.

That girl Myra bustled about the village for a while, then vanished without a trace. I had been thinking that if she truly wanted to perform the full prayer ritual, I would give her the painting I drew for her. After all, it's remarkable for an outsider to be interested in local traditions. 
 
Understanding the ritual is important, but it's normal to get sidetracked. Young people always have greater ambitions in mind. A quick glance amidst their busy lives is enough. 
 
During her stay in the village, she seemed to have become friends with many people. Some who tried her Harvest Pancake said it tasted quite good. I also heard she drank her own Aerux Brew and got tipsy, even biting her tongue while speaking. 
 
The girl was also very helpful, not only working on the prayer ritual but also assisting the villagers with many tasks. After she left, some curious children began imitating her prayers; It turned out to be a fun way to learn. 
 
It's not bad. If more young people take an interest in the ritual, even if it's just for fun, over time, it will surely plant new seeds of genuine interest. 
 
I'm waiting for that day.

As an ancient artifact from the Dreamweave Plains, the Harvest Bell plays a significant role in various social functions such as politics, business, and folklore. The Societies have conducted several investigations of the Harvest Bell, each focusing on their own areas of focus and expertise, and compiled their findings into this report. 
 
The Harvest Bell was first discovered by the Seeker Society in the riverbed. Archaeological investigations determined it to be a relic of the Sanctified. Crafted with exceptional precision and adorned with intricate carvings, it appears linked to some ritual. However, due to its age, the specific nature of this ritual remains to be studied. 
 
During the Aerflow Anomaly, the Craft Society moved into Harvest Fields. Leveraging their advanced Mechcraft techniques, they dismantled the Harvest Bell and found it contained immense energy. Considering that the people of Harvest Fields were then suffering from the anomaly, the Craft Society modified the bell, enabling it to channel Aerflow and nourish all living things.

Author: Huai Zhuo, Sorcery Instructor 
 
When you first step through the gates of the School of Sorcery, someone will surely tell you, "The true art of sorcery lies in grasping the essence." But what is this essence? And how do you uncover it? Answers to these questions are scarce, or perhaps they left you even more perplexed. However, these two questions are not as complicated as they seem. Headmaster Zhuangzi once said, "Observe the cloud silkworm, forget all attachments, and you shall grasp its essence." I misunderstood this statement at first, spending my days simply staring at the cloud silkworms. Yet mere observation reveals only the surface: spinning silk, weaving cocoons, emerging anew. The heart of his words lies in "forget all attachments." 
 
These four words may seem profound, but they can be broken down into two parts: "forget external attachments" and "forget self-attachments." What does "forget external attachments" mean? Forget all surface-level characteristics, forms, colors, origins, and preconceived notions. And what about "forget self-attachments"? Let go of your uniqueness, your subjectivity, and see yourself as part of the world's tapestry. To truly let go of both external and self-attachments means combining these two states, clearing the fog of preconceptions, and uncovering the essence unencumbered by previous ideas. 
 
Here is a description of Headmaster Zhuangzi, the master of letting go, from my mentor's mentor: "Don't be fooled by the headmaster's youthful appearance—his true age is unknown. His fellow sorcerers speculate that his secret to eternal youth is actually sleep! Not just any sleep, but utilizing dreams to experience countless lifetimes, where he even forgot the distinction between self and the world." 
 
So, what exactly is this essence? That's something for you to discover on your own. But I'll share my perspective—it might help. I believe everything is constantly changing, and their essence lies in the laws governing those changes. Mastering sorcery isn't about controlling and manipulating energy; it's about understanding the laws of transformation and seeing the interconnectedness of all things. 
 
I know everyone who enters the School of Sorcery wants to grow stronger. Remember, patience is key in sorcery training—patiently uncover the essence of things. Only then will you be able to handle it with ease when facing any challenge. 
 
Editor's note: An engaging read with clear insights. (Regarding my love for sleep, I think I just enjoy closing my eyes.)

Hello everyone! Today I've come to Frostcloud Town, and I'm glad to share with you some knowledge about musical instruments. 
 
 
 
I'd like to introduce a few of the instruments most often used at Jixia Academy. Though they may look ordinary, each carries deep history and culture. With the help of Aersilk, they produce tones that are clearer and more melodious. 
 
 
 
Let's begin with the guqin. The guqin is one of the most representative instruments in Jixia—its tone is beautiful and expressive. 
 
 
 
At the Academy, many students of the Music Society love to play the guqin, using its music to express emotion and refine their character. Some even modify their instruments with Mechcrafts, making the sound richer and more powerful. 
 
 
 
Next is the flute. Among wind instruments, the flute is the most widely played in Jixia. Its sound is bright and graceful, and Musicians often carry one at all times to capture sudden sparks of inspiration. 
 
 
 
To tell their flutes apart, students decorate them with unique designs. The one I remember most vividly bore a painting by a Crafter—a scene of a hundred birds gathering in flight. Truly unforgettable. 
 
 
 
Now let's look at the erhu. Its sound is strikingly distinct—able to draw out mournful melodies or stir up joyful rhythms. At the Academy, it is another favorite of Musicians. Many professors even use the erhu in class to accompany their lessons. Simple Aersilk twisted into strings can create melodies of endless variety. 
 
 
 
But the erhu's shifting tones are difficult to master. Some Musicians have begun experimenting with Mecharms to help with memory. The project is still in progress, but it's one many look forward to. 
 
 
 
Lastly, the yaogu. This percussion instrument has a powerful rhythm and is an essential feature of festivals and celebrations. During Academy festivities, when the drums resound and the students sing and dance, the sight is simply magnificent to behold. If you have the chance, you should come and see it for yourself. 
 
 
 
The yaogu is also a favorite of Martial Arts students who take Music as a minor. Its bold, lively rhythm matches their spirit, while drumming itself helps strengthen the body. Its strong beat improves coordination and reflexes—skills that are invaluable in training. 
 
 
 
These instruments are not only widely played at Jixia Academy; they are also vital parts of this land's ancient musical heritage. I hope that as you listen to them, you can feel the history and culture they carry. That is what it truly means for the Music Society to carry on this land's legacy.

In Jixia, there's a unique and charming addition to the scholarly community: the Scholar Geese. These aren't your ordinary geese; they're adorned with mortarboard hats and feather fans, and engage in clever repartee. While they may not be official teachers, their dedication to spreading knowledge is unwavering. Legend has it that the ancestor of the Scholar Geese was a domesticated white goose that set out on a continent-spanning quest for its missing owner. It mastered every human language, became a vessel of vast knowledge, yet never found the whereabouts of its beloved owner. 
Now, Scholar Geese are a common sight along Jixia's main roads and intersections. If you happen to strike up a particularly delightful conversation with them, beware of their "honking" laughter, as they might seize the opportunity to pose a question. 
These geese have become an integral part of the educational landscape, thanks to the collaborative efforts of the Hunting Society and the Academy. Fluent in human languages, they'd ask questions based on where you meet them. Answer correctly, and you might be rewarded; Otherwise, expect a peck from them. 
While Scholar Geese retain some of their wild instincts, they have largely adapted to societal life in Jixia. Dressed in attire that reflects their roles, these geese lead lives much like Croaky's—though such details are seldom seen by the public. Out of respect for their privacy, we'll refrain from delving deeper here. 
Regarding their ability to speak, I must keep the secret techniques of our amazing hunters confidential. In short, our transformation of an ordinary goose into a Scholar Goose doesn't rely on heartwarming tales but on thorough training. Even though they're often seen with the Seekers, don't be too quick to believe any unverifiable anecdotes from them. 
We must collaborate with the Academy to incorporate the origins and stories of the Scholar Geese into the curriculum. By doing so, we can ensure that these feathered scholars continue to enlighten students for generations to come.

As one grows older, the vast world seems to lose its flavor, like a thin veil of silk between oneself and life's taste. Yet the Harvest Bell stands in quiet defiance of that fading. It endures wind and snow year after year, its surface etched by time, rust spreading like old scars. 
 
The bell often rings, but few stop to listen. Perhaps that is a blessing. It means that Harvest Fields has known long peace, untouched by war or unrest. 
 
Still, I can never quite let go of the old prayer rites. In the deep of night, I sometimes wonder if it is only nostalgia—that the grand ceremonies I joined as a child left me too fond of their form. But then I understand: it is not the rituals I miss, but the memory of hardship that once befell this land, and the need to remain watchful even in peace. 
 
I can only imagine that earlier age—the calamity I never lived through—when the clans and villagers, young and old alike, stood together against disaster. From that shared struggle grew the deep bond that made Harvest Fields what it is today: steadfast, prosperous, whole. 
 
The elders used to tell the tale with laughter. When the calamity struck, thunder rolled across the sky, strange lights appeared, and the village stood on the brink of ruin. Yet in an instant the storm vanished without a trace, as if some immortal hand had gathered it away. 
 
Now I, too, have become one of the elders. The mystery of that day will likely never be solved. But I can still tend the bell, offer prayers for the four corners, paint a few small pictures, and tell the young travelers who pass by about the traditions that once were. 
 
May those who dwell here live without fear or want; may their lives flow calm as water, content without struggle, gentle enough to nourish all things. 
 
This humble record is offered only as a token of my heart.

Jixia is home to many plants nourished by the Aersilk, with Aurous Grass and Glowworm Grass being the most representative. These plants are widely distributed, emitting golden and pale blue halos respectively. 
 
And there are other plants that also contain mystical energy, each thriving in distinct environments. Let's explore them one by one. 
 
 
 
Bluegleam Grass is often found on plains, with petals that glow like blue lamps. Drooping Lotus grows exclusively in the waters of the plains, with broad leaves and flowers that hang upside down beneath the water, shimmering with light. Luminara GrassLight is rare on the plains, resembling a trumpet with dark green leaves edged in golden veins. Its central bud emits a faint blue glow, becoming more prominent at night. 
 
 
 
Frosted Bellflower is more common in mountainous areas, with slightly larger petals that hold blue-glowing energy. Goblet Grass grows exclusively in the mountains, entirely purple, and shaped like a small cup. Lady Lantern is a rare mountain species, with leaves that rotate around the stem and emit a dazzling light in the darkness, possessing abundant energy. 
 
 
 
Dreamstar Grass is star-shaped with spiked edges, while Dreamcage Grass has winding branches resembling tiny cages. Both are unique to the Dreamscape Area in northern Jixia, swaying and glowing in the dreamy night. In the flowing rivers, there is a rare plant called the Luminous Lotus, floating on the surface like a glowing cradle, mysterious and dreamlike. 
 
 
 
The Aerflow energy should be harnessed responsibly, whether for practicing Martial Arts, studying Sorcery, or refining Mechcrafts. Properly acquiring this naturally condensed energy from heaven and earth maintains the Aersilk ecology and ensures continuous self-improvement.

Author: Lu Chi, Senior Seeker from Jixia 
 
Subject: Discoveries Exploration Log 
 
Editor's Note: Passion and courage are the soul of the School of Martial Arts, but remember not to risk your life in every battle. 
 
 
 
I've been a Seeker for many years and have seen countless strange things, but there's one place that keeps drawing me back. 
 
Aerfall Highlands. 
 
Seekers believe that a great civilization once thrived there, but something happened that led to its rapid decline and fall. 
 
The news of my expedition to the Aerfall Highlands didn't attract other Seekers, but it did draw many students from the School of Martial Arts. 
 
"It's a long journey." I warned them. 
 
"No problem!" They replied. 
 
"It will be dangerous." 
 
"That's better!" 
 
Their overflowing enthusiasm moved the trip up by two weeks. 
 
 
 
After a long journey, we arrived at an underground structure by dusk. An elderly local warned us to leave, saying the place was unsafe and that monsters roamed at night. 
 
I planned to wait until morning to explore, but just as I made that decision, the enthusiastic Martial Arts students popped in. 
 
It was pitch black inside, but I was prepared and lit the torch I brought along. 
 
Before the torch could even illuminate the dark passage, a piercing howl echoed through our ears. 
 
I started to regret coming down with them. 
 
 
 
I heard the creature's heavy breathing and the sound of its claws scraping the ground. Then I saw its crimson eyes, drooling mouth, and sharp teeth glinting eerily. 
 
Even though I've encountered many terrifying beasts in previous expeditions, this unknown creature left me frozen in place, unable to move. 
 
"Guys, run quickly! I'll... hold it off." 
 
I managed to stutter those words out, trembling. 
 
These Martial Arts students came here with me, and no matter how scared I was, I couldn't let them get hurt. 
 
But before I could even draw my weapon, the students shouted and charged at the creature. 
 
I had never found myself in such a perilous situation, nor had I ever faced such a vicious enemy—or such fierce companions. 
 
They dodged its sharp claws and evaded every bite. 
 
When it tried to escape, they surrounded it and kept fighting. 
 
 
 
As dawn broke, both the students and the creature were lying on the ground, exhausted and gasping for breath. 
 
It was a thrilling encounter, but fortunately, no one was injured. 
 
I gathered valuable records, and they got to apply their martial skills in a real fight. 
 
However, ever since then, I always warn other Seekers: if your companions are from the School of Martial Arts, your expedition is bound to be anything but peaceful.

The success of Lee Jinchai and Hua Changhui soon drew the attention of merchants across the land. More and more traders flocked to Aerux Town. The market flourished, commerce boomed, and profits soared. But where prosperity gathers, shadows follow. At last, the wolf appeared. 
 
"Return this! Look at this—what kind of quality is this supposed to be?" The man slammed the goods onto the counter. His sleeve was stained a deep green. Li Jinchai picked up the item, studying it carefully. This was already the third customer to complain that day. The product bore her workshop's mark, yet someone had brushed it with cheap dye that easily rubbed off. 
 
She couldn't make sense of it. Hua Changhui, who had been manning the shop as usual, finally said, "None of our merchandise uses that color. But all three customers today had the same green stain. I think a bulk buyer tampered with the stock before reselling it." 
 
Their motives were unclear. The two went out for lunch, still puzzling over the matter. The town had grown since their arrival—wider streets, larger crowds, new faces everywhere. Familiar merchants greeted them in passing, and even strangers often stopped to talk. Their names had become known throughout the region. 
 
"Master Lee! How goes business? You won't believe what's happened at my shop." A bearded elder from Aerpaper Shop waved to her before continuing, his voice anxious. "Our customers have been returning paper by the bundle. They say it stains their hands green the moment they open it! The color's exactly like the one on your right hand." 
 
Lee looked down. It was the same hand she had used to inspect the returned goods that morning. "I understand, Master Wang. We've been facing the same issue," she said, explaining everything. The two gathered other merchants, visiting each shop in town. Everywhere they went, they found the same problem—every reputable local business had been hit. 
 
Soon, Aerux Town's reputation plummeted. Sales plummeted overnight. A web had been cast, vast and unseen, and the shadow beneath it felt both distant and familiar. 
 
"We can't just sit and wait for ruin!" Lee declared, calling an emergency meeting of all affected merchants. "This happened because each of us acted alone. The culprit behind this must be powerful—someone capable of purchasing from all our shops and destroying our reputation in a single stroke. If we don't unite, everything we've built will be lost." 
 
Her words rang with conviction. One elder spoke up, "Master Lee, Master Hua—what do you propose?" 
 
Hua Changhui stepped forward. "First, we'll share our buyer records and descriptions of anyone who's picked up suspicious orders. I'll personally contact Misthill Bull Express and pay out of pocket to help trace these deliveries. And we should issue a joint statement, backed by evidence, to show the customers the truth." 
 
Their sincerity moved the room. For the first time, the merchants of Northton stood as one. Each shop identified several suspicious buyers, and after the public declaration, customer trust gradually returned. 
Not long after, the green-stained goods vanished completely. 
 
From this incident, the Aerux Chamber of Commerce was born, and Lee Jinchai and Hua Changhui were unanimously chosen as its first co-directors. 
 
A young seedling may be fragile, but when roots intertwine and strength gathers, it will one day pierce the heavens and grow into a towering tree.

I was born during the war between Jixia and Dawnsong, a time of intense battles and widespread despair... 
That March, the Dawnsong forces broke through our defenses. Springbrook Plains fell, and the Academy was forced into a desperate night retreat. Dozens of students vanished, never to be heard from again... 
By May, the enemy pressed forward unchecked. At Crosswind Bridge, a small squad stood their ground for two days. Against all odds, they forced the invaders back—but only the captain returned. Pierced by a hundred arrows, he still marched home carrying the banner... 
In August, the conflict grew fiercer, the balance tilting neither way. A centuries-old tree in Serene Wilds was felled and cast into the forges of war. The Brutalhorn Bull, who had lived by the rivers for generations, had its eyes veiled, horns set aflame, and were driven onto the battlefield to terrify our foes... 
My master beheld these cruelties and grieved deeply. How unjust the invasion of Jixia! What crime had the innocent or the creatures of the land committed to deserve such suffering? 
And so my master took the field in mortal flesh, leading fifty puppets to halt the enemy advance. Thanks to his sacrifice, Harvest Fields were spared from war—but he himself was left gravely wounded... 
Over the following years, I remained alone in the mountains, guarding Jixia. Nature decayed and rejuvenated, and the Pearlized Tree bloomed and faded. I diligently executed my master's commands, tirelessly working day and night, faithfully fulfilling my duty...

A sub-volume of *The Saepes Compendium* by Muping, a Hunter from Jixia, covering their habits and social structures (if any).

Many view Saepes negatively, hence the "pest" in their name. As a Hunter, I find this unprofessional. After regional studies, we've gained insight into this peculiar species.

Saepes live in groups with strong territoriality, usually around powerful Saepes Colossi, accompanied by around ten smaller Saepes, forming a communal group.

Unlike Wolvines marking territory with xx, Saepes release an imperceptible substance for communication, which only Saepes can perceive. I
intend to name this mysterious substance "pheromone," as this year's research achievement to submit!

Comment (Seeker): You mean feces?
Comment: Keep quiet.

This grouping prevents conflicts over resources. I also suspect they use pheromones for daily communication, alongside body language.

Saepes Colossi are rare within a group, acting as elders with more "life experience." As noted in *The Physiological Structure of Saepes*, most Saepes become Saepes Trees at the end of their lives, returning nutrients to the soil. Other Saepes remain with them until the end. With their long lifespan, Saepes Colossi have witnessed many life cycles, perhaps accumulating deeper emotions? They seem less active, always walking slowly and thoughtfully.

When Saepes return to being Saepes Trees, they nourish new births, making death a celebration of renewal and inheritance for Saepes. If you see Saepes dancing around a tree, it's a newly returned Saepes. It's best not to disturb. Such scenes are rare and need documentation for research. If you can record it (preferably with sketches), send a copy to the Hunters' Association at Jixia Academy for academic contribution and receive compensation.

Comment: I've only seen it once or twice; Saepes really have energy, dancing for three days and nights.

Saepes convert sunlight into sugars, so they often sunbathe quietly, sometimes standing in water puddles, absorbing both water and sunlight.

Although they enjoy sunlight, Saepes are plant-derived, so they naturally fear fire. Consequently, they avoid areas where Embermane-like creatures are present.

I didn't tell them that that elderly was once a student at Jixia Academy. He was quite famous back then, not the odd, lonely old man he is now, with only me as his friend. 
He always told me not to tell anyone, fearing it might cause trouble. 
Actually, whenever I shared his amazing stories, I ended up being laughed at. 
 
The elderly told me that in his youth, just passing "the Heroes' Path" on the Jixia Mountains meant you had earned the qualification of the enrollment. People called it "Climb the mountain first, then enter the Academy." 
Later, as Jixia Academy became famous, it attracted talents from all over Primaera. Students would sail from the north and land at Baiming Harbor. This helped Springbrook Plains grow, but also made the Academy's entrance exams harder. 
Every time I failed the entrance exam and cried while watching the fireworks at Upstream Camp, I thought of the old days when "Climb the mountain, and you're in." 
"What was the Academy like before you joined?" I asked the elderly. 
"I may not have been among the first students, but I know that Master Fuzi built the Tower of Enlightenment and founded the School of Martial Arts. Later, Master Zhuangzi and Master Mozi came and founded the Schools of Sorcery and Mechcrafts. I joined the School of Martial Arts and always ranked first." 
"You're amazing!" 
"Ah, it's all in the past..." 
"Can you show me some of your skills? I want to see you break a stone on your..." 
"Ahem... That's too dangerous!" 
Unfortunately, even after I got into Jixia Academy, I never got to see his martial arts. 
"I'll find out if you were telling the truth," I joked as I packed my bag and said goodbye. 
"People go there to seek answers, why are you going to ask about an old man like me..." He seemed a bit sad, muttering to himself. 
"Stories are answers to me." 
"My story is coming to an end." 
"But I can go to Jixia Academy and find more past stories about you." 
 
Before writing this application, I realized that for me, answers are stories. Stories of the wild Springbrook Plains, the majestic Aerfall Highlands, the mysterious Oneirland, and that young and vibrant martial artist. 
So, I hope I can join the Student Affairs Committee. If rejected, I'll just write another application.
