If there's anything besides Jixia's mysterious powers and sorceries that could truly rival Navenia, it would be the cuisine. The food here is definitely the most captivating aspect of their culture! 
 
In Jixia, mastery of flame comes from two places: the classrooms of the School of Sorcery and the stoves of every Gourmet. Here, cooking is no longer just a craft; it has become a form of art. Rare ingredients from snowy peaks and the depths of the ocean are prepared using ancient oriental techniques, offering my taste buds the greatest satisfaction I've ever experienced. The various cooking methods, the choice of ingredients, and ingenious combinations... these are what I've learned the most about during my time in Jixia. If I stayed longer, I daresay I could become a proper Gourmet myself. 
 
Back home, I once thought Navenia's dishes were both refined and abundant. But after spending time here, I must admit—to borrow the words of the Orient—Navenia cuisine could barely count as a single branch of this great culinary tree, perhaps best known only for its cold plates and pastries. The oath I made before my journey now feels laughable: I swore to taste all the flavors of the Orient within a month, yet after three, I still haven't exhausted what Jixia had to offer. (You wouldn't believe how many pounds I've gained since arriving here!) Just thinking that I'll soon return to Navenia, where none of these delicacies exist, fills me with sorrow. 
 
I must apologize; perhaps in my earlier writings, penned on the road to Jixia, I was guilty of exaggeration. But now that I've seen it for myself, all those artistic flourishes have become reality. 
 
Choosing what to bring back has been no easy task; as everything here is simply too precious to part with. In the end, a wise oriental scholar offered the perfect advice. Do you remember that girl who could shatter stone with a veil of silk? Her eye for treasure is extraordinary (she must have a story of her own). She told me to take back a good supply of Aersilk and rare herbs. The silk here is finer than any I've ever touched, and the herbs are beyond compare. I can hardly wait to return home, to cook these oriental dishes for my mother, to use their healing herbs to restore her health. And next time, to bring her here, to this wondrous land.

Continuing from where we left off, Frenetic Fanglion was trapped in the Aersilk Flower Array by the heroes and geniuses of the Society. It bared its two long fangs and struggled to free itself, but only became more immobilized. 
 
The great crisis in Harvest Fields was resolved. The clouds cleared, and the warm sun shone. The Society was hailed as heroes. For the next few days, the members were treated with great hospitality by the locals, who even gave them Harvest Pancakes as a parting gift. 
 
From then on, Harvest Fields enjoyed perpetual peace and prosperity. Even the virtuosos of Jixia Academy would attend the annual Harvest Festival. Some exceptional individuals could even single-handedly subdue Frenetic Fanglion. For the last hundred years, there have been no more disturbances from the dark clouds. 
 
This satisfying tale should have come to an end, but some curious readers might say, "They enjoyed the fruit without knowing its roots." 
 
The initial thunderstorm in Harvest Fields triggered the crisis, but it vanished as suddenly as it appeared, leaving only the dark clouds. Why did that thunder disappear without a trace? 
 
Hold your breaths, dear readers, as the story unfolds. 
 
It turned out that the thunder vanished because a divine beast was protecting Harvest Fields! Even in Harvest Fields, few people have seen this divine beast—or even heard of its illustrious name. 
 
What does this divine beast look like? The books describe it as a cow with a entirely green body and the size of an elephant. It remains hidden in the wilderness, and when it does appear, it's like a small mountain rising from the ground! Why does it resemble a cow? Because this divine beast has two tall, curved horns on its forehead, exuding great strength and toughness! 
 
Don't underestimate these horns—they have the power to touch the heavens! On the day the thunderstorm struck Harvest Fields, someone saw this divine beast in a field struck by lightning, using its sharp horns to deflect the giant thunderbolts from the dark clouds! Not just one, but two Thunder Bulls appeared, pawing the ground and facing the sky, then charging forward to confront the thunderstorm! 
 
Boom! 
 
In that moment: Dark clouds choked the heavens; golden lightning shook the peaks. Yet with horns raised, the storm-bulls stood. Turning back the thunderbolts they took! 
 
Through the power of these two Thunder Bulls, the initial thunderstorm in Harvest Fields was averted! 
 
However, in the centuries since, no one has seen these two Thunder Bulls again. Over time, their heroic act has faded into a vague legend. 
 
Some say that the Thunder Bulls absorbed the powerful thunderbolts and have been carrying that burden within themselves ever since. Despite their pain, they refuse to unleash the storm upon Harvest Fields again, truly embodying the spirit of selfless saviors. 
 
But I wonder, are these guardians of Harvest Fields still present today?

The second installment of this work explores the marvels that thrive in the realm above—hawks and bats. 
 
Someone once found a stunning indigo feather and treasured it, inquiring about its origin. While carrying it near a cliff, they were attacked by hawks and barely escaped, losing the feather. It came from the Bluegale Falcon's fan-shaped crown, which gleams indigo, slicing through the sky with icy swiftness. 
 
In contrast, the Flamebearer Falcon has a scarlet crown, flowing like fire. Both species begin as Swiftbolt Falcons before diverging into adults, with theories varying on the basis of their divergence. Falcons are born masters of guerrilla warfare, striking with lightning speed once they lock onto their prey. They excel at surprise aerial assaults, often landing a single, decisive blow. Falcons wield their attributes adeptly; Flamebearer Falcons command Scorch, while Bluegale Falcons wield Quake, unleashing bursts of fire and lightning to claim victory. Apart from this, the force of their talon strikes should not be underestimated. If you find yourself within their range and lack the means to defend yourself, seek immediate cover from bushes, trees, or terrain features, or take shelter in a cave. Prioritize defense to ensure your safety. 
 
As mentioned earlier, if you plan to take refuge in a cave from falcons, be sure to investigate beforehand to ensure that the second type of monster discussed in this chapter—the bats—are not nesting within. Generally, both predators and prey find it challenging to navigate in the dark, but Moon Bats are an exception; darkness is their paradise. With their slender bodies and narrow wings, they can navigate through tight crevices with ease. Their acute hearing, combined with their swift flight, allows them to pinpoint their enemies' positions and launch precise attacks. Young Moon Bats rarely venture out of their caves unless faced with an unknown disaster. In contrast, adult Full Moon Bats are larger, with more refined wings, and they have a penchant for gathering on full moon nights, circling the moon and stirring up unusual phenomena. The full moon itself carries an air of mystery, and people often view the widespread appearance of Full Moon Bats as a bad omen. Whenever such phenomena occur, people retreat to their homes to rest and pray, partly due to the Full Moon Bats' indiscriminate attacks on humans. When encountering Moon Bats, exercise extreme caution, as disturbing one can trigger a chain reaction, drawing the entire colony into a siege.

Among the many students of Jixia Academy, I, Ruan Xiaogui, am perhaps the most ordinary. Maybe it's because I come from a distant place that I don't quite fit in with my classmates. Sometimes, when looking at those bright and lively peers, I can only silently envy them. 
 
I don't know when it started, but my classmates gradually became cold towards me, often mocking me when I tried to talk to them. 
 
"Ruan Xiaogui, you're just a country bumpkin! How dare you come to Jixia Academy?" 
 
"With students like you, our academy is losing face!" 
 
They looked at me with strange eyes, as if I were an unnecessary existence. Every time this happened, I would secretly hide in a corner of the library and cry. 
 
It was also here that I first met him. 
 
How can I describe our first encounter? It was during my most disheveled moment. After being mocked by my classmates for ruining my new school uniform, I couldn't help but quietly cry in Pastoral Garden. Senior Yango handed me a handkerchief at that moment, embroidered with his puppet emblem and carrying a faint cool scent. He didn't say a word, his pale lips tightly closed, but his slender puppet beside him spoke in a low tone: 
 
"Use it to wipe away your tears, you poor thing." 
 
Through my tangled hair, I looked at him. I had seen Senior Yango before, elegantly dressed in blue at the opening ceremony. Now, he remained just as composed, while I resembled a dirty little puppy. 
 
I bit my lip, still accepting the handkerchief and smiling at him. Before I could even express my gratitude, Senior Yango quickly left, leaving me alone, holding the handkerchief and blushing profusely. 
 
I knew that Senior Yango had simply helped a crying junior. But from that day on, I began to think about him frequently... 
 
I thought about how confidently he controlled his puppets, speaking at the opening ceremony—a self-assurance I admired deeply. I recalled the handkerchief he gave me, which I washed and kept with me, hoping to find a chance to return it. I remembered the descriptions of him as a Mechcraft genius, a puppet master... titles I could never hope to match. 
 
But these mundane days were about to end. 
 
That day, the academy organized students to form teams and explore the nearby Jixia Forehill. Although no one wanted to team up with me, I still looked forward to this journey. The scenery of the Jixia Mountains was breathtaking, as if it could wash away the pain in my heart. 
 
I skipped along, humming a tune. Though lonely, I felt content. However, fate decided to play a trick on me at my most unguarded moment. While climbing, I accidentally stepped on a loose stone, and everything before my eyes suddenly blurred. 
 
The pain turned my world black... 
 
When I opened my eyes again, I found myself lying in an unfamiliar place. A mysterious atmosphere filled the space, making me feel uneasy. I tried to stand up but realized my movements had become unusually stiff. Struggling to lift my hand, I discovered my fingers had transformed into ball-jointed puppet limbs. 
 
Panicked, I rushed to the mirror in the room and stared in shock— 
 
My body was no longer its original form; it had transformed into Senior Yango's puppet. 
 
-End of Book 1-

In the first unit of this work, let us together explore the clan of the earth, the totem of freedom – the Wolvine tribe. 
 
Have you ever heard the legend that Wolvines snatch children? Nomadic tribes in the grasslands and mountainous areas unanimously describe Wolvines as extremely terrifying, using this to intimidate children at home and make them return early. In fact, Wolvines are a highly territorial species that live in packs and have very poor eyesight, so they rarely venture far from their territory. Therefore, such legends are essentially false tales used by parents to scare children. 
 
However, it is undeniable that the Wolvine tribe has a fierce and combative nature. In the most widely circulated legend about them, two Wolvines set up an ambush for a butcher: one pretended to sleep as bait, while the other dug a hole behind him to attack. In the end, the butcher saw through the trick and survived. But in reality, encountering a Wolvine would not be so fortunate. These monsters, common in grasslands and mountains, are nocturnal, love to howl, and are extremely swift. They are covered in snow-white fur and brown scales, with sharp front claws evolved from their burrowing habits, making them experts at underground ambushes. They often appear in groups, surround their prey, and swarm in. The Wolvine's attack process consists of three stages: hiding in a hole, charging up, and pouncing. Once they knock down their prey, they first use their front claws to tear and attack, weakening the prey's counterattack, then bite the throat with sharp canine teeth, making them a highly dangerous species. Within their tribe, there is a strict hierarchy, often identifiable by the state of their tails. The alpha wolf, the leader of the pack, usually holds its tail high as a symbol of status, while the lowest-ranking Wolvines always tuck their tails between their legs, walking timidly as if with tail tucked. In my view, the organizational skills of Wolvines are exceptionally strong; their pack is absolutely united. In battle, all Wolvines act as one, advancing and retreating together. Moreover, they possess a cunning nature; often, even when seemingly outmatched, they display a degree of wisdom, using tricks to achieve their hunting goals, just as the legend tells. 
 
In daily life, be careful to identify Wolvine territory and detour around it once discovered. If you accidentally enter it or spot a Wolvine in your sight, you must be extremely vigilant, as its companions are likely lurking nearby. At the same time, never flee in panic, as the Wolvine's hunting instinct will prompt it to quickly attack moving prey. Instead, observe the surrounding terrain and use any available objects for self-protection. If there is a tree nearby, climb it immediately, because Wolvines cannot climb trees and will leave after waiting for a short while.

Both common colds and bruises can be treated by the Herb Family, but certain "difficult and miscellaneous ailments" cannot be cured by folk remedies. Out of a rigorous research attitude, this volume collects several typical case studies of illnesses and folk remedies under the premise of protecting patient privacy, all of which have been annotated with commentary and suggestions for reference only. If you have any doubts, please try them with caution. 
 
Case I: Wanting to grow taller or lose weight because of being short or getting fat from overeating in order to improve one's physique. 
Folk remedy: Rumor has it that a purple cloud mushroom growing in the forest has the effect of increasing height and losing weight, and it can be used to boil a height-increasing and weight-loss soup. 
Commentary: There is no such mushroom plant. Purple mushrooms grow in northern Jixia and only have edible value. To lose weight, one can only rely on down-to-earth exercise; if one is still young, there is also the possibility of growing taller through stretching and other sports. 
 
Case II: Those who fail every exam want to pass their exams. 
Folk remedy: Rumor has it that applying bee paste grass residue chewed by a scholar goose to the forehead can make one as smart as a scholar goose and pass exams. 
Commentary: Bee paste grass only has healing effects, and being chewed by a scholar goose will not change its pharmacological components. Diligent study is the only proper path; even a smart scholar goose needs accumulation to master knowledge. 
 
Case III: Hair loss 
Folk remedy: Rumor has it that adding crushed medical boat leaves to gugu's hair growth potion can make people's hair dense. 
Commentary: Directly crushing medical boat leaves will cause the loss of most active ingredients, and everyone's constitution cannot be generalized, let alone between humans and gugu... It is recommended to carry out reasonable washing, nursing, and maintenance of hair in daily life, while letting go of pressure and maintaining a good mindset. If it is not a congenital constitution and age issue, it will generally improve after several months. 
 
Case IV: Insomnia 
Folk remedy: Rumor has it that boiling soup with poisonous insects as medicine and drinking it can make one fall asleep on the spot. 
Commentary: Without the professional knowledge of the Zhendong School, it is not recommended to handle potentially poisonous insects on your own. Often, such toxins that make people "fall asleep on the spot" will directly paralyze the body and cause a coma, and such a radical method will cause immeasurable harm to the human body. 
Physiological insomnia can seek health preservation and recuperation from the Yixia School. If insomnia is caused by a knot in the heart, you may need to seek counseling and heart-to-heart talks from others.

常规风寒感冒和跌打外伤都可以找百草家就医，只是某些“疑难杂症”并非偏方能救，出于严谨的研究态度，本册在保护患者隐私的前提下收集了若干典型病情案例偏方，均作了批注来进行点评与建议，仅供参考，如有存疑，还请谨慎尝试。 
 
病症例一：因为长不高或者暴饮暴食吃胖了，想增高减肥来让体型变好。 
民间偏方：谣传一种生长在林间的紫云菇具有增高减肥的功效，可以用它来熬煮出增高减肥汤。 
批注：没有这种菌菇植株，颜色呈紫色的菇类生长于稷下北部，仅有食用价值。要想减肥瘦身唯有踏实锻炼；若尚且年轻，通过拉伸等运动也有长高的可能。 
 
病症例二：逢考必挂者想考试必过。 
民间偏方：谣传用学士鹅咀嚼过的蜂膏草残渣涂抹在脑门上，就可以变得和学士鹅一样聪明来过考试。 
批注：蜂膏草仅有疗伤效用，经过学士鹅咀嚼并不会改变它的药理成分。唯有勤学苦读是正途，聪明的学士鹅也需要积累才能掌握知识。 
 
病症例三：脱发 
民间偏方：谣传用碾碎的医舟叶加入到咕呱的生发药水，就可以让人的头发变得茂密。 
批注：医舟叶直接碾碎会流失大部分有效成分，且人与人的体质都不能一概而论，何况是人与咕呱……建议在日常里就对头发进行合理的洗护与保养，同时放下压力，保持良好的心态，如果不是天生体质与年龄问题，一般情况下都会在数月后好转起来。 
 
病症例四：失眠 
民间偏方：谣传用毒虫入药熬汤喝下，可以当场睡着。 
批注：若没有鸩冬派的专业知识，不建议擅自处理潜在有毒的虫类。往往这类让人“当场睡着”的毒素会直接让人麻痹造成昏迷，如此激进的方式会对人体造成不可估量的危害。 
生理上的失眠可以寻求益夏派的养生疗养，若因心结而失眠，那可能需要寻求他人疏导谈心。

Back in Alsahraa, I heard whispers of a mysterious figure known as "Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade."

In Alsahraa, numerous vagabonds claimed to be disciples of "the Lone Blade," but they all ended up losing their teeth after facing me.

Roaring Tiger Training Hall.
"I will verify personally whether the rumored 'Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade' is fact or fiction."
"Am I not tiger-like enough?"
Head Trainer Tigon burst into laughter upon hearing my declaration.
His thunderous chuckle shook the air.
When I first met Head Trainer Tigon, I was struck by his rare appearance—white base coat with black stripes, broad forehead, and high eyebrows. His tiger head resembled a boulder perched atop a towering physique, with thick limbs like tree trunks, even more imposing than the tales described. As he approached, the ground seemed to tremble beneath my feet...
Little did I know that his name "Tigon" actually came from being a rare white tiger half-breed!

I must admit, seeing him made my heart race.
Though my blade skills might match his, martial arts duels often come down to a single decisive move.
If I sparred with this mountain of a man, I wasn't sure if I could withstand his full strength before hitting the ground.
Just as I hesitated, Tigon declared, "I have never turned down a challenge!"
With that, I steeled myself for the duel.
As I unsheathed my curved blade, Tigon's eyes lit up—is this the unspoken bond between fellow blade enthusiasts?
I chose not to attack first. Given our size difference, my offensive would likely be swiftly neutralized.
Instead, I planned to use my agility to lure him into making the first move. After all, my primary goal was to witness the legendary warrior's skill.
Tigon's swordplay was fierce and powerful, each strike difficult to evade. When my curved blade clashed with his sharp edge, sparks erupted from the metal collision.
After several rounds, I began to tire, feeling pain in my jaws, my steps slowing, and my defensive speed noticeably decreasing.
Tigon's swordsmanship was exceptional, his blade seemingly imbued with life. He and his weapon were connected, each movement and breath synchronized in perfect rhythm.
Before my eyes unfolded a living legend.
I once heard that though Navenian blade practitioners are scarce, similar techniques have been developed there. Did Tigon inspire Navenia's warriors, or was it the other way around?

The outcome of this duel was already decided, but adhering to the spirit of martial arts, I fought until the end.
I lost.
Despite the gap in power, I saw how much effort Tigon put into defeating me.
Tigon earned his nickname "the Lone Blade" because few can withstand even a single strike from him. To have exchanged blows multiple times was an honor in itself, regardless of defeat.
After the match, Tigon generously praised my blade skills and invited me to return for another sparring session—or better yet, stay on as one of his disciples.
Although I deeply appreciated his recognition and admired his martial prowess, the vast lands of Jixia beckoned, filled with countless warriors waiting to be encountered.
Seeing my resolve, Tigon recommended another training hall in Jixia—Obsidian Flame Training Hall.
What new sights awaited me this time?

After class today, a student from the School of Sorcery invited me to join his newly formed "Saepes Purgesquad" to help nearby villagers drive away the troublesome Saepes. \nI'm responsible for recording our operations and we have two teammates from the School of Mechcrafts and one from the School of Martial Arts. \nWhen we encountered the Saepes, the team quickly set up a Mechcraft trap and was ready to activate them with Sorcery. But the Martial Arts student provoked too many Saepes and we had to hide into our own trap.
Sharing a camp makes us family. Family doesn't fight, and everyone's happy. \n \nMeeting here makes us buddies. Hand in hand, we'll make lots of money!

Jihu Barley: 16 crates. 
Inkspar: 12 tons. 
Fish Fruit: 4 crates. 
Clawshooter Fruit: 15 bags.
Someone at the camp was bragging about digging for treasure near the Stargazing Terrace. You guys hear? We’ll tail them from a distance—once they’ve got the goods, we’ll hit them with a surprise.

After being dragged to this underground realm by the Rebels, I was depressed for a few days, but I also discovered some peculiar minerals never seen in Jixia. 
 
Initially, I mistook this blue ore for Aerux fragments, but after those Rebels accidentally placed it near a campfire and triggered a large fire, I realized it was actually a strange mineral generated underground, completely different in nature from Aerux. 
 
Now, I have gained the trust of the Rebels and can move around in a limited area. 
 
Through extensive research, it appears that a group of people once mined the purple minerals here on a large scale. From the notes they left, it seems they called this mineral "Volcanic Stone." 
 
These people, who lived hundreds of years ago, even made many weapons and items using Volcanic Stone as material. Some of them are still usable today. 
 
Next, I need to collect more Volcanic Stones. Once I gather enough, I'll definitely prepare a big surprise for these Rebels!

There are indeed treasures here, but your mission remains unchanged. 
 
The primary objective is still the Stargazing Terrace. After excavating the ancient observatory, you may proceed as you see fit. 
 
Any treasures you unearth are yours to keep—I won't interfere. 
 
But remember, your mission must be completed first. If anyone acts recklessly and disrupts the plan, don't expect me to show any mercy.
What is this place? It's feathered cloak on the ground. The stone ahead might conceal a Dream Rift. But how can I open it? I'm getting too weak to get back to Dreamless Cliff.
When exploring, be cautious. Never risk your life on a whim.

Aspire to create the ultimate culinary masterpiece? 
Ready to share your passion with the world? 
 
Join the Gourmet Society! 
With diverse ingredients and challenging techniques, 
you'll savor a feast for your hands, taste buds, and soul! 
 
The heat is on!
Violent winds rise, and the earth cracks for hundreds of feet. My friends will never return. This item is hidden within a secret chamber, left for those who come after.

Left: Wondrous Maze. Animals may appear along the road, but they are gentle and do not pose a threat. \n \nRight: Stargazing Terrace. Those heading to the trial site should exercise caution and avoid harming animals.

The Jade Heart contains the Jade Pivot, an ancient demonic creation that requires sealing and research.\nDo not enter without permission; <span color="#07AAFFFF">only with immense strength</> can it be opened.

How long have I been here? The sea of lights blooms and fades, flickering out only to rise again... It feels as though ages have passed, yet somehow it is just as it was when I first arrived. To shape a dream is no simple whim. And when the moment comes... when I finally become a butterfly... what visions shall unfold before my eyes then? What fine dream awaits me in that flight?

Construction Manual II 
 
Requester: Mozi 
Equipment Status: The tower body is intact, but the attack core was forcibly removed, and the Mechcraft components are severely damaged and need to be rebuilt. 
Improvement Plan: Increase the thickness of the Treasure Tower's outer shell and, as instructed by Fuzi, eliminate the modular design. 
 
Construction Personnel Comments: 
 
Site Manager's Comments: 
Fuzi personally instructed to remove the modular design. Please construct according to the design drawings provided by Fuzi.

The Circulatory System and Acupoints of the Human Body: A medical text available at the Herb Garden. 
"An Introduction to the Five Elements": A beginner's guide to the Five Elements and their cycles of generation and restraint. 
"Journal Astrologica": A guide to constellations and celestial calendars, available at the Stargazing Terrace. 
"A Stroll in Dreamscape": Just listen carefully in class and take good notes, you don't need to buy my book. 
"Sorcery Rune Diagrams": A reference book on how to create sorcery runes. The fifth revised edition was compiled with help from Senior Kongming.
It appears to be used as an altar before. There's a ring-shaped socket on it.
The Senior is in secluded training. Please come back another day.

Routine maintenance: all normal. 
 
Routine maintenance: all normal. 
 
Routine maintenance: some parts were worn and replaced. 
 
Routine maintenance: all normal. 
 
Routine maintenance: strange noises reported during elevator use, resolved after part replacement. 
 
Routine maintenance: all normal. I'm so used to this job now that I can think about other things while I work. 
 
Routine maintenance: all normal. I've shared many of my design ideas with my master, but he just tells me to focus on the task at hand without commenting on my plans. Is this what frustration feels like?
Rusted weapon fragments scattered about still show traces of battle.

(A few notes on ingredients and cooking methods are recorded here.) 
 
The dishes at Come-true Restaurant are far too rough in both presentation and preparation. They simply cook the ingredients through, then add seasoning, nothing more. 
 
Most of their dishes rely on simple techniques like frying, boiling, or steaming; quick, efficient methods that also help mask the flaws in the ingredients themselves. 
 
Still, their prices are remarkably low, which draws in plenty of students. High volume and small profit; it's the perfect strategy for them. 
 
Watching those kids eat so happily... I suppose giving up my chance to go to Chang'an and staying here as a cook at this inn wasn't such a bad choice after all.

After fitting the Mech Core, Prototype V operated for a while before executing its second command. Thankfully, its weapons module wasn't installed, or my invention might have...



Next, I'll follow the backup plan and find some lower-quality or cheaper replacement parts. Hopefully, they won't cause too many issues.

A reward is offered for the capture of three Rebel leaders: 
 
<69D0FF>Youjie</>, seen in the northwestern mountains of Iridescent Basin. He has been raiding Mechcraft parts. 
 
<69D0FF>Weichan</>, seen in the southern ruins of Iridescent Basin. He is known for crafting strange Mechanoids from scraps. 
 
<69D0FF>Sichu</>, last seen in the eastern canyon. Beware of her strange fragrance. 
 
These Rebels have stolen my family heirlooms! Return them to me, and you will be rewarded generously. 
 
I await brave souls at Horizon Retreat, east of the basin. 
 
Zhaochou, Owner of Horizon Retreat

There are plenty of clocks in Jixia—just like those stubborn people—that need fixing, but I'm done! 
 
Owner Shi Yu has let all of us apprentices go. We regret to inform you that Yongsheng Clock Shop will be closed indefinitely starting today. 
 
We are truly grateful for your support over the years. We hope you will continue to treasure every moment, just as you cherished each unique clock we made for you. 
 
Thank you for your understanding.

The Rebels' firepower was overwhelming, and several of us were injured. We had no choice but to retreat to the underground river in the Shattered Land... There, we encountered a remarkable creature with a round head and pink skin. Miraculously, the slime on their bodies could heal wounds. Fortunately, these creatures have shown no hostility towards us, and the team is safe for now.

This supplement to the Saepes Compendium, authored by the Hunter, Mu Ping, contains some unsettling content. Thanks to the Seekers' Association for deciphering the ancient texts. 
Below are two ancient scrolls found by a Seeker named Xu Wei at the old battlefield ruins outside Seclusion City. They have been translated and transcribed for my review. The content regarding the attitude one side held toward Saepes during the wars is truly horrifying. 
First Scroll 
Squad Leader, 
Listen closely, for I will not repeat myself. I learned from your troops that two days ago, you encountered a group of "Tree Monsters" while patrolling outside the camp but let them get away! 
Animals that can outrun our vanguard soldiers? This land is indeed full of amazing things. Allow me to teach you a basic principle of Sorcery: All beings possess inherent qualities in their flesh, which can be extracted using our arcane knowledge. These "Tree Monsters" you saw, bursting with vigor, could be processed to create potent energy potions. With them, our soldiers could move faster and fight for days without rest. 
As punishment, you are demoted to infantry. In tomorrow's assault, you'll join the first charge. 
Centurion ███ (Signature damaged) 
Second Scroll 
Day 15 
Though barely more intelligent than animals, the local Tree Monsters hold great potential—as containers for souls. Once we extract the life from their husks, they can house the soul of an adult human and follow orders obediently. With this discovery, we can rapidly bolster our front-line forces by using these mindless forms as expendable units to drain the enemy's strength. 
We haven't yet begun tests on the larger Tree Monsters, as they are too tough to capture with ease. Still, my theory holds that the husks of these larger entities could contain souls far more robust than those of ordinary humans, or perhaps even multiple souls. Should practical tests prove successful, we could create an unstoppable puppet army that doesn't require sleep or sustenance. 
Experiments must proceed without delay. I need a large Tree Monster within three days. Should have kept those professional hunters alive had we learned about it sooner. 
Deputy Commander ███ (Signature unreadable) 
The origins of the ancient scroll authors are unknown, but their evil intent is unmistakable. The Seekers have confirmed that these ancient people have long disappeared, leaving only ruins behind. I hope they never return. 
But even today, many unscrupulous individuals still covet the Saepes. Below is a transcription of a letter I found near Labyrinth Cave: 
Guys, 
Listen, we won't get a good price for this batch right now. The docks are heavily guarded and the buyers are scared. We need to stash them well and wait until things cool down. 
Don't panic, though, for I'm not the type to run off with the loot. But to be honest, I don't fully trust you either. So, for peace of mind, here's my plan: 
We'll stash everything at Hasong's place, in a chest with four locks. Each of us gets a key. When it's safe, we'll meet at his house, fetch the goods, and split the money fairly. Sounds good? 
De Winter 
Note: Definite evidence of a Saepes smuggling ring. Based on the signature, the leader is from Navenia. To avoid alerting them, I didn't take the note but made a copy instead. I must pass this information to the teachers at the Academy to help catch these criminals.

Oars dance with waves; swords swirl like a storm. Drums crack like thunder, shaking the world. \n<span color="#07AAFFFF">Ka-ka-dong!</> \nThis rhythm can be played on the large drum somewhere.

Name: Hypnotic Pillow 
 
Type: Sorcery Creation; silk; embroidered with a Sorcery circle. 
 
Location: Reported by the School of Sorcery. 
 
Appearance: A square-shaped medicinal pillow with intricate silver embroidery. 
 
Function: Possesses ▇▇ and hypnotic effects. 
 
Side Effect: The Sorcery circle has a strong adhesive effect and will corrode and dissolve any creature it adheres to. 
 
Suggestion: Use only as a last resort and most unsafe baiting method; ensure strong willpower and sufficient rest when maintaining or using this item.

During long journeys or emergencies, food shortages are frequently encountered. This volume will detail how to obtain enough food in the wild and how to cook it. 
 
First, Starting a Fire 
Fire is an essential element for wilderness survival. When adventuring in the wild, carry flints or various fire-starting mechanisms with you. If you don't carry them, you can also search for natural fire sources, such as plants like Oil Immortals or Blazing Fruits. 
Once you have a fire source, you need to gather some dry sawdust, cloth strips, and other flammable materials. Be careful not to put down too much or apply force too suddenly, otherwise it will lead to failure in starting the fire. Gradually add firewood only after the flames grow strong, and build a campfire or wooden rack. 
 
Second, Obtaining Food 
Direct gathering: There are some fruits in nature that can be eaten directly, such as Splitwood Fruit, Rabbit-Ear Fruit, and Sleepy Fruit. There are also those that cannot be eaten directly, such as Snailmeat Mushrooms, Thick-Cap Mushrooms, and various wild eggs. 
Hunting: All rivers in Jixia are rich in fish, which can be caught using fishing rods. There are also some small creatures that can be hunted, such as rabbits and foxes. Try not to provoke large animals. 
 
Third, Cooking 
Pay attention to hygiene when handling ingredients, and keep raw and cooked ingredients separate. It is best to wash fruits and vegetables, and remove the internal organs of animals before cooking. 
There are many cooking methods. Threading ingredients onto tree branches and roasting them on a grill is the simplest method. You can also pan-fry them on heat-conducting ores such as Copper-Veined Stone or Dark Steel Stone. Of course, if you are carrying containers like pots and bowls, you can also boil the ingredients. 
Note: Choose fresh and hygienic ingredients, and consume them only after thoroughly cooking. Eat immediately after cooking and finish as soon as possible.

在进行长时间旅途或遇险时常会遇到食物不足的情况，本册将详细介绍如何在野外获取足够的食物，如何烹饪食物。 
 
一、引火 
火乃是野外生存必不可少之物，在野外冒险时要随身携带火石或者各种打火机关。如果没有携带也可以寻找自然火源，如比如油仙客、滚焰果等植物。 
当有了火源之后，便需要采集一些干燥的木屑、布条等易燃物，注意，千万不要放得太多或者用力过猛，否则会导致引火的失败。在火苗旺盛之后再逐渐添加柴火，搭建火堆、木架。 
 
二、获取食物 
直接采集：自然中有一些可以直接食用的果子，如：裂木果、兔耳果、眠食果等。还有不可直接食用的，如螺肉菇、厚顶菇等菌类，以及野外的各种蛋类。 
狩取：稷下的各条河流之中都有着丰富的鱼类，可以用钓竿钓取各种鱼类。还有一些小型生物可以狩猎，如兔子、狐狸。尽量不要去招惹大型的动物。 
 
三、进行烹饪 
处理食材的时候要注意卫生，生熟食材要分开。且蔬果最好要洗净，动物要去掉内脏进行烹饪。 
烹饪方法就有很多了。将食材穿进树枝放在烤架上烤制，这是最简单的办法。也可以在铜纹石、暗钢石等传热好的矿石上进行煎制。当然，如果携带了锅、碗一类的容器也可以将食材煮熟。 
注意：选择新鲜卫生的食材，充分煮熟后食用。烹饪后立即食用，尽快吃完。

The results look good, but it still needs more calming ingredients. 
 
"As the toxin weakens, unwanted reactions are getting worse. The new ingredients are clashing." 
 
"Should I consider the detox methods Toxineers usually use?" 
 
... 
 
A small note at the bottom reads: "Reduce leftover substances to avoid raising suspicion."
I'll reach the end of Dreamless Cliff if I enter this Oneiric Gorge again. What waits for me inside?

I've been tracking signs of a mysterious trace for the past few days and finally caught sight of its owner. But what are they? They resemble lizards with leaf-shaped tails. The smaller one was playing in the forest energetically, while the larger one watched it silently from a distance, possibly protecting it.
Some mechanical cannons and parts are neatly stacked on the ground, all having lost their luster.
A Mechcraft that can record and play back sound. It is a bit old but has clearly been well-maintained.
Some newly displayed local snacks haven't officially gone on sale yet, so they're not available for tasting at the moment.
Ordinary people will never know that within the ancient Dreamscape lies immense power.

Franche, \n \nMy dear child, how have you been in Jixia, so far away from home? Everyone here still misses the cheerful days when you were with us. We heard you've been helping the merchants with cargo transport, but why didn't you return with the caravan? The Chamber of Commerce never mentioned that you'd be staying in Jixia for good. Your little nephew, the one who adores you most, often waits for you at the docks. Please come back and see him sometime. We all miss you dearly.
Legend says the Bone Chime answer the wishes of the heart. This dust-covered chime points <69D0FF>due north</>.
Legend says the Bone Chime answer the wishes of the heart. This dust-covered chime points <69D0FF>due north</>.

I never expected the Saepes to bring me a fish. How in the world did they learn to fish?! 
 
 
 
And to think there are swimming fish inside Aerux Skywell as well... I suppose the waters here really do connect to the outside world. 
 
 
 
Once I recover, I must study this properly. 
 
 
 
But first things first: grilled fish for dinner! Ha! It may not compare to the chefs back in Aerux Town, but right now, this rough little grilled fish tastes like a feast. 
 
 
 
...Though I have to admit, my head was still spinning, so I forgot to take out the innards. No wonder it tastes bitter.

I am determined to go to the forbidden land and perish with it. 
If you are following military orders to aid, please return swiftly. 
The situation has escalated beyond earlier expectations. With slim hopes, I retract my request for aid. 
Regards.

This appears to be an ancient beacon tower used to monitor the coastline. It was believed that once a beacon was lit, all others would soon follow, signaling the approach of enemies. \nNow, only one ruined beacon tower remains. Nothing lasts forever, indeed...
I know your cheap tricks! I'll expose you both as swindlers! Just wait and see!
The drill needs power from Volcanic Stones to start digging.

December 7th 
 
 
 
We rallied our forces to surprise the students. I wonder how shocked those students will be when they see us appear out of nowhere. Heheh. 
 
Before we set out, someone said he saw suspicious figures, but I wasn't concerned. 
 
 
 
December 8th 
 
 
 
As expected, the students were not very vigilant, and we infiltrated easily and encountered minimal resistance. 
 
I noticed some strange shadows. I thought those were our own people. 
 
 
 
December 9th 
 
 
 
Those cunning students set a trap! 
 
As soon as we entered the room, the statues transformed into Mechanoids—clearly the work of the School of Mechcrafts. 
 
The cramped space disadvantaged us, and as we tried to retreat, Sorcery students blocked the exit while Martial Arts students ambushed us from hidden tunnels. 
 
Day 4 
 
We returned to camp at dawn, battered but all accounted for. 
 
This defeat is a lesson. When we return with a larger force, it'll be your turn to face defeat. 
 
Jixia Academy, just you wait!

Name: Luminara Grass 
Appearance: A luminous plant shaped like a goblet, exuding an air of luxury. 
Rumors: Occasionally sighted on the Jixia Plains, this glowing plant carries a faint metallic sheen and resembles a lamp cup. It’s said that certain Mechanoids are drawn to it, gathering around to stare in silence at night. (Source: Intelligence Society) 
Habitat: Found mainly in plains and hilly regions, more common in the south. 
Research Notes: Pending verification on whether it can be used to lure Mechanoids.

First, be friendly with small animals. Any use of Ice Sorcery on them will be punished. Note! Someone has already been penalized for freezing a frog without authorization.

Second, casting spells to create ice blocks at will causes huge hidden dangers; no one is allowed to act recklessly.

Third, people often pass by outside the hall; do not cast sorcery at will to cause trouble for others.

Fourth, if not necessary, stay away from the dream area.

This volume introduces the various Societies of Jixia and answers the question of how many Societies there are in total. 
 
According to the author's list of popular topics, the most frequently asked question about the Societies is: "How many Societies are there?" Instead of dwelling on this question, let us first discuss the well-known Societies that exist today. 
 
Herbalists: 
Healing hearts with medicine, helping people with herbs. 
Herbalists are dedicated to finding hundreds of herbs to cure hundreds of diseases. They often travel between the countryside and mountains of Jixia, searching for plants and animals with medicinal value. 
They have kind hearts and wish for a world without sickness, earning them a good reputation among the people. The Jixia people believe that those who look kind and reliable are usually Herbalists. 
However, as the number of Herbalists grows and branches into different factions, it's inevitable that some impostors will appear. Be cautious when encountering strange medicines being sold. 
A friend of the author once fell victim to such a scam, buying a bottle of intelligence-boosting medicine before an exam, only to discover after the exam that they had been deceived. 
 
Gourmets: 
Savoring flavors in cooking, seeking beauty in abundance. 
With an iron wok and spatula, Gourmets devote their lives to satisfying the taste buds of every family in Jixia. 
If you see someone carrying various seasonings, they are likely a Gourmet, able to whip up delicious food at a moment's notice when inspiration strikes. 
Those who can create aromatic dishes have fiery tempers; they are short-tempered and quick to anger. Although they humbly accept feedback from diners, they never tolerate food waste—unless someone wants to experience the power of their spatula. 
 
Anglers: 
Sitting by the water, watching fish swim. 
Anglers know Jixia's fish like the back of their hand. They often sit by lakes all day, finding peace of mind during fishing—a key part of their training method. 
What interests people most about Anglers, aside from their unmatched patience, is their ways of eating fish. In fact, even Gourmets might concede defeat when it comes to the variety of fish-eating methods employed by Anglers. 
Since angling skills vary, some Anglers are often mistaken for stones by lake shores. 
 
Hunters: 
Crouching in the wilderness, making their saddle their home. 
Hunters are the group that understands animals the best in Jixia. They are innocent and curious like children, but also passionate and enthusiastic like teenagers. They come and go like the wind, working energetically and curiously, but can also crouch silently in the bushes for three days and nights to observe a red falcon. 
Hunters' passion for animals rivals that of Gourmets, but their goals are completely different, leading to occasional confusion between the two groups. 
However, apart from Hunters, no one would wear strange costumes and blend into animal herds to live alongside them. 
 
Crafters: 
Preparing materials for use, creating tools that achieve results. 
Crafters have the most skilled hands. They are responsible for Mechcraft transportation, manufacturing, construction, and other aspects, deeply influencing every aspect of life in Jixia. 
People may think Crafters often look dirty because they value simple living, not fancy clothes or food. They prefer to savor plain meals and focus more energy on building things. 
Their aesthetic of simplicity is reflected in their Mechcrafts. Crafters pursue the principles of practicality, simplicity, and durability, making life easier for households across Jixia. 
Don't dismiss Crafters based on their plain appearance, or you might find yourself homeless—they not only excel at building structures but also at tearing them down.

When exploring the wilderness, one often finds oneself in an awkward situation: missing a tool that suddenly becomes essential. In such cases, it's best to rely on your own hands. This section introduces a few simple yet practical methods for crafting tools in the field. 
 
Rope: Use a sharp blade to peel the bark from a tree, extracting the tough inner fibers. Dry them in sunlight, then twist and rub them into a cord. Alternatively, gather climbing vines, strip away the soft tissue, and braid the remaining fibers together. Once finished, stretch the rope to test its durability and strength. 
 
Fishing Rod: Find a straight, sturdy branch to serve as your rod. Sharpen one end into a hook using a knife or a sharp stone. Tie a thin cord made from bark fiber or woven grass to the hook, then fasten a thicker cord to the base of the rod. Thread worms or bait onto the hook, and tie a small branch or length of rope at the thicker end to serve as a handle. Check that the hook and float are secure before fishing in nearby rivers or lakes. 
 
Simple Trap: Build a cage-shaped frame from sticks, covering the top with leaves and leaving a small side opening as an entrance. Place food bait inside to lure small animals. You can also dig a pitfall trap concealed with branches and soil to catch larger prey that wanders over it. 
 
Improvised Water Filter: When the only water source looks unclean, craft a makeshift filter pouch. Roll leaves into a cone to form the shell, then fill it with layers of coarse sand, small pebbles, and clean grass or wood ash at the top. Pour water slowly into the top; it will filter through the layers and emerge clearer at the bottom for collection and use. 
 
Mosquito-Repelling Sachet: Gather Bitterword Grass and Green Elder Herb, dry and grind them, then pack the mixture into a small cloth pouch and tie it tightly. In summer, it works as an excellent natural insect repellent, and its fragrance is pleasantly refreshing.

A fine wine may be found now and then, but old friends are hard to come by. 
 
The old man's face was slightly red, but he showed no sign of fatigue. "Two more jugs!" he called out. 
 
"Coming right up! These are the last two jugs of the year. If you still can't decide a winner, it'll be a draw." The shopkeeper retrieved the last two jugs from the cellar, stepping over the empty jugs scattered on the floor, and set them on the table. 
 
At this point, the wine taster, "Huzi," finally spoke up: "No more... I can't drink anymore. You can have my title as Master Wine Taster..." He hadn't even finished speaking before he collapsed. 
 
The shopkeeper raised the old man's hand, which was unusually broad and powerful. "The winner is Fuzi!" The crowd cheered, surrounded by the sea of empty jugs. The shopkeeper lamented, "But you've drunk all the prizes I prepared." Fuzi waved his hand: "No matter, no matter. These last two jugs are enough." Then, he picked up the last two jugs, one in each arm, and strode away. In the empty cups, the only thing left was the payment.

Day after day, I stayed by Senior Yango's side, watching him create and interact with others. 
 
I began to notice every detail about him. Each gesture and word he spoke touched my heart. I realized my feelings for him had grown beyond admiration into deep dependence. 
 
But neither the puppet nor the weak, timid person I once was deserved to be beside him. I tried to hide my emotions, enduring the pain alone. 
 
Yet others noticed my secret. 
 
"You're just a flawed puppet. How dare you love our creator?" 
 
"Give up your fantasy. Puppets don't deserve emotions." 
 
"You must be broken. Tell Senior Yango to scrap you." 
 
Their scorn increased my pain, making me question my existence. 
 
When I felt my lowest, Senior Yango suddenly became cold, no longer controlling me with his usual gentleness. He distanced himself without explanation, treating me like a stranger. 
 
I didn't know what happened. I could only retreat, overwhelmed by sadness. 
 
Later, another puppet revealed the truth. Senior Yango had heard from others that I wanted freedom. He was saddened and chose to ignore me. 
 
Even though puppets can't cry, why did my eyes burn? I never wanted to leave him; I just longed for his attention. I knew our status differed, and my feelings were doomed to silence. Yet even as a puppet, I wasn't allowed to enjoy his kindness in peace. 
 
Now, I've lost the courage to face him. I've decided to leave him and this painful place to find my own freedom. 
 
Once I made my decision, I started planning my escape. Every third day of the month, Senior would leave for his secret chamber to study puppetry. If I could evade the other puppets on that day, I could leave undetected. 
 
Sometimes, I still observe Senior Yango quietly. He remains elegant and composed, charming in every way. However, none of this concerns me anymore. 
 
The day I left, everything went as planned, almost too easily. But just before I stepped out, I heard familiar footsteps. 
 
It was... Senior. 
 
I turned, and his eyes were as profound and distant as ever. I knew the distance between us could never be bridged. His lips moved as if to speak, but I had already turned away, running toward the moonlight. 
 
The moonlight illuminated my face and surely saw my tears. Senior, when we meet again, what will we be like? Is my hopeless love just a grain of sand in your sea of feelings? I don't know, but it seems I'm still expecting to see you again.

Dawnsong's vanguard has been stirring outside the Dragonshade Pass for days, testing our lines, waiting for an opening. 
 
Zi Min, one of our most promising Dragonriders, and Zhu Di, an elder dragon long seasoned by war, were assigned to the Dragonshade Pass. 
 
The ambush came fast. Dawnsong troops surged forward. Zi Min took blow after blow, barely managing to stay in the saddle. Zhu Di was wounded as well, wings torn, scales split, but he pushed through the enemy regardless. He shielded Zi Min with his own body, broke the encirclement, and carried him back inside the pass. 
 
Zhu Di died the next dawn. Zi Min has yet to wake.

That question set off a storm of voices across the land. Some argued that "the people live on food"—revival must begin with ending hunger. Others believed medicine was the key—healing disease and warding off disaster. Still others insisted that joy mattered most—that true revival would come only when the people found delight again. 
 
When no agreement could be reached, Fuzi set down the Academy's very first rule: anyone may claim resources and gather students, but they must prove their vision through action. And so it began. Those who championed food became the Gourmets. Those who turned to medicine formed the Herbalists. Those who prized joy above all gave rise to the Musicians. From this, the Societies took shape. 
 
Even now, each Society thrives in its own way. As for Fuzi's question—perhaps no single answer exists. Or perhaps the answer has already been found in the flourishing of the Societies themselves.

The Moonelia Sprout, a massive, dangerous plant, has always been considered forbidden by the Herb Society. Its poison is extraordinarily potent; even the slightest contact can bring death. I crept toward its growth site. The sprout loomed before me, vast and tangled, like a beast waiting to devour any life that dared approach. With trembling hands, I used tweezers to pluck a single tender shoot. At once, faint poisonous vapor seeped from the vial's mouth, and the air grew heavy. Content: Record of the Mechcraft Dismantling Practice Course 
 
Editor's Note: It is not always a good thing that some Mechcraft parts can still function after dismantling and reassembling. 
 
The Academy's teachers have always encouraged us to engage in more hands-on practice. As students of Mechcrafts, we have been working closely with the masters who manage the parts since our first day at the academy, forming lasting relationships in the field. Recently, a new batch of students entered the School of Mechcrafts, and it was our responsibility as seniors to guide them on their journey of discovery in the field of Mechcrafts. 
 
As I led these young students to move the Mechcrafts and parts into the experimentation field, I paid close attention to their expressions. Among them were introverted students with timid eyes, but most of them had curiosity and excitement sparkling in their eyes. I knew they were waiting for my command, so I waved my hand, just as my seniors did years ago. 
 
"Let the dismantling begin!" 
 
As expected, the room gradually filled with chattering discussions. The students looked astonished by the Mechcrafts before them, while my fellow guides and I exchanged amused glances. We didn't rush them until a bold girl stepped forward and took a Mechcraft Dice, sparking the room like a fire in the wilderness. 
 
"Dismantle at will!" This was a concise yet powerful lesson that Master Mozi had instilled in us over the years. Knowledge can indeed be learned from books, and experience can certainly be sought from predecessors, but these theoretical concepts are ultimately stagnant without practical engagement. Without touching the grooves of the parts and feeling the subtle yet precise leverage between mortise, tenon, and lever, all learning would remain mere theory. 
 
This practice session ended amidst chaos. The ultimate goal of this class was to restore the dismantled Mechcrafts; even those who barely managed to piece together a semblance of the original form were few and far between. That bold girl remained the standout performer, with her restored dice functioning nearly flawlessly and transforming shapes as smoothly as before. Strangely, though, she ended up with extra parts after reassembly, which she seemed to regard merely as unintentional simplifications rather than major issues. No matter, as they progress further in their studies, they will naturally come to understand the underlying principles.

While organizing stories in Jiebei, I met a traveler at a teahouse. He was wandering around looking for traces of past wars. I treated him to a meal and asked him to share his story.

He said it all began with a tale he had heard from his elders:

"A long time ago, an army suddenly attacked my hometown, burning, killing, and plundering."

As he ate, he slowly continued, "Everyone was frightened and despairing. Suddenly, many tall soldiers descended from the sky, like heroes from myths, and quickly defeated the enemy, saving everyone."

"These tall soldiers left as swiftly as they came and were never seen again. My elders remained grateful and hoped to see their saviors once more."

He took a sip of water and continued, "After hearing this legend, I decided to find these legendary tall soldiers."

Over the years, I wandered throughout Jixia. In Springbrook Plains, I saw giant bronze limbs scattered across the plain. Excited, I thought I had finally found them, but closer inspection revealed discrepancies from the elders' descriptions. Reluctantly, I continued my journey.

Later I headed to the mountainous regions of Jixia, drawn by rumors of numerous ruins. Unexpectedly, I encountered many ferocious beasts there."

At this point, he raised his hands, vividly describing the scene.

"Truthfully, I once faced a pack of Wolvines. They chased me relentlessly; I fought back, kicking one down while punching another, but their numbers overwhelmed me. I spent a night hiding in a tree."

"After searching the mountain ruins fruitlessly, just as I was about to give up, the heavens smiled on the determined. In a cave, I discovered a colossal, nameless bronze statue—majestic and perfectly matching the elders' descriptions.

Tears welled up instantly—a surge of indescribable emotion: joy, gratitude, relief... that profound clarity when truth unveils itself. I straightened my clothes, knelt, and bowed deeply in reverence. Thank you for protecting my kin, for making this quest worthwhile.

I meticulously cleaned the statue; we cannot let our benefactor's likeness be shrouded in dust. I resolved to bring this news to my elders, fulfilling their long-held wish. If possible, I'll bring them here to witness it, though I wonder if their health permits..."

Setting down his chopsticks, he said, "Speaking of which, I should depart without delay."

"No rush," I replied with a smile. "Finish your meal first. There's still plenty here."

He shook his head. "Thank you for your hospitality—we'll talk another day. I must complete my task first."

With that, he rose, bid me farewell, and resumed his journey. Yes, like me, his travels had yet to reach their end.

At last, everything was ready. After a long, dusty journey, we arrived at our destination, stretched our limbs, and prepared for a good day's work. But as I stood on the shore, gazing at the long, uneven edge of clear water before me, a question arose: where's the best place to fish—where should I cast my line? It's a fine question, and a complex one. Allow me to explain briefly from the perspectives of season, time, and terrain. 
 
As the saying goes, "In spring, fish the shallows; in summer, fish the depths; in autumn, fish the shade; in winter, fish the warmth." Spring calls for the shallows, when the weather begins to warm and fish gather near the banks to spawn. In summer, head for deeper waters—the heat drives fish downward, and they linger in the cool depths. Autumn is for shaded spots, when fish feed actively, often near aquatic plants, fallen leaves, or shady trees where food is plentiful. In winter, seek warmer waters, such as sheltered coves or areas bathed in sunlight. 
 
Another old rule says, "Fish the shallows at dawn and dusk, the depths at noon." Morning and evening are quiet, and fish often swim close to shore—sometimes even the big ones. By midday, changes in light and temperature push them back into deeper water, so that's where you'll want to cast your line. 
 
Terrain matters, too. Places thick with vegetation are ideal—fish like to gather in gaps between reeds or near patches of natural grass. If you find a small depression along the riverbank where the water flows against the main current, congratulations: you've found a backwater cove. The swirling current there collects debris and food, drawing plenty of fish. And finally, there are the old fishing spots—places worn smooth by years of use. They usually offer a wide view, little undergrowth, and a simple bottom terrain. And since people have been fishing there for so long, it's a fair sign the spot itself is a good one.

I'm glad to be at Upstream Camp, a place I've heard much about. Today, I'll give a brief introduction to the music theory of the Music Society for those interested in music.                
First off, this isn't some esoteric science; music theory is present in every corner of our world with melodies.    
So, what are the Do, Re, Mi, Sol, and La? Simply put, they represent the traditional five musical tones. They're just like the five languages of music, each with its unique flavor and feeling                    
Do is the foundation, steady and solid. Re is bright, like autumn. Mi is soft, akin to spring. Sol is passionate, like summer. La is light and airy, like winter's snowflakes.                          
These five tones can be combined to create endless music, much like how five spices can produce a variety of delicious dishes.                          
You might think, "Oh, this is basic music theory," and you'd be right!                          
But this basic theory forms the elegant compositions of the Music Society. It carries our history, wisdom, and emotions.                          
The Music Society's music theory is actually quite straightforward, rooted in a keen observation of life and deep emotional experience. Every note and chord holds profound emotion and thought. Music theory isn't isolated; it's closely connected to our lives.                          
As I experience here at the Darkpool Camp, music and nature are intertwined. The flow of water, the sound of the wind, and birdsong — all are nature's music.                          
The original Music Society used music theory to interpret and imitate these natural sounds. They expressed reverence and gratitude for nature through music and used nature's power to enrich their compositions. This perspective still influences us today.                          
Legend has it that a Musician with exceptional hearing once listened by the waterfall at Darkpool Camp for hundreds of dawns and dusks. After the seasons passed, he composed an eternal masterpiece using the five tones in just one day.                          
Though the five tones are the basics of sound, the emotions they can convey are profound. These simple tones can encapsulate the Music Society's thoughts, experiences, and even more.                          
So next time you hear a beautiful piece of music, take a moment to appreciate it. From these same five tones, you might discern the countless emotions and thoughts of the Music Society.                          
For the Music Society, music theory is also about heritage and promotion. They use it not only to create music but also to teach disciples and pass on their skills. Through practice and exploration, disciples gradually master the secrets of notes and the soul of music.                          
In conclusion, music theory isn't mysterious; it's embedded in our lives and emotions. With heartfelt engagement, we can all become both listeners and creators of music.

One day, feeling weary, I stopped to enjoy the warm sunlight and beautiful scenery in Springbrook Plains.

Before I knew it, I had leaned against an ancient tree and fallen asleep.

Suddenly, I was awakened by a melodious bird song. The sunlight was too bright, so I squinted and caught a glimpse of a stunning figure.

The figure soared through the sky like a red cloud, resembling a peony blooming in the clouds.

This chance encounter began my connection with Head Trainer Maple.

I learned that the red figure was a Red Falcon, one of the famous divine beasts in Jixia and Maple's beloved pet.

Maple used the feathers shed by the Red Falcon to make special arrows. It is said that these arrows were only used when Maple faced an opponent worthy of her full effort.

I decided to visit the Red Falcon Training Hall, hoping to become a worthy opponent for Maple.

Maple was initially hesitant to spar with me, a newcomer, and only agreed to an archery match. She explained that her combat skills were focused on practicality and might not be beneficial for me.

I had no choice but to present the introduction letter, requesting her to accept a full spar.

After reading the letter, she no longer hesitated.

Before the spar, Maple asked me to try drawing her bow.

With all my strength, I managed to pull the bowstring, but my fingers were left numb. At this point, Maple finally put aside her concerns and took the spar seriously.

I had thought that in a match against an archer, distance would be crucial.

Even if my opponent was a skilled archer, as long as I could close the distance, I would easily gain the upper hand.

However, Maple proved to be no ordinary archer.

At the start of the spar, Maple, as I had expected, kept her distance. Then, she drew her bow and released her arrows, which came at me as swiftly as lightning.

Although the arrows were fast, they lacked power, and I easily blocked several of them with my knife. I adjusted my footing, seized the opportunity to counterattack, performed a somersault, and landed directly in front of her.

But just as I was about to end the spar with a flourish, Maple drew out an arrow unlike any I had ever seen, as thick as a spear.

The arrow came straight at my face.

I quickly blocked it, but the impact was so great that the knife slapped back onto my face.

With that, I fainted, and the spar came to an end.

When I came to, Maple told me that these skills were all tricks of the border military.

It turned out that the border military archers used different arrows for different distances. For long range, they used light arrows, swift and unexpected. For close range, they used heavy arrows, with great force, directly striking the vital points. When facing enemies in heavy armor, the border military would often use light arrows to lure them forward, then switch to heavy arrows for close-range attacks.

I had fallen for this very tactic.

Fortunately, Maple had used practice arrows, which, although powerful, would not cause serious injury. If she had used real arrows, I fear my chances of survival would have been slim.

From the moment I left the Red Falcon Training Hall, the cold sweat on my back never faded.

Although I had not witnessed the Red Falcon arrows in action, I still gained a great deal. After I explained the purpose of my journey, Maple laughed and showed me some of the arrows she had recently made.

Each arrow was exquisitely crafted, sharp yet aesthetically pleasing, much like Maple herself.

Finally, Maple gave me a wooden Red Falcon pendant she had made as a keepsake of my journey.

Author: Xingyan, Graduate of the School of Sorcery 
 
 
 
Summary: An introduction to Telepathic Threads and their uses. 
 
 
 
Aersilk, known for its ability to resonate with and channel the energies of nature, is an exceptional Sorcery medium and is widely used in the Academy, with its most important application being "Telepathic Threads". Finely woven and intricately detailed, Telepathic Threads conduct energy and can be used to project it outward. 
 
 
 
The primary purpose of Telepathic Threads is to assist students in channeling energy before they have fully mastered energy flow and corresponding Sorcery Circles. These threads are attached to specific energy points along the body's main energy channel and aid in spell casting and practice. As students become stronger, these threads are gradually removed, as Headmaster Zhuangzi once said: "The threads help you better understand the art of Sorcery and reveal the patterns of the world. But remember, they are still just a tangible tool. Telepathic Threads merely serve as a conduit for energy within the body, and while they are useful, they are ultimately man-made. You must transcend their limitations and move from understanding Sorcery to fully mastering it—establishing a direct connection between your body and the outside world without the need for an external medium. 
 
 
 
Telepathic Threads can also be used for communication and competition. For example, two people connected by these threads can sense each other's emotions and some of each other's internal energy. These threads also play a role in duels known as "Telepathic Duels". During these duels, the participants hold opposite ends of a thread, and as they cast spells, the energy flows along the thread, creating vibrant colors that collide and form stunning, intricate patterns. 
 
 
 
As someone who's been through it all, here's a little advice: be careful with Telepathic Threads. They only become strong when they are attached to your energy points, but when they are detached from your body, they are quite fragile. Always handle them with care when disassembling or storing them. Trust me, you don't want to repeat my mistakes... 
 
 
 
Editor's note: A practical and informative article. (And for the last time, no, I do not use Telepathic Threads to control my Bubble Fish. It doesn't like that. We have a friendly, mutual, and supportive covenantal relationship.)

"Talks by Candlelight" focuses on renowned Cannoneers, featuring an interview with a different Cannoneer in each issue. Through these candid conversations, we reveal the secrets behind their research and share the stories behind the scenes, bringing readers closer to the heart of these individuals with warm and engaging writing. 
 
 
When we arrived at the agreed-upon terrace, the familiar and striking figure in red was nowhere to be seen. The lively atmosphere of Ember Garden was as bustling as ever, with the sounds of firing pins and hissing steam filling the air, mingling with the sharp scent of gunpowder, creating an overwhelming sensory experience. 
 
 
Many can't endure this kind of life. Grease stains often find their way onto cuffs and scarves, and the meticulously arranged outfits from the morning inevitably end up in the wash by evening, requiring at least three rounds of rinsing to restore their original colors. The chaotic air is another challenge; seasoned Cannoneers have mastered the art of breathing just right to avoid choking on the dust that newcomers often struggle with. After enduring the dual trials of cannons and their environment, those who remain inevitably develop unique quirks and temperaments. It seems that those who choose to live alongside fire eventually become it themselves. 
 
 
When those hands playfully landed on my shoulder, I wasn't surprised, yet I still let out a small yelp, drawing friendly laughter from my companion and the prankster. The newcomer apologized for the scare while setting down three drinks for us. As the wooden cups were passed around, slices of Phantom Dewcap Grass danced in the clear water, leaving a trail of playful bubbles. 
 
 
"Sorry! Two kids called me to help with some equipment, so I got held up," Blazen said as he pulled out a chair and sat down, immediately grabbing his cup and taking a hearty drink. I took the opportunity to glance at the name tag pressed against the bottom of my cup, and after confirming it had my companion's name on it, I discreetly returned it and quickly picked up the correct one. 
 
 
The boisterous man before us is none other than the beloved Blazen, a teacher at the School of Mechcrafts. According to the students, Blazen never acts like a typical teacher. He sports a youthful hairstyle, pays no mind to age differences, and plays alongside them without a care. But if there's one thing that causes trouble, it's probably his slightly flawed vision. 
 
 
As a scholar dealing with cannon Mechcrafts, one would naturally expect him to have exceptional eyesight, necessary for working with precision components. That's the general assumption about Cannoneers. However, Blazen chooses to ignore such rumors, neither hiding his visual impairment nor giving up his study of cannons. He has carved out his own space in the field. 
 
 
It's hard to say whether Blazen cares much about his eyesight. We only know that he rarely explains the cause. Some speculate it's a congenital condition, while others think it's an injury sustained while saving someone. But the real answer remains obscured by the smoke of battle, hidden from view. 
 
 
After some small talk, we broached the question that had piqued everyone's curiosity. As expected, he waved it off, signaling that he didn't want too much attention on the subject. However, through bits and pieces of his words, we managed to piece together a plausible story. 
 
 
Just like every ripe fruit once had its green days, Blazen was once a spirited youth. During his time at the Academy, his fiery heart burned bright, refusing to settle into a mundane life under the heat. As his ambition grew, one day, a burst of vibrant color shot from the muzzle, and sharp fragments grazed the skin around his eye. 
 
 
When the topic of his younger days came up again, Blazen instinctively brushed over the scar near his eye. "I know some people, after their own failures, can't stand to see others succeed. Instead of offering congratulations, they harbor resentment," he spoke lightly of emotions long buried. Outside, in the garden, groups of students were shouting, seemingly preparing for some grand performance. "But what's the point of that? I chose the path of pursuing the power of firearms, so I won't complain. Protecting them as they continue to explore this path, celebrating and seeing them off with fireworks, isn't that a joyful and proud thing to do?" 
 
 
As his words trailed off, a thunderous boom echoed beside us. We all turned to look, and there in the students' hands, stars and bouquets of firelight blossomed. The sky darkened, and the brilliant flames burst forth, blending with the evening glow on the horizon, illuminating the joyful figures of children rushing in from all directions. At that moment, I seemed to understand why Blazen chose this location for our interview and what lay behind his carefree smile that has kept him going all these years.

Editor's Note: Food and medicine alike nourish martial strength. Students of the Herb Society are encouraged to apply! 
 
 
 
Respected Headmaster of the School of Martial Arts, 
 
 
 
Thank you for taking the time to read my letter and for giving a young man devoted to the study of food therapy and martial arts a chance to reach out with hope. 
 
 
 
My name is Yu Dazhi. Since childhood, I have studied under Healer Gu Shansong of the Herb Society. I currently work in the Herb Garden, gathering herbs and conducting pharmacological analysis. I was honored to receive a nomination in the Herb Society's annual evaluation at Jixia Academy, making me a prospective Herbalist. 
 
I am well-versed in the properties of herbs and skilled in applying their principles to create nourishing dishes and tonics. After years of study, I have developed a special herbal cuisine that significantly benefits martial arts training. The Art of Martial Cuisine—currently serialized in Issue 530 of the Jixia Daily, Martial Studies section. 
 
I believe martial arts should draw upon the spirit of heaven and earth—motion and stillness in balance, nurturing both body and mind, strengthening muscles and bones, balancing qi and blood, and using herbs as a nutrient source to achieve a higher level of enlightenment. 
 
 
 
I have also devoted much of my work to studying the spiritual nature of herbs. 
 
Once, while collecting on the Aerfall Highlands, I slipped from a cliff and barely survived by clinging to a tree. As I caught my breath, I noticed a small gray-blue flower blooming defiantly from a crack in the rock—Canine Poria, one of the rarest plants on the continent. 
 
It is known as the chosen flower of martial artists due to its remarkable effects in strengthening the dantian and revitalizing inner energy. 
 
The dantian is the reservoir of one's essence. Therefore, martial arts place great emphasis on it, regarding it as "the root of life." Canine Poria, however, is highly potent and extremely bitter, and few can harness it to create something both safe and palatable.

The grandeur she had once admired seemed almost ordinary amidst the wonders of the world. Beyond the bridge lay Yun'gen Town, a bustling merchant hub built around a massive cloud root, surrounded by dense forests, towering mountains, and vast deserts—a true haven.

A merchant traveled with them, and at the town gate, she saw even more merchants dressed in various attire.

"Let's start with Baihui Market!" the merchant suggested. "Yun'gen Town is an important trading hub for Jixia. As I mentioned on our way here, nearly every region in Jixia works closely with Jixia Academy. This place is the heart of Jixia's trade with other parts of the continent. Students here have developed thriving businesses in commerce, tourism, and especially handicrafts."

"Handicrafts? Please tell me more," Li Jinchai asked, intrigued, as this was her area of expertise.

"The unique cloud-silk products make local handicrafts extremely popular—they're durable, lightweight, and beautifully crafted. Paper and pottery made from cloud-silk are highly valued across the continent, so many merchants come here to purchase goods. However..." The merchant glanced around cautiously before continuing in a low voice, "Public order can sometimes be a concern."

Li Jinchai, who grew up within Chang'an's city walls, couldn't yet grasp what that meant.

Li Jinchai quickly explored Yun'gen Town. She met the material suppliers—the Cloud-Silk Harvesters and Hunters—and saw where raw materials were processed into products—at the Shuyun Paper Workshop and Taoyun Pottery Studio. She also saw those responsible for logistics—the Mist Mountain Bulls—and those who sold goods—the Baihui Market and Jiebei Trading Post.

During her visit, she realized that Chang'an had given her a special gift—marveling at its bustling prosperity, where noise and dust filled the air.

She invested half of the funds from selling her Chang'an shop in several rolls of cloud-silk and some accessories. Combining these materials with her years of experience since she was eight, she created her first products in her room at the Yun'gen Inn. Within just a few days, they sold out at four times the price she had expected!

But good fortune never comes easily.

"Hand over your earnings for the day!" A large man wielding a massive hammer, accompanied by several rough-looking individuals, demanded this for the third time that week. The first time, Li Jinchai was frightened and handed over all her money. The second time, she hid some, and they didn't notice, making her wonder if they weren't very smart. So this time, she only gave them a third of her earnings.

One of their companions remarked, "Boss, did you notice she's been giving us less each time? Does she look down on us outsiders..." Before he could finish, a green figure leaped from the side, kicking him so hard that he flew to the ground with a clear footprint on his face.

"Thank you for your help," Li Jinchai said.

"No problem!" The person turned around. This was the most polite greeting they had ever exchanged.

"It's you!" They exclaimed in unison.

Indeed, Hua Changhui's parents had eventually mortgaged their shop and spent everything on mechanical models. Disheartened, Hua Changhui sold all their stock and became a caravan guard with the Honglu Temple, traveling across the continent.

"Let's stay here and do business together!" Encountering an old acquaintance while abroad prompted Li Jinchai to persuade Hua Changhui to stay, and she too wanted to further her martial arts studies in Jixia. From then on, they began their long-term partnership. Those outsiders, actually just poor souls from elsewhere, became their first employees after witnessing Hua Changhui's martial skills and Li Jinchai's craftsmanship.

Li Jinchai's products gained attention among Jixia students and, due to their incorporation of cloud-silk craftsmanship, were bulk-purchased by wandering merchants. The names Li Jinchai and Hua Changhui became synonymous with fashion and quality here.
