The Day Before Entering the Cave 
Years ago, someone asked me why I wanted to become an Herbalist. 
"Maybe it's because I like the scent of flowers and grass," I said. 
Today, for that same fondness, I've come to an unfamiliar forest with a friend, hoping to find the legendary flower said to grant its discoverer the ability to understand the speech of all animals. 
If we could really find it, we'd make our names known across Jixia. 
Before setting out, my friend warned me that the legend sounded suspicious, that maybe this so-called "understanding of animals" was nothing but hallucinations from poisoning. I didn't take it to heart... 
 
Day One in the Cave 
We found a narrow, hidden cave. The entrance was too smooth, almost unnatural. Someone must have dug it. 
That could only mean one thing: there was something inside worth hiding. 
Sure enough, the tunnels wound and split like a spider's web, but we marked our path with colored ribbons, no challenge for us. 
I can hardly describe it... the sight of that flower, the color, the radiance, at once I was certain this was it, the fabled bloom that let one hear the voices of beasts. 
We transplanted it carefully into a travel pot and prepared to head home immediately. 
 
Day Two in the Cave 
It must be our third day since leaving home. We've run out of fuel; no torches, no light. The cave is pitch black. 
I can't tell time anymore, so I just call one sleep a "day." 
We seem to be lost. Our own ribbons are everywhere. My limbs are weak, perhaps from eating nothing but dry rations for three days straight. 
 
Day Three in the Cave 
Fear and endless darkness drove us to make the worst decision possible; we split up to search for an exit. 
As expected, I lost my way completely. Every tunnel looks the same. 
I shouted his name, but only my own echo answered back. 
My vision blurs... the air feels too thin... I can hardly breathe. 
 
Day Four in the Cave 
I regret everything. 
That flower was poisonous after all. My curiosity blinded me to reason, made me ignore my friend's warning. 
Now I only wish he were here, alive, beside me. Maybe he made it out? 
 
Day Five in the Cave 
When despair had drained the last of my strength, I leaned against the rock wall... and heard a faint tapping sound. 
Was it him? Was he trapped in the next chamber? 
I tried to speak to him, but only the tapping replied. 
Could it be he's lost his voice? 
 
Day Six in the Cave 
Desperate, I followed the sound through the twisting dark. I don't know how long I walked, but when sunlight finally struck my eyes, it hurt; it was so bright I thought it must be a dream. 
My friend was shouting my name from the cave's mouth. 
He wasn't beside me all along. 
"Why are you here?" I asked. 
He pointed back toward the cave. I looked and saw a cluster of furred figures, huddled in the dim light. 
"What are they...?" 
"Ask the Hunting Society, they'll know. I'm just glad you're safe. I was about to call for a rescue team... Here, drink this." 
"Wait." 
"Hmm?" 
"Who made this medicine?" 
"They did. They healed me just yesterday." 
I never saw their faces clearly, only the backs of their heads, round and covered in fur. 
"Leave the hat for them."

Editor's Note: In the ancient and prosperous land of Jixia, music flows like a never-ending river, gathering notes and melodies from all directions and forming various distinctive musical genres and styles. This book records a lecture by Mo Li from the Kongmou Family at Jixia Academy, where he explores the different musical genres and styles of Jixia with everyone on the Enlightenment Plaza.

The main content of Master Mo Li's lecture is as follows.

Greetings to everyone at the Enlightenment Plaza. I am honored to be invited by Master Zhuangzi. Today, I would like to introduce you to musical genres and styles.

Musical genres are like a large family with many different branches, often divided by the creator's hometown and occupation. Each genre has its unique characteristics and
styles, differing in melody, rhythm, harmony, and more. While styles can be understood as different forms of expression within the same genre.

In addition to the divisions by hometown and occupation we mentioned earlier, musical genres and styles are also influenced by region. Different regions have their own unique musical styles, closely related to local culture, history, environment, and other factors.

For example, the music played by students and villagers in Springbrook Plains is often full of vitality and liveliness, closely related to the natural scenery and way of life in Springbrook Plains. Meanwhile, the music born in Aerfall Highlands is
quiet, beautiful, solemn, and dignified, echoing the magnificent landscape and inner world of the people in Aerfall Highlands.

Additionally, regional musical styles also incorporate elements of the local environment. For instance, the musicians of Dreamweave Plains compose mostly pastoral idylls, with themes mainly praising nature. This is because Dreamweave Plains is a vast region with beautiful natural scenery, where students live in harmony with farmers and nature. On the other hand, the musical style of Aerux Town is closely connected to the local market life, blending worldly flavors with exchange from all over the world.

The vendors' cries at the Enlightenment Plaza could also be considered a unique musical genre if they were turned into tunes. Try listening carefully; the pitches are either high and soaring or gentle and melodious, adding rhythm to the bustling market life here. Through their calling tunes, the vendors not only attract business but also convey their love for life. Their tunes are rarely formally taught, often improvised, and rich in personality. Sometimes light and bouncing, sometimes deep and touching. The Kongmou Family records such tunes as well; do not belittle these minor works. Any evolution of musical genres, like a witness to history, tells the story of changing times and flourishing market life.

Whether it is music rich in emotion and atmosphere, or music that emphasizes rhythm and dynamism, or music that focuses on form and technique, each has its unique charm and appeal. By understanding different styles, we can better recognize the diversity of musical genres and also better feel the wonderful experiences and spiritual shocks that music brings us.

Musical genres and styles are essential components of music, and region is one of the key factors influencing them. By understanding the musical styles of different regions, we can better comprehend and appreciate the content and charm of a song, getting closer to the creative background of the Kongmou Family.

Editor's Note: As Master Mo Li lectured, every corner of Jixia overflows with music of different styles. Some are passionate and fiery; some are warm and delicate; some are elegant and timeless; others are innovative and dazzling. These genres and styles, not only distinctive but also closely tied to Jixia's history, culture, and natural environment, collectively form the unique charm of Jixia's music.

Deep within this cave, I found what seems to be relics left by those who came before, and even a stone stele! What luck! There might be a new discovery waiting to be made. \nHowever, the path leading to the stele is blocked by what appears to be a solid stone gate. No, on closer inspection, it's likely not natural at all, but something crafted by human hands. If I want to investigate further, I'll have to find a way to open it first.

I don't know how long I've been trapped here, losing track of day and night. I'm at my limit. My body is getting colder, and the only feathered cloak here, seemingly left behind by Dreamslayer, tempts me, but I dare not wear it...

To Master:

When you were at Cloud Mirror Lake the other day, you asked me a few things about maintaining a fishing rod. I thought about it for a long time afterward, so I just came down here and cast a few lines myself. If you want to catch big fish near this cape, fishing gear is important, but experience is what matters more. The currents under this sea are complex and the coral is dense. Without an experienced angler, a novice will find it hard to get a bite. As for my catch today, I'll leave it in this basket as a gift for you. It's not much, but please accept it!

Angler, Tang Yingliu.

P.S.: I'm not good with words and didn't mean to imply you don't know how to fish. Please forgive me. Let's cast a line together when you have time.

Today, I helped a merchant from Navenia move his luggage. It was literally dozens of cases. 
 
So, I embarked on a tough portering task. His cases were as heavy as lead, and he repeatedly warned me not to damage them. I had to handle them with great care. Initially, I thought about moving several cases at once, but I soon realized that moving two at a time was my limit. I just didn't have the strength.

During the war, three ordinary men who failed the original Enlightenment Trials—were assigned to a logistics squad. In the Bastion Fort, they witnessed firsthand the overwhelming power of the Mechanoids commanded by the Sanctified. Slowly, they grew restless, no longer content to remain mere foot soldiers. \nOne of them, Y'chen, took inspiration from the Sanctified Mechcraft and devised a device for transferring energy. But after a disastrous accident, the companions were scattered, the army destroyed, and Y'chen left his treasure hidden within the Bastion Fort. It is said that whoever gathers the three relics may unlock the energy pillar deep beneath the fort—and claim the true treasure within.

Day 10 
 
When I returned to the camp, I found Rebels rampaging through the place. They seemed very arrogant, but as soon as they saw me, they immediately became timid and ran away. 
 
These rats must have come for the Frostmane Spike Bear. 
 
I figured that since I was already here, I might as well leave with something. So, I confiscated their weapons, although I don't think much of them.

Alive or dead, I will find you! 
 
 
 
Yet with my strength alone, I fear I shall never reopen the great gate of the Underhall... 
 
 
 
Perhaps by borrowing the hands of Jixia Academy's students, I may yet achieve my purpose...
You take a large gulp—the liquid sears your throat. The world spins, darkness closes in, and you collapse into unconsciousness.

For now, rebuilding the tower takes precedence; all other trivialities can wait

Ever since we got separated from the main crew, it's been over a week that we've been wasting our time in this godforsaken place. We've been hiding from those Bronze Mechanoids, and from those nosy students from Jixia, too. So far, we haven't found any real treasure—just a bunch of worthless junk. 
 
I'm starting to think we got conned by that mysterious guy. He was so secretive, mumbling about <span color="#07AAFFFF">"activating the Mechcrafts in the three ruins"</> and <span color="#07AAFFFF">"the light cascade will illuminate your path"</>... 
 
And what really freaks me out is that I saw a stone pillar lying on the ground. It wasn't until I got closer that I realized it was a statue. The cross-section showed huge, neatly clawed marks that made my skin crawl! Judging by the size and depth of the marks, they couldn't have been left by any ordinary beast. If the owner of those claws is still in the Underhall... I don't even want to think about it! 
 
What bad luck! I only followed the boss down here to make a quick buck—I don't want to lose my life in this awful place!

This was my first time entering the Dreamrealm. Though Master Zhuangzi had often suggested I seek the answers myself in my dreams, I still didn't dare to face them. 
 
 
 
But this dream was too strange, like a dagger piercing my heart. I couldn't ask for help. 
 
 
 
Well, this time, these three happened to be by my side. I hope they can help me again when the nightmare haunts me. 
 
 
 
But unexpectedly, soon after entering the Dreamy Grotto, the shadows grew thicker, and a voice began to rise. 
 
 
 
Only I could hear the murmurs hidden in the smoke. The sound grew louder, and fear made my legs tremble. The other three simply walked away, minding their own business... 
 
 
 
I did my best to chase after them, following the direction they had taken, but I couldn't find them and ended up wandering around the cave. 
 
 
 
When I reached the deepest part of the Dreamy Grotto, I saw a lonely figure sitting on a rock, her arms around her knees. When she heard my footsteps, she lifted her head. Her clear eyes made my heart skip a beat. 
 
 
 
She was the legendary Dream Weaver... 
 
 
 
She seemed a bit surprised, staring at me. Then her gaze softened, even with a touch of... pity? 
 
 
 
I wanted to ask her about the nightmares haunting me, but I realized I couldn't speak. 
 
 
 
She stood up slowly, gently stretching her wings. Then she said, "Dreamer, the one who can unravel the dream's karma is right beside you. But this truth is too cruel for you now. Oh, how I wish the nights in Jixia were an endless dream that you'd never wake from... But when the dream ends, it will all vanish like morning dew at sunrise..." 
 
 
 
"Please... forgive me..." 
 
 
 
The faint glow of the cave fell on her wings, reminding me of the solitary moon in the Wei Jun sky. A childhood lullaby echoed in my ears, and my consciousness drifted away... 
 
 
 
When I opened my eyes again, I saw the familiar faces of the same three people. Though I didn't know why Kongming's clothes were soaked, Zhou Yu's hair seemed singed, and Yango looked unusually happy... 
 
 
 
A peaceful sleep, long overdue. Unfortunately, I still didn't find the answers behind the nightmares.

From intelligence experts who keep Jixia's secrets flowing, to Secrets Club editors chasing down rumors, there's a place for you among us. Join in, and you'll have plenty of chances to match wits—riddles, strategy games, battles of the mind. It's all part of the fun. 
 
 
 
I'll look forward to meeting you here.

A few days ago, my brothers and I secretly followed Wuyan and witnessed a incredible showdown! 
 
Our three former bosses crumbled one after another under her giant hammer—some even faked injuries to extort compensation before her hammer even landed. Ugh, guess we backed the wrong leaders back then. 
 
I hereby declare: Wuyan is our true leader, the one and only Big Sis! 
 
When she defeated everyone and hauled off a mountain of loot, we couldn't help but marvel: Now that's a Big Sis! 
 
(Of course, we made sure to stay quiet—or she'd have flattened us too.) But hey, there's hope! Someday, she'll notice us loyal followers, and when she does… we'll finally make it big!

Confidential: 
 
Brother, your skills are exceptional and your courage is immense, and you are adept at securing transit. The previous batches of Jixia firearms have all been received in full, and they possess impressive prestige. We will surely step up our research and drills to make good use of them, living up to your divine capability to steal the heavens and swap the sun. 
 
Knowing that you have been operating covertly in foreign lands for several years, enduring hardships to accomplish your mission, you are truly a role model for us all. Perhaps the only way to escape war is to distance oneself from people. 
 
At least that's what the people of Hermitage believe, up until today. 
 
Whether it's due to my efforts or just sheer luck, a friend told me that if I wished to learn about the past wars, Hermitage would be a good place to visit. 
 
True to its name, Hermitage is nestled in tranquil hills and clear waters, isolated from the world. If not for the friend who had spoken in advance to the villagers, I might have struggled to integrate into the community. 
 
The villagers are warm and genuine, yet cautious. I've been living here for several months and still haven't learned a single thing about the war. The few elderly men in the ancient village hall, as well as the young folk by the pond, all seem to know nothing about it. 
 
But all the signs point to this not being an ordinary Jixia village. 
 
In the village workshops, the blacksmith's forging and quenching techniques were rare; the fabric woven by the weavers was embroidered with ancient patterns unique to the region; and there was a strange old man in the training field who displayed incredible strength. 
 
Time passed, and just as I was beginning to accept that I might leave with no answers, I saw something unusual: a child was running back and forth, carrying a solid grinding stone. His mother scolded him for his mischief. 
 
I saw this as a chance. 
 
The next day, when the boy's mother wasn't around, I struck up a conversation with him. He told me that some of the villagers were exceptionally strong, and some could harness great Sorcery energies. He said their ancestors had been heroes, and when the war ended, they returned here. 
 
"What war was that?" I asked him. 
 
"I'm not sure..." the boy scratched his head. 
 
"Are all the villagers like you? Different from others?" 
 
"Sort of. But the strongest is Grandpa Red Brow from our village. Have you seen the big hole in the mountain? He used his Sorcery to burn a hole in the stone—his whole body was on fire!" 
 
The boy pointed to a large circular hole in a nearby rock. 
 
"Have you met Grandpa Red Brow?" I asked. 
 
"No, but he has. Mom told me he used to fish with Grandpa Red Brow," the boy replied, pointing to an elderly man sitting by the water with a fishing rod. The man's hair and beard were gray, but he had a lively spirit. 
 
"Excuse me, have you ever met Grandpa Red Brow?" 
 
I asked, sensing the man might know something. 
 
"Well, many people come and go in this village; at my age, I can't remember them all. And even if I do, it's hard to say what's real anymore." 
 
As he spoke, his wrist flicked in a subtle motion, and a large blue fish leapt from the water and landed directly into his hand. 
 
"Go to a warm place," he said, releasing the fish back into the water. The fish flicked its tail and swam away, disappearing beneath the surface. 
 
"Winter's coming..." 
 
He muttered to himself.

Next, let's move on to the second part: fly-fishing versus pole-fishing—the greatest divide among Anglers. 
 
 
 
Why call it the greatest divide? We'll hold that thought for now and start with a quick overview of the two methods. 
 
 
 
Fly-fishing uses a rod with a reel and artificial lures. The angler casts the lure far out; when a fish bites, a bell or other signal device on the rod may ring—though some anglers rely only on feel or the movement of the line. The reel is then cranked to draw the fish in, and a net is used to catch it. Fly-fishing works best in wide waters like lakes or the sea, where weeds and obstacles are few and the depths are greater. 
 
 
 
Pole-fishing, on the other hand, uses a hand rod with a float and live bait. It's simpler: bait the hook, cast into the water, and watch the float. If it jerks, sinks, or skims quickly across the surface, a fish has likely taken the bait. Then raise the rod—gently, without too much force—and lift the fish out. Pole-fishing is best for smaller waters, such as riverbanks and ponds. 
 
 
 
These are the two main fishing styles, and naturally the biggest divide among anglers. But the real reason is the endless debate over which is superior. Over time, "fly-fishers" and "pole-fishers" became two camps, bickering without end. 
 
 
 
In my humble view, the quarrel is laughable. Neither side has leaders or structure; it's all talk. In fact, most anglers are skilled at both. The dispute is nothing more than a way to elevate oneself by belittling others. But fishing techniques carry no rank or hierarchy. A true angler chooses the right method for the setting—or simply follows the heart and fishes as they please. As the saying goes: "No matter the method, the one who catches the fish is master, and the one at ease finds joy."

Hey, if you're reading this book, you're probably as passionate about angling as I am, so we might get along well. Anglers are the most serene people in Jixia. They spend most of their time patiently waiting for a catch, savoring the feeling of blending into the environment. Absorbed in this feeling, Anglers often contemplate life like a philosopher with an angling rod in hand. 
 
Angling is an activity that helps you experience the present moment and enter a state of mindfulness. Only when you sync with the breaths around you and the water's ripple can you truly understand the underwater world. At that point, locating a fish feels as natural and comfortable as discovering a part of yourself. Immersed in this serene state amidst a noisy world brings immense pleasure, and catching a fish or a rare aquatic creature at that moment is a bonus—though it's even better if it's larger or rarer. 
 
To avoid misunderstandings, let me clarify: often, fish are merely an accessory in this state of oblivion to self and surroundings; their presence or absence isn't crucial. Some Anglers, while exploring the ultimate meaning of life, can become obsessed, reaching a state of mania. I know of one Angler who, in the middle of the night, ran through the streets carrying a fish as big as an adult, banging on every door and shouting to invite people to go fishing. This caused quite a stir, and eventually, he was subdued, and a Gourmet was called to... um, quickly handle the fish. Remember, this man was only suffering from hysteria, not from the joy of catching a big fish. 
 
Do remember, don't share your midnight fishing exploits with those who aren't into it, or they might eat your fish and not even leave you a bite of soup. Don't ask me how I know.

Author: Linqiu, a Sorcery student

Today in class, I suddenly remembered the story of Li Dapo. My father used to tell it often, and it was quite amusing. Li Dapo wasn't his real name, but I couldn't remember what it was. He had a limp and was the eldest in his family, so everyone called him Li Dapo.

Interestingly, no one could figure out what Li Dapo actually did. During farming season, he worked in the fields. On idle evenings, he'd sometimes set up a small stage by the roadside and perform storytelling. In the summer, he'd sell ice pops from a cart or carrying a pole. In the cold winter, he'd set up a stall outside his home, selling hot noodles and wonton. Essentially, Li Dapo seemed capable of anything and did them all well, yet he had a troublesome son who kept him busy all his life.

Once, my father attended a banquet and encountered Li Dapo resting after kitchen work. He remarked, "I never knew you could cook!" Li Dapo pointed to the pot beside him and chuckled, "What's so hard about this? I'm like this wok—whatever ingredients you give me, I have to put them in. It's just what I do."

After Headmaster Zhuangzi's lecture today, Li Dapo came to mind. I never understood how he could be so versatile, but I think I do now. Li Dapo's success lies in finding the "Dao" in his trades. Similarly, when learning sorcery, though spells vary and formations differ, we should focus on the underlying principles. As Headmaster Zhuangzi explained, "All things are interconnected, and these connections are constantly changing. Only by uncovering their patterns can we truly understand their essence and see beyond their surface-level differences."

"Once, there was even a monarch who sought to employ me for this gift. But I had no wish to become a ceremonial ox, wrapped in brocade and placed on an altar." 
 
"Fortunately, here in Jixia, I can continue dreaming freely, without constraint." 
 
"In one dream, I became a great Peng and soared high above the sky. From there, I saw worlds rise and fall upon a sea of stars, tiny as grains of sand. They appeared, shone with dazzling brilliance, and vanished in an instant." 
 
"I also dreamed a very long dream, of an age long past, filled with astonishing sights: towers piercing the heavens, countless in number; horseless carriages racing through the streets; iron birds with broad wings roaring overhead." 
 
"Ah, you ask whether living in dreams brings me joy?" 
 
"Life has its limits, but dreams have none."

March 6, Awakening of Insects. 
Another day of light rain. The Herbal Brewery was unbearably noisy with today’s exchange demonstrations, so I had to climb onto the roof of Shennong Hall Hall just to catch my breath. 
Professor Tong Bo seemed to notice something in me. He only nodded, as if afraid to disturb my thoughts, and asked nothing more. 
Three years ago, on this very day, Mother suddenly fell ill. She passed before we could find help in time. 
I cried for two days at home. When Father finally returned, he looked at me, but said nothing. After Mother’s funeral, all he said was: “The mountain is full of herbs. You should spend more time with your books.” 
I knew he was really blaming himself for being away, yet when he looked at me, I could tell he blamed me too. And perhaps he was right. If I had read more, if I had known how to treat her—even a little—maybe she could have held on until Father came back. Maybe she would still be alive. 
Now I’ve joined the Herb Society, healing the sick wherever I can. But no matter how many I save, I cannot bring Mother back. 
And Herb Garden is so quiet. Too quiet. That silence always reminds me of those two days at home—when her voice was gone, and the house was filled with a suffocating stillness. 
Even now, the memory of it presses on my chest, until I can hardly breathe.

During my journey, I often imagined how I would feel when I reached this eastern land. But from the moment I first saw the towering building on the horizon from the ship, to the instant I set foot on this land, I have no clear memory of my feelings. Today is my 12th day in Jixia, and as I sit at my desk trying hard to recall those emotions, I realize after nearly two hours that it's all in vain. I can only honestly write the following: I feel a bit frustrated and ashamed. I've never ever been in a place that leaves me speechless, where I can only widen my eyes and stretch my ears to absorb all the information I can. I have no time to ask questions because my mouth has been unconsciously open the whole time. This reminds me of an old shepherd I met in Navenia. He lived his whole life in the mountains, far from towns. When he first stood on the streets of Navenia, his astonishment made me laugh. His life was spent with sheep, and everything in Navenia was shocking and unimaginable to him. My feelings here in Jixia are probably not much different from his. In my previous books, I have shown many strange and dangerous journeys and adventures—the terrifying and powerful Mechanoids of Navenia, the fierce poisonous beasts attacking caravans in the vast sands Alsahraa, the dangerously alluring sirens, and the lost ancient underwater city hidden in storms. And of course, the unexaggerated courage and strength of the greatest traveler! \nDespite all the dangers and hardships, I am determined to leave my footprints in every corner of the world. From the moment my frail, sickly mother stood in front of me and fought back against those who mocked me, I set my life's goal and dream. \nAnd if I can find what I need on this land, all the better.

The Societies searched every corner of the Dreamweave Plains but could not find the source of the strange disturbance. Then one night, a Seeker gazed up at the stars and discovered the culprit—a "Black Cloud Monster" watching from on high. 
 
Once the cause was known, the rest was only a matter of ingenuity. If there's one thing the Societies excel at, it's finding solutions. Each faction poured its skill and wisdom into the task. Together they forged four runestones: the Hunter's Cloud's Hunt, the Angler's Fishcatcher, the Crafter's Nature's Art, and the Herbalist's Golden Wheat. These runestones became sacred tools to subdue the Windling Lion, and with them, the people finally felt their hearts settle. 
 
The Crafters then worked through the night and raised the Cloudreach Tower, so tall it seemed to pierce the heavens. No one needed to crane their necks skyward anymore—they could now climb right up and see what that monster was doing among the clouds. 
 
With the tower built, one of the Anglers had a revelation: "That Black Cloud Monster is just a big fish, isn't it? Then I'll go up and catch it!" And, remarkably, he was right. With a cast of his rod and the smell of a freshly baked cake on the hook, the monster came darting toward it, only to plunge straight into the Aerdense Flower trap crafted by the Herbalist. It thrashed and roared, but all its struggle was in vain. 
 
The Black Cloud Monster has not been seen for a hundred years. Yet one mystery still lingers among the Societies: the thunderstorm that ended so abruptly that night. It was no stroke of chance. Some greater force must have halted it. No one truly knows what happened. 
 
It is said that only by completing the Stabilization Ritual can one glimpse the truth behind it all. But the rite itself is complex—some say it calls for blessings to the four directions, others that it requires the four runestones once more. With so many differing tales, the rite was forgotten, left to legend. 
Even so, the Societies still hope that one day, someone destined may uncover its secret.

Splendor upon splendor—its reflection fractured in shadow. 
 
Light filters through the wooden railings high atop the grand buildings, striking one roof after another, each layer dimmer than the last, until it can no longer reach the ground. Perhaps the master engineer who once designed this city could never have imagined that the lines and grids on his blueprint would one day become homes for generations. In this three-tiered city, meant to symbolize peace and prosperity, countless ordinary lives have become tightly bound together. 
 
Chang'an, before the Pavilion of Blossoms. 
 
"Li Jinchai! You stole another one of my customers again!" A girl in a green blouse grabbed the collar of a smaller girl, her rolled sleeves exposing round, sturdy arms. 
 
"Nonsense! How could our little street stall steal business from your grand shop? The customers probably just don't like your shop's name. Pavilion of Blossoms, it sounds tacky! You should tell your father to change it!" Though small in stature, Li Jinchai never lost a quarrel. 
 
The bystanders, long accustomed to this daily squabbling, barely looked up. Pavilion of Blossoms and Li's Jewellery had faced each other across the same street for decades, both jewelers by trade, both in decline. 
 
The owners of Pavilion of Blossoms had become obsessed with Mechcraft models, passing the shop to their only daughter, Hua Changhui, when she was just ten. The jewelry she sold was old-fashioned and slow to move, her shelves stacked with unsold stock; only a few loyal customers kept the business alive. 
Across the street, Li's Jewellery fared no better. The shop specialized in refurbishing old ornaments for resale, and business had once been good—until the owner, Old Lee, lost the use of his hands in an accident. His daughter, Li Jinchai, only eight at the time, stood on a wooden crate just to reach the workbench and took over her father's tools while her mother traveled seeking a cure. 
Her work was clumsy at first; many refurbished pieces were unsellable. To practice, she began buying up odd trinkets of mixed materials and strange designs. But her father's condition worsened, and she had to start calling out to passersby from the doorway to draw in business. That, inevitably, started her rivalry with Hua Changhui. 
 
Day after day, their childish bickering brought a touch of color to otherwise bitter days. And in time, the two little girls grew into young women. 
 
"You're stealing customers again!" Hua Changhui snapped, waving a fist. She had grown tall and strong, having learned a bit of Martial Arts during a part-time job with the Office of Grand Envoys. 
 
"This might be the last time," Li Jinchai said quietly. "Mother met a traveling healer—she says there's a miraculous material in Jixia called Aersilk. It might be able to cure Father's hands." 
 
"When are you leaving?" Hua asked. 
 
Li Jinchai didn't look up. "Now." 
 
"Wait." Hua ran back inside, then returned carrying a large wooden chest. She pushed it into Li Jinchai's arms. 
"Take this. These are my father's prized tools for crafting Mechcrafts. Better you use them than let him waste away tinkering with toys. Let the scholars in Jixia see what Chang'an craftsmanship can do!" 
 
Li Jinchai's face turned red, her eyes still downcast. "Thank you," she murmured. She didn't refuse—she knew that even if she did, the chest would somehow find its way onto her cart before she left. Hua Changhui was stubborn that way. 
 
Hua watched as the cart rolled off, swallowed by the fractured light filtering down through the city's layered bridges and rooftops. At that moment, she felt entirely out of place in her own home. 
 
The splendor of Chang'an, she realized, belonged only to those meant to possess it.

Back in Alsahraa, I heard whispers of a mysterious figure known as "Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade." 
Regrettably, I entered this world too late to witness his prowess or engage in combat with him—a true lament for any martial artist. 
 
In Alsahraa, numerous vagabonds claimed to be disciples of "the Lone Blade," but they all ended up losing their teeth after facing me. 
As legends piled up, my curiosity about the Lone Blade himself grew. Upon arriving at Jixia, I finally had the chance to follow in his footsteps! 
 
Roaring Tiger Training Hall 
"I will verify personally whether the rumored 'Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade' is fact or fiction." 
"Am I not tiger-like enough?" 
Head Trainer Tigon burst into laughter upon hearing my declaration. 
His thunderous chuckle shook the air. 
When I first met Head Trainer Tigon, I was struck by his rare appearance—white base coat with black stripes, broad forehead, and high eyebrows. His tiger head resembled a boulder perched atop a towering physique, with thick limbs like tree trunks, even more imposing than the tales described. As he approached, the ground seemed to tremble beneath my feet... 
Little did I know that his name "Tigon" actually came from being a rare white tiger half-breed! 
 
I must admit, seeing him unsettled me. 
While my blade skills might match his, martial arts duels often come down to who has the greater strength. 
If I were to spar with this mountain of a man, I wasn't sure if I could withstand his full power before hitting the ground. 
Just as I hesitated, Tigon declared, "I have never turned down a challenge, no matter who it is!" 
With that, I put aside my doubts and prepared for our duel. 
When I unsheathed my curved blade, Tigon's eyes lit up—is this the unspoken bond between fellow bladesmen? 
I chose not to attack first. Given our size difference, my offensive would likely be swiftly neutralized. 
Instead, I planned to use my agility to lure him into making the first move. After all, my primary goal in this sparring session was to witness the legendary warrior's skill. 
Tigon's blade strikes were fierce and relentless, making them difficult to evade. When my curved blade clashed with his sharp edge, sparks flew everywhere. 
After several rounds, I began to tire, feeling pain in my jaws, my steps slowing, and my defensive speed noticeably decreasing. 
Tigon's swordsmanship was exceptional, with his blade seemingly imbued with life. He and his weapon moved in perfect harmony, each movement and breath synchronized with a unique rhythm. 
This was a living legend unfolding before my very eyes. 
I once heard that although Navenia lacks skilled bladesmen, similar techniques have been developed there. Was Tigon inspired by Navenian warriors, or did he inspire them? 
 
The outcome of our duel was already clear, but adhering to the spirit of martial arts, I fought until the end. 
I lost. 
Although our strengths differed, I saw that Tigon also exerted considerable effort to defeat me. 
Tigon earned his nickname "the Lone Blade" because few can withstand even a single strike from him. To have exchanged blows with him multiple times was an honor in itself, regardless of victory or defeat. 
After the match, Tigon generously praised my swordplay and invited me to return for another bout—or even become one of his disciples. 
Though I deeply appreciated his recognition and admired his skill, the vast lands of Jixia beckoned, filled with countless warriors waiting to be encountered. 
Seeing my resolve, Tigon recommended another training hall in Jixia—Obsidian Flame Training Hall. 
What new experiences awaited me this time?

Author: Wenyi, Sorcery Instructor 
 
Study cannot rely on books alone. True strength comes from facing real opponents. Sorcery training is no different. For this reason, the academy has established a series of sparring trials to help students practice and experiment, to feel power's shifting tides and battle's ever-changing pace for themselves. 
 
Broadly speaking, these trials fall into two types: internal and external. Internal trials help students grasp the inner relationships between the world and the laws them. The most common is: 
 
 
 
Sorcery Circle Duels. Across the academy you will find Sorcery Circle-duel platforms resembling Go boards, laid with Aersilk and node-points for students to compete upon. To prevail, you must understand and master complex Sorcery Circles and the interactions behind them—restraint, reinforcement, and mutual generation. These patterns, woven from point to line to shape, mirror the laws governing all things. Through repeated study and contest, your grasp of essence and principle will naturally deepen. 
 
 
 
Internal trials alone are not enough; external training is equally important, as it can hone a person's response strategies in actual combat. Sorcery carries inherent risk, so duels are commonly conducted as Telepathic Duels through Telepathic Threads. Each duelist holds one end of the thread, arranges Sorcery Circles, and releases Sorcries through the thread. The Sorcries collide, and victory is decided without physical harm. Yet some believe only the edge of danger reveals the truth of oneself. These students—usually already formidable—enter sanctioned arenas within the Tower of Enlightenment, where power restraints are lifted and duels take place as though on a true battlefield. 
 
 
 
Internal and external training are inseparable. To favor one at the expense of the other is a mistake. It is not enough to say "I enjoy head-on combat, so I will only train externally." Balanced practice is essential. Only then can your strength grow steadily, and securely.

I regret not fully shutting down this Mechanoid. I hope you weren't injured. 
I was once an Instructor of Mechcrafts at Jixia Academy, but lost my legs in an accident and have since lived in seclusion in this cave. 
This old companion has accompanied me for many years, and I owe it for helping me avoid a lonely death in a foreign land. 
Now my life is coming to an end. Although I shouldn't be overly sentimental, I can't bear to shut down its power, setting it to the lowest power setting for a trial in my place. 
... 
I apologize for writing so much. As one faces death, they often feel overwhelmed with thoughts and do not know where to begin. 
Deep within the cave are my most accomplished Mechcraft creations. They shouldn't gather dust after my death.

What do I truly desire? 
Living in solitude within this deserted cave—is this the life I want? 
I've gazed upon my crippled body more than once, questioning my existence. 
The moment I lost my legs, I knew the distance between myself and the sky would remain eternal. 
I'm trapped in this cave, having lost everything, including the courage to escape. 
I'm alive, yet merely existing. 
Would ending this miserable life bring me relief? 
As I placed the noose around my neck, I saw her. 
Her fiery red attire shone like the sun. Before I could react, she vanished, leaving behind only the elegant feather from her head, gently drifting into the cave and into my hands. 
I clutched the feather tightly, yearning to escape this crippled form, though I knew I couldn't. 
I often wonder, if I could complete these wings, perhaps I could fly out of this cave and meet her again. 
From that day forward, I dedicated nearly all my energy to studying the wings. She had rekindled my courage to live. 
However, when the final touches were complete, I barely had the strength to hold a pen. 
It seems... these youthful wings cannot bear the weight of my aged soul. 
Whoever finds this next, I hope you can glance at her for me from Crosswind Bridge. 
As long as you try flying your wings on the bridge, attracting the gaze of the crowd, she is sure to appear. 
My successor, use your eyes to help me see her, see this world, and see that azure sky.

I've found the perfect spot for gathering energy—the Stargazing Terrace! 
 
 
 
I know you're going to scold me, maybe even point at me and say, "Quit wasting time with those damned experiments!" But even if there's just the slightest chance, I have to try. 
 
 
 
One day, I'll find a way to bring him back from wherever he disappeared.

Exclusive scoop! News from the Guixu Dream Performance. The Jixia Guixu Dream Performance has temporarily come to an end. The third round of trials, which is also the final, will be held later. What kind of feast will the Gui Die team and the Star team bring us next? Every student, stay tuned. This time, our reporter will bring you a series of interesting anecdotes interspersed between the matches and information about the second round of assessments through an exclusive visit. It is reported that before the second round of assessments, members of the Star team appeared at the Fengyun Celebration. It is said that the Fengyun Celebration was originally held to commemorate the heroes who saved Fengyun Wild from evil spirits, and over time it evolved into a celebration to drive away evil, celebrate the harvest, and pray for peace. The Star team's appearance during the competition—was it just for relaxation and enjoying the celebration, or was it a 'secret pre-match training' planned long ago under the guise of the celebration? There were witnesses who saw mysterious freshmen at the Climbing Cloud Tower trying to challenge the records left by Gui Die, which makes it hard not to think of it as special training for movement techniques. At the same time, there is a thank-you letter from the Herbology group in Fengyun Wild, who wanted to express their gratitude to the Star team through our publication for helping to resolve the Shuo Spring Bud mutation incident. From this, I speculate that perhaps the Star team members intended to use this celebration for training to improve team tacit understanding and strength, but accidentally encountered the mutated Shuo Spring Bud. This plan makes one have to admire the captain of the Star team—Novar. As for the final training results, let's wait for the third round of trials. Compared to the many events at the celebration, the process of the second round of trials can be said to be very simple, direct, and bizarrely dreamy. The rule of the Heart Trial in this year's Dream Performance is to hand over your treasures to Teacher Zhuangzi, who will then hide them in an ancient dream. The participating students need to find their way in the dream filled with endless secrets, observe the fog with their hearts, and find the treasures again to pass the assessment. The dream realm is dangerous and unpredictable, and the assessment process is like a dream, with all kinds of changes. Even the students taking the assessment cannot tell what is true and what is false. However, the students who have participated in the assessment have indeed achieved growth on some level. Although it is difficult for me to clearly explain to the readers what happened during the assessment, there are many interesting anecdotes that happened before the assessment. Many teams that advanced to the second round of trials discussed for a long time in the lounge, unable to decide which 'treasure' to hand over. The Star team members decisively handed over the Star team badge and successfully completed the assessment. Some teams confused the concept of 'treasure', thinking only of valuable items, but because of the lack of emotional connection, these items were permanently lost in the dream. Some teams were troubled because they felt their 'treasure' was the world's delicacies and didn't know what to hand over. Being troubled by what is most precious to oneself, and through this, knowing oneself and finding one's true self—perhaps this was also in the teacher's design. Finally, thank you very much for providing the opportunity for this publication to let me accompany all readers to witness this Guixu Dream Performance. Let's meet again in the third round of trials.

For martial artists, competition can be brutal. For Gourmets, it's even more so. A tasteless bite or a slightly furrowed brow can deal a crushing blow, leaving them crestfallen for days. 
 
 
 
Even Mann, a recognized culinary master, has experienced gloomy days in his youth. Years ago, during the climax of the Grand Chef Tournament, an unknown youth battled his way into the finals. Unlike the other contestants, this dark horse didn't flaunt his cooking techniques or showcase elaborate knife skills. Instead, he presented the judges with nothing but steamed buns. 
 
 
 
As the steaming buns were served, the crowd fell silent. Could such a simple dish really win? One judge took a small bite and quietly teared up. "Grandma, I miss you so much." 
 
 
 
Another judge asked Mann, "What's the secret of this bun? The flour? The steamer? The seasoning? What's this taste I can't forget?" 
 
"It's the flavor of your memories," Mann replied. "That's why it's irreplaceable."

Volume of the Saepes Encyclopedia written by Muping, a Hunter from Jixia. It documents the various uses of Saepes products in daily life, with special thanks to the Herbologist Association for their significant assistance. 
 
Saepes are a common sight in the wilds of Jixia. As they grow and migrate, they frequently shed leaves and aged bark. However, these leaves and bark should not be underestimated. For us Jixians, they are essential items in daily life. 
 
Firstly, there are the Saepes Leaves. 
 
The leaves shed by Saepes as they grow are considered top-grade medicinal herbs. According to herbalists, "All herbs and insects have their ideal environments, with unique properties and scents... Thus, we name them after their origins, for the land enhances their spirit." This ancient Jixian saying emphasizes that while the herb itself is crucial, its origin also significantly impacts its quality. In Jixia, where Aersilk nourishes the breath of life, leaves from living Saepes produce medicines of superior quality and efficacy compared to those from other regions. These exceptional herbs are known as "terroir herbs." 
 
Saepes Leaves are bitter and pungent, inducing sweating, regulating energy, and promoting blood circulation. They also help to balance lung and stomach energy, making them useful for clearing heat. Decoctions and tonics made from these leaves can invigorate the mind and leave one feeling refreshed, though excessive consumption may lead to diarrhea.

Comment: There's a rumor that many Navenians use it as a laxative for "body sculpting." I'm not sure I follow the logic. 
 
Next, there's the Saepes Extract, which is related to our daily food. 
 
Making buns and noodles requires proofing the dough, but there's a persistent issue with fermentation leaving the dough with an unpleasant sour smell. Initially, Jixians used plant ash to solve this problem—burning ordinary straw or weeds into ash, filtering it through hemp bags, and adding the solution to the dough to eliminate the sour smell. Later, it was discovered that using collected Saepes bark for ash and then filtering it produced an even better effect, not only removing the sour smell but also making the dough softer and the noodles more elastic. This is the Saepes Extract, a staple in every household and noodle shop. 
 
Navenians also enjoy noodles, but theirs are different from ours. I've heard that Navenia has a remarkable Mechcraft that can dry Saepes bark into Saepes Extract automatically, with high speed and yield.

Finally, here are some golden rules for the outdoor adventures. Many have found them incredibly useful, so be sure to pay close attention. 
 
 
 
Rule No. 1: Fight when you can, flee when you must.

Rule No. 4: Stay alert at all times, even when you sleep!

Author: Wei Yan, Seeker 
 
When it comes to lifestyle, the students of the School of Sorcery are the most unique. Their pursuit of beauty and excellence is almost a natural instinct, and every aspect of their lives reflects a deep philosophical contemplation. Some might say they are pretentious or overly secretive, and while there is some truth to that, it's not entirely accurate. From my own observations, I would sum up their lifestyle in one word: elegance. 
 
 
 
For example, when it comes to food, most Martial Arts students focus on whether the food will help their training, so they're willing to try the bizarre dishes concocted by the Gourmets (some of whom exaggerate the benefits of their creations), focusing solely on nourishing the body. Mechcraft students, on the other hand, prioritize efficiency, often opting for quick and convenient meals. But Sorcery students are different. They are extremely particular about what they put into their bodies, placing great importance on the presentation of dishes and the balance and harmony of flavors. For them, eating is more than just filling their stomachs; they see it as a way to connect with the world around them and even as an extension of their practice. So if you see someone in a restaurant asking the owner endless questions or secretly seasoning their food at the table, they're probably from the School of Sorcery. 
 
 
 
Their approach to other aspects of life follows the same pattern. In fashion, Sorcery students prefer intricate, finely crafted clothing that emphasizes aesthetics. They also integrate their clothing with "Telepathic Threads" from key acupoints to enhance their visual appeal. In their living spaces, they seek harmony and elegance, always striving to integrate with nature. Each Sorcery student has their own style, never blindly following trends. Even their travel habits reflect this taste. They move with a deliberate grace, often following patterns they've carefully considered. Once, while conducting research on the Springbrook Plains, I encountered a Sorcery student who seemed lost. I tried to offer some help, but he replied, "I am riding the wind and seeking its source. Please do not disturb me." Looking back, I still find that amusing. 
 
 
 
Editor's Note: Although this article wasn't written by a Sorcery student, it's a fairly objective and detailed portrayal that can help Sorcery students better understand their own ways and integrate into Academy life. (And remember, never question a Sorcery student's taste in hairstyles, clothing, pets, or appetites.)

Authors: Zhao Qian, Zhu Moran and Qi An from the School of Martial Arts 
 
 
 
Subject: Martial Arts Students' Summer Notes 
 
Editor's Note: Knowing your limits is also key in one's training. 
 
 
 
Zhao Qian's Note 
 
This morning began with an unexpected chase. My father, armed with a fire poker, pursued me for two miles, muttering frustrations under his breath. 
 
 
 
I have to say I was confused. I've stuck to the Headmaster's teaching that life is training, and I haven't missed a single day of practice during the summer, with the aim of improving my grades in the new semester. 
 
 
 
To support my training, I crafted several dummies from trees in our backyard—selected for their sturdiness and the refreshing scent of their wood. 
 
 
 
With minimal effort, I uprooted the trees and shaped them into dummies using palm strikes, guided by designs from my peers at the School of Mechcrafts. While these homemade dummies aren't as sophisticated as the Mechanoids at school, they serve well for home practice. 
 
 
 
This morning, my father was pleased to see me practicing martial arts and kept nodding approvingly. However, his mood shifted dramatically upon seeing the dummies. He fainted and, when he came to, he started chasing me. 
 
I'm baffled. What more could he possibly want from a good son like me? 
 
 
 
Zhu Moran's Note 
 
Summer has unveiled unexpected masters among ordinary folks. Today, a visit to the bathhouse on East Street led to a surprising encounter with an old attendant passionate about Martial Arts. Realizing which school I belonged to at first glance, he enthusiastically engaged in a vigorous scrub, commenting on my muscles and strengths. 
 
 
 
Proud to represent the School of Mechcrafts, I maintained composure and focused my energy, enduring his intense scrubbing in silence. 
 
 
 
The attendant's eagerness escalated to a challenge for a spar. 
 
Under normal circumstances, I would have welcomed the duel, but the setting—a crowded, steamy bathhouse where everyone was naked— less than ideal. 
 
 
 
Qi An's Note 
 
Lately, I must be getting stronger because I hardly feel the weight of the hundred-pound sandbags I've been carrying. Before the break, I asked my teacher for three times more sandbags so I could intensify my training during the holidays. I wear them all the time, even while sleeping, integrating training into every part of my life. 
 
 
 
With the added weight, my stamina has been improving rapidly. 
 
 
 
The only problem is that I can't use the Mechcraft elevator anymore. Every time I stepped on one, it'd loudly announce, "Overweight!" 
 
This even startled a girl who was waiting for the elevator with me... What a shame.

The name "Scholarly Tiger" comes from popular usage. As Hunters who value folk traditions, we'll continue using this term in our writings. Despite their feline title, Scholarly Tigers are actually small, friendly creatures. 
 
 
 
Long ago, when Jixia Academy was just a humble schoolhouse, a teacher prepared to discipline some distracted students with his ferule. Suddenly, a fluffy little creature darted onto the podium, curiously surveying the room before settling down. Its presence eased the tension—the teacher put away his ferule, and the students refocused. From that day on, the amazing creature appeared punctually at every lesson, eventually becoming a part of the school. That's how it earned the name "Scholarly Tiger." 
 
 
 
People love cuddling these adorable creatures for their soft, snowy fur and gentle, fresh scent. Scholarly Tigers love being groomed, which speaks to the close relationship between humans and animals. 
 
 
 
About the size of a child, Scholarly Tigers have muscular bodies, broad chests, and short, thick necks. Their large, wedge-shaped heads are flat on top, with two small horns crowning their heads. Dark, bright eyes shine above round muzzles and slightly sunken noses. Their long, fluffy ears flick with interest, and teal and peach markings adorn their brows and the corners of their eyes. 
 
 
 
As Jixia's most beloved pets, Scholarly Tigers prefer living indoors and enjoy playing with children. They often wear name tags on collars made of fine red strings, indicating their owners. These friendly pets share a close bond with their humans, favoring comfortable companionship over wild antics. Interestingly, they have a habit of sneaking into classrooms and sitting in on lessons. Students are baffled: why would anyone enjoy attending class? Some speculate that Scholarly Tigers feed on knowledge, especially savoring the driest lectures. Others believe they embody wisdom itself, sent to the mortal realm to ensure academic rigor among the youth... 
 
 
 
In our search for truth, we've visited villages and towns with the help of tools from the School of Mechcrafts. Our findings suggest that Scholarly Tigers' large ears allow them to detect rhythms in teachers' voices that are imperceptible to humans. While research into these special frequencies remains inconclusive, this evidence-based hypothesis holds more value than the fanciful legends shared as gossip.

text:
Jixia Academy will be hosting the Enlightenment Trials competition in the Dreamrealm. During this time, students studying here are asked to move aside. 
 
 
 
Thank you for your cooperation.
Exposed Aerux, bearing the marks of sharp claws and teeth.

This was probably an arena where competitors fought in the center, with the winner receiving a reward. 
 
But strangely, the traces of power left here are unlike anything I've seen before. 
 
Could they have wielded powers completely different from ours? 
 
This is just a theory based on preliminary research. Further verification is needed with the help of Martial Arts students.
In those dark hours when invaders stormed Jixia, by the Sanctifier's order we sealed the Key to the Eternity Cauldron here. May our descendants return to reignite the power of Divine Imprint

Confidential reports have noted unusual Rebel activities. To prevent any incidents in the mountains, you are ordered to monitor the Rebels by patrolling the area east of the Forbidden Chamber. During your patrols, pay close attention to the Northeastern peaks, as well as the safety of the essential Academy facilities, the Aero Plateaus, located in the <69D0FF>east and west</>.

An oddly complicated research drawing of a Mechcraft contraption. One can barely make out the writings. \n"An attempt to duplicate Mozi's Mechcraft Armor research project... stand in for me for the Q&A lesson... need more time for research and testing..."
It tells the story of a young Dreamweaver facing a battle, filled with hope and trepidation.

Located in the northern region, Aerux Town is a crucial passage for those traveling to and from Jixia. Over time, it has become a bustling trading hub. With the growth of Jixia Academy, students from all over gather here, making the town an even better place to live and transforming it into a thriving residential area.

Star of Strategy Set 
 
A premium set featuring the essence of mountain and sea delicacies! It is packed with the essence of deep sea fish, which is beneficial for mental work and is a must-have for students who are skilled in strategy. 
 
Tip: Following the advice of a certain strategy expert, "Hunger is the best catalyst for strategy," this set is smaller.

Do you know why I've always wanted to venture out to sea? It's because my time is running out. Due to complications from being born prematurely, my heart is under increasing strain. I secretly asked a herbalsit and learned that it's unlikely I'll live to see my eighteenth birthday. 
I've spent my entire life in Seacliffs, seventeen years has passed, even the most beautiful views lose their charm. My parents, the elder and everyone in the clan are kind to me, and I can't bear the thought of them witnessing my passing. 
Thus, I plan to leave. I want to see as much of the world as possible in the little time I have left. Maybe I'll even visit the legendary lands of our ancestors, the Three Kingdoms, or perhaps I'll pass away on this journey. 
Without you, none of this would be possible. That's why I trust only you with this truth. 
Please keep my secret safe. 
And I hope we'll have the chance to meet again.
A plan outlining a field study with three students, but only the opening lines were written.

Monday: Headmaster Mozi 
Tuesday: Mr. Feitang 
Wednesday: Headmaster Mozi (On leave, Mr. Feitang is substituting.) 
Thursday: Mr. Feitang 
Friday: Headmaster Mozi (On leave, Mr. Feitang is substituting.)
Today, after six months in the making, the Wondrous Maze is finally complete. \nThe remaining Mechcraft components will be sent into storage near the elevator south of the maze.

During Trial 37, some Mechcrafts suddenly malfunctioned, and came to a standstill. The cause is unknown 
 
 
 
Similar issues occurred with the Mining Mechcrafts earlier, but most were caused by debris stuck in the joints. 
 
These Mechcrafts fell into an icy lake during transport. Could the cold have immobilized them?

Phew, good thing I'm quick. Otherwise, I'd be having another nightmare right now. 
 
That woman is really strange. Every time she talks about Oneiros, she gets as excited as if she'd found treasure. I can't stand her. 
 
Although the key to advancing in Sorcery lies in constant experimentation, she can't keep sneaking up on the guys to practice her skills. If it weren't for the boss protecting her, I'd definitely give her a good scolding. 
 
Last time, she used some kind of Sorcery Technique that made me fall asleep while eating. At first, I just felt a little tired, and then the bed in my dream broke, and I fell straight into endless darkness. In that darkness, one nightmare followed another. Just thinking about it gives me chills. 
 
I've been wondering: can that strange woman really control our dreams, or does she influence the environment to affect our dreams. 
 
Every time I think about it, I start yawning... My eyelids are getting heavy. I hope I don't have any nightmares tonight.

I focused on weaving dreams over and over again, yet I couldn't form a Dream Cocoon. This is the first time I've encountered such a phenomenon. 
 
 
 
Could it be because of the dreamers I encountered the other day? Unfortunately, I haven't seen them since. 
 
 
 
Maybe it's because... we're about to leave here... but at least let me leave them a small parting gift.

Gong Du mastered the art of Sanctifier, skilled in carving <69D0FF>mystical patterns</>. 
He harnessed the power of heaven and earth, transforming it into pillars and walls. 
With this marvelous method, he protected the refugees within the pillar. 
Alas, he was consumed by the divine imprints, his body perishing as his path vanished. 
 
The people pitied him, engraving stone to commemorate his memory. 
Beholding the divine imprint, one senses his heroic spirit endures!

This is the ancient method soldiers used to master their movements. 
 
To move easily and seize opportunities in battle, they learned to find the right path and adapt to sudden changes. 
 
Remember, move quickly like a shadow, and even in small spaces, you will find the way.

Struggling with constant defeats in martial trials? Can't break through your training plateau? Don't miss out! The Greenwhisper Pool Arena Champion's Treasure and the long-lost martial arts manuals are up for the taking! As long as you find two of the missing key fragments, you'll be able to claim the treasure that everyone has been dreaming of! 
 
 
 
During your breaks from training and trails, why not take a hike up the nearby mountain? Getting your hands on the Greenwhisper Treasure will save you twenty years of detours! This adventure will be worth your while!

First, do not attempt to damage mechanisms, avoid brute force, and reject violence.
Second, report unexpected situations to the nearest Sentinel Drive mechanism in a timely manner.
Third, carving a boat to find a lost sword in a constantly changing maze is not a wise move.
Fourth, rushing through multiple trials in a single day is not recommended.

text:
Topic: Hunting Society—Wolvine Claw Collection 
Evaluation: Pass 
 
Although Wan Jing completed the Wolvine hunt competently, this choice for a graduation project lacked both challenge and originality—mediocre at best. We expect Wan Jing to strive for greater heights in future Pathfinder endeavors and grow into an outstanding hunter. 
 
Attachment: 
Appeal Record: Denied 
Wan Jing made thorough preparations for hunting the Blazing Falcon, but tracking prey is also a fundamental skill for a Hunter. Countless preparation make no sense for a failed hunt. This is the awareness a Hunter should have. Therefore, Wan Jing's appeal is not approved.
A submerged Mechcraft remnant—something seems to be missing from the fish eye.
The Astrology Society showcased two of its essential tools: the astrolabe and the compass. Both seemed to carry a mysterious power.

The earth and sky merge, with my emotions drifting among the clouds. 
 
 
 
A towering spire stands, with waves gently brushing against the wind. 
 
 
 
Clouds dance amidst the mountains and rivers, with ripples leisurely spreading their light. 
 
 
 
Green peaks rise one after another, with the shallow sounds of footsteps on stones. 
 
 
 
Cloud shadows sway, evoking the beautiful images of the past, only to vanish without a trace. 
 
 
 
The hopes in my heart weave and spread across the sky. 
 
 
 
I have sought the traces of the past amidst the wind and moon. 
 
 
 
I have joined the flow of the crowd, savoring the fleeting moments of life. 
 
 
 
White waves and green moss overlap with the years, with cloud shadows dancing as they always have.. 
 
 
 
A weary wanderer has finally returned to the vast lands they call home.

Did humans discover the Dreamscape in this way? 
How did they realize that they were dreaming? 
In the Dreamscape, they are like children taking slow steps, innocent and unsure... 
Children can indeed be curious and perceptive. 
Perhaps we should try their method. It might bring new insights.

Tips for the Path of Ingenious Talent: 
 
1. <69D0FF>Bring ranged weapons</>. 
 
2. Search around the Treasure Tower and <69D0FF>shoot all the targets</>. Don't miss any! 
 
3. Shoot all <69D0FF>targets</> <69D0FF>within the time limit</>. 
 
4. Destroy the exposed core of the Treasure Tower. 
 
If you choose to take on this challenge, make sure to follow these tips carefully.
The signboard is missing, and it seems to have been vandalized by someone.
It looks like someone got here first. The place is empty.
A detailed ledger recording the inn's expenses and earnings. The neat, graceful handwriting suggests it was kept by a woman.

We refine and store Oneiros in containers, hoping that after prolonged fermentation, we will obtain the purest form of Oneiros. 
However, most containers are failures, and opening them would release toxic gases or even summon monsters. 
 
Only one container can produce Dream Butterflies that can be attracted to the Dream Guidestone on the stone pedestal, which will surely stimulate a strong Oneiros response. I am on the verge of success！ 
 
Dreamslayer attacked, and we had to flee in a hurry. I sealed the <69D0FF>only</> successful container with <69D0FF>a special butterfly symbol</> and didn't have time to take it with me.

The great dragon makes the valley its lair, resting there from dawn till dusk. 
 
As the remnants of the enemy forces lingered in the valley, the Dragonrider, well-versed in the lay of the land, devised a strategy. 
 
Like catching fish in a barrel, they launched a siege within the valley, defeating the enemy with ease. 
 
This was both a trial of strategy and a commemoration of the dragon's feats.
A previously unknown, unsealed force has emerged.

Thorns! The problem is the thorns! They're not native to this place, and they've disrupted the balance between fine dreams and nightmares! 
 
We were ambushed by beasts we had never seen before, and they seemed to be distorted by unbalanced dreams as well...  
 
In the blink of an eye, the monster vanished again... Do they really exist? 
 
I can no longer tell... if it's reality or a dream... 
 
We can't go on. We must...  
 
leave...

A fruit brew jug left by Bai Ming. Written on it is a line in a style unlike his: \n"Cloud-piercing sails part morning haze; A reed boat drifts across distant tides." \nThe brushwork is elegant, with a soaring yet delicate grace, as if the writer had something more to say, yet chose not to.

Rise with sun, rest at dusk. 
Train only in grounds; no fights elsewhere. 
Youth stay within; villagers don't roam. 
No outsiders dwell; no deals with merchants.
\n \nWritten by Wei An,  Intendant of Wind's Rest Pavilion

Time's mark can be seen on the keepsake. \n \nIt bears a few words of longing. Signed, "Wei An".
The stone pillar gleams with a soft light. A tower rises into the sky. Ancient battles take place atop the Mausoleum's Peak.
A set of plush toys featuring the whole Team of Stars. Many students have come to claim them, but so far the rightful owner has not been found.

The boat arrived at the shore near Jixia; upon inspection, it was determined that this place was indeed delightful.  
 
Moreover, the cave was rich in bronze ore deposits. As the saying goes, fortune and misfortune are intertwined, and there must be a divine will at work behind it.  
 
The Energy Ring canbe retrieved from the ship as the central drive for Mechcraft creation. 
 
 Everyone gathered here to repair the Secret Box of Littoral Spirit Drive to master Essentials of Mechcraft, and to display the brilliance of our divine power.

The innermost chamber of Mechcraft, a place of hidden treasures. Only the wise may enter. \n \nThe art of forging the silent giant is concealed here. To reforge the giant, follow the pattern of divine imprints to unlock the door.

Cannon Proving Ground Rules 
Safety is the foremost rule of the proving ground. As the proving ground is a public area and Cannon pose inherent risks, all students must conduct Cannon manufacturing or testing under the guidance of a qualified Cannoneer instructor.   
Before engaging in any Cannon manufacturing or testing activities, students must report relevant details to Mr.Blazen for approval.   
During experiments, strict attention must be paid to safety at every stage. Negligence or carelessness is unacceptable to prevent accidents and injuries.

Yesterday, a passenger attempted to board the Aership with dangerous belongings. Fortunately, the staff promptly disposed of the materials in the water, ensuring the safety of all passengers on board. 
 
 
 
The Academy would like to reiterate the following rules: 
 
It is strictly prohibited to carry flammable, explosive or other dangerous materials. Personal weapons must be stored with the personnel on the Aership. 
 
 
 
Dangerous behavior while on board is also prohibited. Such behavior includes, but is not limited to: opening windows and leaning out to watch birds, boiling water in your seat, attempting to climb on top of the Aership, racing the Aership, attempting to jump from the Aership to nearby trees, or attempting to modify the internal Mechcrafts while the Aership is in motion.

Day 1: It hesitated for a long time before it ran into the woods, not daring to approach other animals. 
... 
Day 3: It's become more confident now. Its range of activity has expanded, and it's bravely approaching other animals. 
... 
Day 6: It has successfully integrated into the Wolvine pack. I can leave with peace of mind now.
The water flows endlessly. \nThe Dreamweavers thrive. \nTherefore, it is called "Waterspring Vale".
Delve into ████. ████ in harmony, mirrored in the pair of ██.
Southwest: Aermore Valley, "East: Red Falcon Training Hall", "Northwest: Dragon Valley".

Power Transmission Optimization: Balance transmission and weight distribution using the primary and secondary Mecharms. The power transfer paths from the core shell to each part need to be re-engineered. 
 
 
 
Efficiency Optimization: Upgrade the Mech Core to enable the Fabricator to handle multiple tasks simultaneously. 
 
 
 
Cooling Optimization: Add a steam cycle cooling system.

The person operating the console has already fallen to their own "masterpiece."
It depicts the scenery of Dainty Vale. I heard that Piner bought it from a disciple at Dainty Alley.

Dreamy Fantasy World combines humor with a touch of sadness. It's an excellent read, but someone circled a name in the first chapter. Hey, it's a mystery novel. You spoiled the surprise. I've hidden it on a less accessible bookshelf to prevent further spoilers.

Observation Log Day 1: 
 
Mayene slept through all her classes today. Initially, I thought she was studying in secret to maintain her top exam scores, but she spent the entire night playing with Master Zhuangzi's Bubble Fish. 
 
Observation Log Day 2: 
 
She slept through classes again today. Afterward, she joyfully stole dried fish from the Pastoral Care Canteen. I chose not to report her and maintained surveillance. 
 
Observation Log Day 3: 
 
She skipped the morning classes and slept through the afternoon ones. She spent the night fishing by the pond. I kinda like her lifestyle. 
 
Observation Log Day 7: 
 
After a week of observation, it's clear Mayene has the talent to excel despite her lackadaisical approach. However, neglecting proper training may eventually limit her abilities. I am determined to surpass this so-called Martial Arts genius.

August 18th \nWe were told to be aware of the Rebels. I've got a plan: I will hide her bag and research report in my locker for safety. This will impress her! Maybe then she'll start noticing me—what a clever plan! \nAugust 19th. The Rebels came. I must...

New Recipes for Cooks to Master 
 
Mushroom Fish Stew 
 
Ingredients: 
A selection of fresh mushrooms, tender bamboo shoots, sliced fish, and a pot of soy milk. 
 
Instructions: 
Slice the fish into thin pieces and marinate them in a mixture of salt and egg for a tender and smooth texture. Wash the mushrooms and bamboo shoots thoroughly. 
 
Heat the pan with onions and ginger, then pour in the soy milk and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer. 
Add various mushrooms and bamboo shoots, cooking until the fragrance fills the air. 
 
Gently add the fish slices and season with spices when they turn white. Serve hot and garnish as desired.
Why are you treating me this way? I didn't report you. That's not what I meant when I spoke...
Strange Stones Ignite the Peaks, shining like the radiant blaze. \nBestowing us unlimited power, to break through any obstacles. \n
The scanning device was set up by a Seeker, which can be activated remotely on hit.
No entry without authorization. Any interference with the item restoration is at your own risk.

Old Yuan is always talking nonstop. From the moment he sits down to the moment he leaves, he can down five whole pots of tea. It wouldn't be so bad if he were young, but for an old man, being that talkative is annoying. No wonder he's still single to this day. Still, he seems quite carefree... \n \nI have to admit, I envy him. Now, I can barely leave the house. I wonder when I'll next see the Honor Tower, see the fruits of his labors over the years...

Beauty is a deadly delight! Controlling puppets or hearts—it's all the same art! Don't miss the premiere! 
 
 
 
"This play was amazing, but now it's time for the curtain call." 
 
 
 
"Could these be messages left by the legendary seniors?" 
 
 
 
"Front row group photo!" 
 
 
 
"I wish I could've seen Master Yango's performance back in Frostcloud Town!" 
 
 
 
"I heard senior Kongming and Zhou Yu once had a musical duel! The crowd stretched from Garden of Delight all the way to the town gates..." 
 
 
 
"Really? My next novel might just take that as its theme!"
The frame of the warrior's drum was assembled using mortise and tenon joints, seems to have been in use for quite some time.
The wondrous things seen in dreams can only endure in the Oneirland.\n\nThe Dreamweavers treasure their woven creations here.
The many Red Falcon Statues in the training hall are a tradition left by the Training Hall. \n \nThey symbolize the close bond between the archers and the falcons.

A weathered long sword seems to have lain here for a long time. 
Upon closer inspection, the name "Yunnie" is carved on it. 
There seems to be another line in tiny font... 
"From where the flute's mournful tune now drifts, 
All night, the guard man gaze homeward through the rift."

The method to unlock the gate remains unclear, but occasional sounds of Mechcraft operation can be heard from the trial area. The Upper Squad has discovered a new cave. We are gathering personnel to expand our exploration to include water bodies in the mountains. The camp must investigate suspected cave locations and keep records.

May 10th, Weather: Warm, I like it. 
 
I'm truly a genius to have changed the author of "Cloudreach Tower Challenge Guide" to Wuyan. If I had put my name on it, no one would have bought it. But with just a slight change, people lined up to buy, and it sold out in no time. This is the power of wisdom. 
 
Tonight, I had another batch of books printed and plan to sell them at the same place tomorrow. I expect them to sell out again. Making money without lifting a finger feels amazing!

Your puzzle is indeed ingenious, but sadly, I'm not interested in playing your little trickies. 
 
I expected you to have left behind some remarkable clues, but surprisingly, they are similar to what I've discovered. Since that's the case, I won't beat around the bush either. This place is not suitable for the Academy to explore, but your trial can serve as the perfect cover. When the time is right, the truth will be revealed. By the way, here's a new gadget for you. I'm not sure what this badge is for, but since you love puzzles and have so much free time, why not give it a try? Also, don't you remember? That Mechcraft Duel was supposed to be counted in sub-rounds!. The overall score between us is already even! 
 
As for the rest... if you really care, come find me in the Three Kingdoms. Choose whatever you want!
Agricultural Mechcraft access point. Please use it as needed. If damaged, it can be repaired at the nearby Craft Society Camp.
From here onward lies the great hall of our people. Guard well the Volcanic Stone Key.
