The art of archery lies in a focused mind and unwavering precision. 
Are you curious about archery, or do you wish to take another step forward? 
If your heart is inclined, give it a try. 
 
 
Hit the mark, and the right opportunities will come your way!

My first encounter with a Blazing Falcon occurred shortly after I joined the Hunter's Society. During a practical lesson in the forest, it suddenly appeared. Its fiery red feathers glistened in the sunlight as it spread its massive wings and let out a cry, leaving us in awe. 
 
Our instructor explained how fortunate we were to witness such a rare creature. From that day on, I set a goal to obtain its red feather, a significant milestone in my studies at Jixia. 
 
Known for its rarity and elusiveness, acquiring its feather not only proves challenging due to its formidable nature but also demonstrates a Hunter's skill. Blazing Falcons are solitary, fiercely territorial, and will confront any threat to their nest without hesitation.
A dazzling crystal. Its mesmerizing hues make it impossible to look away.

Four-eyes: The Bubble Fish's Tear sounds like some kind of potion. Does it extend life or enhance strength? 
 
Muscular speaker: I think the Bubble Fish's Tear might be some kind of Sorcery Artifact that can make the Bubble Fish cry. 
 
Old Three and Four: Four thinks it could be a kind of gemstone, like something you'd mount on a trident that emits light. That sounds plausible! 
 
Intellectual speaker: Yesterday, I saw someone in the village selling pearls called "fish eyes"... Could it be that the Bubble Fish's Tear is just a fancy name for pearls? 
 
The Boss's Sidekick: Anyway, let's figure out how to get it first. Even if it doesn't do anything, it'll at least boost our reputation!

The Jade Heart contains the Jade Pivot, an ancient demonic creation that requires sealing and research.\nDo not enter without permission; <span color="#07AAFFFF">only with immense strength</> can it be opened.

The facility here was intended for researching how to transport goods upstream from Baiming Harbor directly to Jixia Academy. However, the proposed solutions were too expensive, and it was temporarily abandoned. 
 
To prevent people from getting trapped here, the method of using the facility is temporarily recorded here. 
 
Use the <69D0FF>lever switch</> to raise the water level. 
Place the <69D0FF>weight on the raft</> and use the lever switch again to transport the goods to the appropriate position.
The noise from the training hall seems normal. Best to return when it's quieter at night.

After traveling the world for two years, I have returned to Jixia. I once felt as if I were trapped in this tiny corner, longing to explore the world beyond. 
 
Yet, after witnessing breathtaking landscapes and marvels, I have come to realize that it is the sights and sounds of Jixia that I cherish most. 
 
As I delve deeper into the stories of this place and its people, I discover that every brick and tile here holds a legend, and every person has a tale to tell. And I, for one, wish to be the one who shares these stories.

Always prioritize safety with cannons at the night market! 
 
When developing new weapons, consult the experts at the School of Mechcrafts.

For years, my father has always said, "Heaven is fair to every family." 
Take ours, for example: my older brothers — each with their own strengths — are well-behaved and have managed the family business smoothly. That's our good fortune. 
However, the youngest son idles away his days, uninterested in the family trade, and causes trouble wherever he goes, relying on his meager martial skills. That's our misfortune. 
Every time he finishes, my father would cast a meaningful look at me. 
 
Yes, I am the youngest son, but I completely disagree with his sentiment. 
Besides, my martial skills aren't as trivial as he thinks — I've even contributed to the improved safety in Jade City. 
 
One day, while I was dealing with a group of suspicious individuals, our butler hurriedly summoned me back home. 
It turned out my father had a letter for me. 
He explained that it was a letter of introduction, written by a prominent figure in Chang'an whom he had specifically asked for on my behalf. 
This figure, as my father had told me before, was renowned in both Chang'an and Jixia. With this letter in hand, I would have free passage through Jixia. 
"Jixia is full of Training Halls and martial arts masters. Since you're so obsessed with martial arts and have no intention of taking over the family business, why not venture to Jixia? It would keep you from causing us more trouble..." 
My father earnestly advised me before my departure. 
 
Jixia is renowned for martial arts, and I've been fascinated by it since childhood. Armed with my trusty emerald saber, I bade farewell to my father. 
Starting from Alsahraa, I passed through Chang'an, took a ship across the sea, and after many twists and turns, finally arrived in Jixia. 
 
With the letter of introduction in hand, I explored Jixia, enjoying the sights while seeking out martial arts masters. 
After several setbacks, I finally found the Head Trainer of He & Ming's Training Hall — Mr. Bai He. 
I had heard from his disciples that Head Trainer Bai He was as elusive as a crane in the clouds, and despite his status, his whereabouts were often a mystery. 
Some even said his martial skills were as unfathomable as his movements. 
It took quite an effort, but I eventually managed to meet him. Once I stated my intentions, our duel began. 
 
I initially assumed that someone so tranquil would have a gentle and refined fighting style. But in the heat of the duel, he revealed to me the deeper mysteries of martial arts. 
That day, he wore a dark, simple robe, holding a teapot in his hand. As steam rose and curled around his fingers, a gentle breeze brushed past, causing a few strands of hair to graze his cheek. 
When our eyes met, a slight smile appeared at the corner of his eyes, his gaze as serene as distant mountains shrouded in mist, tinged with a deep, dark green. 
I brandished my saber, focusing my grip and launching myself toward him with a side flip. But in an instant, a crisp sound rang out, and I found myself crumpling to the ground, my waist suddenly weak. Meanwhile, Bai He merely took a slight step back, leisurely savoring the scent of his tea, the smile on his lips clearly taunting me. 
You sneaky crane! 
Looking closer, I realized that the crisp sound was his twin blades clashing with my weapon. 
I hadn't even noticed when he had set the teapot down or when those blades appeared in his hands. 
In the following exchanges, I adjusted my tactics, countering his speed with endurance, and using the terrain to fend off his techniques. But in the end, he defeated me so thoroughly that I couldn't help but admire him. 
Though frustrated, I knew I was no match for him. 
Bai He, seemingly calm and collected, was in fact swift and precise in his movements. His blades struck with such speed and force that they were almost imperceptible, as elegant as a white crane. 
Despite my loss, the duel left me exhilarated, a sense of fulfillment I had never felt before. 
But there was one thing that puzzled me — why did his dual-blade technique seem so familiar? 
Years ago, I met a valiant female general in the Central Plains whose blade technique was strikingly similar. 
I asked Bai He if he knew her, but he only smiled and remained silent. 
As we parted, Bai He told me, "Martial arts is a path where all roads lead to the same destination. If you devote yourself to it, one day you will find your answer." 
I am determined to find that answer, for I will see this journey through to the end.

"Tales and Legends of the Fourth School" 
This book is a collection of legends and ghost stories about the "Fourth School" that I, Kongming, came across during my time as a Jixia Student. 
 
 
 
<69D0FF>Kongming's Note: This is a work falsely attributed to me, though it's written with some creativity. It can serve as light reading for idle moments.</> 
 
 
 
1. Immortality 
 
There is a legend in a village on the eastern side of the Jixia Mountains. Many years ago, on the day when the sun was at its highest, two brothers went up the mountain to gather fruit. As they reached the summit, a beam of intense light descended from the sky and enveloped the older brother, causing him to vanish. No trace of him was found for years. 
 
 
 
Many years later, the now white-haired younger brother climbed the mountain again and encountered a person glowing with light. 
 
 
 
Upon returning to the village, he told the villagers that he was certain the glowing person was his brother, who looked just as young as the day he disappeared. 
 
 
 
2. The Stone 
 
Many years ago, a foreigner found himself stranded in Jixia. To survive, he worked for the town's stonemasons. Over the years, he honed his craft and frequently ventured into the distant mountains to quarry stone for the masons. 
 
 
 
One day, he heard a stone speak, asking to be taken home. The foreigner was bewildered and shared the story with the other quarry workers. 
 
 
 
However, the others couldn't hear the voice and dismissed it as the foreigner's imagination. They treated the stone like any other and used it to build a house. 
 
 
 
Not long after, the residents of that house began to hear strange noises, like a voice repeating, 
 
"Take me... home."

"Hey, stop! I give up!" 
"You know, all you can do is defend—you never attack. That means you get beaten up every day, right? That's pretty tough." 
"I passed the entrance exam by a hair... I can barely keep up with daily challenges, and I always turn down sparring invites. If anyone finds out how weak I am, I'm done!" 
"At least you don't mind listening to me complain." 
"Waited around forever! Where were you?" 
"Oh, sorry, coming right away!" 
 
Training Record No. 690. 
Student Info: Nice Guy. 
Skill Level: Class A. 
Record Transcription: 
"It's been eight years now... 
I thought becoming an undercover Rebel in the School of Martial Arts would be my last mission... 
But when I became a top student, got appointed as a teacher by Master Fuzi, everything changed. 
You know what happened last month? I defeated a monster and saved some students—got awarded as Jixia's Hero of the Month and Teacher of the Year... 
Now I'm confused. Am I really a teacher or still a Rebel? 
If you could talk, maybe you'd tell me what to do. 
Yesterday, a student said he wanted to be just like me. But how could I ever reveal who I truly am? 
You're right—I should follow my heart. 
Today, I'll cut ties with the Rebels. Thank you." 
 
Training Record No. 773. 
Student Info: Slacker. 
Skill Level: Class C. 
Record Transcription: 
"This is exhausting... 
I was slacking off yesterday, but then the teacher caught me and made me take a bunch of tests—and I failed them all! 
Luckily, I told him I wanted to grow up to be someone like him, and somehow that worked! Hahaha... 
But what about next time? I wish I could slack off forever..."

这么快就倒了？该向院长申请一个更厉害的机关人了，这完全不尽兴嘛……唉，高手就是如此寂寞，看来，用不了多久，稷下第一高手的名号就是我的了哈哈哈……说不定，到那时全学院都举着我的立牌，就连夫子院长都得敬我三…… 
老师好！没事，我刚练完，在总结一下练习的心得……唉，老师再见，慢走！

啊你别过来啊！我投降！ 
哎这你好像只会招架，不会主动攻击哎……那你每天都要挨打，也太惨了吧…… 
大机关人，我只敢告诉你，我入学考试是擦着线过的……

已经是第八年了…… 
我本以为，考入武道学院做卧底，刺探消息给破门生，我的任务就结束了…… 
可当我成绩名列前茅，被夫子院长接见，随后被任命成老师之后，一切就再也没法回头了。

机关人，你如果会说话，应该能告诉我该怎么做吧？

你说的对，我应该遵从自己的内心。 
我这就和破门生断了联系，谢谢你，机关人。

录入身份信息：咸鱼。 
学员水平：丙。

真累人……

Major Announcement! Full breakdown of the Jixia Academy's 'Dream of the Void' tournament schedule!

Recently, the Jixia Academy's annual marquee event—the Dream of the Void—has arrived as scheduled. This year's tournament continues to be led by the Academy, guided by the core motto 'Truth is told to oneself by oneself,' with assessments held across various regions of Jixia. Through three rounds of testing—Body, Mind, and Sentience—students are encouraged to face themselves and understand who they are.

According to the organizing committee, the Dream of the Void is a signature event held every three years. It consists of three rounds of trials, with specific questions and rules to be officially announced by the Three Sages at the Grand Ceremony. Registration officially opens after the ceremony. After three rounds of intense competition, the final winning team will be crowned.

The first round, the Trial of Body, aims to test students' basic combat abilities and physical limits. By challenging their physical limits through combat, students witness the breakthrough of their own willpower. In previous years, it was held in the Dragon's Sorrow region, where students used a dragon-calling ritual to awaken the residual dragon might within dragon remains. Students had to resist this might to seize the Void Beacon. Only after all team members obtained a beacon could they proceed to the next round.

The second round, the Trial of Mind, takes place in the Dream Realm. This round uses dreams as a medium to test students' character, allowing them to face their true essence. Led by Dean Zhuangzi, students are guided through layers of dreams to confront their desires, obsessions, or fears. The dreams are chaotic and complex; students must recognize their own insignificance within them and rediscover their original intent. Past challenges have included the 'Ring Dream' of facing inner fears and the 'Butterfly Debate' of facing inner desires. Regardless of the form, students must successfully emerge from their inner dilemmas before the entire team can advance to the final round.

The third and final round, the Trial of Sentience, is held in the Colorful Cloud Basin. It is designed to lead students to find the true meaning of self among the masses through team combat. The first two rounds deepen the students' understanding of themselves, while the third round's team competition prevents them from focusing solely on the self. Through tacit understanding and trust with teammates, they naturally realize where their true meaning lies. This round determines the final and only winning team.

The champions, under the guidance of Master Laozi, will have the opportunity to face the Cloud Silkworm and seek enlightenment. As we know, while this reward is tempting, many students participate not for the prize, but to prove themselves and refine their skills. Now, the teams are in the tense final stages of preparation. Let us look forward to the start of this tournament feast and wish all the contestants good luck!

Unofficial Freshman Tips (Version 89, Trial Edition 3)

Fifth, today's you is tomorrow's hero; find your position and persevere with hard work.

When I left home, my wife was pregnant. I never found out if my child is a boy or a girl. I promised her that I would return victorious... 
 
As these thoughts fill my mind, I desert the battlefield tonight, hoping to see my wife and child one last time. 
 
I have come this far and my lamp is dry. As I near my end, I carve these words, hoping my wife and child are safe...

April 9th. I adjusted the temperature, and the second one hatched. Turns out it needed a cold environment. It's a cute little blue creature, and thankfully, the first one doesn't bully it. With their enormous appetites, they're growing up fast... 
 
December 15th. They're getting bigger, and their tempers are becoming volatile. There's not enough food for them. What should I do? I don't want to put the students in danger. Should I leave this place? 
 
December 30th. I have to leave today. It's too dangerous now. They're exactly what I suspected. I'll destroy this report and take them with me. I can't let anything happen to Jixia, though it might already be too late.

When the Seekers first saw this mural, they thought it was a prank. But as the light revealed its weathered stone and faded colors, they realized it was part of the ruins. 
 
The village in the mural is beautiful, with lush greenery. Villagers are gathered around a stone platform, looking fearful as they bow to a Croaky on top. 
 
This mural caused quite a stir among the Seekers. One question puzzled them all: Why would people fear Croakies when they're gentle and have been domesticated for years, surviving by serving humans? 
 
"Could this painting be from before humans domesticated Croakies, when they weren't in their current symbiotic relationship?" 
 
"But the Croaky in the mural is bald, suggesting it's been using its head to carry heavy loads for humans for a long time..." 
 
To uncover the truth, the Seekers consulted Hunters. 
 
"Croakies go bald with age too," explained a Hunter. 
 
"So you're saying they were bowing to an old Croaky?" 
 
"Not just that. Look at the villagers' clothing... Jixia was hotter back then." 
 
"Oh... I get it! Maybe the Croaky could relieve the heat!" 
 
"No, it's the opposite. People were baffled why Croakies thrived despite thick fur coats while humans suffered in the heat." 
 
"..." 
 
"The time this mural was created coincided with Jixia's environmental downturn, during which most Croakies perished. This might be the last one. And look at the villagers' expressions—they're not afraid, but sad." 
 
After much debate, a Seeker offered a more plausible explanation: 
 
"If it's sadness, it makes sense. In early stages of human civilization, people often used reverence to preserve things or beings about to disappear. This Croaky—or rather, Croakies as a species—had always been friends with the villagers. They believed if they channeled everyone's spiritual strength into it, it wouldn't leave like the others." 
 
"But in the end, it still did..." 
 
"This Croaky lives on in this mural, in the nights and days it spent with the villagers, and now in the eyes of you and me who behold this artwork."

Editor's note: The Aercocoon is the source of all things, and diligence is the path to knowledge. 
 
The Aercocoon embodies both form and concept, the root of matter and philosophy. In Jixia, everyone, from children to elders, has a unique understanding and experience of Aersilk, its creation. This free interpretation and widespread exploration of the source of life have made Jixia's philosophy a place of contention among a hundred schools of thought, forever enduring. 
 
For Mechcrafts, Aersilk's high malleability and light texture hold great practical value, while its abundance of Life Particles further increases its affinity with the human body, making it possible for Mechcrafts to spread throughout Jixia. 
 
As a student at the School of Mechcrafts, from the moment you step foot in the school, you must understand one thing: Here, you need to abandon all the common sense you have accumulated. 
 
This does not mean overturning the precious experiences left to us by the past. On the contrary, we hope that every incoming student will stand on the shoulders of giants and look toward even higher mountains. However, it is easy to fall into a trap when learning from past experiences — relying solely on experience, as if every problem has a fixed solution or plan. 
 
No, your life is in your own hands, created by your own two hands. There are no certainties and no limits. As a Mechcraft student, the most important thing is to always keep a heart willing to try, not to give up because of others' words or your own laziness. You must dare to ask questions and doubt, think carefully, constantly uncover the mysteries behind the problems. Do not follow others blindly or trust the ancients without question. You must dare to venture into new fields, dare to climb the peaks, and do not worship so-called authorities. If you hold these beliefs, I believe you will certainly gain something during your time at the School of Mechcrafts. 
 
Remember, the ultimate purpose of any Mechcraft is to serve humanity: To break through human limitations and improve everyone's quality of life. Even if you invent aggressive Mechcrafts, it should be to end conflicts, not to start wars for personal gain. 
 
But human life is short, and your time at the School of Mechcrafts is limited. Here, everyone needs to learn to use Mechcraft inventions and master life skills to increase efficiency and reduce time spent on other tasks. I believe that one day, through the continuous revolution of Mechcrafts, everyone will be freed from trivial matters and have more time to care for and love those around them, ultimately resolving all contradictions and creating a society of "universal love and non-aggression."

All things exist within the universe, interconnected and following their own paths. The heavens cover and the earth carries, complementing each other. From this transformation of things into others and then into what we use, the art of transformation is what Crafters strive for throughout their lives. 
 
The work of a Crafter encompasses various daily aspects such as transportation, architecture, cooking, and clothing. The life of people in Jixia has long been inseparable from Mechcrafts. You can see their shadows everywhere: the Moocart that sells goods, furniture that cleans itself, various insect-control devices, and all kinds of cooking devices that quickly produce delicious meals.... 
 
Crafters have always pursued simplicity and humility, never desiring luxurious clothes or food. They seek to experience the taste of simplicity in simple food and drink, devoting more of their energy to studying inventions, preparing materials for use, creating useful works, and focusing on the art of Mechcrafts. 
 
The simple philosophy of Crafters is not only reflected in their lifestyle but also in the aesthetic of their Mechcrafts. Crafters adhere to the principle of "practicality, simplicity, and durability," avoiding anything superficial or impractical. The numerous new and reliable inventions they develop greatly facilitate the daily life of every household in Jixia. 
 
For example, various agricultural Mechcrafts scattered across Harvest Fields not only help farmers escape from heavy labor but also increase crop yields. There are also various Aersilk Mechcrafts in the mountains, making it easier to travel along steep mountain roads. 
 
I believe that today's Crafters fall into two different categories. One is the "theorists" who emphasize theoretical research and relatively neglect practical operation. The other, which I call the "Artisans," focus more on practice and relatively ignore theory. 
 
In my opinion, these two factions share a common trait: many of them are old-fashioned and stubborn. These Crafters not only lack any spirit of innovation but also love to point fingers and criticize others' works. 
 
Take myself as an example. I once spent years researching and developing an Aquatic Vehicle and showcased it to them, hoping to receive some... if not praise, at least useful feedback. 
 
However, those old-fashioned theorists criticized my invention mercilessly, pointing out structural problems, non-compliance with standards, and violations of regulations. Meanwhile, the Artisans believed that my invention had little practical value and no commendable features. 
 
It wasn't just this one time; my other inventions received similar treatment, constantly being dismissed as useless. This gradually made me realize that many of our current Crafters are losing the pragmatic qualities of our predecessors, becoming bound by various rules and frameworks. This is why they fail to recognize the value of my works. 
 
So, I decided to create a widely applicable encyclopedia that combines theory and practice, tracing the source to clarify my aspirations.

The ancient saying goes: "The earth produces five metals, to be used for the benefit of the world and future generations." From this sentence, we can see that the ancients did not use many metals. However, thanks to the efforts of everyone at the academy, more and more metal materials have been discovered and put to use, and we now have dozens of kinds of metallic materials in common use. 
 
Next, I will talk about some of the most commonly used ores, introduce some of the more common mining and smelting techniques, and compare the advantages and disadvantages of these methods. 
 
These ores are often used in three main areas: weapons, furniture, and other daily necessities. Ores commonly used for weapon forging include Coppervein Stone, Pupil Iron Ore, Azure Iron Ore, Alumine Ore, and others. Others, such as Inkrock, Azurefall Rock, and Violetfall Rock, are often used in furniture production. 
 
Of course, this is not to say that these ores can only be used in these areas. For example, Alumine Ore is also used in lamp manufacturing, while Inkrock is used to produce a variety of stationery. 
 
Ores collected directly cannot be used directly to create artifacts and must undergo smelting. Next, I will introduce two of the most commonly used smelting methods: the Water Infusion Method and the Charcoal Burning Method. In addition to these two methods, there are also the Thermoregulation Method, the Quenching Casting Method, and others, but these methods are usually only suitable for one or a few ores and will not be introduced here one by one. 
 
The Water Infusion Method is simpler. Place the ore in a stone barrel filled with "Restorative Liquid", heat it to a boil, then let it cool, repeat several times, melt the ore, and you're done. 
 
The Charcoal Burning Method involves placing the ore in a furnace containing charcoal for smelting, using the "qi" generated by the charcoal to transform the ore. After that, it needs to be cooled and molded. Some metals also need to be repeatedly hammered to remove impurities, making them easier to use later. 
 
Before smelting metals, carefully choose the method based on the type of ore and its intended use. Although the Water Infusion Method is simpler, many ores cannot be processed by this method, and the purity of the metal produced by this method is lower. 
 
Although the Charcoal Burning Method is more complex, it can be used for more than half of the types of ores, and the purity of the metal produced is higher. When creating special Mechcrafts or buildings, metals produced by the Charcoal Burning Method are often used. 
 
In addition, in pursuit of better performance, some artisans will add Aersilk during forging, but many people do not know the right way to do it. According to my long-term research, Aersilk must be added before forging, and the ratio of Aersilk to metal cannot exceed 1:5 nor be less than 1:10. I once developed an Aersilk alloy that was highly flexible and resistant to breakage, so much so that it could even be used as rope. Impressive, right?

The art of dyeing, once called "Danqing," derives from "Dan" meaning red and "Qing" meaning black—the two most common dye colors. 
 
 
 
Throughout history, people have explored and refined methods to color textiles, leather, and other materials. This pursuit led to various dyeing techniques, generally categorized into two types: extracting natural dyes and creating synthetic dyes. 
 
 
 
Natural dyes are mostly sourced from plants, and many common plants in Jixia can be used, such as Pawpaw, Peach flowers, and Azuregrass. 
 
 
 
The simplest way to produce natural dye is through the "Liquid Extraction Method." This involves cleaning the plant's leaves and stems, placing them in water or another solvent, heating, filtering, and concentrating the solution. 
 
 
 
Most synthetic dyes are by-products of industrial processes. For example, residues from metal smelting can be used as black dye, and some leftover pharmaceutical by-products can also be processed into dyes. 
 
 
 
Next, I'll briefly introduce the craft of ceramics. It starts with selecting the right raw materials—not just any soil will do. To find usable clay, one must dig over two feet deep to locate sand-free clay. Porcelain clay is even rarer, found only in specific areas. 
 
 
 
After preparing the raw materials, the next step is crafting the ceramics. Pottery is relatively simple: shape the clay into a cylindrical form, adjust the size as needed, spin it on a pottery wheel, refine the shape, and then fire it. 
 
 
 
Porcelain crafting is more difficult, often requiring two or more types of clay. Before shaping, the porcelain clay is placed in a vat, mixed with water, and allowed to settle. I've traveled across the entire continent, but my heart remains in that one night. 
 
It was a night by the campfire in a cave where I met a group of fascinating people. They laughed, chatted, and shared their shiny Cirroflow Cards with each other. 
 
I was drawn to their camaraderie, and it was during that gathering that I became a Panoramist and met Adong. 
 
Adong didn't say much—his eyes seemed to be fixated on the beautiful Cirroflow Cards. 
 
"The cards hold many stories," he told me. 
 
Since then, I've been to many places, sending Adong a few handmade Cirroflow Cards along the way, and he sent me his in return. 
That's how Panoramists connected. 
 
 
 
One day, I received a letter from a fellow Panoramist, saying they had gone to the marsh for fieldwork and were attacked by the Giant Saepes.  
Everyone made it back except Adong. 
 
I went to the marsh and searched the area for days but found no trace of him. 
 
A few days later, a messenger handed me a sparkling Cirroflow Card, and I recognized it—it was the Crazed Tree. 
 
Could this be Adong's work? 
 
Eventually, I found him. That day, he had escaped the Giant Saepes' attack, studied it, and crafted a brand-new Cirroflow Card, which he sent to me. 
 
I felt a surge of emotion, with so many words unsaid. But in the end, I only managed to say, 
 
"Don't forget our deal—let's keep exchanging the cards, okay?"

As the saying goes, "A craftsman must sharpen his tools to do his job well." This highlights the importance of tools in daily work, especially for crafters who rely on diverse and efficient instruments. 
 
Let's start with basic tools like hammers and files. The hammer, regarded as the "fist" of crafters, is indispensable for tasks ranging from furniture-making to repairs.  
 
The file, a refining assistant, smoothens and polishes materials like metal and wood.  
 
Precision knives, the most versatile tools for artisans, come in two types: one emits concentrated energy for cutting hard materials, while the other uses sharp metal blades for carving and general cutting. These tools are vital in mechanical crafting. 
 
Measuring instruments like rulers, cauldrons, and scales are equally crucial. Rulers gauge length, cauldrons measure volume, and scales determine weight. Choosing the right tool ensures accuracy, as "a tiny error can lead to massive mistakes." 
 
Auxiliary mechcrafts also play key roles. Mecharm assist with dangerous or complex tasks—some combat-ready, others dismantle mechanisms, transport items, or retrieve forged metal from furnaces. Protective goggles shield eyes from debris, while specialized variants block intense light or analyze materials. 
 
Aersilk tools deserve special mention. Despite gradual adoption by some crafters, their popularity still lags behind traditional tools. I believe these crafters are overly conservative—they should embrace innovations. 
 
For instance, Aersilk saw cut common materials with precision far surpassing traditional saws. Recently, a new Aersilk Mecharm emerged, adjustable in thickness and length, proving highly practical. 
 
I once proposed a theft-proof portable backpack with an Aersilk energy device that activates a protective shield upon detecting unauthorized access. Such a brilliant idea, yet ignored! Those stubborn, old-school crafters who dismiss innovation—You'll regret it sooner or later.

By the time I reached the peak of Aerfall Highlands, it was already afternoon. The wind brushed against my face, carrying away the sweat on my skin. Looking down from above, clouds drifted across the sky, and sunlight filtered through their gaps, casting dappled shadows over the mountains and rivers below. 
 
Over these past few days, I've been wandering like a restless child, tireless in my travels from bustling Horizon Harbor to towering mountain peaks. Though my spirit remains high, my body is soaked in sweat. 
 
Along the way, a student in academy uniform noticed my heavy footsteps and offered to help carry some of my load. Unable to refuse such kindness, I handed him the heaviest package. To my surprise, he effortlessly leaped up the stone steps, saying he'd wait for me ahead—only to vanish without a trace. After chasing after him for half a day, I finally found both him and my luggage. "We're used to hiking with loads, so we move quickly. Sorry about that..." He scratched his head in apology. 
 
A few days after thanking and parting ways with him, I finally arrived at Aerfall Highlands. Legend has it that this place was once an ancient battlefield, with many ruins still scattered throughout the valleys and caves. A group known as the Seekers spends years exploring and studying here in search of traces of the past. As I climbed the peak, I met a group of them complaining about today's poor "harvest." 
 
As dusk approached, half of the sun's golden disk sank behind distant mountain ridges. The cool breeze from above chilled my damp skin, causing me to shiver involuntarily. 
 
The evening wind grows stronger, swaying the trees like waves on a green sea. 
The leaves turn yellow, autumn arrives with frost. 
Summer gives way to winter, cycles come and go; if trees endure, how can humans not? 
Perhaps my own life has also entered its season of decline.

A volume of "The Encyclopedia of Wood-Walkers" written by Muping, a hunter from Jixia, documenting methods for communicating with Wood-Walkers.

Wood-Walkers are highly territorial and usually unfriendly to outsiders, but this doesn't mean they cannot be reasoned with—at least the smaller ones can.
First, small Wood-Walkers understand simple body language. Do not carry weapons; show them your empty hands to signal you have no hostile intent. Here are a few simple gestures:
Cup your hands around your cheeks and look up to ask, "Is your sky clear?" For Wood-Walkers who love the sun, this is a greeting.
Place your hands on your hips and hop once to the left, then once to the right to ask, "How are you today?" If the Wood-Walker repeats the action, it means they are happy; if they raise their hands and drop them, they are unhappy.
Place your hands in a cat-claw shape in front of your temples and lean your neck forward to say, "I want to pass." If the Wood-Walker moves aside, they agree; if they stay put, they refuse, and you had best take another route.
There are many more, and if you wish to learn further, come find me at the Academy. Finally, if you are too lazy to learn and don't want to detour around Wood-Walker camps, there is another trick I heard from the locals in Jixia: most small Wood-Walkers have a bit of OCD and feel compelled to clean up anything spilled on the ground. You can carry some melon seeds or beads, toss them on the ground, and stroll right past while they are busy picking them up (don't feel embarrassed; small Wood-Walkers love collecting these trinkets).

Another way is to communicate using 'Floral Language.' Certain special flowers, fruits, and fungi hold specific meanings for small Wood-Walkers. We call these 'Floral Language.' You can place these items on the ground before them to express your intentions. Known Floral Language includes:
Rock-Cymbal Grass: Thank you.
Butterfly-Lure Flower: Hello.
Phantom-Butterfly Flower: Blessings to you.
Step-Color Mushroom: I understand how you feel, little mushroom (a hug).
Heavenly Peach: Goodbye.

Additionally, placing a Cloud-Pattern Beast Claw in front of a small Wood-Walker while holding your palms upward signifies, "We have a common enemy; we are friends." If they take it, it means they bear you no ill will.

Note: There is one thing you must never bring out in front of a Wood-Walker: a Fresh-Bathed Twig. These drop from plant-based creatures, mostly from defeated Wood-Walkers. Showing a Fresh-Bathed Twig to a Wood-Walker is an act of war, and they will fight you to the death.

Annotation: I, Muping, the hunter who knows Wood-Walkers best, am currently researching a third method: using naturally shed Wood-Walker bark and leaves collected from crawling on the ground to craft a realistic Wood-Walker costume! Theoretically, wearing this suit should allow one to blend perfectly into a Wood-Walker community for close-range observation. Although the field test results for the first prototype were... less than ideal, I have absolute confidence!

Annotation (Herbalist): To the reader, after student Muping performed his first field test in the costume, he used up my six-month supply of external bruise ointment to recover. Please exercise caution.

Regardless of the method you use, the primary secret to communicating with Wood-Walkers is sincerity. Don't think of them as mindless creatures; in fact, Wood-Walkers can judge from subtle body movements whether someone is truly sincere or has ulterior motives. If they encounter someone who genuinely wants to be friends, a small Wood-Walker may rarely bloom—but only a single flower on its head.

According to ancient Jixia legends, this is a flower grown from the Wood-Walker's own life, representing its heart. Only those with pure hearts and no evil intentions can cause a Wood-Walker to grow such a flower, which they will carry with them always. When their life is nearing its end, they will come to their human friend's doorstep under the cover of night, place the flower on the lintel, and quietly depart.

If the human friend has already passed away, the Wood-Walker will place the flower at their burial site. Miraculously, they always find the right place.

Though it is just a legend, it is truly romantic.

Editor's note: There are no born geniuses; true mastery comes from repeated reflection, practice, and refinement.

Silk cocoons have lower gum content, resulting in poorer tenacity, making them unsuitable for use as fiber materials in Mechcrafts. In developing silk fibers and their products, Mechsmiths ultimately discovered the similarities and differences between Aersilk and silkworm silk, and through experimentation, formulated various hybrid recipes. This greatly expanded the scope of Mechcrafts while reducing development and usage costs, effectively extending its reach into everyday life.

These notes are compiled from records in the library. While reviewing the research findings of predecessors, I became particularly interested in the mentioned proportions of Aersilk. Both Aersilk and common silkworm silk serve as connectors and control mediums in Mechcrafts. The incorporation of Aersilk enhances the solidity and maneuverability of Mechcrafts. At that time, the application of Aersilk was not as widespread as it is today, so blending silk threads was a reasonable approach. However, with Aersilk now ubiquitous in daily life, why do critical Mechcrafts, such as the Mechanoid Bird designed for cargo transport, still contain mixtures of ordinary silk or even older wooden joints in their materials?

At the time, Mr. Wei simply asked me to get a spare Mechanoid Bird from the parts artisan. I replaced many of its materials with Aersilk based on my own insights, then carefully recalculated and tested it before handing it over. Watching it soar gracefully under the eaves, performing sharp turns and mid-air suspensions beyond its original design capabilities, filled me with pride. Seeing Mr. Wei nod in approval as he watched, I felt recognized and ideas for at least three research papers popped into my head.

But what followed was a harsh lesson. Mr. Wei excused me from a week of classes, allowing me to leave Jixia with my improved Mechanoid Bird to broaden my horizons. Not fully understanding but eager nonetheless, I set off immediately. To my surprise, as the distance from Jixia grew, the Mechanoid Bird, which had been flying steadily above my head, began to shudder as if struggling to stay aloft, eventually crashing to the ground with a broken wing. Dismayed, I returned to visit Mr. Wei with its fragments, and only then did he explain leisurely: once away from Jixia, Aersilk gradually loses its vitality—a fundamental yet often overlooked principle; blindly pursuing technological advancements disconnected from practical contexts often leads to disastrous outcomes after fleeting successes.

Based on my research, I believe the operation principle of the Aersilk picker is not complicated. It simply collects scattered Aerflow and converts it into Aerpower Chips. 
 
There are two pieces of direct evidence: First, the concentration of Aersilk particles in the air here is higher than in other areas. And when we place it far from the Tower of Enlightenment, it stops functioning. Second, I noticed that of two Aersilk picker placed at different distances from the Tower of Enlightenment, the one farther away has a slightly lower collection efficiency than the other. Of course, the difference is very slight. 
 
Though the principle is not complex, the true genius of the creator lies in their ability to design appropriate Mechcrafts that utilize environmental differences. Their designs are both ingenious and practical. This creator truly deserves the title of master.

Day 1: 
I observed the stars from a high vantage point at sunset and saw a beautiful pair of twin stars—one orange and the other blue. 
 
Day 2: 
The sky was slightly darkened by clouds, and the view was blurred due to high humidity. I could barely see the faint Polaris, so I decided to return. 
 
Day 3: 
The visibility was even worse than the previous day. A faint globular star cluster briefly twinkled before being completely obscured by dust, leaving the sky pitch black. 
 
Day 4: 
The sky was dim, but after midnight, the clouds dispersed, revealing a bright sky filled with twinkling stars. I wandered through the Milky Way. 
 
Day 5: 
A meteor shot across the sky, passing by Alioth, creating a brief and bright moment before disappearing in an instant. 
 
Day 6: 
The bright moon illuminated Springbrook Plains. The stars were bright and clear, with an apple-shaped nebula in the center of the sky. 
 
Day 7: 
The sun and moon shone together, and Alkaid appeared small and bright in the morning glow. 
 
My mentor instructed me to observe the stars for seven days, following the ancient tradition, without using the observatory. I was puzzled but followed the instructions. On the first day, I found it fascinating. However, the following days were challenging, with cold, hunger, and poor visibility. Despite this, I persevered. 
 
After a period of despair, the beauty of the vast starry sky suddenly filled me with awe. I had an epiphany and understood my mentor's intentions. Stargazing is like the practice of Sorcery. In the beginning, rapid progress is made, and small achievements are accomplished. In the middle stage, darkness and obscurity lead to despair. However, by quieting the mind and persisting in the path, one can eventually reach a state of sudden enlightenment and rebirth, achieving great success.

Recently, a senior sent us two carts of components for the Mechcraft parts of Cloudreach Tower, ordering us to decipher it within five days.  
 
Day 3 
The parts were seamlessly interlocked, nearly impossible to disassemble. Today, we finally managed to dismantle them without compromising the internal structure. Inside, intricate components interlocked with such precision that I began doubting whether this Mechcraft could truly be deciphered at all. 
 
Day 5 
The deadline arrived. Yet, we had only grasped the design logic of the Cloudreach Tower's Mechcraft. To fully unravel and control it? Time was far from sufficient...

The "Sparks of Creation" column continues to explore the interesting and unexpected tales of everyday life, bringing countless inventions to readers. Creativity isn't the exclusive domain of scholars; with a curious and courageous heart, anyone can be an inventor. 
 
 
 
"The crackling of fireworks marks the year's demise, as the spring breeze warms the Tusu wine before our eyes. A thousand doors bask in the sun's first glow—Hey! Foxtail Wheat, are you cooked or no?" 
 
 
 
Nearly every child goes through a phase of mischievously altering classic poems. Those complex verses, memorized by rote from textbooks, often get humorously twisted into silly rhymes shared among friends, giving a subtle thrill of rebellion. However, such childish antics usually fade with age, becoming buried memories. If brought up later, one might blush and sheepishly explain it away. 
 
 
 
Every morning at the crack of dawn, Guanhe could be found at the door of his small workshop, stretching and humming indistinct nursery rhymes. Passing children loved to greet him, and though he would respond with a shy smile, he never spoke. Instead, he'd pull out a handful of sugar-coated barley from his pocket, offering it as a crunchy snack. Only after seeing the kids off would he leisurely open the workshop door and begin his day's work. From a young age, Guanhe was never what adults considered a "smart child." Poems had to be read to him ten times before they stuck, and even then, he'd sometimes recall them entirely wrong. But when it came to food or fashion, he had his own distinct taste. 
 
 
 
The round-bellied machine sat quietly in the center of the room, waiting for its lookalike, the chubby Guanhe, to pull the lever and start it up. The sugar-coated barley wasn't just in his pocket; sacks of it were neatly stacked around the room, filling the air with a faint, sweet aroma. While waiting for the popcorn machine to warm up, Guanhe would recite a little rhyme, shyly smiling as if performing some ritual. The machine would then let out a puff of steam, perfectly timed with the rhyme's cadence—a coincidence or perhaps a clever design? 
 
 
 
People grew up eating rice made from Foxtail Wheat, so much so that the scent of wheat had become ingrained in their blood. Guanhe, in particular, loved rice balls, eating half as a child and two as an adult. When he was sent to Jixia Academy to study, he channeled all his efforts into food research. He couldn't stand how his peers and teachers sacrificed enjoyment for efficiency, so he threw himself into studying cannons, determined to show his family—and the world—the potential of Mechcrafts and the value of his passion. 
 
 
 
When placing plump Foxtail Wheat on the stove, if he wasn't careful, the heat could cause a small explosion in the iron pot, leaving a few charred grains. These scorched wheat kernels, which should've been tossed in the trash, were secretly chewed by Guanhe. Beneath the bitter burnt taste, he found an aroma even more fragrant than cooked rice. Emboldened, he persuaded a friendly gourmet to sell him a well-crafted large pot, which he eagerly brought back to his workshop for tireless experimentation. 
 
 
 
Now on its sixth iteration, Guanhe's popcorn machine had come a long way. The original prototype, wrapped in floral cloth, was carefully stored in the corner of the room. After sufficient preheating, the machine's round belly could maintain an even temperature. Once the heat indicator light dimmed, a small side door could be opened to add in blocks of congealed resin. Made from pine resin and fats, these blocks, mixed with sugar, melted into a golden, sweet-smelling pool under the heat. When the indicator light came back on, it was time to pour in a full measure of Jihu Barley. As the control system steadily heated the furnace, the barley first let out a few tentative pops before bursting into a full-blown crackle, eventually quieting down. 
 
 
 
Unfortunately, since Guanhe hadn't yet mastered the precise relationship between temperature and popping, not every batch of Foxtail popcorn turned out perfect. The carefully prepared sugar often clumped together, some parts too sweet while others remained bland. The popped wheat was often misshapen, with a few stubborn kernels refusing to pop, leaving their husks charred while the insides stayed undercooked. A frequent visitor, the Naughty Civet, seemed to have a sweet tooth and often snuck a pawful to snack on. But Guanhe wasn't discouraged. He filled one notebook after another, and on the last page, he jotted down a new sugar-fat ratio, with the addition of strawberries turning it a delightful pink. 
 
 
 
Perhaps, someday, restaurants in Harvest Fields would serve a signature snack called "Popcorn Delight," available in a variety of colors and flavors. And Guanhe would continue to hum softly to his endlessly refined popcorn machine, as if chatting with an old friend: "Foxtail Wheat, are you cooked or no?"

Lin,

Something's been worrying me, so I have to write and remind you. Contraption Master was seriously injured when he came to hide the key recently. I asked around, and everyone thinks his injury was a result of his research backfiring.

Horizon Lantern offers a platform for Cannoneers to express emotions and thoughts. We focus on your discoveries and listen to your stories. In this ever-changing world, we are always here. 
 
When cold winds frost the windows and cats refuse to venture out, I know winter has arrived. 
 
Do people truly love winter? With bare trees and frozen flowers, many wish to hide their hands in sleeves until spring. The sun rarely appears, and when it does, its warmth depends on the north wind. Adults have learned to cope with the cold, breathing on their hands before continuing their work. 
 
Year by year and day by day, we become essential cogs in the grand Mechcraft of life. Children, not yet burdened with responsibilities, either cling to warm beds or eagerly play in the snow. Between these two extremes, I often feel a disconnect: too old for carefree games, yet unwilling to numb my feelings. So I watch, until adults close their stalls and children return home, the sun disappearing behind the mountains. 
 
It's known that despite heavy snowfall, the Glowworm Square remains relatively clear due to constant activity. Both leisurely travelers and busy students stop here to rest and pass time. Recently, with some festival approaching, the cleared snow has been piled into small snow mountains in corners; meanwhile, tofu-like blocks have been outlined in the previous snowy areas, and after a few days, various flourishing stalls have sprouted like mushrooms. 
 
These stalls aren't always attended; often, they're just covered goods left with drifting snow. Only at night do people arrive as if summoned, filling the square with laughter and debates that melt the ice between happiness and heartache. 
Red, yellow, and warm lanterns are raised high, while new snowflakes drift silently from the sky. Sometimes I think that in another life, I'd want to be rain nourishing the earth or thin snow promising a bountiful year. But even the lightest rain makes a sound, while falling snow is silent. It drifts without considering those who complain of the cold, nor does it care if children hide or cheer; it falls until it touches the bright world. 
 
As night deepens, the sounds of selling and bargaining grow more lively. Under the snow and lights, goods change hands, leaving both parties with unerasable smiles. A thunderclap surprises everyone, but only children laugh and point at the sky. The fireworks launched by vendors create a spectacle that attracts more spectators. 
 
The wrapped goods will soon reveal their beautiful colors in the hands of adults and children—like falling meteors, burning bouquets, shining lights, and fireworks. After echoing through the sky, they become tributes from the mortal world to the heavens.

Academy Observatory — Sunny 
 
Wanting to add some novel elements to the academy observatory for a change, I brought Luban No. 7 along here.

It's said that the Harvest Brew from this brewery wasn't always so popular. 
 
Everyone thought it tasted strange—just one sip of its sour bitterness could travel from your mouth straight to your stomach. People claimed it was a failed brew, and even the brewery owner couldn't hide her disappointment after tasting it. 
 
The backyard of the brewery soon piled up with unsold bottles, their odd smell noticeable from afar, causing workers to sneeze as they passed by. 
 
But then, as if fate intervened, one morning a rich, malty aroma filled the air. 
 
No longer harsh, but instead carrying a intoxicating floral scent mixed with herbs. Combined with the original grain aroma, it felt like stepping into the Harvest Fields, where seasons changed in a breath and crops grew amidst blooming flowers and fading grasses. 
 
Where did such a mystical scent come from? Could it be an immortal blessing or a miracle visiting the brewery? 
 
With these fantasies in mind, everyone followed the fragrance, eagerly pushing open the yard gate. 
 
But what awaited them were just scattered jars—and a Naughty Civet who had slept peacefully through the night inside. 
 
There was no blessing from the gods, nor any miracles. 
 
Only a Naughty Civet who enjoyed savoring fine drinks. 
 
Perhaps drawn by the taste, it snuck in at night. The unguarded backyard became its playground, where it happily drank from various jars. 
Its small pouch, full of dried fruits and herbs it had collected, spilled its contents into the liquid. 
 
After a night of fermentation, a miraculous reaction occurred within the once bitter and acidic drink. 
 
The crowd gasped in surprise, finally waking the Naughty Civet. 
 
Stretching and opening its eyes, it found dozens of eyes staring directly at it. 
 
Looking around at the messy scene, realizing it had caused trouble, the Naughty Civet leaped away before the owner could say a word. 
 
This fragrance wasn't a gift from the gods, but rather a coincidence courtesy of a mountain sprite. The brewery owner carefully preserved the lost pouch and studied it, using it as a starting point to explore the flora and herbs of the Harvest Fields. 
Over time, the brewery, aided by generations of research and refinement, eventually crafted a world-renowned brew—the now-famous Harvest Brew. 
 
Today, a sign still hangs at the brewery entrance offering free drinks to Naughty Civets. 
 
But can a Naughty Civet really read signs?

"When the energy runs wild," the chief pressed, "will it not surge a hundredfold fiercer? Is this not quenching thirst with poison?" 
 
"Before that day," the Sage assured, "the Dream-Destined One shall appear. The instability of Oneiric Energy will unravel like tangled silk." 
 
"Who in this world knows dreams better than you?" the Chief challenged. "If even you cannot control it, what mortal could?" 
 
"Each soul walks a fated path." The Sage's voice held moonlit certainty. "Saving the Oneirland requires karmic convergence – a thread not woven into my tapestry. The Dream-Destined One need not be a master of Sorcery but must carry three virtues: courage as unflinching as mountains, sincerity as clear as glacial streams, and strength tempered in the crucible of tribulation." 
 
"Zhuangzi," the Chief murmured, "such heroes live only in legends. Are these not empty words to placate my clan?"

I would like to extend my gratitude to all who have read thus far. As the editor of this book, I, Mozi, have received manuscripts from all over Jixia since taking over the revision of this series. They come from teachers who toil diligently at the Academy, children who arrive with dreams in their hearts, alumni who have made their mark in various fields after graduation, and even village folk who may not be learned but possess an innate understanding of Mechcraft. Through these diverse contributions, I have caught glimpses of the vibrant, thriving world of Mechcraft unique to Jixia. 
 
While the School of Martial Arts and the School of Sorcery strengthen students' bodies and minds, the School of Mechcraft enriches life in Jixia through subtle innovations in daily living. Martial Arts students hone their physique before delving into theory; Sorcery students immerse themselves in literature before exploring doctrine; Mechcraft students, on the other hand, blend theory and practice, merging imagination with execution. Each new student to the School of Mechcraft is greeted with a single principle: knowledge comes from putting ideas into action. 
 
This volume tells the stories of two Mechcraft students—Su Qing and Song Tuantuan. Though they are from different generations and their stories were submitted years apart, together they illustrate the journey of learning within the School of Mechcraft. No matter how erudite a Mechsmith may become—even myself, the founder of the School of Mechcraft—all begin by dismantling a single, simple Mechcraft die, progressing from there to grasp the intricacies of each component through hands-on experience. By the time this book was compiled, Song Tuantuan was still grappling with the concept of "non-aggression," while Su Qing had long since set out into the vast expanse of the world beyond the Academy.  
 
Meanwhile, villagers have begun using more practical and portable Mechcraft devices, and Mr. Guo Rongfu has become a powerful ally for Mechsmiths in the study of agricultural tools, having "made friends" with the Academy through a few rounds of sparring. Anyone who has visited Jixia Academy will surely remember the array of transportation devices—Mechcraft skeletons capable of carrying a person up a staircase are no common sight. Indeed, until the joint research findings of Li Ru and Teacher Wei Min were published, even natives of Jixia had never imagined their lives could become so convenient. 
 
Every step forward in Mechcraft is built upon countless failures and setbacks. However, true Mechsmiths understand that innovation only holds meaning when combined with practice, lest it remain forever idle. Perhaps some might view the School of Mechcraft as indolent; allow me to offer my defense: behind the trivialities of life managed by Mechcrafts stand the figures of Mechsmiths, fighting tirelessly day and night; efficiency is the eternal theme woven throughout both practice and true knowledge.

Editor's Note: Music flows through the river of time, connecting souls across eras. Yet shifting aesthetic values may obscure the original meaning carried solely by melody. Herein lies the power of lyrics, as words can directly channel the creator's intent. Only when beautiful melodies are paired with thoughtful lyrics can a piece truly resonate with listeners. 
 
The following is an excerpt from Master Mo Li's lecture: 
 
Ladies and gentlemen at Cloudreach Tower, today I'd like to talk about composition and lyric writing. 
 
First, let's understand what composition entails. Composition is the process of creating music, involving the arrangement of melody, harmony, rhythm, and timbre. A skilled Musician will first arrange scales into groups of notes, then have various instruments perform these notes in perfect coordination. Only then can a piece of music with graceful melodies, harmonious accompaniment, and captivating timbre be produced. 
 
So, what about filling in lyrics? Filling in lyrics involves adding suitable words to a composed song. This requires considering the melody's flow, rhythmic changes, and the song's theme and emotion. According to the Musicians' standards, overly elaborate language is not preferred. Good lyrics should accurately convey the song's message and enhance its beauty. 
 
For a Musician to create good music, both lyrics and melody are indispensable. There's a story that has been passed down among the Musicians. Kongming and Zhou Yu were both prominent figures at Jixia Academy, and their talents extended far beyond martial arts or sorcery. 
 
Legend has it that one day, Kongming and Zhou Yu met by chance at Garden of Delight. Encouraged by the surrounding students, they decided to compete. Kongming played a melody he had composed, a piece so melodious and enchanting that Zhou Yu was deeply moved, though he refused to admit it openly. The students urged Zhou Yu to write lyrics to prove his talent. Zhou Yu accepted the challenge and wrote lyrics based on Kongming's melody. The lyrics described the grandeur of Jixia's landscapes and sincere emotions, leaving Kongming astonished. Subsequently, Zhou Yu showcased his compositional skills, playing a spirited and stirring melody. Kongming was also deeply touched and responded by writing lyrics for this piece. 
 
As they alternated between composition and lyrics, each inspired the other creatively, filling the Garden of Delight with music for days. While everyone wanted to argue over who excelled in lyrics or melody, their collaborative work spoke for itself. In the end, the observing students realized that composition and verse are two sides of the same coin, inseparable in spirit. Only when both unite in harmony can a masterpiece truly stir the soul. While the tale's historical accuracy remains unverified, its message endures, echoing through the halls of the academy to this day. 
 
Composition resembles painting a picture with outlines and colors, giving music its initial form and vitality. Without a compelling melody and harmony, even the most exquisite lyrics would remain hollow words. Lyric writing, on the other hand, is akin to adding delicate brushstrokes and soul to the painting. It gives music concrete imagery and emotional depth. When both elements combine, only then can a perfect artwork emerge—beautiful in form and profound in meaning. 
 
Whether it's composition or lyric writing, one must possess a deep understanding of life and emotions, coupled with boundless love and pursuit of musical art. Only then can we craft pieces that genuinely touch hearts, allowing listeners to experience the endless charm and power of music during every performance.

text: I don't want to repeat myself. This hole was dug years ago out of necessity. If you're not in trouble, please leave it alone. Thanks.
The view here is breathtaking. After overcoming the challenges to get here, it's time to take a moment to rest and enjoy the scenery.

I have confirmed that this is where the Nightmare Weaver placed the nightmare. I have come to investigate the truth about that shipwreck and have ventured into the Evernull Forest for it. I'm not sure what I'll encounter next, but if anything happens to me, I hope this letter can provide some useful information.

Northeast side, 2 horizontal and 2 vertical, Enchanter, looking around and scratching their head, remembering once.

I fear this first exam will be my last.
After the results are posted, those who pass will head to the battlefield.
I can see all the students are ready for action.
How splendid!
When drumbeats slow, pull oars below; When the rhythms race, hoist sails with grace. \nAt silence dread, hold fast ahead; Till drums resound, press homeward bound.

These days, a girl named Mayene arrived in our village. 
 
It was impossible not to notice her. Though I spend my days tending to the old bell and rarely meddle in village affairs, her name seemed to echo through the village a thousand times a day from all the chaos she caused. 
 
Yet surprisingly, this little troublemaker came bustling to my door after some villagers told her about the blessing rituals. 
 
Stranger still, while local children yawn at such tales, this girl listened with burning curiosity. But I've seen this kind of person before, today they're enthralled by ancient legends, tomorrow they'll be frolicking on some mountain peak, forgetting all about rituals and traditions. So I gave her only the bare bones of the ceremonial procedures. If her interest proves true, she'll return. 
 
Last night, they say she pestered the master baker all night learning to make Harvest Pancake. Whether the bread turns out edible, or whether Mayene patience lasts longer than a mayfly's lifespan... well, we'll see.

Congratulations to student Zhong Wuyan for winning the championship of this Cloudreach Tower Climbing Competition. 
 
In this competition, Zhong Wuyan adopted a completely different tactic from the others. Facing various cumbersome and tricky mechanisms, she showed no fear, skillfully operating her giant hammer, spinning it at times and bravely charging forward at others. All these elaborately designed mechanisms were smashed to pieces under the fierce attacks of her hammer, truly showing how brute force overcomes all techniques. Zhong Wuyan easily swept the competition and claimed the top spot. 
 
This victory set the biggest record since the inception of the competition—the record for causing the most damage. The craftsmen responsible for repairs were busy for three days and three nights to repair all the damaged mechanisms. 
 
As of the writing of this article, this record remains unbroken.

Chapter 1: Dress Code 
Before inviting a Leafy Slumberstone to dance, it's essential to wear the right attire. Leafy Slumberstone think their dance partners should wear a grass skirt woven from fresh leaves, preferably from the Swaying Shrub, though Fish Fruit branches are also acceptable. The skirt should be embellished with ancient vines across the upper body and Skirtleaf Flower at the hem. Avoid using the Bitewood, as it may incite a battle rather than a dance. Headwear should be a hat carved from Orchid Stone, ideally made from bright-colored rock materials to keep the Leafy Slumberstone from becoming drowsy. 
 
Chapter 2: Basic Etiquette 
Many fail to understand the proper etiquette when inviting a Leafy Slumberstone to dance, often ending up as its pillow instead of its dance partner. Never disturb a resting Leafy Slumberstone with loud noises. Instead, find one in the wild and gently sweep its hard head with a branch from the Flutterbloom. According to renowned Hunter Cincin, removing moss from its head about 1,200 times should awaken it. If it doesn't stand and roar in anger, congratulations, your dance invitation has been accepted. Otherwise, retreat promptly, or wait for a passing Hunter to rescue you. 
 
Chapter 3: Dance Rhythm 
When a Leafy Slumberstone is in a dance state, it will remain motionless. As its approved dance partner, sit in front of it, gently sway the stone-carved hat on your head, while extending and swinging your arms like freely growing wild grass. If the beast's gaze follows your movements, the dance has commenced. The choice of dance steps should then be guided by how you twist your neck, but avoid shaking your shoulders or lowering your head. If the hat falls off, leave immediately. Otherwise, maintain your posture unchanged until the Slumberstone Beast closes its eyes again.

Chapter 1: Dress Code
Before inviting a Sleepstone Beast to dance with you, appropriate attire is required. For a Sleepstone Beast, its dance partner should wear a grass skirt woven from fresh grass leaves, with the upper body adorned with ancient vines. The Sleepstone Beast particularly prefers its dance partner to choose branches and leaves of the Guisui tree to weave the grass skirt. Of course, Zhiyun wood is also a good choice, and if paired with swaying skirt leaves as skirt decorations, that would be even better. But remember not to choose split-fruit wood, or you will kick off a storm-like battle instead of completing an elegant dance. Headwear is best styled as a hat carved from cloud-ball stone; do not choose dull-colored rock materials, as this will make the Sleepstone Beast feel extremely drowsy.

Chapter 2: Basic Etiquette
Many people do not understand the invitation etiquette for dancing with a Sleepstone Beast, often resulting in people turning into their beloved pillows rather than dance partners. First, disturbing a resting Sleepstone Beast and shouting or urging it to wake up and dance with you is strictly discouraged. The correct method is to first find a sleeping Sleepstone Beast in the wild, then use a Zhanchi wood branch to sweep across its hard crown. According to the practical experience of well-known ranger Hu Qianqian, continuously clearing the moss on its head about twelve hundred times will successfully awaken the Sleepstone Beast. If it does not stand up and roar angrily at you, then congratulations, your dance invitation has been successfully accepted. Otherwise, you should leave as soon as possible, or else you can only wait for passing rangers to rescue you from its embrace.

Chapter 3: Dance Rhythm
A Sleepstone Beast that enters a dancing state will not move, and you, as its recognized dance partner, should sit gracefully before it, gently shaking the stone-carved hat on your head, with your arms naturally extended and swaying like a freely growing wild grass. If the Sleepstone Beast's gaze follows your movements, it means it has begun dancing with you. At this point, the choice of dance steps depends on how you twist your neck, trying your best not to shake your shoulders. In addition, never lower your head. If the stone-carved hat falls off, you should leave immediately; otherwise, keep your posture completely unchanged and wait for the Sleepstone Beast to close its eyes again.

第一章 着装要求  
在邀请一只眠石兽与你共舞之前，需要穿着合适的服装。对眠石兽来说它的舞伴应该穿有新鲜草叶编织的草裙，上身饰有古老的藤蔓。眠石兽尤其中意它的舞伴选择桂岁木的枝叶来编织草裙，当然织云木也是不错的选择，如果能搭配摇裙叶作为裙摆的装饰，那就再好不过了。但是切记不要选裂果木，否则你将掀起一场狂风骤雨般的战斗，而不是完成一支优雅的舞蹈。头饰以云球石雕刻的帽子为佳，不要选择颜色黯淡的岩石材料，这会让眠石兽备感困倦。 
 
第二章 基本礼仪  
很多人并不了解与眠石兽共舞的邀请礼仪，导致了时常会有人变成它们心爱的枕头，而不是舞伴。首先，打扰一只眠石兽休息，大喊大叫催它醒来与你跳舞是绝不可取的。正确的方式应当先在野外找到一只沉睡的眠石兽，然后使用战迟木的树枝扫过它坚硬的头顶。根据知名游猎家胡芊芊的实践经验，持续清理它头顶的青苔大约一千两百次左右，这时眠石兽就会被成功唤醒，如果它没有站起身来向你生气吼叫，那么恭喜，舞蹈的邀请已经被它成功接受了，反之，你应当尽快离开，否则只有等待过路的游猎家将你从它的怀抱中拯救出来。 
 
第三章 舞蹈节奏  
进入舞蹈状态的眠石兽是不会移动的，而作为它认可舞伴的你，应该端坐在它的面前，轻轻晃动你头顶的石雕帽子，双臂自然舒展摆动，像一株自由生长的野草。如果眠石兽的目光随着你的动作转动，那么说明它已经开始与你共舞了，此时舞步的选择取决于你脖子的扭动方式，尽量不要抖动你的双肩。另外，千万不要低头，如果石雕帽子掉落，你应该立刻离开，否则请姿势不要有任何变化，等待眠石兽重新闭上眼睛。

text: I will be on leave for over a month due to personal reasons. Another teacher will take over my duties starting next week. Please be patient and wait for my return.

The enemy is approaching, but our soldiers remain steadfast. It's too early to call this our final stand. After all, beyond the Crosswind Bridge, there is still a glimmer of hope of survival in the east of Aerfall. \nI hid the treasure at the <69D0FF>southern end of the Crosswind Bridge</>. Those with fate on their side may find it.

Boss! We snagged a complete Mech Core from a new shipment of Mechcraft parts the academy was transporting to the Iridescent Basin! 
 
 
 
As you know, those guys' tech is nowhere near your level of mastery, and their ideas aren't half as sharp as yours. Maybe you can have a laugh at this outdated design and mock those academy bookworms!

Boss! We snagged a complete Mech Core from a new shipment of Mechcraft parts the academy was transporting to the Iridescent Basin! 
 
 
 
As you know, those guys' tech is nowhere near your level of mastery, and their ideas aren't half as sharp as yours. Maybe you can have a laugh at this outdated design and mock those academy bookworms!
The claw marks tell the tale of the brutal wars of the past.

The free meals are so good! I'll definitely come back next time! 
 
"Had a fallout with my roommate in school. Thanks for taking me in here for a week! The price is pretty affordable." 
 
"Years after graduation, the teachers in Jixia are still as kind as ever. Springbrook Plains haven't changed either, always bustling with life." 
 
"I slept so soundly here. Practicing Sorcery Technique at Dreamwhisper Lake made me exhausted."

A day with Society makes you a lifelong member. 
 
 
 
Now, let's go through the process of joining, learning, becoming a full member, and advancing in Society. Over the years, this system has evolved slightly across different societies, but the overall process remains the same. 
 
 
 
As you know, Jixia Academy is divided into three main schools of study: Martial Arts, Mechcrafts, and Sorcery. However, there are many other research areas, collectively known as Society. These societies focus on practical applications of the three main schools. The three schools are compulsory, while societies are optional. During their four years at Jixia, students can join societies at any time and even be part of multiple societies simultaneously. Societies not only provide students with knowledge but also give them a deep understanding of each society's research direction. 
 
 
 
So, joining a society is just the beginning of your journey. Students who already find the academic workload challenging need to choose their societies wisely! 
 
 
 
Each society has its own top performers, most of whom are selected by their society mentors. These top performers are all experts in their respective fields. It is said that the top performers of the Herb Society possess unparalleled rejuvenation techniques, the top performers of the Seekers can even determine the quality of a treasure by smell alone, and the top performers of the Traders are familiar with all the businesses in Jixia. 
 
 
 
Therefore, the path of training is long and arduous, with unreachable heights at the end. But the journey to climb those heights is the most valuable experience for us students.

Master Mozi said that if we can take apart a Mechcraft and reassemble it without leaving a single screw behind, we can truly claim to have made progress. 
 
... 
 
But I've taken this bird apart nearly ten times, and each time, I'm left with a pile of parts that refuse to fit back in. And yet, it still flies perfectly! Why? What are these parts even for? 
 
... 
 
Wonderful news—Senior Meng Ya has broken that bird! I never have to take it apart again!

If not for our friend rescuing the original manuscript from some careless Academy members, the first volume of this collection would have been lost to the sea, just like the secrets of Littoral Cave. 
 
Littoral Cave, also known as Littoral Maze, was where the author, in his quest to unravel the mystery of the statue at the foot of the mountain deep in Springbrook Plains, accidentally stumbled into an underground chamber. To his amazement, the mountain concealed a hidden world! 
 
After navigating jagged rocks and bypassing dangerous Mechanoid guards, he uncovered a colossal battleship buried in the sand, as tall as the Tower of Enlightenment. 
 
In front of the battleship stood a towering platform inscribed with ancient texts, which the learned author quickly deciphered. The inscriptions revealed that the deep-sea vessel was a super battleship from another world, capable of firing a green flame cannonball that could pierce the ocean floor and unleash tsunamis powerful enough to destroy Jixia. 
 
But that wasn't all—the battleship held countless advanced super technologies and magical secrets, including ores for forging ultimate divine weapons, an endless mechanism power source, and a laboratory used by Mechanoids from another world. 
 
However, the Seekers dispatched by the Academy never revealed these ancient texts to the public. Instead, they hurriedly translated the content into obscure, misleading poetry, keeping the truth hidden from the world. 
 
This discovery finally brought these hidden facts to light, exposing the Academy's plan to monopolize this ancient power! 
 
As the author prepared to leave, he witnessed some Academy profiteers scheming to sell off this ancient legacy. Sadly, outnumbered, they had to end the operation prematurely. But at least the truth didn't sink into the sea.
Ding Wu Hai went out of control after devouring several beasts. Research has been suspended, and the Forbidden Item Ding Wu Hai is now under guard by a Mech-Man.

Prototype No. 2: Failed. The energy was too chaotic, with no pattern. 
Prototype No. 3: Success? Energy transmission can now be stabilized! The input of flow is now controllable. 
Prototype No. 4: Success. Flow input is more stable than before.

Endless waves roll, swayed by the wind. 
Guided by the Bubble Fish, I came. 
With bountiful catch, may generations thrive. 
Looking out to the sea, I await your return.

Volcanic Stone No. 3 is dedicated to powering the Giant Drill below.
Alas, we received evacuation orders early this morning and will never witness the grand activation of that giant drill.

If I ever returned here, I'd head straight to the Forbidden Land just beyond the wall to fire up this mechanical giant.
But when that day might come is anyone's guess...

In the fourth episode, we'll turn our attention to the gentle and peaceful creatures of nature — Armadillo Rats and the Bulls. 
 
 
 
The Armadillo Rat is often the subject of countryside tales. They inhabit the forests and mountains of Jixia, especially in densely wooded areas. One popular story tells of a Herbalist who rescued a dying Armadillo Rat. The rat mysteriously disappeared after recovering from the injuries, only to return later, leading the herbalist to a rich trove of medicinal herbs as a gesture of gratitude. This story highlights the creature's gentle nature and deep bond with humans. 
 
 
 
Young Armadillo Rats are known as Armored Mice. They typically curl up in their shells to avoid conflict, making them a favorite among locals as pets, despite their strong instinct for freedom. As they grow, their shells become gourd-shaped for enhanced protection. The larger Guardian Armadillo Rat, a subspecies, features a sturdier shell and stronger limbs for defensive retaliation, though they remain non-aggressive. 
 
 
 
Much like the Armadillo Rat, the Bulls are not naturally aggressive. These creatures are found across Jixia's grasslands, where they prefer a calm and peaceful life. Young Brutalhorn Calves are covered in dense brown fur and are similarly docile, rarely initiating attacks. When faced with a threat, their underdeveloped horns offer little in terms of offense, so they stay close to adult Brutalhorn Bulls. The adult Brutalhorn Bull is a massive beast with a large hump on its back and a pair of formidable horns. These bulls are highly territorial, and any perceived intruders will face a powerful charge until they are driven out. If you find yourself mistakenly seen as a threat by a Brutalhorn Bull and lack the means to defend yourself, escaping becomes crucial. The key is to run in a zigzag pattern to avoid being overtaken in a straight-line chase.

Basic Information 
Name: Liu Xia 
Gender: Female 
Affiliation: Student of the School of Mechcraft 
Chief Complaint: Bitten by a leaf-tailed lizard during combat, experiencing severe pain. 
Diagnosis: Leaf-tailed lizard bite, wound deep enough to expose the bone. 
 
Treatment Plan: 
First, thoroughly wash the wound with plenty of clean water, then administer an anesthetic. 
Second, once the anesthetic takes effect, apply a high-concentration poison made from venom-bubble buds to the wound, three times a day. 
Third, rest quietly for three to five days until the wound heals before getting out of bed to exercise. 
 
Treatment Records: 
First, this poison can eliminate the toxins in the leaf-tailed lizard's saliva, but the patient experienced side effects of dizziness and nausea. 
Second, the herbalists suggested giving the patient some raw ginseng juice. I tried it, and it did have some effect, though not very significant.

After inspections and repairs by the instructors of the three schools and several experts, the Academy has decided to restart some of the mountaineering trials.
