Kindling the Furnace is a special column for cannon researchers, This section features the latest research findings in the Cannons industry, helping researchers stay at the forefront of the field. With the brightest light, we guide the way forward. 
 
 
As cannon research becomes more open, various materials are being widely adopted. Different types of cannons are interconnected yet independent, and their applications from a materials science perspective have sparked a new wave of discussion. By analyzing the various consumables used in fireworks products and exploring their unique characteristics, we can discuss their potential applications in other types of cannons, providing more options for future development. 
 
 
 
Fireworks, originally a byproduct of cannon research, have recently shown rapid growth, incorporating many experimental technologies and staying ahead of the curve. However, research on the application of various materials has been limited to fireworks alone, without broader promotion. Therefore, choosing fireworks consumables as a starting point for research can reveal more possibilities. 
 
 
 
Grinding Aluminum Glintstone into powder and adding it to fireworks in specific proportions can make them flash on and off in midair. After multiple measurements and comparisons, it was found that the fragments of Aluminum Glintstone always present with irregular surfaces, which absorb and refract light and heat differently. It is this characteristic of Aluminum Glintstone that gives it a flashing visual effect after exposure to intense heat. 
 
 
 
This means that the flashing effect of Aluminum Glintstone originates from its interaction with light and heat. In other words, applying it to cannons that release heat instantaneously could also produce a flashing effect. Based on this hypothesis, adding Aluminum Glintstone powder to arrowheads or cannonballs could potentially create signaling devices. Further analysis of the absorption and refraction efficiency of different surfaces may even allow for controlling the rhythm and pattern of the flashes. 
 
 
 
Violetfall Rock and Cyanfall Rock can make fireworks emit purple and cyan lights. After investigation, it was found that current fireworks manufacturing simply involves crushing these rocks and directly mixing them in, resulting in poor color effects and low mineral utilization efficiency. While this meets fireworks production needs, it's difficult to achieve mass production or apply it to other cannon units. In fact, the color display of these two rocks comes from long-term pigment deposition. By adopting the approach used in mineral pigment research, we can extract the pigments from the rocks and directly dye other materials. This would not only result in more pure colors but also significantly reduce the overall weight of the required materials. Combining this with the aforementioned Aluminum Glintstone, it's possible to create various signaling devices such as flashing purple signals or flashing cyan signals. If this research is proven feasible and implemented in military contexts, it could enhance information transmission efficiency to some extent.

I wrote the first line of this book sitting on a stump in the mountain ruins. I want readers—especially anyone dreaming of becoming a Gourmet or a food critic—to see things clearly: this line of work is not for those who tire easily. 
 
 
 
"Let's stop here and rest up before heading deeper." The Gourmet interns with me today looked a mess, slumped every which way—clearly shaken after being chased by that flame-spitting sentry. 
 
 
 
"Master Mikirin, what are we even doing holding a cooking class in a ruin? Are these bronze lumps supposed to cook?" asked one student, hair singed at the tips. It was as good a moment as any to teach. I opened my pack and took out a slab of game meat. 
 
 
 
"People argue about where Jixia's food culture began. Here's my guess. Long ago our ancestors ate like beasts—raw, bloody. Back then, 'cuisine' wasn't a thing." I set the meat over the campfire; its color darkened as it cooked. 
 
 
 
While the flames built, I cut a slice for him. "Better," he said after chewing, "but still not good." I didn't answer. I kept turning the meat. As the fat began to render, I gave him another slice. "Perfect medium rare. Tastes great." 
 
 
 
"The moment our ancestors learned heat changes flavor," I said, "Jixia's cuisine began. So don't sneer at something as simple as roast meat. It might have been the first dish anyone ever called 'delicious.' Picture it: a circle of hungry folk around a fire, all eyes on a skewer slowly changing color, the smell making their mouths water." I bit into a piece that had gone a little past done. Still good. 
 
 
 
"Cooked meat isn't always the tastiest, but it won't make you sick. That was hard-earned wisdom." The critic in me couldn't help commenting. 
 
 
 
"And if you think they stopped there, you don't know foodies," I went on, pulling a few vegetables and a jar of seasoning from my pack and mixing them in. 
 
 
 
"I've heard our ancestors already knew how to make sauces—so good you could dip anything in them. There's even a tale about a glutton who 'ate a whole mountainside bare'—I'd bet that sauce had something to do with it. Sadly, the recipe's been lost." 
 
 
 
"Once, at a festival, Master Fuzi told me about an ancient brew called "Shadow". Open a jar and every bird in the sky would drop, drunk on the aroma. The Master doesn't make things up… does he?" 
 
 
 
"So many flavors burned bright and vanished into history. That, right there, is why we do fieldwork—to track them down." I walked back to the stump. 
 
 
 
To my surprise, up close, the "stump" resembled a finely made container. I rapped the top: thunk, thunk—hollow. Thunk! At the last knock the cap cracked. A strange fragrance rushed up my nose, and suddenly the world turned upside down; I felt myself floating. 
 
 
 
When I came to, the students had gathered around me. They'd been farther from the "stump," so they woke sooner. I looked inside—empty. Only a smear of clay seal clung to the broken lid, proof it had held liquid. The Master's story flashed through my mind. Could this be the legendary Shadow Brew? 
 
 
 
Taking this as a sign, I began writing "The Gourmet Records of Mikirin"—to inspire future food enthusiasts like myself.

In Jixia, there's a well-known tale about a farmer who, after working in the fields until noon, rested under a fruit tree. When he woke up, both the fruit and the tree were gone. A flock of Red Pome Magpies, disguised as fruit, had carried him into the sky. 
The peculiar birds would only set him down once they found a new tree they liked. 
Another, even more frightening tale for farmers, tells of Pome Magpies disguised as fruit during the day, coming alive at night to devour crops. This led some superstitious farmers to become so paranoid about red fruit that they would check their fields at night, eventually suffering from insomnia. 
 
To trace the origins of these tales, I spent some time closely observing the Pome Magpies in their habitat. 
Traditionally, people believe Pome Magpies are timid, wrapping themselves in their wings and hanging from branches to disguise themselves as fruit. 
However, my observations revealed that their disguise is not driven by fear or the need to avoid predators. When I discovered their "disguises," they would fly up and circle in the sky before finding another tree to resume hiding, almost as if they were inviting me to keep searching and interacting with them. 
This led me to believe that they are not only unafraid but also sociable and playful. 
The reason behind their fruit disguise remained unclear. 
As the weather grew colder and it became less convenient for me to camp outdoors, a curious event occurred. 
The young Pome Magpies, unable to fly and with insatiable appetites, would call out loudly when their supply of sweet and sour fruit was exhausted. 
At these times, the older Pome Magpies would fly around, disguising themselves as fruit. This seemed to calm the young birds, perhaps because they were reassured by the sight of the "food." 
Whether this behavior is a form of anxiety relief or self-deception, it underscores one fact: we still know very little about these creatures. 
Therefore, I bought some fruit from Frostcloud Town as a gesture of thanks and made plans to visit them again in the spring.

Follow me on a journey through mountains and rivers, experiencing the beauty of the four seasons. 
 
Jixia is a great place for adventure and sightseeing. I have traveled to many places and found Springbrook Plains to be the most unique. The area boasts enchanting natural scenery, with every plant and tree exuding an untouched, pristine charm. What is most surprising is that there are many ancient ruins here, providing evidence of the origins of the civilization on Springbrook Plains. 
 
I took a different route and specifically chose two lesser-known attractions to deeply appreciate the cultural and historical charm. First, I visited the He & Ming's Training Hall, where the magnificent architecture and fragrant flowers around the clear pond were a feast for the eyes. The sound of students practicing their swordsmanship filled the air. Master Bai He commands great respect with his extraordinary demeanor. As a master of Light & Heavy Swords, his sword moves are as fast as lightning and unmatched in ferocity. Therefore, a friendly reminder: if you want to visit the He & Ming's Training Hall, you've got to be prepared before challenging him. 
 
Outside the He & Ming's Training Hall, the wetland landscape is like a beautiful and pleasant ecological painting. It caused me to stop and admire it repeatedly. Heading further south, I saw massive, ancient ruins. The structures there would have been an extremely complex project even by today's standards. Some believe that they may have been built with the help of a now-extinct civilization in ancient times. It seems that the creativity of the ancients was indeed astonishing. Regrettably, due to the menacing Saepes and intimidating Mechanoids, I had to watch the ruins from a distance.

The Philosophy of Dreams is boundless. The more I delve into it, the smaller I feel. 
 
 
 
Dreams are ever-changing and elusive, a shadow of the vast world—a fleeting glimpse of all things. 
 
 
 
I've spent years in this cave studying Dream Energy. Dreams now surround me, drawing me deeper into their ethereal embrace. 
 
 
 
Even if ice freezes everything before my eyes, I can still sense part of my consciousness drifting away from my mind. 
 
 
 
Not even the coldest snow of the Northlands can freeze dreams. 
 
 
 
Perhaps I should stop exploring Dreamscape before I get completely lost—leave with what I have learned and return to dull reality. 
 
 
 
No, never. 
 
 
 
Even if I forget who I am or everything worldly, so what? 
 
 
 
I will continue to seek within Dreamscape until I'm fully immersed.

Every day, I reflect on what Mechcraft means to people. 
It has reached astonishing heights. 
But with great power comes the potential for both good and harm. 
I hope that the students of the School of Mechcrafts will always choose kindness.

During my travels, I encountered a rare and devastating wildfire. 
 
The fire began in the Saepes' habitat and spread rapidly. I could hear the agonized screams of the Saepes in the flames, a sight too cruel to behold. 
 
I struggled to save myself, soaking myself in water and running towards the only place without flammable materials. 
 
Just as the flames were about to engulf me, I saw a magnificent immortal bird. 
 
Its beautiful face was filled with compassion, and its body was surrounded by cool mist, as if born from pure water. Even its feathers shimmered with flowing water. 
It saved all the creatures in the area, leaving cool raindrops wherever it flew. 
 
After extinguishing the endless flames, it gracefully departed. 
 
I would like to thank it, even though I am just one of the many people and things it saved.

To the Brave Angling Society Members: 
 
A great crisis has struck the waters of Dreamweave Plains: numerous white, ferocious, giant monster fish have appeared in lakes everywhere. 
 
These monster fish are indiscriminately devouring fish of all sizes in the lakes. If we don't intervene, Dreamweave Plains may soon be devoid of fish to angle. 
 
Anglers aspiring to leave your mark in history! We cannot allow this to happen. The only solution now is to pick up your angling rods and thoroughly eradicate those white monster fish. 
 
Additionally, the mentor has announced that whoever catches the most and the largest monster fish will be crowned the Angling Champion of Jixia Academy!

To the Head Trainer of the White Plum Training Hall,

I hope you have been well. 
 
There has been a surge in demand for elixirs recently. I'm not sure if it's because your disciples have been too careless during training, resulting in a sharp increase in injuries. Our elixir production is currently insufficient to meet such high demand. I hope you can take care of your needs.

Where did the Societies come from? The answer may be hidden in a dusty corner of the Jixia Academy's publication department database. 
 
"Ah, you're here again. You've been coming so early lately. Got a new project? Tell an old man about it." 
 
This was my first assignment as a Sorcery instructor after taking over the publication department, but it quickly turned into a problem. I looked at the old man who greeted me—the one responsible for cleaning the academy's library—and fell into deep thought. He had been there since I was a freshman. Perhaps he knew something. 
 
"Hello, well, I've recently been troubled by a research project—where did all these Societies come from?" I tried to answer his question. 
 
"Hmm... that is a good question." He looked at my instructor uniform. "What do you think?" His eyes sparkled with curiosity. 
 
"You might be onto something!" I realized he must know something. 
 
"Based on the few records available, at the beginning of the academy, the Intelligence Society united everyone, creating the harmony we see today among the Societies. So, here are my two guesses: First, the Societies existed before the academy, and they were formed from various forces at the time. The academy and the Intelligence Society reached some kind of agreement, making them ambassadors who established the current system." He nodded slowly, neither confirming nor denying, so I continued. 
 
"Second, the academy also has its own history. But at some point, the academy closed down. Its students scattered across Jixia. They couldn't return to school, so they established their own strongholds. Later, someone claiming to be from the Intelligence Society appeared, seeking to rebuild the academy. However, too much time had passed, and each stronghold had developed on its own. Some returned to the academy, while others stayed behind. This could have led to the formation of the Societies." I proposed another possibility. 
 
"Ha ha ha, interesting theories. But you've overlooked some important questions." He paused before continuing, "If your first guess is correct, where did the records of the original forces disappear to? If your second guess is true, why would the academy bury that part of its history?" 
 
He turned around. "It's been nice chatting with you, but I need to go feed an old friend." He said and turned away. I looked at what he was feeding. 
 
It was a big-eyed owl unlike any I'd ever seen before—old yet full of spirit.

The 5th unit discusses legends related to dream monsters. 
 
 
 
Dream monsters generally fall into two types. The first are creatures changed after being exposed to dream energy. The second are beings born directly from Dreamscape. We begin with the first type. 
 
 
 
Some once asked: do monsters dream? According to old accounts, they do. A Hunter once researched this topic. It is widely believed that ordinary monsters living long within Dreamscape absorb dream energy and gradually take on traits similar to Dream Butterflies, eventually becoming dream monsters. The Hunter also discovered that these creatures seem to become dreamers themselves. Curious about the content of their dreams, he used certain methods to enter them. 
 
 
 
The first case was a Nightmare Wolvine. In its dream, the Hunter saw a vast grassland. The wolf, originally a Wolvine, ran freely, hunted, and fought. Even though its body had changed and its eyes had grown dim, in the dream it returned to its original state, pursuing simple instinctive desires. 
 
 
 
The second case was a Nightshadow Falcon. Transformed, its feathers turned iridescent and gained hallucinatory properties. In the dream, it flew freely above the clouds. In real life it had been an injured Swiftbolt Falcon that could no longer fly. 
 
 
 
The third case was a Nightshadow Lizard. Covered in bright scales, originally a Tailed Lizardling. In its dream, it imagined itself as a powerful dragon, no longer hiding or ambushing prey but ruling the forest. 
 
These records gave rise to many rumors. People who accidentally entered the Dreamscape in the middle of the night often described similar frightening shapes afterward. 
 
 
 
Whether this Hunter and her research truly existed remains uncertain. The idea that monsters can also be dreamers has still not been proven. 
 
 
 
Next, we discuss the second type of dream monsters: those born from Dreamscape itself. These include the Eerie Dreamtangle and the Eerie Dreamcage. The Eerie Dreamtangle has a large canopy-like body and four long tendrils that restrain prey and drain dream energy. The Eerie Dreamcage resembles a cage and can launch dream energy to trap prey in the Dreamscape. Both are connected to the Dreamslayer, a strange bird-like species that once triggered a Dreamscape riot, heavily injured the Dreamweavers, and seized the Palace of Butterflies. In the Dreamscape, Dreamslayer can control Eerie Dreamtangles to block intruders.

This is the prophecy made by the Dream Interpretation Basin for that Dreamslayer.

No one knows where it came from, but it will remain in your memory.

The First Prophecy
They said it shouldn't have come here. This was the cradle of Dream Butterflies, the place where they watched over the dreams of all beings.
When it fell through the rift, battered and broken, the sage practicing in the Dreamy Grotto rescued it.
"Why do you eat dreams?"
"The woman in the dream... she's crying... I don't like it..."
Its bewildered gaze met the sage's calm face.
"Eat away... the tears... Eat away... the fleeting regrets... of life..."
"You are special among them. I'll convince the Dreamweavers to let you stay until you..."
The sage's words suddenly became blurred in the memory.

The Second Prophecy
The Dreamweavers still refused to associate with it. They were skilled at weaving dream cocoons and hatching Dream Butterflies. But all it knew how to weave was thorns, cages for living souls.
Its claws were most adept at hooking newly hatched butterflies from their cocoons, tearing apart their fragile wings, then stretching its neck and tilting its head before swallowing them whole.
"Such a greedy creature is truly ugly! When will the sage cast it out?"
It heard the Dreamweavers talking and paid them no mind.
Perhaps it would be better without claws. Perhaps it could be as majestic as a dreamer, clad in armor and wielding a sword, free to roam.
But the general in that nightmare sighed for his homeland day after day, weeping ceaselessly.
"You predicted... his victory... Why does he still... have nightmares?"
"He is trapped in an endless cycle, yet believes he can bring peace."
"If I keep helping him... eating those dreams... Will peace ever come?"
"Wars never end, like snails fighting on horns. If that day really comes... you..."
It struggled to recall what the teacher had said next.

The Third Prophecy
"Why do you cry before the Dream Interpretation Basin?" The girl was the only Dreamweaver willing to talk to it.
"I saw... what you and the teacher foresaw..."
"Dreams follow their own rules. Those dreaming creatures will remember me."
"But you too will wander in pain..."
"Then will you eat me?"
"I only eat dreams... You have none..."
The girl looked sad, just as she did in the Dream Interpretation Basin.
"The teacher should help you. He will help you all."
"Our future cannot be changed, not even by the sage. But if one day you leave the Dreamy Grotto, please stop by my statue and bid me farewell."

The Fourth Prophecy
Training wasn't meant for it.
Whenever it sat on a mat trying to listen to the teacher's teachings, the Dreamweavers would get up and leave, occasionally watching from the corner.
Their dislike didn't stem from its appearance.
Now it understood—the thorns it wove so skillfully were the cage they feared most.
"Dreams change and shift, and dangerous dreams may avert future disasters."
The teacher's lectures grew clearer; no longer obscure or profound.
"Then why didn't the teacher tell the martial artist how to win when he clearly foresaw his defeat?"
Its accurate observation drew surprised gasps from the corner.
"I've seen all his victories, but the one who defeats him holds far more victories."
"I... don't understand..."
In that instant, it felt as lost as it once was. Yet the teacher smiled.
"One day you will understand. I've foreseen every moment of your enlightenment, and you..."
Those words faded into the monotony of its training days—perhaps it never truly grasped them in the first place.

The Sage's Prophecy
Dreamweavers spin dream cocoons. Dreamslayers weave thorns.
Dreamscapes shift endlessly, but only a sage who has witnessed past and present can traverse them freely.
He foresaw the day the rift would open in the Dreamy Grotto, foresaw its battered fall.
The Butterfly Envoy asked the sage what fate awaited it. The sage remained silent, summoning it to his desk instead to impart the ways of dreams.
"They are cunning and elusive, hunters in the dark, forever coveting the beauty of dreams."
"It's different."
"Have you seen its future?"
"After all of you have left this place, it will continue to wander the Dreamy Grotto, tormented by the pain of nightmares."

The sage pointed toward something unseen.

The city has crumbled, massive stones pile up. The root of a tall tree is entwined around the ruined walls.

March 5 
Sprouts emerged. Though called seedlings, their color perfectly resembles withered plants. They are responsive to touch, fascinating. 
 
April 10 
The seedlings have grown to half a person's height, with more branches and leaves. 
Other plants now grow in the surrounding soil—an intriguing symbiotic phenomenon? Worthy of study. 
Their reactive response to external touch remains intense. Such force is astonishing for a plant. 
 
May 17 
The part above, which I thought was a fruit, started to glow and emit heat. Interesting, is it some special method of seed dispersal? 
The roots of the main plant and its companion plants have grown thicker and are thriving. 
 
 
June 20 
The development of the Moonelia Sprout has completely exceeded our expectations. The vines at the base are occasionally producing bubbles. If you accidentally touch them, it can make you feel dizzy. Though it could also be due to exhaustion from days of intense research.

Day 1 
Even though everyone in the village advised me not to go up the mountain alone, I've really made some progress this time! In a cave, I saw a Fanged Lion with fangs as long as the legends say. 
 
Day 2 
A traveler one told me, "Record what you've seen and summarize often." So I recorded what I observed about the Fanged Lion. 
 
Day 3 
Is the cave so cold because the Fanged Lion breathes frost? I can't even start a campfire. I'll need to go back and get something to handle this big guy. 
 
Day 4: 
Everything is ready. Once I capture this Fanged Lion, I'll return to the village with pride...

The Rebels holed up in the mountains are better organized than the ones we've encountered before. For some reason, several Intelligence Society members sent to gather intel have gone missing. The latest message says, "Beware of the scorpion." What does that even mean?

I pummel the three schools with my fists and kick the Tower of Enlightenment with my feet. \nThe Society of Heroes takes a detour around me. Rebels acknowledge my superiority.

In the past, legendary brutal creatures roamed Primaera. They were called dragons and once attempted to enslave humanity but were defeated by heroes wielding divine weapons.

Just as the Academy tries to shut down our base, hoping to extinguish hope with darkness, their efforts are in vain. My work will see the light of day.

In the Forest of Life in southern Jixia, a group of creatures known as dragons lived. Their size was enormous, and their nature was savage. With each breath, mountains turned to dust, and even death could not bring peace to all living things.

When these dragons sought to devour everything and enslave us, dragon slayers appeared—armed with massive blades and giant war machines, they clashed with the largest dragon overlords in a fierce battle that lasted until nightfall.

The dragons' armor was shattered by dragon-slaying blades; their will was broken by dragon-breaking drums. The dragons' remains lay on the dragon-slaying pillars until the seventh day of the great battle. At dawn, the dragons' proud heads finally fell, and our heroes successfully subdued the dragons, crushing their ambitions and forcing them to coexist with us.

After victory, the heroes gained the powerful ability to tame dragons. They made a contract with the dragons, requiring them to share their abilities. From then on, they could ride giant dragons into battle, becoming dragon tamers.

As our colleagues continue to decipher ancient texts, I believe I will eventually acquire such power. Riding dragons through the sky, surely the Academy won't catch us printing books then, right?

Remember those who get seasick, can't swim, or are clumsy — tomorrow, we'll have them leave. Our plan doesn't have room for such burdens holding us back.

And that "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" song—I listened to it ten times and didn't think it was that special!

text: I thought I was fully prepared, but I didn't expect to encounter an angry giant lizard and suffer a severe beating. In a panic, I escaped to this isle—fortunately, the lizard didn't follow. Next time, I'll bring the new sword I bought from Aerforge and ensure the lizard gets a taste of its own medicine!

Every dish served at the table must be accountable to the customer. In other words, the food presented must at least maintain the dignity of the customer. I am absolutely generous with my praise for good food, and equally unreserved in my criticism of those who use gimmicks to deceive customers. 
 
Jixia's current prosperity attracts visitors from all regions to come and enjoy its offerings. From Horizon Harbor to Springbrook Plains, then Aerux Town and Northton. There are always new faces arriving, each filled with expectations and anticipation before they arrive. 
 
Some merchants will use various gimmicks to promote their dishes—I call this "fan culture." While there are masterpieces like Cloudreach Festival BBQ, there are also poorly made dishes like Kongming Riding a Dragon or Zhou Yu's Tiger Claws. 
 
Ironically, these two types of dishes sell very well, with fans even fighting to buy them until they were sold out. To prevent everyone from being deceived by superficial bestsellers, I've listed some popular but terrible foods to avoid. 
 
Name: Master Fuzi's Jump 
Review: A stew named after Master Fuzi, which is actually just a pot of mixed meats. When opened, it presents a gray mushy texture with unidentified lumps. 
The smell is tolerable, but the color and liquid consistency are appetite-suppressing. The flavors of unknown fish, beast meat, and fowl are completely mixed together, losing any original taste of the ingredients. 
It's said that Master Fuzi jumped for joy after eating this dish. In my opinion, he didn't jump for joy; he was furious at the poor quality. 
Jump may not mean jump, but trample is real. 
 
Name: Ruo Family Lucky Drink 
Review: As we all know, the Ruo sisters have long been responsible for issuing various requests. This drink name, I can only say, is very targeted. After all, who doesn't want to receive easy-to-complete requests? 
Countless students, hoping for good luck, would buy this drink before picking up their daily requests. However, upon tasting it, I found it's just an ordinary tea drink loaded with sugar. 
While it does replenish energy before completing tasks, from a flavor standpoint, it leaves much to be desired. 
If tourists reading this want to try something truly delicious, I recommend visiting a small, unadvertised stall that always has a line—that's a reputable shop with genuinely great taste. 
 
Name: Power Porridge 
Review: A slightly salty, plain porridge with no special features, but it comes in a beautifully decorated bowl with cotton threads drawn as clouds. 
Most of my fellow diners were tourists, claiming it made their bodies feel warm and energized. Based on my analysis, this is simply the normal feeling one gets after eating. 
There was also a particularly strong young man sitting by the door, continuously drinking porridge with a table full of empty bowls. He kept saying, "I'm so strong because I drink this Power Porridge!" Interestingly, when he left, I didn't see him pay. Those in the know understand what I'm implying. 
... 
 
In this vast Jixia, there are inevitably some scammers trying to swindle people. I hope everyone keeps their eyes open and discerns the truth. In short, follow me, old gourmet Mikyo, and you won't go wrong.

They begged me to play the same piece of music as before. Though reluctant, I agreed, out of gratitude for their silent listening in the past. However, when I was about to play, the Dreamers took out their instruments, claiming they wanted to play along with me. What did that mean？ 
 
 
 
As we played together, I saw for the first time so many Dream Butterflies flying out of the Dreamers. These Dream Butterflies circled around us, as if our music had merged us into one. 
 
 
 
When the piece ended, to my surprise, the music played by the Dreamers harmonized perfectly with mine. Is this what the Dreamers meant by being of one mind?

Four ironclad rules that must not be violated. Violators will face severe punishment.

A volume of the Saepes Compendium compiled by Mu Ping, a Hunter from Jixia, documenting the classification and characteristics of Saepes. 
 
 
 
Jixia is home to many fierce animals that are natural predators of Saepes. In self-defense, Saepes have developed various strategies. They possess a degree of intelligence, capable of using brute force or simple tools to attack any creature that enters their territory, and they even collaborate as a team. 
 
 
 
Regrettably, this hostility also extends to humans. Listed below are some common Saepes and their combat characteristics. If you accidentally trespass on Saepes territory, this knowledge might prove helpful. 
 
 
 
Saepes Brute: The little Saepes embed their own shed hard bark onto a hardwood club, creating a wolf-tooth club that wields considerable power when swung. 
 
 
 
Note: The club is not long, so as long as you run fast, you should be fine. Or at the very least, make sure you run faster than the people around you. 
 
 
 
Saepes Lancers: Some little Saepes prefer to use longer sticks, topping them with a piece of their own hard bark to create a spear-like weapon. This has a longer attack range than the wolf-tooth club, capable of both slashing and piercing. 
 
 
 
Note: Be cautious, as the Saepes Lancers are taller than a person and they can rapidly charge. Make good use of horizontal dodging. 
 
 
 
Saepes Toxin Archers: These little Saepes know how to hollow out a stick to create a blowpipe, firing the sharp spines shed from their bodies to attack enemies from a distance. Be extra cautious around them, as the bark of these Saepes contains toxins, making the spines they fire essentially toxic arrows. A single hit can inflict poisoning. 
 
 
 
Note: These ranged Saepes usually appear alongside melee types. Be careful not to get caught out by them. As a precaution, it's best to carry antidotes prepared by the Hunters when venturing out. 
 
 
 
Saepes Hunters: The slings used by Saepes are different from ours; they don't use rubber bands but instead use a wooden fork to pick up stones from the ground and throw them. Don't be fooled by their size; Saepes Slingsers have considerable strength, capable of easily hurling stones larger than a human head. It's best to dodge them if you encounter them. Additionally, it seems that Slingsers can emit a special pheromone to call for help from other little Saepes, making them particularly troublesome opponents. 
 
 
 
Note: Absolutely! Encounter one Hunter, and you'll likely face three. I nearly didn't make it out a few times. I suggest taking out the hunters first before dealing with their reinforcements; otherwise, the battle could drag on indefinitely. 
 
 
 
Arbor Saepes: The Arbor Saepes represent the pinnacle of combat strength within the Saepes community. Although they move somewhat slowly, their strength is equivalent to that of ten adult humans. Leveraging their long arms, they can easily knock several people flying with a single punch. Moreover, the little Saepes usually act alongside the Arbor Saepes, making them even more challenging to handle. 
 
 
 
Note: It's best to run fast. If you do end up fighting an Arbor Saepe, don't engage in a direct confrontation; maintain your distance or wear it down gradually. 
 
 
 
Arbor Saepes Tallshield: Most Arbor Saepes fight bare-handed, but some have wide, shield-like bark on their arms, offering enhanced protection. 
 
 
 
Arbor Saepes Heavy Warriors: These special Arbor Saepes have arms that resemble spears, capable of piercing attacks with a larger range than regular Arbor Saepes. 
 
 
 
Arbor Saepes Grenadiers: Some Arbor Saepes grow various large fruits that they throw like grenades. These fruits can explode, some freezing you in place, while others are highly toxic. Interestingly, some of these fruits have healing properties; the mist produced by their explosion can heal the wounds of other Saepes. 
 
 
 
Note: After throwing a fruit, they experience a brief stun. Seize this opportunity to escape or attack. 
 
 
 
Arbor Saepes Cannoneers: These creatures have a large opening at the end of their arms, from which they fire cannonballs made of condensed life essence to attack enemies. It's somewhat like the Mechcrafters' cannons but is a masterpiece of nature. Certainly not something those toy makers could match. 
 
 
 
Note: Such fantastical claims... 
 
 
 
Note: Hey, you're from the School of Mechcrafts, right? 
 
 
 
Giant Saepes: Perhaps to conserve energy, Giant Saepes usually remain buried in the soil, with only their backs exposed, resembling a small hill. Their tail remains upright, with a large flower at the tip that observes the surroundings. This gives the appearance of a hill with a solitary large flower growing on the side. If other creatures get too close, the flower on the tail rapidly fires fruits to inflict a painful attack. At this point, any creature with sense would quickly retreat. If not, the Giant Saepes will awaken, and a collision with such a massive creature could be fatal. 
 
 
 
The Primary Saepes: It's merely a legend. So far, I haven't personally seen a Primal Saepes, and I couldn't find any relevant information. Only the folklore recorded by the Seeker Society mentions it, but each story describes it differently, making it useless for any serious academic research. 
 
 
 
Note: Well, don't come asking to borrow our materials in the future, okay? 
 
 
 
Note: Don't take it so seriously, What's the big deal...

Contributor: Wang Mingshun, Student, School of Martial Arts

Content: Questions About the Cleaning Aunt

Editor's Note: All work is training, and no mundane task should be belittled.

Headmaster Fuzi once explained that martial arts are divided into external and internal schools.
The external school focuses on training the muscles, bones, and skin externally, while internal school practitioners often explain boxing techniques through inner logic, discussing the dantian and bones.
I've seen many skilled external school practitioners, such as Senior Novar and Senior Wuyan.
But the only internal school practitioner I've ever seen is the cleaning lady in the Enlightenment Plaza.
You might think I'm joking, but if you had seen what I did, you'd be even more shocked.
Once, my clothes tore during a sparring match with a classmate, and I had to return to my dormitory to change.
As I entered the room, I saw the cleaning lady lifting a stone bed with one hand and dusting underneath it with the other.
When she finished cleaning, she lowered the stone bed, and it made a loud thud, snapping me back to reality. I quickly ran away.
As I left, I heard her mutter something.
"So much dust. Should have put it down gently..."
The second time, the flying Mechcraft from the School of Mechcraft fell from the sky for some reason. Just as it was about to hit the ground, I saw the cleaning lady put down her broom and dustpan, strike the flying Mechcraft with a backhand, seemingly absorbing its energy, and then use her other hand to support it and gently set it on the ground.
That was a flying Mechcraft as tall as two people!
The first two incidents were only witnessed by me, and there's not enough evidence. But this time, many classmates saw it with me. If you still think I'm making it up, then you're the one who's mistaken.
About a week ago, to repay Uncle Zhang for always sending us fruit, a few of us students decided to clean his house.
We borrowed a broom from the cleaning lady and promised to return it within half a day.
On our way down the mountain, we encountered many wild beasts. They seemed to have been affected by something and attacked us like they were out of control.
We couldn't handle the beasts, so we had to run and ended up trapped in a cave.
Just when we lost hope, the cleaning lady appeared.
With just a tree branch, she quickly defeated all the beasts. Before we could even thank her, she hit each of us with the branch again.
"Has no one taught you to return things on time?"
She said, snatching the broom from my hand.

This volume introduces the Societies of Jixia and tackles a question often asked: how many Societies are there in Jixia? 
 
 
 
Seeker Society: 
 
 
 
From dawn to dusk, the Seeker Society's footprint spans across Jixia, excelling in treasure hunting, exploration, artifact collection, and archaeological research. 
 
 
 
As the inaugural volume of the Contention of Societies series, this book will introduce the renowned Societies of Jixia. 
 
 
 
The Societies are a collective term for various groups primarily composed of graduates from Jixia Academy. For students graduating from Jixia Academy, joining a society is an inevitable path towards further education. As an editor at the Jixia Academy Journal Club, this is my interpretation of the Societies. However which society among the societies—such as the Herb Society, the Gourmet Society, the Angling Society, the Hunting Society, the Craft Society, the Seeker Society, the Music Society, the Astrology Society, the Cannon Society...—was the first to be established in Jixia has always been an issue I wanted to figure out. 
 
 
 
Due to differences in the Societies chosen by editors for further study, this significant introduction has been revised by successive editors for various purposes. 
 
 
 
The establishment of a Society is an arduous process. Firstly, the founder must have authored at least one renowned work, this work had to be significant enough to pave the way for the creation of a completely new field of study. Afterwards, the founder must submit an application to Jixia Academy. And only upon approval could they begin conducting small-scale lectures and teaching their ideas. It was not until the founder gained the recognition of all Jixia's Three Sages that they were allowed to recruit their own students and formally establish a new Society. 
 
 
 
It is said that some Societies have only a handful of members, making it hard to imagine how their establishment and succession occur. 
 
 
 
The Societies of Jixia are renowned worldwide for their unconventional academic and regional cultural practices. The most prominent are the "Rustic Societies," where members often use the natural environment as their classroom, teaching anywhere except traditional classrooms. The "Contention of Societies," as the book title suggests, refers to the frequent debates between Societies, each presenting their theories. These discussions are purely based on the correctness of the arguments, rarely involving personal biases. This pure and flexible academic atmosphere is what has made Jixia so prosperous. 
 
 
 
In the following volumes, we will gradually unveil the mysteries of the Societies of Jixia, exploring both their widely circulated and lesser-known anecdotes. 
 
 
 
From an academic perspective, Jixia Academy, as the most renowned institution of learning, attracts all knowledge-seeking scholars from Primaera. Therefore, the formation of Societies was an inevitable trend in the academy's development history. (Since I have the privilege of editing this volume of Contention of Societies, I will take the liberty of listing the Seeker Society, dedicated to historical research, as the first Society!)

March 14th

April 3rd 
 
Forged Item: A sharp longsword 
 
Self-Evaluation: Acceptable 
 
Process: With the teacher's help, we adjusted the borax ratio to balance hardness and flexibility. After days of quenching, a sharp and sturdy longsword emerged. It's no legendary weapon, but as the teacher said, "Success starts with the basics." 
 
 
 
May 21st 
 
Forged Item: Resolute Blade 
 
Self-Evaluation: Satisfied 
 
Process: The teacher provided significant help with theoretical knowledge, and we engaged in discussions about materials, heat treatment, and the craft of forging. Our skills improved rapidly, but I still sought his ongoing support—hoping he would be there to witness the creation of a legendary weapon. 
 
After many days of hard work and laughter, a unique blade was born.

The teacher said my hands could one day forge a legendary weapon. 
 
I believe that one day, I'll become Jixia's greatest weapon smith.

In Jixia, entering the Academy isn't your only path. Whether you were once mired in the Academy's quagmire or wandered aimlessly at home, joining the Failed Students will help you find your ideals. 
 
No one is born to obey rules, yet the Academy attempts to shackle everyone with constraints—restraining power with rigid frameworks and confining thoughts with dogmatic principles. 
 
But they cannot halt the wheels of time. We will ultimately break through the blockade and reach the skies we aspire to.

Source: Li Wanwan, Student Affairs Committee 
 
Subject: Academic Support Work Summary 
 
"Think back over your life—do you have any particular strengths or interests?" 
"Yes, as you can see now." 
"Eh...?" 
"I'm talking to all of you, yet I don't feel nervous at all." 
"Hmm... anything else? Physical coordination? Sensitivity to Aerflow? A passion for Mechcrafts?" 
"Not really." 
"But you've been here for two years; it's time to make a decision. Martial Arts, Sorcery, or Mechcrafts?" 
"Now I'm starting to feel nervous." 
The above is a record of a conversation between our support group and Liu Ming, a student who has been at Jixia Academy for two years but still hasn't chosen a school. 
 
We helped many students who felt lost or insecure. With our guidance, they gradually discovered their inner passions, overcame obstacles, and joined the school best suited to them. 
 
Liu Ming, however, was an exception. 
Despite our best efforts, we couldn't find any school—or even Society—that suited Liu Ming's aspiration. 
"I don't know why it's so easy for everyone else... The entrance exam drained all my energy," he confessed. 
 
We've been following the procedure: taking turns to reassure him, telling him he's got potential, stuff like that. 
Amid the chatter, I suddenly remembered why I had joined the group. "Wait, this isn't fair." 
The others stopped talking and looked at me. 
 
"This student has joint issues and feels pain on rainy days, so the School of Martial Arts isn't an option. He can't sense Sorcery Energy, so the School of Sorcery is also out. And he can't even get the Mechwings properly installed, so the School of Mechcrafts..." 
"Watch your words, please!" someone said.  
"I'm just stating facts. Everyone has potential, but we can't just lie to them..." 
"Your words. please!" 
"I'm not, I'm just..." 
 
After a long silence, Liu Ming asked in a low voice, "Can I join the support group?" 
Their eyes lit up like they had found a lifeline, eagerly nodding. 
To everyone's surprise, after joining us, Liu Ming's unique experiences resonated with many of the students we were helping. Before long, he became the most popular member, with students lining up to see him. 
 
Liu Ming has found his value, and our support group gained recognition because of it. 
But... can we really take credit for that?

I thought joining this Rebel would lead to something big, but all we've done for days is observing the Windling Birds. At first, he got me all hyped about capturing them—It's something no one has ever done before. But now, after all this time there is still no action being taken, it seems like just empty talk.

Day 6 
 
 
 
Shye arrived at the camp safely with our expedition team. I could tell from her expression that she was sorry. She is very enthusiastic about exploring the ruins, but she chose safety over an ill-prepared expedition. 
 
 
 
We sat around the campfire, chatting and laughing. Shye shared her dream of forming a team like ours, but not for exploration, for treasure hunting. After all, that is her greatest aspiration and pleasure. I believe she will make it come true.

A terrible thunderstorm struck Harvest Fields! The thunder was so loud that no matter where you hid, it felt like it was exploding right next to your ears! 
 
Ladies and gentlemen, this storm was not just loud—its impact was devastating. The first bolt of lightning made the water churn wildly. No clean water was left. The second bolt turned all the fish in the ponds into monstrous creatures. The third bolt withered all the golden wheat fields. A year's worth of harvest, destroyed in an instant! 
 
If the storm had continued, Harvest Fields would have been doomed. But suddenly, in an instant, the thunder stopped! Everyone was still covering their ears when, just as suddenly, silence fell. As for why the thunder stopped, that's a story for another time. But even without thunder, the danger remained. The monstrous fish were still waiting! 
 
The people of Harvest Fields were baffled when the storm ended as suddenly as it had begun. They stepped outside to find their home almost destroyed—fish turned monstrous, water undrinkable, food gone! 
 
The Society investigated and discovered that all these strange events were connected to the Aerflow in the sky! They knew they had to act fast. In just a few days, new wheat sprouted in the fields. The villagers worried it might wither at any moment, but the wheat kept growing tall and strong. The Herb Society called it Jihu Barley, and it can still be seen in the fields today. 
 
With food taken care of, the Society turned to the water crisis. A team of students created a Mechcraft device called the Aerflow Purifier that turned polluted water into steam, keeping the villagers safe from illness. 
 
Just as that problem was solved, the Angling Society returned with baskets full of fish—the monstrous creatures had been caught. The village was safe once more. 
 
But a monster in Alsahraa was still lurking. A massive beast roared, its presence like a dark cloud. It opened its mouth, and everything that had been safe just moments before was gone. The villagers ran, calling it the Blackcloud Monster. 
 
The Society knew they had to act. A great battle was about to erupt on the Dreamweave Plains! 
 
Epic Verse: Black mists swallow heaven's light, Barren stalks haunt sleepless nights. Hundred Schools shift cosmic tides, Blades aimed skyward—mankind's might! 
 
How did the Cloudbeast overreach? What linked it to the thunder calamity? Gentle listeners... this tale awaits you next time.

Master Qin Li created countless intricate Mechcrafts during his lifetime. After completing his greatest creation, a giant flying Mechcraft, he fell into deep contemplation. 
 
His fame spread far and wide, but in a world free of war, his creation served no purpose. Every day, Jenner would stroke the Mechcraft three times and sigh deeply. 
 
 
 
One of his friends advised, "There are endless ways to use Mechcrafts in this world. Why limit yourself to soaring through the skies and slaying dragons? What about helping people in the mountains?" 
 
Qin Li retorted, "The art of Mechcrafts is a divine gift. How can it be wasted on the mere soil of the earth?" 
 
 
 
The friend left sadly, while Qin Li tossed and turned through a sleepless night. With the first light of dawn, he quietly packed his belongings and descended the mountain. 
 
The wind rustled through the wheat fields, and the golden sun slowly rose, bathing the land in light. 
 
Qin Li, who had once been so absorbed in creating Mechcrafts for war and destruction, had never really noticed the beauty of the fields he passed every day. 
 
 
 
In the nearby villages, Qin Li began repairing tools for the farmers, refusing to be paid. However, out of gratitude, the villagers insisted on treating him to freshly brewed rice wine, fragrant barley tea, and fresh caught fish... 
 
After several such occasions, Qin Li's once sharp and lean figure had become noticeably rounder. When his friend asked where he had been lately, Qin Li simply grunted, "Still researching the art of flying Mechcrafts." 
 
 
 
Not long after, Qin Li received an order from Harvest Fields, requesting a Mechcraft capable of slicing fish and slaughtering sheep. 
With little interest in the task, Qin Li threw himself into it for days on end, combining his decades of expertise in creating Mechcrafts with the practical knowledge he had gained from repairing farm tools. 
 
Eventually, he succeeded in creating a Mechcraft that was remarkably sharp and efficient, yet safe for the user — truly the pinnacle of Qin Li's skills. Even today, these Mechcrafts can still be found throughout Harvest Fields. 
 
 
 
When the Mechcraft was finished, Qin Li read the letter again and realized that the client had asked him to deliver it personally. Confused, he set off with the Mechcraft in tow.  
 
Along the way, villagers offered to help, and together they transported the Mechcraft to the client. Upon arrival, Qin Li recognized the familiar figure before him and finally understood. 
 
 
 
His friend looked around at the gathered villagers, smiled, and said, "So, Qin Li, it seems that your dragon-slaying skills have finally found their place in the soil of the earth. How does it feel?" 
 
Qin Li looked at the simple smiles of the villagers beside him, and for once, his face turned a bashful shade of red.

The residual effects of the Oneiros disruption caused by Master Crafter in Northton have yet to subside. If not resolved in time, the Oneiros disruption could spread further. The academy dispatched Aerwatch to investigate its source, while Hao Xian and I were tasked with exploring Dreamwhisper Lake. 
 
In the ruins of the Dreamweavers' clan, we discovered that all Butterfly Envoys descended from them. However, the latest generation surprisingly chose a pair of sisters. Their abilities complemented each other—the elder sister was a little-known Nightmare Weaver, while the younger sister was the well-known Finedream Weaver. 
 
Afterward, a great war broke out between the Dreamweavers and Botu. The Nightmare Weaver went missing after the battle, and the Finedream Weaver's power began to wane due to exhaustion. This could very well be the root cause of the Oneiros disruption. It is speculated that the shattering of the Runestone was the spark that ignited the chaos. 
 
Fortunately, the situation has stopped deteriorating for now, but the Finedream Weaver remains missing. Will she ever reunite with her sister? What truth lies behind Botu's deception? These mysteries still require our investigation.

The first lesson of Martial Arts training is to calm and steady the mind. 
Mastering this skill depends on controlling the rhythm of each breath. This state of mind is fleeting and hard to maintain, requiring constant effort. 
 
Diary 2 
 
The girl I met today in the Herb Garden, Lofu, bandaged my broken arm and advised me not to challenge Aermore Valley again. 
But how can I admit defeat? Leaving my mark on the Hunters' List is the best proof of a Martial Arts student's successful training. 
 
Diary 568 
 
What exactly are Martial Arts? Is it talent, hard work, or relentless effort? 
Or is it the pursuit of invincibility? 
Martial Arts are a form of power, but what exactly is this power? What can it achieve? Is it to be admired by the crowd? 
Can I really become like Senior Novar? 
Lofu says she believes I can do it. She's even more determined than I am. 
 
Diary 623 
 
I heard that the new student Senior Novar recommended recently defeated an Aersim. 
It took me years of schooling just to barely hold my own in such a battle. 
Could it be, as Jiangsuan said, that it's talent, not effort? Is talent really innate? 
Lofu mentioned that she once saw a method unrelated to talent in the Forbidden Chamber. What could that be? 
 
Diary 1,097 
 
"The realm of Martial Arts is like a mountain peak, or a vast, misty sea. Those without talent will find it difficult to achieve. Therefore, I have turned to study Sorcery for several years, eventually grasping the principles of Martial Arts that beyond the human limitation.... Maintaing treasures, balancing the organs, burning the battle will to overpower strong enemies, and finally, attaining enlightenment and reaching the pinnacle of Martial Arts..."

Perhaps it was the influence of the dream, but my body grew heavier, and even breathing became difficult...

I can never forget that deep-seated fear! It was like a nightmare—dark, inhuman monsters that seemed to wield the power of destruction. In an instant, the village was overrun with disaster. Fire mercilessly swept through, destroying homes, and monsters trampled houses into ruins. There were screams everywhere; many who couldn't escape were badly injured. My mother was hurt badly protecting me. The enemy's brutal actions filled the entire village with a tragic atmosphere. Fortunately, during our panicked escape, we met a group of soldiers. Their armor bore special markings that resembled a glimmer of hope in the darkness. Under their protection, we took refuge in a cave. The Saepes around the cave seemed to sense the danger and quickly blocked the entrance, finally allowing us to escape the monsters. Inside the cave, we sat around a campfire and prepared food. In that brief moment of peace, our anxious hearts found a little comfort. But this peace was short-lived. The terrifying monster was still roaming the wilderness, like a dark shadow ready to pounce on us at any moment, filling our hearts with fear. What should we do next?
The catastrophe arrived. Sacrifices became the last weapon of the guardians, sparking a glimmer of hope.

I held my Mechanoid in my hands, my heart filled with unease. 
 
"This Mechanoid, despite limited testing, performed well in previous matches, defeating opponents one after another. But the final is next—can it still hold up? Plus, the final will be held outdoors, and Father will definitely be there to watch..." 
"Whatever. Even if I don't win, I must prove myself!" 
With these thoughts, I resolutely walked into the venue. The area was small but packed with people, and my opponent was already there. I nervously approached and realized the figure seemed familiar. On closer inspection, it was Zhou Yan. 
 
"Wait, him? What a twist of fate," I thought, "No wonder—after all, he's got the result of my weeks of work in his hands." 
 
"You actually made it this far? But this is where it ends. Get ready to embarrass yourself in front of our father!" Zhou Yan taunted. 
 
"Hmph. It's not decided who will lose yet," I replied. 
 
 
 
"Begin!" The judge had barely finished speaking when our Mechanoids were already in battle. His Mechanoid moved quickly and aggressively, its punches like a storm. Mine could only defend, with no chance to counterattack. 
 
What should I do? Sweat beaded on my forehead. 
 
"Looks like the outcome is clear," Zhou Yan sneered. 
 
I quickly shot back, "Not necessarily. I think your Mechanoid has used up all its strength. It's almost done for." 
 
"What are you implying? Huh? Looks like I need to teach you a lesson." Clearly, my words had angered him. 
 
Zhou Yan's Mechanoid suddenly exerted all its strength, leaning forward to deliver a fatal blow. 
 
Now's my chance! While it's off guard, I must land a critical hit to turn the tide. The Mechanoid's weakness... 
 
Right! That unused tenon and mortise Mechcraft! 
 
With this thought, I controlled my Mechanoid to rapidly fire an Aersilk bullet, striking the opponent's neck. 
 
Zhou Yan's Mechanoid abruptly stopped moving, and then, amidst a loud noise, it collapsed, its parts scattering on the ground. 
 
Silence. The arena was quiet as a tomb, as if time had frozen. 
 
"Zhou Ying wins!" The judge's announcement shattered the stillness, followed by thunderous applause and cheers that echoed over the academy. 
 
 
 
"You... you cheated! I demand a rematch!" Zhou Yan's voice was drowned out, and when he realized no one was listening, he slunk away in defeat. 
 
 
 
After basking in the celebration, I prepared for the award ceremony, only to find my stepmother and brother arguing in front of my father. 
 
"This is ridiculous!" My stepmother turned to me. "You, explain! What kind of trickery did you use to beat our Zhou Yan?" 
 
I ignored her and explained to my father, "Father, the reason I won so easily is simple. The Mechanoid my brother used was originally my creation." 
 
"How is that?" My father seemed surprised, and the audience near the stage began to whisper among themselves. 
 
"This Mechanoid was designed by me. They stole the blueprints when I wasn't in the dorm. During the design phase, I added a tenon and mortise lock Mechcraft for easy maintenance. If it's hit just below the neck with a bullet, the Mechanoid will dismantle. It had never been used until now." 
 
"No wonder I was puzzled earlier..." My father's expression was serious as he nodded. 
 
"He stole someone else's design and couldn't even understand it properly!" 
 
"He had the nerve to use it without any changes? Couldn't he read the blueprint?" 
 
"This is a disgrace to the School of Mechcrafts! A student like him should be expelled!" 
 
As the crowd discussed, I couldn't help but smile. 
 
"You're slandering Zhou Yan! How could he steal from you? Do you take pleasure in lying?" My stepmother shouted wildly, but her words lacked power. My brother hung his head, silent and no longer arrogant. 
 
"Enough! You've spoiled him into this state. He's now brave enough to steal!" 
 
My father's face turned red with anger as he scolded my stepmother, "You two, go back and pack your bags. Tomorrow, you'll go back to Chang'an with me. No more embarrassing me here!" 
 
My stepmother dared not speak, only glaring at me with venomous eyes. 
 
"Father, please calm down." I mimicked my stepmother's tone, "It's just a small matter. Don't let it upset you." 
 
My father calmed down and said, "Daughter, were you frightened? Let's have dinner and talk tonight. For now, go back. I'll deal with these two and come find you." 
 
I nodded. 
 
"A true shame!" My father turned and dragged the pair away, leaving behind only ruined reputations and gossip. 
 
 
 
Later, I inherited my father's legacy, and my tenon and mortise lock Mechcraft was listed as an outstanding design by the academy. 
 
As for my stepmother and brother, they reaped what they sowed and were never again involved in the Zhou family's Mechcraft business. 
 
On the other hand, several workshop owners from the bustling market have extended olive branches, awaiting the top tenon and mortise Mechcraft expert from Jixia to bring their talent to their workshops. 
 
My life had never been better.

My dear daughter, 
Though I never write you letters, urgent family matters now compel me to ask your swift return home. 
 
Lately I've been plagued by persistent abdominal pain. The Herbalist diagnosed me with gastric ailment requiring frequent acupuncture treatments this month. To spare your mother worry, I entreat you to take her on an extended outing - this would grant me peace to focus on recovery. 
 
May you stay in good health.

January 13 
 
 
 
Today, I began training with the <5ea8f3>Tiger Leap</>. I couldn't handle it and was punished by Master to clean up after dinner. I feel like I'm not cut out for martial arts. 
 
 
 
March 5 
I've almost adapted to the current training intensity, and my progress has been quite rapid, thanks to my senior. Today, I witnessed a challenger. Master's fight with him was fierce and exciting, indicating that our usual training barely taps into a tenth of our potential. 
 
 
 
July 8 
Yesterday, I challenged another training hall and sustained a minor injury. Neither of us intended to harm, so I didn't make an issue of it. However, today Master insisted on avenging me by challenging that training hall. When he returned in the evening, he was more battered than I was, which shocked my seniors. Yet, he grinned and said he taught that training hall a harsh lesson. I must work hard to honor Master and the Roaring Tiger Training Hall.

Half a century has passed since you first cast your line, the King Fish said, gazing at the rusty hook. 
 
The angler, once a spirited youth with wild black hair, now stood as an elderly man with only a few wisps of transparent white hair. He shook his head and sighed, "I won't stop until I reel you in." 
 
Fifty years ago, the young angler had made a bet with the King Fish. Full of confidence, he vowed to catch the fish, but the wise King Fish was never tempted by any bait. 
 
Over time, the angler caught many of the King Fish's offspring and companions, leaving it almost alone. Now, only one small fish remained. 
 
The little fish swam cheerfully around the worm on the hook, creating bubbles in the water. 
 
This was the last fish in the pond besides the King Fish. Its parents had been lured away by hooks soon after it was born, making it the only new life in the pond. 
 
"Do you intend to take this one too?" The King Fish looked at the old man through the clear water with its cloudy eyes. 
 
The old man nodded. 
 
The King Fish turned to the young fish, then willingly bit onto the hook that had rested here for fifty years.

Before coming to Jixia, I only knew that the Obsidian Flame Training Hall was an expert in developing mechanical cannons, which seemed to have nothing to do with someone like me, who practiced martial arts. 
 
I never imagined that I would have an interesting encounter with it in the future. 
 
This story begins by the lake. 
 
In order to find the Obsidian Flame Training Hall and challenge its Intendant, I spent a long time in Ji Xia. 
 
As I passed by the lake, I decided to take a rest and see if there were any fat fish in the water. 
 
If I could catch a couple of them and cook them in the way of Jade City, that would be a truly delightful experience. 
 
However, just as I was playing with the fish in the lake, I suddenly heard a loud explosion, and at the same time, a huge whirlpool emerged in the center of the lake. 
 
At that moment, I thought I had been attacked by a monster and prepared to fight it. But before I could even see what the monster looked like, my legs were frozen in the lake water. 
 
I couldn't understand how the clear, sparkling water of the lake could suddenly freeze over. If it wasn't a monster, could it be a unique natural wonder of Jixia? It seems I've really been in Jade City for too long; I need to go out and see the world more often. 
 
As I was marveling at the wonders of Jixia, the cold had already spread throughout my body. Before I lost consciousness, a nimble figure flashed by in front of my eyes. 
 
When I woke up, I was already inside the Obsidian Flame Training Hall. The students there told me that it was the Intendant who had rescued me from the frozen lake. 
 
"Sometimes, fate leads us to see unexpected wonders, and that is probably the beauty of life..." I muttered to myself, wrapped in a blanket and warming myself by the stove. 
 
When I mentioned the "frozen lake" wonder of Jixia, the students apologized repeatedly. They explained to me that what I had experienced was not a natural wonder of Jixia, but a new type of Mechcraft developed by the Intendant of the Obsidian Flame Training Hall. This Mechcraft was capable of firing projectiles that could freeze the surface of the lake. During the test, they had forgotten to check if there was anyone in the lake, so they accidentally attacked me. 
 
"Is this letter yours?" 
 
The Intendant appeared beside me without me even hearing her footsteps. 
 
I now understood why the head trainer of the Roaring Tiger Training Hall had highly recommended me to come to the Obsidian Flame Training Hall; both the Intendant of these two places were of the cat-like beast kind. However, while Tigon was fierce and aggressive, the Intendant before me was kind and elegant, with a playful and cunning spark in her eyes. 
 
The Intendant saw my letter of recommendation and guessed my purpose, but she was not interested in fighting with me. 
 
After my repeated requests, I don't know whether it was because of the letter of recommendation or out of guilt, but she agreed to fight with me. 
 
Before the fight, she insisted on showing me around the Obsidian Flame Training Hall. 
 
I didn't know much about Cannon Mechcraft, but the cannons displayed throughout the pavilion were of such an enormous size that I even wondered if they were meant for the study of Cannon or for attacking cities. 
 
"It's already started..." As I was wondering, the master had already taken out two exquisite cannons and said softly, "As long as you hit me, you win." 
 
With that, she soared into the air and jumped from one building to another like a cat. I took out my weapon and followed closely behind. 
 
It was only after the fight began that I understood why the master had such confidence. 
 
I thought she would run away in a flash, but instead, she often stopped in one place, seemingly inviting me to attack. The moment I approached her, she would use her nimble steps to distance herself from me, and at the same time, fire the cannons in her hands, catching me off guard. 
 
I not only had to find ways to get close to her but also constantly avoid the cannons. Before long, I was out of breath. 
 
For a martial artist, breathing is of utmost importance; once one's breathing becomes irregular, all one's moves will be affected. 
 
Yet, even as she moved up and down, she maintained a steady breathing pattern. Perhaps the reason she was so agile and nimble was her strong control over her breathing. 
 
If I wanted to win her, I had to find a different approach. 
 
As dusk fell, the fight came to an end with me covered in soot from the gunpowder. 
 
The master was still calm and playful as ever. 
 
"I'm sorry; I was a bit too forceful..." she said with a smile. 
 
"The master's agility is truly remarkable; I feel inferior in comparison. But... according to the rules, it seems I won." 
 
I picked up a tassel from her shoulder. 
 
It was the tassel from the hilt of my sword. During the fight, when I realized that I couldn't win by speed, I came up with this strategy. 
 
I had hung the tassel between the branches in advance, and then I pretended to attack from the opposite direction. In order to avoid me, she would naturally use the trees as cover to distance herself from me. 
 
In this way, the tassel might end up on her. 
 
In the end, although neither my sword nor I touched her, the tassel landed on her, so it was considered that I had won. 
 
After understanding what had happened, the master fell into deep thought. She said that she had never seen such a "tactic" before. 
 
"Perhaps, both the body and the mind need to be more flexible..." she sighed at the end.

Dreamslayer lurks in the hidden depths of the realm of dreams. 
Dreamweavers maintain the balance of the Dreamscape, while Dreamslayers, who also consume precious Oneiros, only bring instinctual plunder and destruction. 
Nightmare Dreamthorn shadows them, relentlessly eroding the boundaries of the Dreamscape. 
No one knows where Dreamslayers come from, what keeps them alive, or where the Oneiros they absorb goes. 
But this is certain: if you doubt your dreams, when you wake, you will be indistinguishable from the thorns. 
Whether you are a Dreamweaver, human, or beast, Dreamslayer could be your fate.

Contributor: Long Feng, Teacher at the School of Martial Arts 
 
Content: Letter of Resignation 
 
Editor's Note: To embark on a journey of self-discovery is never an empty notion. Those who embrace their destiny, chart their own path, and define their truth shall not be hindered by me. 
 
Whenever I watch Aersilk drift across the sky, transforming into various forms with the breeze, I am reminded of a particular individual. 
 
His name was Mu An, and he was once my classmate. 
 
Years ago, I traveled from the Southlands to Jixia to pursue my studies. After overcoming numerous trials, both great and small, I finally became a student at the School of Martial Arts. 
 
Yet even so, amidst the sea of talented individuals and fierce competition within the school, I could not afford to slacken for even a moment. Day in and day out, I trained relentlessly, honing my skills and techniques, fearful of falling behind my peers. 
 
I had always believed that all students shared my unwavering dedication until I met Mu An. 
 
During our monthly tests, our teachers would ask us to transform Aersilk into a weapon of our choice. In an instant, all the new students were flustered, unsure of how to shape the chaotic mass of Aersilk into a blade. 
 
Mu An, however, transformed the Aersilk in his left hand into a white crane and in his right hand into a butterfly, before changing them into various shapes. 
 
His mastery of Aersilk was nothing short of remarkable, astonishing everyone present. 
 
The only issue was that, for reasons unknown, he refused to transform Aersilk into any form of weapon, which meant he failed the test just like the rest of us. 
 
In the days that followed, Mu An used Aersilk to create hammocks for naps, crafted exquisite accessories to flaunt before his classmates, and even turned it into fishing rods for angling. 
 
On one occasion, while we were undergoing physical training in the mountains, the ground began to shift, and boulders started tumbling down. If Mu An hadn't used Aersilk to create a safety net in the nick of time, several of our classmates would have fallen off the cliff. 
 
His talent with Aersilk was unparalleled, and even our teachers couldn't help but marvel at his creativity. However, unless he transformed Aersilk into a weapon, he wouldn't be able to pass the exams. 
 
I asked him privately why he was so opposed to using weapons. 
 
Mu An explained that he had come to Jixia from the Great Wall to study, and upon graduation, he planned to join the Great Wall Guards. He would then spend his days battling the Demon Tribe, which would provide ample opportunity to handle weapons. 
 
A few years later, Mu An joined the Great Wall Guards, just as he had said, while I remained at the academy as a teacher. 
 
Though we were separated by distance, we continued to exchange letters over the years. 
 
Until recently, when I received his last letter. 
 
The letter was returned to me by Mu An's comrade-in-arms, who told me that Mu An had covered everyone's retreat during an encounter battle and then disappeared without a trace. 
 
Headmaster Fuzi, I am deeply aware of the weighty responsibilities that come with being a teacher at the School of Martial Arts. But I must go to the Great Wall to find him. 
 
Today, as a student of martial arts, as Mu An's close friend, and simply as myself, I am submitting my resignation to you. I hope you will approve it.

October 15th 
 
After days of research, I finally uncovered the secret of the Moonelia Sprout toxin. In a secret cave near the Herb Garden, I analyzed its components step by step. The toxin indeed has powerful therapeutic effects, capable of eliminating pain, but it is also extremely unstable, and excessive use can cause fatal damage to the body. Its flaws made me cautious; perhaps its therapeutic effect is not worth the risk. 
 
Before long, the Herb Society discovered my traces, forcing me to leave hastily. Although the research was not completed,  I harbored no lingering regrets. After all, abandoning this perilous and imperfect toxin scarcely counted as loss. The mystery of the Moonelia Sprout, I will never know again, but its toxin has long lost its allure in my heart. 
 
This journey will finally come to an end.

Jixia is currently in a thriving period of food culture. Every week, I receive invitations from diners of all backgrounds to sample new dishes. 
 
I firmly believe that pleasing everyone is impossible, as personal preferences and experiences vary greatly, leading to vastly different standards for judging good food. 
 
This article simply documents some of the Jixia dishes that have left the deepest impression on me. If you have any disagreements, I welcome your opinions. 
 
 
 
Name: Academy Dumplings 
 
Review: The dumplings are as big as fists, perfectly round and plump, with consistent pleat counts and spacing. They have a white color with a yellow tint and are marked with different colors to distinguish the fillings. 
 
Before taking a bite, the rich aroma of fermented dough fills the air. Once bitten, the dumplings burst with juice and ample filling, filling the mouth. The sweetness and a hint of strange spices balance out the greasiness, making them irresistible. 
 
As the signature dish of Zhang, the renowned Gourmet, it is said to sell thousands every day. The most impressive aspect of this dish, aside from its taste, is its consistent quality. 
 
If I could only choose one dish to eat every day, it would definitely be dumplings made by Zhang. Additionally, I can confirm that the legendary seasonal limited fillings do exist. However, at Zhang's strong request to keep it secret, I regretfully cannot reveal the details of the taste to other diners. 
 
 
 
Name: Dragon Wontons 
 
Review: Though this is a bowl of wontons, the ingredients are top-notch. The wonton wrappers are made from the finest Jihu Barley, and the filling consists of tender and springy meat mixed with Fish Fruit Tree for added flavor. 
 
Not only are the ingredients of high quality, but the appearance of this dish is also a masterpiece. The wrappers are as clear as the full moon, and the filling is as rich as jade. Serving it in an emerald bowl is the perfect touch, evoking the image of green mountains under the moon. 
 
At this point, I crave a steaming hot bowl of Dragon Wontons. 
 
 
 
Name: Rain-kissed Spring Rolls 
 
Review: If we're talking about elegance and refinement, Rain-kissed Spring Rolls undoubtedly take the lead. 
 
The dish features lotus leaves filled with petals, the green and pink colors blending in a delicate and charming beauty. As you unwrap the layers, you reveal the exquisitely tender and translucent fish. The fish has absorbed the fragrance of the lotus during steaming and is seasoned with Pano-Seasoning and Bitewood, resulting in a lingering flavor. For those who prefer sweeter tastes, drizzling an extra layer of flower honey enhances the sweetness. 
 
The ingredients required to make this dish are not complex; as far as I know, there are only four. This shows that the deliciousness of a dish is not always related to the richness of the ingredients.

Review: This is a new and popular healthy dessert among students, made from the finest Skipple and Crackle. 
 
The soft and chewy glutinous rice wrapping encloses a dense fruit filling. One bite fills the mouth with a rich layering of wrapper and filling, creating an excellent texture. 
 
The natural sweetness of the fruit and glutinous rice, combined with the freshness of the ingredients, makes it no surprise that this dessert is such a bestseller. 
 
 
 
Jixia offers many more delicious foods, and I'm sure there are even more waiting for me beyond its borders. 
 
Though this is my aspiration, after more than thirty years, I still haven't left Jixia. The journey of food exploration is indeed long.

I believe this will be of great help in our research of the entire Dreamscape area.

Further observation is needed.
