Have you ever heard of the legend that Wolverines snatch away children? The nomadic tribes living in the grasslands and mountains often depict Wolverines as fearsome creatures to scare their young into returning home early. In reality, Wolverines are a territorial species that live in packs. They have poor eyesight and rarely stray far from their territory. So, these legends are likely nothing more than tales told by parents to frighten their children. 
However, it's undeniable that Wolverines are naturally fierce and combative. One of the most widespread stories about them tells of two Wolverines plotting to ambush a butcher: one pretends to sleep as bait while the other digs a hole behind the butcher, waiting to strike. The butcher sees through their plan and survives, but encountering a Wolverine in real life would not end so fortunately. These creatures, commonly found in grasslands and mountains, are nocturnal and known for their piercing howls. They are swift, with snow-white fur and deep blue scales covering their bodies. Their sharp front claws, evolved from their burrowing habits, make them excellent at ambush attacks. Wolverines typically appear in packs, surrounding their prey and attacking in unison. Their attack process involves hiding in a burrow, gathering strength, and then launching a pounce. Once they bring down their prey, they first use their claws to tear and weaken the prey's resistance, then their sharp fangs to grip the throat, making them a highly dangerous species. The Wolverines' social structure is strictly hierarchical, and their status can often be identified by the position of their tails. The alpha, or wolf king, usually holds its tail high as a symbol of leadership, while the lowest-ranked Wolverine keeps its tail tucked between its legs, walking in a submissive manner. In my view, Wolverines are exceptionally well-organized creatures, with a strong sense of unity within their packs. During combat, they act with one mind, advancing and retreating together. Additionally, they possess a cunning nature, often displaying a certain level of intelligence even when seemingly outmatched, using tricks to achieve their hunting goals, just as the legends describe. 
In daily life, it's crucial to recognize Wolverine territory and avoid it at all costs. If you accidentally wander into such an area or spot a Wolverine in your field of vision, stay extremely alert — its companions are likely lying in wait nearby. Never flee in panic, as the Wolverine's hunting instincts will drive it to quickly attack a moving target. Instead, assess the surrounding terrain and use anything at hand to protect yourself. If there are trees nearby, climb up immediately, as Wolverines cannot climb trees. Wait quietly, and they will eventually leave on their own.

Month, Date 
 
Today my big brother came back grinning, carrying a long narrow package. He said it had to be a sword inside. I asked him why, and he raised his brows and said, 
 
"Just look at the patina, the sheen—this is an antique!" 
 
But when we opened it, there was only a flute. He was furiously. 
 
He couldn't understand why anyone would give a twig its own box. Maybe he had never seen one before. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
I secretly picked the flute back. My brother tried to snap it a couple of times and couldn't—so the material must be decent. I remembered the neighbors having one when I was little, but I never touched it. After they played, they'd always shake the spit out, and it seemed filthy. 
 
This one looked clean enough. I rinsed it with spring water and left it to dry. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
After two days of trying, I actually got it to sound! But it's a nuisance—you have to shake the spit out after a while. 
 
On my fourth try, I got spit on my brother's face. He didn't say a word, but I could tell he was upset. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
I picked the flute up again. My brother might not be the sharpest, but when it comes to throwing things, he's a pro. 
 
My head still aches from the smack. 
 
Still, I think I'm getting the hang of it. This time it doesn't sound so harsh. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
I've decided to practice in the northern clearing, far enough away not to annoy my brother. 
 
After I swore to keep the flute out of camp, he finally smiled and said if he ever saw it here again, either I or the flute would get snapped in two. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
Bad news: the flute drew in wolves. 
 
Good news: they also brought it back to me. 
 
We ended up playing together for quite a while. 
 
 
 
Month, Date 
 
I realized that if I follow a rhythm, the flute sounds almost pleasant. 
 
Maybe I should buy a songbook in town? 
 
Might need a new flute too—this one's a little bent after brother's rough handling. 
 
But it still plays. I'll keep at it a few more days.
zh_text:
X月X日 
今天大哥兴高采烈的带回来一个包裹，细长细长的，说里面恐怕是一柄宝剑，我问为什么？大哥眉毛一扬， 
“你看这成色！这包浆！这可是老物件了——” 
结果没想到打开之后里面只有一支箫，气得大哥怒骂不已。 
他不明白为什么树枝也要专门配个盒子，他可能没见过。 
 
X月X日 
我偷偷把那支箫捡回来了，大哥试了两下都没把它撅断，可见料子不错。我小时候邻居家里也有一支，但我看他们吹完之后老得甩口水，脏得很，所以我没碰过。 
这支箫看起来还是挺干净的，我用泉水冲洗了一遍，先晾着。 
 
X月X日 
我试了两天，还真被我吹响了！不过这东西确实不方便，吹一段时间就要把口水甩干净。 
第四次甩口水的时候甩到大哥脸上了，大哥虽然不说话，但是我感觉他脸色有点差。 
 
X月X日 
我又把箫捡回来了，大哥虽然脑子不好使，但是扔东西是真的远。 
敲脑瓜也很疼。 
但是我感觉我已经摸着门道了，这回吹起来应该不会那么吵了。 
 
X月X日 
我决定到北边空地那边练，那边离得远，不会吵到大哥。 
大哥在听我保证后笑着说，不要再让箫出现在营地里，不然我和箫他肯定撅断一个。 
 
X月X日 
坏消息，箫把狼给引来了。 
好消息，狼还会把箫捡回来给我。 
跟狼玩了好一会儿。 
 
X月X日 
我发现只要按照规律来，就能吹得很好听。 
要不去镇上买本曲谱？ 
或许还得买一支新的箫，现在这支细看好像有点弯了，大哥手劲儿真不是盖的。 
但还能吹。再吹几天。

Thank you for your years of guidance and care for Yun Feixie. 
 
Both her mother and I are deeply grateful, though we cannot help but feel some concern. We worry that if she does not apply herself with full diligence, your efforts may go to waste. 
 
As you know, she is hardworking and ambitious, though her youth leaves her at times quick-tempered and impatient. We humbly ask that you continue to guide her with firm discipline and patient instruction, so that she may grow into the student worthy of your tutelage.
zh_text:
卫安阁主： 
 
感谢您对飞榭多年的栽培。 
我与飞榭的母亲十分感激，但也不免有些担忧，担心她不认真学，白费阁主您的苦心。 
您也了解飞榭，她虽努力上进，但年少气盛，心性不稳。还请阁主日后对飞榭严格约束、多加管教。

text:
Day 10 
 
When I returned to the camp, I found Rebels rampaging through the place. They seemed very arrogant, but as soon as they saw me, they immediately became timid and ran away. 
 
These rats must have come for the Frostmane Spike Bear. 
 
I figured that since I was already here, I might as well leave with something. So, I confiscated their weapons, although I don't think much of them.
zh_text:
第十日 
 
今日回到营地，发现破门生正在营地里大肆破坏，好不嚣张。然而见了我立马变怂，拔腿就跑。 
 
这群鼠辈应是为了霜鬃狂熊才闯进来的。 
 
我认为既然来了，总要留下点什么才能走。是故我缴了他们的武器，不过那些武器我也看不上眼就是了。

text:
The earth and sky merge, with my emotions drifting among the clouds. 
 
 
 
A towering spire stands, with waves gently brushing against the wind. 
 
 
 
Clouds dance amidst the mountains and rivers, with ripples leisurely spreading their light. 
 
 
 
Green peaks rise one after another, with the shallow sounds of footsteps on stones. 
 
 
 
Cloud shadows sway, evoking the beautiful images of the past, only to vanish without a trace. 
 
 
 
The hopes in my heart weave and spread across the sky. 
 
 
 
I have sought the traces of the past amidst the wind and moon. 
 
 
 
I have joined the flow of the crowd, savoring the fleeting moments of life. 
 
 
 
White waves and green moss overlap with the years, with cloud shadows dancing as they always have.. 
 
 
 
A weary wanderer has finally returned to the vast lands they call home.
zh_text:
天地交融，心绪落云中。 
  
巨塔耸立，波涛轻抚风。 
 
云舞山水，悠然波光漾。 
 
青峦叠嶂，踏石浅浅声。 
 
云影婆娑，宛若旧时倩影，消散无踪。 
 
胸中热望，编织、蔓延于天穹。  
 
在风月之间，寻觅过往痕迹。 
 
随人潮涌动，赏味浮生迷离。 
 
白浪绿苔，年岁交错，云影轻舞，婆娑如故。 
 
失意游子，终归广阔天地。

text:
Error reporting temporarily suspended. This repair is relatively conservative to avoid accidental damage to the <69D0FF> internal structure of the Hengzhu Flow </>, though we cannot rule out that this area is the epicenter of the malfunction.
We anticipate starting a new round of full-scale testing, removing the isolation measures from the suspected fault center.

Test Item One: Evasion Test
Test Content: Performance of the Mozi Armor's evasion capabilities in live combat.
Test Result: Normal.

Test Item Two: Advanced Test
Test Content: The Mozi Armor's ability to handle different enemy types in combat scenarios.
Test Result: <69D0FF> Slight abnormality </>, with occasional minor deviations in command execution.

Test Item Three: Stress Combat Test
Test Content: The Mozi Armor's endurance during high-intensity solo combat.
Test Result: <69D0FF> Abnormal </>, with massive core errors and, in extreme cases, a tendency for the armor to move autonomously without input.

(This record has been set aside separately; the surface shows signs of being handled repeatedly.)
zh_text:
报错暂时停止。本次修复相对保守，避免误伤<69D0FF>衡注流的内部构造</>部分，但不排除该部分为故障中心点。 
预计开启新一轮全量测试，移除疑似故障中心点的隔离措施。 
 
测试项目一：闪避测试 
测试内容：在实战状态下，墨子甲的闪避能力表现。 
测试结果：正常。 
 
测试项目二：进阶测试 
测试内容：在战斗情形下，墨子甲应对不同类型敌人的能力。 
测试结果：<69D0FF>轻微异常</>，偶现指令执行轻度偏差的情况。 
 
测试项目三：压力战斗测试 
测试内容：在高强度战斗情形下，墨子甲单兵作战的承压能力。 
测试结果：<69D0FF>异常</>，核心大量报错，极端情况下机甲出现不受控制自主移动的倾向。 
 
（这一份记录被单独取出放置在此处，表面有被反复摩挲的痕迹。）

This volume introduces the Societies of Jixia and tackles a question often asked: how many Societies are there in Jixia? 
 
 
 
Seeker Society: 
 
 
 
From dawn to dusk, the Seeker Society's footprint spans across Jixia, excelling in treasure hunting, exploration, artifact collection, and archaeological research. 
 
 
 
As the inaugural volume of the Contention of Societies series, this book will introduce the renowned Societies of Jixia. 
 
 
 
The Societies are a collective term for various groups primarily composed of graduates from Jixia Academy. For students graduating from Jixia Academy, joining a society is an inevitable path towards further education. As an editor at the Jixia Academy Journal Club, this is my interpretation of the Societies. However which society among the societies—such as the Herb Society, the Gourmet Society, the Angling Society, the Hunting Society, the Craft Society, the Seeker Society, the Music Society, the Astrology Society, the Cannon Society...—was the first to be established in Jixia has always been an issue I wanted to figure out. 
 
 
 
Due to differences in the Societies chosen by editors for further study, this significant introduction has been revised by successive editors for various purposes. 
 
 
 
The establishment of a Society is an arduous process. Firstly, the founder must have authored at least one renowned work, this work had to be significant enough to pave the way for the creation of a completely new field of study. Afterwards, the founder must submit an application to Jixia Academy. And only upon approval could they begin conducting small-scale lectures and teaching their ideas. It was not until the founder gained the recognition of all Jixia's Three Sages that they were allowed to recruit their own students and formally establish a new Society. 
 
 
 
It is said that some Societies have only a handful of members, making it hard to imagine how their establishment and succession occur. 
 
 
 
The Societies of Jixia are renowned worldwide for their unconventional academic and regional cultural practices. The most prominent are the "Rustic Societies," where members often use the natural environment as their classroom, teaching anywhere except traditional classrooms. The "Contention of Societies," as the book title suggests, refers to the frequent debates between Societies, each presenting their theories. These discussions are purely based on the correctness of the arguments, rarely involving personal biases. This pure and flexible academic atmosphere is what has made Jixia so prosperous. 
 
 
 
In the following volumes, we will gradually unveil the mysteries of the Societies of Jixia, exploring both their widely circulated and lesser-known anecdotes. 
 
 
 
From an academic perspective, Jixia Academy, as the most renowned institution of learning, attracts all knowledge-seeking scholars from Primaera. Therefore, the formation of Societies was an inevitable trend in the academy's development history. (Since I have the privilege of editing this volume of Contention of Societies, I will take the liberty of listing the Seeker Society, dedicated to historical research, as the first Society!)

本册将向各位读者介绍稷下的各百家，关于稷下百家究竟有多少家这件事。 
 
风物家： 
 
朝碧海，暮苍梧，风物家的足迹遍布稷下，寻宝探险、文物考古他们样样精通。 
 
本册作为《百家争鸣》系列书籍的开篇，将为读者介绍闻名遐迩的稷下百家。 
 
稷下百家是众多围绕稷下学院毕业生为主而组建的团体总称。作为在稷下学院毕业的学生来说，百家就相当于他们继续深造的必经之路。这是作为稷下学院校刊社的本编者，给予稷下百家当下的解释。然而百草家、肴馔家、垂钓家、游猎家、工巧家、风物家、宫羽家、占星家、火器家……究竟哪家是第一个设立在稷下的百家，一直是我想要弄明白的议题。 
 
由于社内编辑最后选择深造的百家不同，这个具有首屈一指意义的抬头，被历代编辑以各种目的进行修正。 
 
百家的创立极其艰难。首先作为创立者本身，必须拥有一部以上的知名著作。而这部著作必须足以开创一个全新的专精领域。之后创立者要向稷下学院提交申请，待通过以后，才可以开始小范围实验性质的传播讲学。只有在创立者获得了全部稷下三贤的认可后，才能够招揽自己的门生，正式成立新的百家。 
 
据说，有一些百家的人数只有寥寥数人，很难想象他们的创立与传承是如何进行的。 
 
作为稷下百家，被世界广为所知的就是不拘一格的学术性地域文化。首屈一指的为“乡野百家”，百家们喜欢以天地为课堂，在除了教室以外的任何地方进行讲学。又如书名的“百家争鸣”，就是百家之间经常以各自的理论相互辩述，而这种讨论只以正确与否为判定标准，多数时候不夹杂主观臆断。正是这种纯粹，不拘形式的学术氛围，才让稷下发展的如此强大。 
 
接下来的书籍就让我们逐步揭开稷下百家的神秘面纱，一览它们或广为流传，或乡野闲谈的轶事。 
 
本着学术角度理性分析，稷下学院作为最著名的学府，吸引着王者大陆所有渴望知识的学子。所以百家的形成是学院发展历史上的必然趋势。（既然现在这个版本的《百家争鸣》轮到本人编撰，那么就让我擅自把研究历史的风物家列为第一位的百家吧！）

When I returned to the camp, I found Rebels rampaging through it. They seemed very arrogant, but as soon as they saw me, they immediately became timid and ran away. 
These rats must have come for the Frostmane Spike Bear.

text:
I've been studying "Tips on Movement" for a while, but I still can't grasp some of its concepts. 
 
 
 
"Motion arises from stillness, and movement returns to stillness"—what does that mean? 
 
 
 
I've tried various methods of exerting force, but to no avail. 
 
 
 
With no answers, I decided to observe the state of the lotus flowers as described in the text. 
 
 
 
The lotus flowers and leaves in the pond stand upright. They're steady without wind, but when the wind blows, ripples spread across the entire pond. Still, I couldn't comprehend the subtlety described in the writing. 
 
 
 
I then observed the branches in winter. Pine branches often break under heavy snow, while plum branches quickly shake off the snow after accumulating a certain amount. 
 
 
 
After a heavy snow, many pine branches broke, but the plum branches remained intact. 
 
 
 
As the spring breeze blows, my long-standing confusion is finally cleared up. 
 
 
 
I rose to practice my movements and, in doing so, found significant insights.
zh_text:
练习“身动诀窍”已经有一段时间了，我还是没办法理解里面的一些内容。 
 
“因静生动，动起归静”，究竟是什么意思呢…… 
 
我尝试了许多种运用气力的方法，一无所获。 
 
思考无果的我只能根据诀窍上的形容，去观察荷花的状态。 
 
满池的荷花与荷叶身姿挺立，无风时沉稳挺立，风起时却有满塘波澜。我却仍旧无法理解，诀窍中所言的巧妙。 
 
我又看见了冬日的树枝。松树坚韧，树枝常常因为积雪过多而压折。梅枝上也有着积雪，积累到一定数量，便快速弹动后将积雪全都抖落。 
 
一场大雪过后，松树多有折断，梅枝却完好如初。 
 
春风徐来，半年的迷惑终于解开。 
 
我起身练习身法，终有所得。

The lotus flowers and leaves in the pond stand upright. They're steady without wind, but when the wind blows, ripples spread across the entire pond. Still, I couldn't comprehend the subtlety described in the writing.

After a heavy snow, many pine branches broke, but the plum branches remained intact. 
 
 
 
As the spring breeze blows, my long-standing confusion is finally cleared up. 
 
 
 
I rose to practice my movements and, in doing so, found significant insights.

November 16th 
Just like its escape, <69D0FF> someone intentionally taught it to harm others. </> 
 
<69D0FF> He actually intended to raise Xinwuwei as a weapon to realize his ambitions. </> 
 
I paced back and forth in the basement, knocking things over. It lay there obediently, knowing I was angry. 
It cannot distinguish between good and evil like a human, so how could it be capable of malicious harm? 
I told Xinwuwei that I would protect it. 
It understood, and happily went back to pouncing on its mechanical toy. 
 
I suddenly remembered what he taught Xinwuwei: 
"Before you, people fall into three categories. 
Those who turn and run are prey. 
Those who attack are enemies. 
Those willing to shake hands with a monster are friends."

text:
After days of travel, I finally arrived at Jixia Academy. 
 
 
 
My weary body reminded me of the arduous journey. I've traveled to many places, but few rival the winding mountain paths of Jixia. 
 
The mountains stretched endlessly, each peak leading to the next, while streams murmured through lush green valleys. One wrong turn, and you could easily lose your way in this charming wilderness. 
 
 
 
Jixia Academy sits atop the highest peak of Jixia Mountain, offering a breathtaking view of the landscape through wisps of cloud: the verdant Springbrook Plains, the fertile Harvest Fields, and the majestic Aerfall Highlands. 
 
 
 
As I gazed at the paths I had traversed, I marveled at how the mountains, which had taken days to climb, now seemed no bigger than autumn leaves, with the people below mere invisible specks busy with their lives. In that moment, I couldn't decide whether to marvel at nature's grandeur or reflect on the insignificance of mankind. 
 
 
 
Jixia Academy, the pinnacle of education in Jixia, was the destination of my long journey. 
 
I explored the campus, taking in the lively Martial Arts classes, the elegant Sorcery Runes, the intricate Mechcrafts, and the magnificent Wonders. 
 
 
 
My visit, however, wasn't without incident. Exhausted from days of hiking, I had to admit my fatigue. The teachers hosting me suggested I rest for a day or two before continuing my tour. 
 
 
 
I was truly grateful for their generosity. They called in a group of students, Herbalists, as I later learned, skilled in treating all kinds of ailments. The balms they provided worked wonders. After a few days of rest in the dorms they arranged for me, I felt rejuvenated—almost reborn. 
 
 
 
The mountains, seas, and clouds of Jixia are rare sights in this world, but what struck me as truly extraordinary were the passionate people of Jixia Academy. Even long after I leave Jixia, their faces will remain vivid in my mind. And whenever that happens, I'll cast aside my doubts and prepare to scale the next mountain peak I face.
zh_text:
数日奔波，终于到达稷下学院。 
 
疲惫的身体让我不禁感叹这一路的曲折蜿蜒。我去过的地方并不算少，但稷下群山的曲折山路让我着实吃惊。 
山峦层叠连亘，越过一座山后，又是更高的险峰，水流潺潺，山涧葱绿，身处其中极易迷失方向，一不小心就会在这茫茫山川里迷失前路。 
 
稷下学院建在稷下山的山顶最高处，从这里俯瞰稷下，种种景色透过细密的云雾映入眼帘：花草繁盛的春溪原、肥沃熙攘的丰云野、壮阔险要的云落高地都在云间忽隐忽现。 
 
望着自己曾踏足过的土地，花费数日得以登顶的雄山险峰现在不过是秋叶大小，而在其中生活、奔波的人则完全不可觅其踪迹，一时间，我不知该感叹天地造物者之伟力，还是人类之渺小。 
 
稷下学院，既是稷下的最高学府，也是我漫漫旅途的目的地。 
活力四射的武道教学、优雅瑰丽的魔道术印、严谨精巧的机关造物，和庄严伟岸的奇迹逐次映入我的眼帘。 
 
参观途中也有些小插曲，经过前些日子的连续登山，我实在气力不支，便只能如实相告。招待我的老师便提议在我休整一两日之后，再仔细参观这座学府。 
 
我由衷感谢他们的热情好客，他们叫来另一群同学，我后来知道这些同学是名为百草家的百家学子，擅长医治各种疾病。百草家们给我外敷的药十分见效，我在学生们为我提供的宿舍床位上躺了几日，身体便如重获新生般复原。 
 
稷下的山、海、云皆为世间罕见，但最令我感到不凡之物，则是稷下学院充满热忱的人。相比即便离开稷下后许久，他们的神情仍会时常出现在我眼前，而每到这时，我就会收起沮丧，着手去翻越面前的一座座高山吧？

text:
You still don't get it, do you? Father chose me, not you! 
 
 
 
The person angrily shouting in front of me was my half-brother, Zhou Yann. Right behind him was my stepmother, clearly here to back him up. 
 
They were here again, trying to convince me to give up my claim to our family's Mechcraft legacy. Just like the last few times, my brother wore that same smug expression — as if he'd swallowed a whole Flameroll Fruit. 
 
 
 
"Zhou Ying, I think it's time you faced reality," Zhou Yann sneered, pulling something out of his bag and tossing it onto the wooden table. 
 
"This is a letter from Father. Take a good look." 
 
 
 
A letter from Father? My heart sank as I opened it, carefully examining every detail, wary of any forgery. 
 
But the handwriting, the tone — it was undeniably his. 
 
 
 
The letter started with some concern for my well-being, a few words about the family, and then suddenly shifted: 
 
"My daughter, there's something I've been considering for a while, and your mother often brings it up too. I'm planning to bring you back to Chang'an from Jixia. Once you're home, I won't force you to study Mechcraft anymore. You can do whatever you like, just as you wish. 
 
Your mother is right — I've been too hard on you. It wasn't my intention, but I can't take our family's legacy lightly, and your last few exam results... To be honest, they've been quite disappointing. 
 
Here's what we'll do: I hear the next Mechcraft exam is coming up soon. I'll return to see how you both perform. If you're still the same as before, I'll have no choice but to leave your brother in Jixia to continue his studies alone. Take care of yourself..." 
 
 
 
Cold sweat soaked through my clothes, and the letter trembled in my hands. 
 
"So, do you understand now? You've already lost," Zhou Yann said smugly. 
 
"Lost? Not necessarily. Father said he would consider the next Mechcraft exam results before—" I started to argue, but someone cut me off. 
 
 
 
"With your bottom-rank Mechcraft scores, can anything you build even function?" My stepmother finally spoke up, her tone dripping with disdain. If Zhou Yann had swallowed one Flameroll Fruit, she must have downed three, and rotten ones at that. 
 
 
 
"Do you really think you're qualified?" Zhou Yann jeered. "I suggest you pack up and head back to Chang'an yourself, before you embarrass yourself in front of Father." 
 
 
 
My stepmother chimed in, "Exactly. You're just wasting time here. Why not go back home and make room for someone who's actually serious?" 
 
 
 
"No way," I snapped. "I'm not giving up just like that. I'll give it my all in the next Mechcraft exam. If you think I'm going to quit so easily, you can forget about it!" 
 
 
 
"You... you're..." Zhou Yann was trembling with anger. 
 
"Enough, why waste energy on someone like her? Calm down, no need to get worked up. Let's go. We'll see who ends up embarrassed," my stepmother said, pulling Zhou Yann away. 
 
He shot me one last furious glance before they left, repeatedly looking back as they walked away. 
 
 
 
The world grew quiet, but my mind was anything but at peace. 
 
To be honest, after coming to Jixia, being away from my family's control, I had gotten a bit too reckless. Skipping classes, getting lost in fishing, failing to live up to my father's expectations, and making little progress in Mechcraft... 
 
 
 
But, can I really give up just like that? I admit I've been lazy and haven't worked hard enough, but if you think I'm going to surrender so easily, especially to those two, it's not happening. No way. I won't let that happen. Even if there's only a slim chance, I'm going to take it!

“你这家伙，难道还不明白吗？父亲选的是我，不是你！” 
 
站在我面前，愤怒地咆哮着的人正是我同父异母的弟弟，周琰。后面还跟着我的继母，很明显，她是来给弟弟撑腰的。 
他们又是来劝我放弃家传机关术的继承权的。跟前几次一样，我这个弟弟还同一副嘴脸——像是往嘴里塞了一整颗滚焰果似的。 
 
“周滢，我看你是不见棺材不掉泪。”说着，周琰从包里掏出了什么东西，扔在了木桌上。 
“这是父亲的信，自己好好看看吧。” 
 
父亲的信？我心中一惊，打开信，仔细检查了一番——以防是他们伪造的。 
但这字迹，这口吻，的确是父亲的亲笔。 
 
信的开头先是关心了一下我的近况，说了下家里的情况，然后突然话锋一转： 
“女儿，有件事我想了很久，你母亲也经常跟我提，我打算把你从稷下接回长安，回家之后我也不逼着你学那些机关术了，你想干什么就干什么，随你性子好了。 
你母亲说的对，我对你是有些太严格了，这并不是我想如此，只是对家传之术我不能当儿戏，而你前几次的考试成绩都……说实话，很让我失望。 
这样吧，听说下一次机关考试马上就要到了，到时候我回来看看你俩的表现，如果你还是之前那个样子，我就只好让你弟弟一个人留在稷下学习了。你好自为之吧……” 
 
冷汗，浸透了全身，还有我手中的信纸。 
“我说，你现在应该明白了吧。你已经输了。”周琰得意地说道。 
“输了？那可未必，父亲说还要参考下次机关考试的成绩再……”突然，有人打断了我的反驳。 
 
“全院倒数的机关术成绩，做出来的机关人能动吗？”许久不说话的继母突然插上一嘴。如果说她儿子是吃了一颗滚焰果的话，她得吃了三颗，还是烂掉的。 
 
“你不会真以为自己够资格吧？我劝你还是乖乖自己回长安去，免得到时候在父亲面前下不来台。”周琰说道。 
 
继母也附和着：“是啊，反正你在这儿也是每天不务正业，在哪儿混不是混呢？不如回老家，给好人腾腾地方。” 
 
“不可能的。”我厉声说道：“我不可能就这么放弃的。我会在下次机关测试中全力以赴，你们若是想就这么让我放弃的话，我劝你们还是死了这条心！” 
 
“你，你这是……”周琰气得发抖。 
“好了，何必跟这种人计较呢。乖，别把身体气坏了，没必要跟她浪费口舌，咱们回去。到时候难堪的可不是我们。” 
周琰愤愤地看了我一眼，然后被继母拉着离开了，走的时候还不住地回头。 
 
世界安静了，但我的内心却久久无法平静。 
说实话，来到稷下之后，远离了家庭的束缚，我确实有些太放肆了，经常逃课，沉迷于垂钓，辜负了父亲对我的期望，而且在机关术方面基本没什么长进…… 
 
但，我难道可以就这样轻言放弃吗？是的，我承认，我是有些慵懒，不够努力，可如果你想让我就这么束手就擒了，而且是败在这两个人手下，不可能，绝不可能，我不会允许这种事情发生。哪怕只有一点机会，我也要试一试！

You still don't get it, do you? Father chose me, not you! 
 
 
 
The person angrily shouting in front of me was my half-brother, Zhou Yann. Right behind him was my stepmother, clearly here to back him up. 
 
They were here again, trying to convince me to give up my claim to our family's Mechcraft legacy. Just like the last few times, my brother wore that same smug expression — as if he'd swallowed a whole Flameroll Fruit. 
 
 
 
"Zhou Ying, I think it's time you faced reality," Zhou Yann sneered, pulling something out of his bag and tossing it onto the wooden table. 
 
"This is a letter from Father. Take a good look." 
 
 
 
A letter from Father? My heart sank as I opened it, carefully examining every detail, wary of any forgery. 
 
But the handwriting, the tone — it was undeniably his. 
 
 
 
The letter started with some concern for my well-being, a few words about the family, and then suddenly shifted: 
 
"My daughter, there's something I've been considering for a while, and your mother often brings it up too. I'm planning to bring you back to Chang'an from Jixia. Once you're home, I won't force you to study Mechcraft anymore. You can do whatever you like, just as you wish. 
 
Your mother is right — I've been too hard on you. It wasn't my intention, but I can't take our family's legacy lightly, and your last few exam results... To be honest, they've been quite disappointing. 
 
Here's what we'll do: I hear the next Mechcraft exam is coming up soon. I'll return to see how you both perform. If you're still the same as before, I'll have no choice but to leave your brother in Jixia to continue his studies alone. Take care of yourself..." 
 
 
 
Cold sweat soaked through my clothes, and the letter trembled in my hands. 
 
"So, do you understand now? You've already lost," Zhou Yann said smugly. 
 
"Lost? Not necessarily. Father said he would consider the next Mechcraft exam results before—" I started to argue, but someone cut me off. 
 
 
 
"With your bottom-rank Mechcraft scores, can anything you build even function?" My stepmother finally spoke up, her tone dripping with disdain. If Zhou Yann had swallowed one Flameroll Fruit, she must have downed three, and rotten ones at that. 
 
 
 
"Do you really think you're qualified?" Zhou Yann jeered. "I suggest you pack up and head back to Chang'an yourself, before you embarrass yourself in front of Father." 
 
 
 
My stepmother chimed in, "Exactly. You're just wasting time here. Why not go back home and make room for someone who's actually serious?" 
 
 
 
"No way," I snapped. "I'm not giving up just like that. I'll give it my all in the next Mechcraft exam. If you think I'm going to quit so easily, you can forget about it!" 
 
 
 
"You... you're..." Zhou Yann was trembling with anger. 
 
"Enough, why waste energy on someone like her? Calm down, no need to get worked up. Let's go. We'll see who ends up embarrassed," my stepmother said, pulling Zhou Yann away. 
 
He shot me one last furious glance before they left, repeatedly looking back as they walked away. 
 
 
 
The world grew quiet, but my mind was anything but at peace. 
 
To be honest, after coming to Jixia, being away from my family's control, I had gotten a bit too reckless. Skipping classes, getting lost in fishing, failing to live up to my father's expectations, and making little progress in Mechcraft... 
 
 
 
But, can I really give up just like that? I admit I've been lazy and haven't worked hard enough, but if you think I'm going to surrender so easily, especially to those two, it's not happening. No way. I won't let that happen. Even if there's only a slim chance, I'm going to take it!

text:
August 5th, Sunny 
 
When I was young, people often praised my stamina. Inspired by this, I would try to outpace my classmates on mountain climbs, charging ahead as soon as we started, leaving everyone behind. 
 
 
 
But soon enough, I'd be exhausted, my initial impatience throwing off my breathing. By the time I rested on a rock, several classmates had already passed me. 
 
 
 
After a few experiences like this, I began to instinctively avoid training, and my technique turned into a mental hurdle. 
 
 
 
But thanks to a tip from Senior Zhang, I realized I should study the experiences of those who came before me. Trying to reinvent the wheel only leads to more obstacles. 
 
 
 
I calmed down and began to study the techniques and training guides left by predecessors. 
 
 
 
I started walking on mountain paths, paying attention to how "Qi" affects my movements. 
 
 
 
I practiced steady breathing and observed the mountain terrain. 
 
 
 
When I tried climbing again, I felt that my energy was no longer being wasted but was harmonizing with my body movements. Despite moving faster, my breathing remained steady. 
 
 
 
The fatigue from using brute force gradually disappeared, and my speed increased several times! 
 
 
 
I now have my own understanding of using "Qi," and I believe this is why our teacher takes us climbing to practice martial techniques. 
 
 
 
By reading and then applying the knowledge to practice, I'm starting to grasp the true essence of Martial Arts techniques.
zh_text:
八月五日 晴 
我少年时总被人夸耐力好，因此过往登山时只一味想把共行的诸位同学甩在身后，每每刚刚开始便立马冲将出去，一骑绝尘。 
 
但很快我就会感受到乏力，又因为先前的急躁，乱了气息。在我气喘吁吁地在一块山石上休憩时，已有多位同学的速度超过了我。 
 
此番几次后，我开始下意识地逃避训练，身法逐渐成了我的一块心结。 
 
但幸得张学姐提点，她告诉我，或许应该看看前人留下的修行经验，闭门造车只会让我陷入一个又一个瓶颈。 
 
我沉下心来，开始细细品读前辈留下来的身法要诀、修行指南。 
 
我开始在山道间踱行，感受“气”对于身法的影响。 
 
我试着平稳呼吸，观察了附近的山势。 
 
在我终于又开始尝试攀登时，我感觉我的气力不再是徒劳地消耗，而是和我的身体动作相合在一起。明明移动的速度越来越快，但我的气息却平稳如常。 
 
先前空用蛮力时的疲惫逐渐消失，我的速度比之前提升了数倍有余！ 
 
我对“用气”也有了自己的理解，我想这就是老师要带我们登山以练习身法的原因吧。 
 
阅读知识后，再运用于登山的实践之中，才能最好地掌握武道身法的真正诀窍。

内容：针对稷下学院师生及百家的探访稿

被探访人：百草家，毕灵飞 
探访地点：学院生活区善生之庭 
问：同学，你毕业之后有什么想做的事吗？ 
答：我已经毕业很久了。 
问：这是你在学院待的第几年？ 
答：大概……十六年了。 
问：是对这里有特殊的感情吗？ 
答：我不想变老。 
问：这两者有什么联系吗？ 
答：只要我不毕业，一直给同学老师找麻烦，就永远年轻。 
问：嗯……是这个原因啊。 
答：还有，我入学那会儿，跟父老乡亲打过包票，必须要在稷下成就一番事业，不然就不回去！ 
问：所以，在你成就一番事业之后，就会回去对吗？ 
答：不用，我最近研究调配了一些草药，如果成功的话，服下之后能改变样貌，到时候我就以陌生人的身份回去，就没人认识我了。 
  
被探访人：准新生，赵昊 
探访地点：溯洄营地 
问：同学，你毕业之后有什么想做的事吗？ 
答：毕业？我连考试都还没通过呢！这回又挂了…… 
问：这是你参加的第几次考试？ 
答：记不清了……他们为什么总是取消我的参赛资格啊？好烦…… 
问：你最近一次是怎么被取消资格的？ 
答：机关人追，我就跑，他再追，我再跑，最后他燃料耗尽歇菜了，但老师居然说我跑出了考试区域，实战中哪有什么区域可言啊，明明赢得是我…… 
  
被探访人：机关学院阿花 
探访地点：机关学院 营造厅 
问：同学，你毕业之后有什么想做的事吗？ 
答：喵。 
问：留在机关学院搞破坏……倒是个很有趣的回答……请问这是你第几次弄坏机关了？ 
答：喵。 
问：是因为你对这种凹凸不平又复杂的环境没有抵制力吗？ 
答：喵。 
问：你觉得这样做不合理对吗？ 
答：喵。 
问：上一次让你有同样感受的人是谁，你还记得吗？ 
答：喵。 
问：所以，你是抱着这种想法，来看待机关学院的对吧？ 
答：哈！ 
问：没关系的，探访可以随时结束，如果你感觉不太……啊……

text:
Back in Alsahraa, I heard whispers of a mysterious figure known as "Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade."
Regrettably, I entered this world too late to witness his prowess or engage in combat with him—a true lament for any martial artist.

In Alsahraa, numerous vagabonds claimed to be disciples of "the Lone Blade," but they all ended up losing their teeth after facing me.
As legends piled up, my curiosity about the truth grew. Upon arriving at Jixia, I finally had the chance to follow in his footsteps!

Roaring Tiger Training Hall.
"I will verify personally whether the rumored 'Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade' is fact or fiction."
"Am I not tiger-like enough?"
Head Trainer Tigon burst into laughter upon hearing my declaration.
His thunderous chuckle shook the air.
When I first met Head Trainer Tigon, I was struck by his rare appearance—white base coat with black stripes, broad forehead, and high eyebrows. His tiger head resembled a boulder perched atop a towering physique, with thick limbs like tree trunks, even more imposing than the tales described. As he approached, the ground seemed to tremble beneath my feet...
Little did I know that his name "Tigon" actually came from being a rare white tiger half-breed!

I must admit, seeing him made my heart race.
Though my blade skills might match his, martial arts duels often come down to a single decisive move.
If I sparred with this mountain of a man, I wasn't sure if I could withstand his full strength before hitting the ground.
Just as I hesitated, Tigon declared, "I have never turned down a challenge!"
With that, I steeled myself for the duel.
As I unsheathed my curved blade, Tigon's eyes lit up—is this the unspoken bond between fellow blade enthusiasts?
I chose not to attack first. Given our size difference, my offensive would likely be swiftly neutralized.
Instead, I planned to use my agility to lure him into making the first move. After all, my primary goal was to witness the legendary warrior's skill.
Tigon's swordplay was fierce and powerful, each strike difficult to evade. When my curved blade clashed with his sharp edge, sparks erupted from the metal collision.
After several rounds, I began to tire, feeling pain in my jaws, my steps slowing, and my defensive speed noticeably decreasing.
Tigon's swordsmanship was exceptional, his blade seemingly imbued with life. He and his weapon were connected, each movement and breath synchronized in perfect rhythm.
Before my eyes unfolded a living legend.
I once heard that though Navenian blade practitioners are scarce, similar techniques have been developed there. Did Tigon inspire Navenia's warriors, or was it the other way around?

The outcome of this duel was already decided, but adhering to the spirit of martial arts, I fought until the end.
I lost.
Despite the gap in power, I saw how much effort Tigon put into defeating me.
Tigon earned his nickname "the Lone Blade" because few can withstand even a single strike from him. To have exchanged blows multiple times was an honor in itself, regardless of defeat.
After the match, Tigon generously praised my blade skills and invited me to return for another sparring session—or better yet, stay on as one of his disciples.
Although I deeply appreciated his recognition and admired his martial prowess, the vast lands of Jixia beckoned, filled with countless warriors waiting to be encountered.
Seeing my resolve, Tigon recommended another training hall in Jixia—Obsidian Flame Training Hall.
What new sights awaited me this time?

早在云中玉城时，我便对“虎步独行凌一刀”有所耳闻。 
但可惜我入世太迟，未能亲眼见识到“凌一刀”的身姿，更无缘与其切磋交流，这可谓是武者的一大憾事。 
 
云中不乏以武混世的登徒浪子，谎称自己的功夫是“凌一刀”亲传，但这些人最后都被我打得满地找牙。 
随着我听到的传说越多，我对“凌一刀”本人的就越好奇。我来到稷下后终于能够追上这位前辈的脚步了！ 
 
虎啸堂。 
“我要来亲自验证，口口相传的“虎步独行凌一刀”，是真是伪。” 
“难道我长得还不够虎么？” 
凌虎堂主听完我的阐述后，发出阵阵大笑。 
这笑声如雷鸣般震耳。 
刚见到这位凌虎堂主时，只看到他白底黑纹、高眉阔目的罕见样貌，一颗虎头如巨石，安置在险峰一般的身躯上，粗壮的四肢如松柏树干比传说所描绘的形象更加威风。他朝我走来时，我甚至产生了地动山摇的错觉…… 
我从未想到，虎步独行，居然是因为他本人是稀有的白虎魔种！ 
 
看到他的样貌后，我承认自己有些心慌。 
虽然我的刀术并不一定比不过他，但比武向来是一力降十会。 
若是与这位高大如山的朋友比试刀法，我不确定能否在倒地前试出其武技的极限。 
就在我迟疑之际，凌虎又发话：“我凌虎向来对比武挑战是来者不拒的！” 
 既然如此，那我不再犹豫，准备同他比试。 
当我亮出弯刀时，凌虎的眼睛忽然亮了，这难道是属于刀客之间的默契？ 
我没有选择进攻。以我们二人的体型差距，我的攻势只会被他迅速瓦解。 
我计划利用自己的灵活优势，吸引他出招，毕竟我此次比试的主要目的，是见证传说中的武者的实力。 
凌虎堂主的刀法刚猛无比，攻势强劲，令人难以躲闪，我的弯刀与他的锋极刃相对时，金属碰撞爆发出的火光四下飞溅。 
几回合下来，我感到体力不支，虎口处隐隐作痛，脚步变得沉重，招架的速度也明显下降。 
凌虎堂主刀术不凡，他手中的锋极刃仿佛被注入了生命。人与刀心灵相通，每一式的运力与呼吸都蕴含特殊的节律。 
这便是在我眼前出现的活生生的传说。 
我曾在听闻海都虽然习刀者稀少，但却开发出了类似的招式，究竟是凌虎堂主启发了海都武者还是海都武者启发了凌虎堂主呢？ 
 
这场对决胜负早已分晓，但本着武道之魂，我同他战到了最后。 
我输了。 
虽然实力有差距，但我看得出凌虎堂主为了赢我，也是费了不少气力。 
凌虎堂主的“凌一刀”绰号，是因为很多人连他一刀都接不住，故而得此称号。而我与他过招数次，已是虽败犹荣。 
比试结束后，他毫不吝啬地赞赏我的刀法，并邀请我日后再来比试，或者干脆留下来做他的门生。 
我虽然十分感激他的认可，也敬佩他的武艺，但稷下天地广阔，武者如云，还有许多地方等待我去探索。 
见我去意已定，凌虎堂主便向我推荐了另一个稷下武馆——墨焰阁。 
这次，我又会见识到何种景色呢？

我没有选择进攻。以我们二人的体型差距，我的攻势只会被他迅速瓦解。 
我计划利用自己的灵活优势，吸引他出招，毕竟我此次比试的主要目的，是见证传说中的武者的实力。 
凌虎堂主的刀法刚猛无比，攻势强劲，令人难以躲闪，我的弯刀与他的锋极刃相对时，金属碰撞爆发出的火光四下飞溅。

凌虎堂主刀术不凡，他手中的锋极刃仿佛被注入了生命。人与刀心灵相通，每一式的运力与呼吸都蕴含特殊的节律。 
这便是在我眼前出现的活生生的传说。 
我曾在听闻海都虽然习刀者稀少，但却开发出了类似的招式，究竟是凌虎堂主启发了海都武者还是海都武者启发了凌虎堂主呢？

我输了。

凌虎堂主的“凌一刀”绰号，是因为很多人连他一刀都接不住，故而得此称号。而我与他过招数次，已是虽败犹荣。 
比试结束后，他毫不吝啬地赞赏我的刀法，并邀请我日后再来比试，或者干脆留下来做他的门生。 
我虽然十分感激他的认可，也敬佩他的武艺，但稷下天地广阔，武者如云，还有许多地方等待我去探索。 
见我去意已定，凌虎堂主便向我推荐了另一个稷下武馆——墨焰阁。 
这次，我又会见识到何种景色呢？

Back in Alsahraa, I heard whispers of a mysterious figure known as "Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade."
Regrettably, I entered this world too late to witness his prowess or engage in combat with him—a true lament for any martial artist.

In Alsahraa, numerous vagabonds claimed to be disciples of "the Lone Blade," but they all ended up losing their teeth after facing me.
As legends piled up, my curiosity about the truth grew. Upon arriving at Jixia, I finally had the chance to follow in his footsteps!

Roaring Tiger Training Hall.
"I will verify personally whether the rumored 'Tiger's Step, the Lone Blade' is fact or fiction."
"Am I not tiger-like enough?"
Head Trainer Tigon burst into laughter upon hearing my declaration.
His thunderous chuckle shook the air.
When I first met Head Trainer Tigon, I was struck by his rare appearance—white base coat with black stripes, broad forehead, and high eyebrows. His tiger head resembled a boulder perched atop a towering physique, with thick limbs like tree trunks, even more imposing than the tales described. As he approached, the ground seemed to tremble beneath my feet...
Little did I know that his name "Tigon" actually came from being a rare white tiger half-breed!

I must admit, seeing him made my heart race.
Though my blade skills might match his, martial arts duels often come down to a single decisive move.
If I sparred with this mountain of a man, I wasn't sure if I could withstand his full strength before hitting the ground.
Just as I hesitated, Tigon declared, "I have never turned down a challenge!"
With that, I steeled myself for the duel.
As I unsheathed my curved blade, Tigon's eyes lit up—is this the unspoken bond between fellow blade enthusiasts?
I chose not to attack first. Given our size difference, my offensive would likely be swiftly neutralized.
Instead, I planned to use my agility to lure him into making the first move. After all, my primary goal was to witness the legendary warrior's skill.
Tigon's swordplay was fierce and powerful, each strike difficult to evade. When my curved blade clashed with his sharp edge, sparks erupted from the metal collision.
After several rounds, I began to tire, feeling pain in my jaws, my steps slowing, and my defensive speed noticeably decreasing.
Tigon's swordsmanship was exceptional, his blade seemingly imbued with life. He and his weapon were connected, each movement and breath synchronized in perfect rhythm.
Before my eyes unfolded a living legend.
I once heard that though Navenian blade practitioners are scarce, similar techniques have been developed there. Did Tigon inspire Navenia's warriors, or was it the other way around?

The outcome of this duel was already decided, but adhering to the spirit of martial arts, I fought until the end.
I lost.
Despite the gap in power, I saw how much effort Tigon put into defeating me.
Tigon earned his nickname "the Lone Blade" because few can withstand even a single strike from him. To have exchanged blows multiple times was an honor in itself, regardless of defeat.
After the match, Tigon generously praised my blade skills and invited me to return for another sparring session—or better yet, stay on as one of his disciples.
Although I deeply appreciated his recognition and admired his martial prowess, the vast lands of Jixia beckoned, filled with countless warriors waiting to be encountered.
Seeing my resolve, Tigon recommended another training hall in Jixia—Obsidian Flame Training Hall.
What new sights awaited me this time?

Talks by Candlelight focuses on renowned Cannoneers, featuring an interview with a different Cannoneer in each issue. Through these candid conversations, we reveal the secrets behind their research and share the stories behind the scenes, bringing readers closer to the heart of these individuals with warm and engaging writing. 
 
 
When we arrived at the agreed-upon terrace, the familiar and striking figure in red was nowhere to be seen. The lively atmosphere of Ember Garden was as bustling as ever, with the sounds of firing pins and hissing steam filling the air, mingling with the sharp scent of gunpowder, creating an overwhelming sensory experience. 
 
 
Many can't endure this kind of life. Grease stains often find their way onto cuffs and scarves, and the meticulously arranged outfits from the morning inevitably end up in the wash by evening, requiring at least three rounds of rinsing to restore their original colors. The chaotic air is another challenge; seasoned Cannoneers have mastered the art of breathing just right to avoid choking on the dust that newcomers often struggle with. After enduring the dual trials of cannons and their environment, those who remain inevitably develop unique quirks and temperaments. It seems that those who choose to live alongside fire eventually become it themselves. 
 
 
When those hands playfully landed on my shoulder, I wasn't surprised, yet I still let out a small yelp, drawing friendly laughter from my companion and the prankster. The newcomer apologized for the scare while setting down three drinks for us. As the wooden cups were passed around, slices of Phantom Dewcap Grass danced in the clear water, leaving a trail of playful bubbles. 
 
 
"Sorry! Two kids called me to help with some equipment, so I got held up," Blazen said as he pulled out a chair and sat down, immediately grabbing his cup and taking a hearty drink. I took the opportunity to glance at the name tag pressed against the bottom of my cup, and after confirming it had my companion's name on it, I discreetly returned it and quickly picked up the correct one. 
 
 
The boisterous man before us is none other than the beloved Blazen, a teacher at the School of Mechcrafts. According to the students, Blazen never acts like a typical teacher. He sports a youthful hairstyle, pays no mind to age differences, and plays alongside them without a care. But if there's one thing that causes trouble, it's probably his slightly flawed vision. 
 
 
As a scholar dealing with cannon Mechcrafts, one would naturally expect him to have exceptional eyesight, necessary for working with precision components. That's the general assumption about Cannoneers. However, Blazen chooses to ignore such rumors, neither hiding his visual impairment nor giving up his study of cannons. He has carved out his own space in the field. 
 
 
It's hard to say whether Blazen cares much about his eyesight. We only know that he rarely explains the cause. Some speculate it's a congenital condition, while others think it's an injury sustained while saving someone. But the real answer remains obscured by the smoke of battle, hidden from view. 
 
 
After some small talk, we broached the question that had piqued everyone's curiosity. As expected, he waved it off, signaling that he didn't want too much attention on the subject. However, through bits and pieces of his words, we managed to piece together a plausible story. 
 
 
Just like every ripe fruit once had its green days, Blazen was once a spirited youth. During his time at the Academy, his fiery heart burned bright, refusing to settle into a mundane life under the heat. As his ambition grew, one day, a burst of vibrant color shot from the muzzle, and sharp fragments grazed the skin around his eye. 
 
 
When the topic of his younger days came up again, Blazen instinctively brushed over the scar near his eye. "I know some people, after their own failures, can't stand to see others succeed. Instead of offering congratulations, they harbor resentment," he spoke lightly of emotions long buried. Outside, in the garden, groups of students were shouting, seemingly preparing for some grand performance. "But what's the point of that? I chose the path of pursuing the power of firearms, so I won't complain. Protecting them as they continue to explore this path, celebrating and seeing them off with fireworks, isn't that a joyful and proud thing to do?" 
 
 
As his words trailed off, a thunderous boom echoed beside us. We all turned to look, and there in the students' hands, stars and bouquets of firelight blossomed. The sky darkened, and the brilliant flames burst forth, blending with the evening glow on the horizon, illuminating the joyful figures of children rushing in from all directions. At that moment, I seemed to understand why Blazen chose this location for our interview and what lay behind his carefree smile that has kept him going all these years.
zh_text:
“烛下谈”栏目聚焦知名火器家，每期呈现一位火器家的访谈文字，揭露生活研究的秘辛，分享人前背后的趣事，用有温度的文字，带领读者走近他人的内心。 
 
我们来到约定好的露台时，并未发现那个熟悉而惹眼的红色身影。星火园的热闹气氛正如往常，撞针击发与蒸汽喷薄的声音接二连三地挤入空中，与灼热的火药气味一起，混合成烫人心神的一口呼吸。 
 
很多人受不了这种生活。油污常常擅自攀附上袖口和领巾，早上出门时收拾妥帖的衣服，到了晚上无论如何都得丢去桶里，让它在至少三次的淘洗后勉强恢复本来的色彩；而混沌的空气也是一大难题，经验丰富的火器家早已摸清每一次吐息的力道，好不让自己跟新人一样，被那些直往肺管子里钻的粉尘呛得涕泗横流。经历过火器与环境的共同拷打之后，仍留下来的人或多或少都染了些别样的脾气、生了些另类的性格。大概选择与火伴生的人，最终总会化身为火。 
 
那双手恶作剧似地拍上我的肩头时，我虽并不意外，却还是发出一声轻呼，惹来同伴与恶作剧者善意的调笑。来人一边为此番惊吓致歉，一边为我们端上三杯饮品。木杯交错推转之际，幻沫菇草在清水中雀跃，带出了一串可爱的泡沫。 
 
“哎！有两个孩子喊我去调试设备，耽搁了。”星芒拉开椅子落座后，立即端起自己的杯子痛饮起来。我趁机垂眼看了看手中杯底压着的姓名牌，确定上面写着的是同伴的名字之后，不动声色地将其物归原主，又迅速地拿过了正确的一杯。 
 
眼前这位豪放不羁的男人，正是在机关学院中受人爱戴的星芒老师。据学生们所说，星芒从不以教师身份自居，反而留着朝气蓬勃的发型，全然不顾年纪差距而和他们玩在一起；但要说唯一一件造成困扰的事，恐怕要数他明显有些缺陷的视力。 
 
作为与火器机关打交道的学者，自然需要有非比寻常的视力，这样才能在面对精密零件时游刃有余。这是一般人对火器家的设想，面对这样的流言，星芒却选择置若罔闻，既不掩盖自己视力损伤的事实，也不放弃火器学习的道路，硬生生在其中闯出了属于自己的天地。 
 
关于视力问题，我们很难说星芒是否将其放在心上，只知道他几乎从来不对外解释个中原委。有人猜是不是先天疾病，也有人猜是不是救人所伤，那个真正的答案却始终掩藏在茫茫硝烟之后，叫人看不清真正的模样。 
 
些许寒暄之后，我们尝试着向星芒抛出了这个众人好奇已久的问题。不出所料，他果然摆了摆手，做出一副并不希望过多在意的样子。不过，在只言片语中，我们还是尽力拼凑出了些许可信的因果。 
 
如同每一颗成熟的果实都有过青涩的年华一般，星芒也曾是个意气风发的少年。在那些就读于学院的日子里，年轻的心火焰般跃动，绝不甘心循规蹈矩地成为炽热之下一撮默默无闻的积灰。于是进取之心越盛，终有一日，绚烂色彩从炮口射向天际，锐利弹片却划破眼周的皮囊。 
 
再度提起年少的日子，星芒下意识地拂过了眼上的疤痕。“我知道有些人自己失败之后再也无法正视别人的成功，不仅不去祝福，还会愤恨地咒怨。”他轻描淡写地谈起心中尘封已久的情绪，露台外面的园子里，学生们三五成群地呼喝起来，似乎在酝酿什么盛大的表演，“但那有什么意义？追求火器力量的路是我选的，我便不会去抱怨。护着他们在这条路上继续探索，用烟花为他们庆祝与送行，不也是很快乐、很值得骄傲的事吗？” 
 
话音未落，旁边便是一声轰雷般的爆鸣。我们不约而同看去，那一簇簇星子与花束般的火光正在学生们的手中绽放。天色黯淡，焰色喷薄而出，正与天边晚霞交相辉映，照亮了孩子们嬉笑着从四面八方涌来的身影。这一瞬间，我似乎明白了星芒将访谈地点选在这里的用意，也明白了他那快意笑容背后究竟是为了什么才坚持至今。

The newcomer apologized for the scare while setting down three drinks for us. As the wooden cups were passed around, slices of Phantom Dewcap Grass danced in the clear water, leaving a trail of playful bubbles. 
 
 
"Sorry! Two kids called me to help with some equipment, so I got held up," Blazen said as he pulled out a chair and sat down, immediately grabbing his cup and taking a hearty drink. I took the opportunity to glance at the name tag pressed against the bottom of my cup, and after confirming it had my companion's name on it, I discreetly returned it and quickly picked up the correct one.

He sports a youthful hairstyle, pays no mind to age differences, and plays alongside them without a care. But if there's one thing that causes trouble, it's probably his slightly flawed vision. 
 
 
As a scholar dealing with cannon Mechcrafts, one would naturally expect him to have exceptional eyesight, necessary for working with precision components. That's the general assumption about Cannoneers. However, Blazen chooses to ignore such rumors, neither hiding his visual impairment nor giving up his study of cannons. I chose the path of pursuing the power of firearms, so I won't complain. text:
November 20
Ever since we visited the Forbidden Chamber and learned of that sealed knowledge, everything has changed.

I told him he was too obsessed with the destructive power of ancient magic, but he claimed it was I who had changed—that the Academy had influenced me so deeply that I had forgotten my "mission."

When he left, Xinwuwei chased after him with a mechanical toy in its mouth, but I immediately ordered it to stop.
It was so frightened it didn't dare move, and that was when I realized it couldn't understand the complex relationships between people, nor why friends could turn into enemies overnight.

Qin Xiao, oh Qin Xiao, I feel like I can see you less and less clearly. You don't even remember many of the things we experienced together.
We created Xinwuwei to prove ourselves, but did you pay a price I know nothing about?
<69D0FF>Yet even true monsters can maintain a pure and kind nature.</>
<69D0FF>And yet, despite how hard I tried to hold your hand, I still became your enemy.</>

The lineage of the Divine Forge is long gone, unrecognizable; what "mission" could there possibly be left?
Before Xinwuwei is tainted by the dust of this world, I think it is time to take it and leave.
zh_text:
十一月二十日 
自从我们去过秘禁阁，了解了那些尘封的知识，一切就都变了。 
 
我说他太痴迷上古魔道术带来的破坏性，他反而说是我变了，学院对我影响太深，让我忘记了自己的“使命”。 
 
他走的时候，辛午未叼着机关玩具追他，我立刻喝止了它。 
它吓得动都不敢动，我才意识到，它无法理解人与人之间复杂的关系，也无法理解朋友为何会一夜之间变成敌人。 
 
秦霄啊秦霄，我好像越来越看不清你，很多原本我们一起经历的事，你都记不得。 
我们一起创造辛午未本是为了证明自己，但你是不是还付出了，我不知道的代价？ 
<69D0FF>可真正的怪物都能保持单纯善良的本性。</> 
<69D0FF>而我那么尽力地握住你的手，还是成了你的敌人。</> 
 
神铸一脉早已面目全非，哪还有“使命”可言。 
在辛午未染上人世的尘污之前，我想，是时候带它离开了。

text:
The name "Scholarly Tiger" comes from popular usage. As Hunters who value folk traditions, we'll continue using this term in our writings. Despite their feline title, Scholarly Tigers are actually small, friendly creatures. 
 
 
 
Long ago, when Jixia Academy was just a humble schoolhouse, a teacher prepared to discipline some distracted students with his ferule. Suddenly, a fluffy little creature darted onto the podium, curiously surveying the room before settling down. Its presence eased the tension—the teacher put away his ferule, and the students refocused. From that day on, the amazing creature appeared punctually at every lesson, eventually becoming a part of the school. That's how it earned the name "Scholarly Tiger." 
 
 
 
People love cuddling these adorable creatures for their soft, snowy fur and gentle, fresh scent. Scholarly Tigers love being groomed, which speaks to the close relationship between humans and animals. 
 
 
 
About the size of a child, Scholarly Tigers have muscular bodies, broad chests, and short, thick necks. Their large, wedge-shaped heads are flat on top, with two small horns crowning their heads. Dark, bright eyes shine above round muzzles and slightly sunken noses. Their long, fluffy ears flick with interest, and teal and peach markings adorn their brows and the corners of their eyes. 
 
 
 
As Jixia's most beloved pets, Scholarly Tigers prefer living indoors and enjoy playing with children. They often wear name tags on collars made of fine red strings, indicating their owners. These friendly pets share a close bond with their humans, favoring comfortable companionship over wild antics. Interestingly, they have a habit of sneaking into classrooms and sitting in on lessons. Students are baffled: why would anyone enjoy attending class? Some speculate that Scholarly Tigers feed on knowledge, especially savoring the driest lectures. Others believe they embody wisdom itself, sent to the mortal realm to ensure academic rigor among the youth... 
 
 
 
In our search for truth, we've visited villages and towns with the help of tools from the School of Mechcrafts. Our findings suggest that Scholarly Tigers' large ears allow them to detect rhythms in teachers' voices that are imperceptible to humans. While research into these special frequencies remains inconclusive, this evidence-based hypothesis holds more value than the fanciful legends shared as gossip.

堂听虎的名字是从坊间流传下来的习惯叫法，本着以民为本的原则，我们游猎家自然会遵循乡野百姓的传统文化，在本书以及后续的文章中沿用这个称谓。虽然以虎为名，但实际上它们是非常亲近人的小型动物。 
 
在很久以前，稷下学院只是一间质朴的学堂，老师在里面传道授课，学子在里面满是困惑，就在老师准备掏出戒尺的时候，一只毛茸茸的小家伙突然乱入，径直地窜到了讲台上，好奇地打探了周围一圈，竟又原地趴了起来——它的出现可以化干戈为玉帛：老师收起了戒尺，而学生也开始认真上课了。再后来这只神奇的生物每逢课堂便会准时出现，成为了学堂里的一份子，也因此得名堂听虎。 
 
也许是因为堂听虎那雪白的皮毛十分柔软，以及它们通体所散发着的淡淡清香，人们也很喜欢和这些家伙进行亲密接触，而定期梳理毛发也会让堂听虎感到舒服，两方双赢，人与动物便到达了一个融洽和谐的境界。 
 
堂听虎的外形跟孩童一般大，身体曲线明显，胸部周长偏宽，肌肉发达，颈粗而短。它们的大脑袋往往呈楔形，头顶扁平，长有两个小犄角，瞳色黝黑，眼睛炯炯有神，吻都呈圆形，短鼻子略有凹陷，耳朵修长且蓬松，在眉宇和下眼尾间还有着缥色与桃色相间的斑纹。 
 
堂听虎无疑是最受稷下人喜爱的宠物，它们分布广泛，喜欢生活在室内，更喜爱与孩童玩耍，家养的堂听虎一般都会佩戴着围脖的红绳，而在绳上的挂牌则会显示出主人的名字。作为宠物，堂听虎很是通人性，相比每天爬高上低、上蹿下跳，它们更愿意去跟人打交道，尤其喜欢陪着主人散心。此外它们还有一个为稷下学子所疑惑不已的习惯，就是总爱窜进学堂中与学子们一同听课。那些学子们做梦也想不明白，怎么会真的有家伙天生就爱上课呢？有人猜测堂听虎其实是以知识为食，越是枯燥的课程，营养其实就越丰富，它也就越爱吃。更有甚者觉得，堂听虎就是知识的化身，它来到凡间是为了监督年轻人有没有好好读书…… 
 
本着溯源的精神，我们游猎家走访了大大小小的村庄与市镇，在机关学院提供的器具支持下，得出了这样的猜测结论：学堂上教书育人的声音可以被堂听虎的大耳朵捕捉到人耳无法察觉的音律，虽然目前有关特殊音律的研究还没有详尽的成果，但比起那些无稽的传说让人当做茶余饭后的谈资，还是有所推敲和考据的叙述更有价值。

堂听虎无疑是最受稷下人喜爱的宠物，它们分布广泛，喜欢生活在室内，更喜爱与孩童玩耍，家养的堂听虎一般都会佩戴着围脖的红绳，而在绳上的挂牌则会显示出主人的名字。作为宠物，堂听虎很是通人性，相比每天爬高上低、上蹿下跳，它们更愿意去跟人打交道，尤其喜欢陪着主人散心。此外它们还有一个为稷下学子所疑惑不已的习惯，就是总爱窜进学堂中与学子们一同听课。那些学子们做梦也想不明白，怎么会真的有家伙天生就爱上课呢？有人猜测堂听虎其实是以知识为食，越是枯燥的课程，营养其实就越丰富，它也就越爱吃。更有甚者觉得，堂听虎就是知识的化身，它来到凡间是为了监督年轻人有没有好好读书…… 
 
本着溯源的精神，我们游猎家走访了大大小小的村庄与市镇，在机关学院提供的器具支持下，得出了这样的猜测结论：学堂上教书育人的声音可以被堂听虎的大耳朵捕捉到人耳无法察觉的音律，虽然目前有关特殊音律的研究还没有详尽的成果，但比起那些无稽的传说让人当做茶余饭后的谈资，还是有所推敲和考据的叙述更有价值。

The name "Scholarly Tiger" comes from popular usage. As Hunters who value folk traditions, we'll continue using this term in our writings. Despite their feline title, Scholarly Tigers are actually small, friendly creatures. 
 
 
 
Long ago, when Jixia Academy was just a humble schoolhouse, a teacher prepared to discipline some distracted students with his ferule. Suddenly, a fluffy little creature darted onto the podium, curiously surveying the room before settling down. Its presence eased the tension—the teacher put away his ferule, and the students refocused. From that day on, the amazing creature appeared punctually at every lesson, eventually becoming a part of the school. That's how it earned the name "Scholarly Tiger." 
 
 
 
People love cuddling these adorable creatures for their soft, snowy fur and gentle, fresh scent. Scholarly Tigers love being groomed, which speaks to the close relationship between humans and animals. 
 
 
 
About the size of a child, Scholarly Tigers have muscular bodies, broad chests, and short, thick necks. Their large, wedge-shaped heads are flat on top, with two small horns crowning their heads. Dark, bright eyes shine above round muzzles and slightly sunken noses. Their long, fluffy ears flick with interest, and teal and peach markings adorn their brows and the corners of their eyes. 
 
 
 
As Jixia's most beloved pets, Scholarly Tigers prefer living indoors and enjoy playing with children. They often wear name tags on collars made of fine red strings, indicating their owners. These friendly pets share a close bond with their humans, favoring comfortable companionship over wild antics. Interestingly, they have a habit of sneaking into classrooms and sitting in on lessons. Students are baffled: why would anyone enjoy attending class? Some speculate that Scholarly Tigers feed on knowledge, especially savoring the driest lectures. Others believe they embody wisdom itself, sent to the mortal realm to ensure academic rigor among the youth... 
 
 
 
In our search for truth, we've visited villages and towns with the help of tools from the School of Mechcrafts. Our findings suggest that Scholarly Tigers' large ears allow them to detect rhythms in teachers' voices that are imperceptible to humans. While research into these special frequencies remains inconclusive, this evidence-based hypothesis holds more value than the fanciful legends shared as gossip.

"Tales and Legends of the Fourth School"
This volume is a collection of legends and ghost stories about the "Fourth School" that I, Zhuge Liang, gathered during my time as a student at Jixia.

<69D0FF>Zhuge Liang's Note: This is a forgery written in my name, though it is amusing enough to serve as a light pastime.</>

First, Eternal Life
There is a legend in a village east of the Jixia mountains: many years ago, on the day the sun was at its highest, two brothers went up the mountain to pick fruit. When they reached the heights, a beam of intense light descended from the sky and struck the older brother, who then vanished. For years after, no one found any trace of him.

Many years later, the younger brother, now with a head full of white hair, went up the mountain and saw a figure glowing with light.

After returning to the village, he told the villagers about this, insisting that it was his brother, who still looked as young as the day he went missing.

Second, The Stubborn Stone
Many years ago, a stranger drifted into Jixia. To survive, he worked for a local stonemason. After a few years, his skills matured, and he often went to the distant mountains to quarry stone for the masons.

One day, he heard a stone speaking, asking to be taken home. The stranger found it hard to believe and told the other quarrymen about it.

But no one else could hear it, so they dismissed it as the stranger's delusion. They treated the stone as ordinary material and eventually used it to build a house.

Not long after, the residents of the house began to hear strange noises, like someone talking:
"Go... home".

《第四学院怪谈传说集》 
本册书是我——诸葛亮作为稷下学生，在调查期间了解到的关于“第四学院”的传说与怪谈。 
 
<69D0FF>诸葛亮批注：此系假借我名的伪作，不过写的还算有趣，可供茶余饭后无聊消遣用。</> 
 
一、永生 
稷下山区东侧的村落中有这样一则传说，许多年前，在太阳最高的那天，一对兄弟俩上山采果子，行至高处时，从天而降一束强光照在哥哥身上，哥哥便消失，此后数年间，都没有人发现他的踪迹。 
 
许多过去，满头白发的弟弟上山时，见到了一个通体发光的人。 
 
回村后他把这事告诉了村民，并且坚称那是他的哥哥，看上去还像当初失踪时一样年轻。 
 
二、顽石 
多年前之前，一位外乡人流落到稷下，为了生存，他帮镇上的石匠干活，几年过去，他的技术已日臻成熟，常常到远处的山区为石匠们开采石料。 
 
一天，他听到了一块石头在说话，让人把他送回家，外乡人有些难以置信，便将这件事告诉给其他采石工。 
 
但其他人都听不到，以为是外乡人的臆想，不以为意，把那块石头当做普通石料使用，最后盖成了房子。 
 
没过多久，屋内的住户总是听到怪声，像是一个人在说话。 
“回……家”。

The study of dyes was previously called the "study of cinnabar and blue," as red and blue are the two most common colors of dyes.

From ancient times to the present, people have been searching for and studying methods to color textiles, leather, and other materials. In this process, various dye production processes have emerged. This process can generally be divided into two categories: extracting natural dyes and making artificial dyes.

Natural dyes are mostly extracted from plants. Jixia has many common plants that can be used for dye production, such as: Buse Ru, Yan Tao Flower, Xuan Lan Grass, etc.

The simplest method for making natural dyes is the "liquid extraction method": wash the branches and leaves of the required plants, put them into water or other solutions, heat, filter, and concentrate.

Most artificial dyes are not specialized dyes but are often by-products of industrial production. For example, some residues from metal smelting can be used as black dyes, and some medicinal residues from pharmaceutical production can also be used as dyes after processing.

Next, I will briefly introduce the production process of ceramics. The most basic is the selection of raw materials. Pottery making is not just any soil; to get pottery clay, one often has to dig two feet deep to find sand-free clay. Porcelain clay is even harder to find and is often only available in very few places.

After having the raw materials, the next step is to make ceramics. Pottery is relatively easy to make. First, take the mud according to the size of the required vessel, remove the excess or add more, knead it into a round barrel shape, then hold the mud with both hands, rotate the pottery wheel, and constantly adjust to shape the pottery, and then fire it.

Porcelain is more difficult and sometimes requires more than two types of porcelain clay to form. Before making porcelain, the porcelain clay is usually put into a vat and clarified with water. The fine material floats on top, pour it into another vat, and discard the coarse material. Only by repeating this can the soil used for porcelain making be obtained. Then it is similar to pottery, shaped, and finally fired. The firing temperature of most porcelain is very strict; if it is too low, it will not form, and if it is too high, it will crack. This is what porcelain makers often say: "When water and fire are both satisfied and the earth is combined, the vessel is formed."

Speaking of ceramics, I previously developed a ceramic containing cloud silk, which is much stronger than ordinary ceramics, smooth and delicate, feels warm like jade, and one can also see different shapes of cloud patterns due to the winding.

I previously gave one of the fine pieces to the School of Mechcraft, but I don't know if they have exhibited it yet. However, I guess that with such a good thing, they will definitely exhibit it.

The "Prairie Fire" column continues to focus on interesting discoveries in life, bringing thousands of inventions to the reader's eyes. Creation is not the patent of scholars; as long as you have a curious and brave heart, everyone is an inventor.

"The sound of firecrackers bids farewell to the old year, the spring breeze brings warmth to the Tusu wine. Thousands of households under the bright sun—hey! Are you familiar with Jixia Fox Wheat?"

Almost all children have a period where they like to mess with poetry. The classics written in books are so complex that secretly changing them into limericks and passing them around with friends actually brings a sense of "rebellion." It's just that this kind of childish behavior often gets lost in the corners of memory as one grows older, and if someone were to suddenly bring it up, one would blush and try to explain it away.

Every morning when the sky just turned white, Guan He would surely appear at the door of his small workshop, stretching his limbs while humming a vague nursery rhyme. The children passing by liked to greet him; he would smile shyly without answering, just pulling large handfuls of sugar-coated wheat grains from his pocket to share with them as snacks. After sending the children off, he would leisurely open the workshop door and start his day's work. From a very young age, Guan He was not the "smart child" the adults talked about. It would take him a dozen tries to memorize a poem, and occasionally he would remember it completely wrong; instead, he had his own unique insights into what food tasted good and what clothes looked nice.

The fat-bellied machine sat quietly in the center of the room, waiting for Guan He to pull the starter lever. The sugar-coated wheat grains were not only in Guan He's pockets but also stacked in sacks all over the room—numerous, neat, and exuding a faint, sweet aroma. While waiting for the popcorn machine to preheat, Guan He would recite a short limerick with a shy smile, as if performing a ritual. The machine would spray steam at just the right moment, landing on the rhyme of the poem—it's hard to say if it was a tacit coincidence or a cunning design.

People grew up eating meals made with Jixia Fox Wheat, having long since integrated the aroma of the wheat into their blood. Guan He especially loved all kinds of rice balls; he ate half as a child and two as an adult. After coming to Jixia Academy to study at his family's arrangement, he put all his crooked thoughts into researching food and drink. He couldn't stand the way his classmates and teachers sacrificed daily enjoyment for efficiency, so he resolutely specialized in firearm research, seemingly holding his breath, wanting to let his family and more people see the possibilities of mechanisms and recognize his pursuits.

Putting plump Jixia Fox Wheat into the stove, if one wasn't careful, excessive heat would cause a small explosion in the iron pot, and the victims were often a few popped wheat grains. Guan He secretly chewed these charred grains that should have been sent to the trash, and found that behind the slightly bitter burnt taste, a fragrance even better than cooked rice burst forth. So he bit the bullet and flattered a familiar gourmet, buying a set of good large pots from him. After moving everything back to the workshop, he threw himself into sleepless research.

Today's popcorn machine is his sixth-generation design, and the original prototype, wrapped in floral cloth, is properly stored in the corner of the room. After sufficient preheating, the popcorn machine's round belly can maintain a balanced temperature. The indicator light marking the heat soon goes out; at this time, open a small side door and put in blocks of cream. The cream blocks are made of rosin and fat, mixed with a large amount of sugar, which easily melts into a pool of sweet, golden spring under high heat. When the temperature indicator light turns on again, you can open the side door again and pour in a full scoop of Jixia Fox Wheat. As the control system continuously heats the furnace, the wheat grains seem to test the waters at first with a few faint pops, and after a few seconds, they finally let go and go all out, eventually returning to calm.

Unfortunately, because he hasn't figured out the exact relationship between temperature and popping, he can't pop perfect Jixia Fox Wheat flowers every time. The carefully prepared sugar-fat often sticks into a lump, sweet to the point of being cloying in some places and bland in others. The popped wheat flowers are also crooked, and some grains refuse to open their hearts no matter what, letting the husks burn into black charcoal while the inside remains raw. The Doudou Raccoon that wanders around seems to love sweets, and reaching out with its little paws to steal a bite is a common occurrence. However, Guan He doesn't feel discouraged by this; his notebooks have been filled one after another, and the last page lists a new sugar-fat ratio, with the addition of strawberry turning it into an exciting pink.

Perhaps one day in the future, a restaurant in Fengyunya will add a signature snack called "Popcorn Flower," with various colors and many flavors to choose from. And Guan He will continue to hum to his popcorn machine, which he has improved countless times, as if asking an old friend: "Jixia Fox Wheat, are you ripe yet?"

Source: Li Wanwan, Student Affairs Committee 
 
Subject: Academic Support Work Summary 
 
"Think back over your life—do you have any particular strengths or interests?" 
"Yes, as you can see now." 
"Eh...?" 
"I'm talking to all of you, yet I don't feel nervous at all." 
"Hmm... anything else? Physical coordination? Sensitivity to Aerflow? A passion for Mechcrafts?" 
"Not really." 
"But you've been here for two years; it's time to make a decision. Martial Arts, Sorcery, or Mechcrafts?" 
"Now I'm starting to feel nervous." 
The above is a record of a conversation between our support group and Liu Ming, a student who has been at Jixia Academy for two years but still hasn't chosen a school. 
 
We helped many students who felt lost or insecure. With our guidance, they gradually discovered their inner passions, overcame obstacles, and joined the school best suited to them. 
 
Liu Ming, however, was an exception. 
Despite our best efforts, we couldn't find any school—or even Society—that suited Liu Ming's aspiration. 
"I don't know why it's so easy for everyone else... The entrance exam drained all my energy," he confessed. 
 
We've been following the procedure: taking turns to reassure him, telling him he's got potential, stuff like that. 
Amid the chatter, I suddenly remembered why I had joined the group. "Wait, this isn't fair." 
The others stopped talking and looked at me. 
 
"This student has joint issues and feels pain on rainy days, so the School of Martial Arts isn't an option. He can't sense Sorcery Energy, so the School of Sorcery is also out. And he can't even get the Mechwings properly installed, so the School of Mechcrafts..." 
"Watch your words, please!" someone said.  
"I'm just stating facts. Everyone has potential, but we can't just lie to them..." 
"Your words. please!" 
"I'm not, I'm just..." 
 
After a long silence, Liu Ming asked in a low voice, "Can I join the support group?" 
Their eyes lit up like they had found a lifeline, eagerly nodding. 
To everyone's surprise, after joining us, Liu Ming's unique experiences resonated with many of the students we were helping. Before long, he became the most popular member, with students lining up to see him. 
 
Liu Ming has found his value, and our support group gained recognition because of it. 
But... can we really take credit for that?

内容：学业帮扶工作纪要 
  
“你可以仔细回想一下，你从小到大，有没有比较擅长的领域，或者是感兴趣的？” 
“就是现在。” 
“嗯？” 
“现在我和你们对话，能够流畅地表达自己的观点，心态平和，没有紧张到说不出话来。” 
“嗯……除了这点呢？比如身体的协调性？对云流的感知？对机关的热忱？” 
“好像都没有。” 
“可是目前只有武道、魔道和机关学院能够选择，你已经入学两年，该做选择了。” 
“我现在有点紧张了。” 
以上对话是我们帮扶会同帮扶对象的一次谈话记录。

Source: Li Wanwan, Student Affairs Committee 
 
Subject: Academic Support Work Summary 
 
"Think back over your life—do you have any particular strengths or interests?" 
"Yes, as you can see now." 
"Eh...?" 
"I'm talking to all of you, yet I don't feel nervous at all." 
"Hmm... anything else? Physical coordination? Sensitivity to Aerflow? A passion for Mechcrafts?" 
"Not really." 
"But you've been here for two years; it's time to make a decision. Martial Arts, Sorcery, or Mechcrafts?" 
"Now I'm starting to feel nervous." 
The above is a record of a conversation between our support group and Liu Ming, a student who has been at Jixia Academy for two years but still hasn't chosen a school. 
 
We helped many students who felt lost or insecure. With our guidance, they gradually discovered their inner passions, overcame obstacles, and joined the school best suited to them. 
 
Liu Ming, however, was an exception. 
Despite our best efforts, we couldn't find any school—or even Society—that suited Liu Ming's aspiration. 
"I don't know why it's so easy for everyone else... The entrance exam drained all my energy," he confessed. 
 
We've been following the procedure: taking turns to reassure him, telling him he's got potential, stuff like that. 
Amid the chatter, I suddenly remembered why I had joined the group. "Wait, this isn't fair." 
The others stopped talking and looked at me. 
 
"This student has joint issues and feels pain on rainy days, so the School of Martial Arts isn't an option. He can't sense Sorcery Energy, so the School of Sorcery is also out. And he can't even get the Mechwings properly installed, so the School of Mechcrafts..." 
"Watch your words, please!" someone said.  
"I'm just stating facts. Everyone has potential, but we can't just lie to them..." 
"Your words. please!" 
"I'm not, I'm just..." 
 
After a long silence, Liu Ming asked in a low voice, "Can I join the support group?" 
Their eyes lit up like they had found a lifeline, eagerly nodding. 
To everyone's surprise, after joining us, Liu Ming's unique experiences resonated with many of the students we were helping. Before long, he became the most popular member, with students lining up to see him. 
 
Liu Ming has found his value, and our support group gained recognition because of it. 
But... can we really take credit for that?

text:
Master Qin Li created countless intricate Mechcrafts during his lifetime. After completing his greatest creation, a giant flying Mechcraft, he fell into deep contemplation. 
 
His fame spread far and wide, but in a world free of war, his creation served no purpose. Every day, Jenner would stroke the Mechcraft three times and sigh deeply. 
 
 
 
One of his friends advised, "There are endless ways to use Mechcrafts in this world. Why limit yourself to soaring through the skies and slaying dragons? What about helping people in the mountains?" 
 
Qin Li retorted, "The art of Mechcrafts is a divine gift. How can it be wasted on the mere soil of the earth?" 
 
 
 
The friend left sadly, while Qin Li tossed and turned through a sleepless night. With the first light of dawn, he quietly packed his belongings and descended the mountain. 
 
The wind rustled through the wheat fields, and the golden sun slowly rose, bathing the land in light. 
 
Qin Li, who had once been so absorbed in creating Mechcrafts for war and destruction, had never really noticed the beauty of the fields he passed every day. 
 
 
 
In the nearby villages, Qin Li began repairing tools for the farmers, refusing to be paid. However, out of gratitude, the villagers insisted on treating him to freshly brewed rice wine, fragrant barley tea, and fresh caught fish... 
 
After several such occasions, Qin Li's once sharp and lean figure had become noticeably rounder. When his friend asked where he had been lately, Qin Li simply grunted, "Still researching the art of flying Mechcrafts." 
 
 
 
Not long after, Qin Li received an order from Harvest Fields, requesting a Mechcraft capable of slicing fish and slaughtering sheep. 
With little interest in the task, Qin Li threw himself into it for days on end, combining his decades of expertise in creating Mechcrafts with the practical knowledge he had gained from repairing farm tools. 
 
Eventually, he succeeded in creating a Mechcraft that was remarkably sharp and efficient, yet safe for the user — truly the pinnacle of Qin Li's skills. Even today, these Mechcrafts can still be found throughout Harvest Fields. 
 
 
 
When the Mechcraft was finished, Qin Li read the letter again and realized that the client had asked him to deliver it personally. Confused, he set off with the Mechcraft in tow.  
 
Along the way, villagers offered to help, and together they transported the Mechcraft to the client. Upon arrival, Qin Li recognized the familiar figure before him and finally understood. 
 
 
 
His friend looked around at the gathered villagers, smiled, and said, "So, Qin Li, it seems that your dragon-slaying skills have finally found their place in the soil of the earth. How does it feel?" 
 
Qin Li looked at the simple smiles of the villagers beside him, and for once, his face turned a bashful shade of red.

制造出无数机关的禽离大师，在完成自己的巨型机关后陷入了茫然。 
空前绝后的巨大飞天机关让他声名大噪，但当世早无战乱，机关空有威力无处施展，禽离每日抚摸三次机关，常叹息不止。 
 
友人劝说道：“世间机关可用之处万千，何必拘泥于登天屠龙之事，不如前往山间帮助村人。” 
禽离怒道：“机关之学皆为天授予，岂可为地上黄土所用。” 
 
友人叹息离去，禽离却辗转反侧，失眠了半宿。趁着晨光熹微，他整理好行装，悄悄下山。 
风吹麦浪，清晨的朝阳将晚霞缀满了天空，金色的土地上缓缓升起金色的太阳，麦苗们发出细碎的声响。 
如此美丽，只是之前禽离太过醉心机关杀人屠戮之道，从未正眼看过这片他每日都要经过的田地。 
 
禽离开始在附近的村庄中给农人们修缮器具，他分文不收，但村人们总是热情地要招待他，新造的米酿、绵长回甘的麦茶、刚钓上的鲜鱼…… 
盛情难却，几次三番下来，禽离连身体都圆润了不少，友人询问他最近都去了何处，禽离只是哼道：“仍在研究机关登天之术。” 
 
不日，禽离收到了来自丰云野的订单，请他设计一个能够切鱼开羊的机关。 
禽离无心他想，闷头制作了十几日，将自己数十年制作机关的技术，与近来修缮农具的经验几经结合，最终制作成功。 
 
这机关切鱼宰羊时刀刃异常锋利迅速，使用时也不会有误伤用者的风险。可谓是禽离机关所学大成之作，如今在丰云野依旧随处可见。 
不过机关制成，禽离才看向信上所说，要他亲自送到定制者面前。禽离疑惑，却还是带着机关前往，路上村人还前来帮忙，众人一并将机关运至定制者面前，禽离才看着熟悉的身影恍然大悟。 
 
友人目光扫视众人，笑道：“如今这屠龙之技终究是用在这黄土之上了，禽离大师，是何滋味？” 
禽离看向身旁质朴农人们的笑容，难得扭捏地红了脸。
